element.name: Persistence Adapter
element.documentation:
Mnemosyne's fifth responsibility tier encapsulates selected provider technology. It performs delegated native operations, receives/interprets engine acknowledgements, correlates native requests/transactions, and performs supplementary reads or out-of-band verification when needed within the delegated operation sequence. It establishes and reports the operation's actual known result under that operation's completion contract.
Dispatch or a native ACK alone cannot establish authoritative success unless it satisfies the required completion evidence. An engine without credible verification for claimed operations is a suitability concern; Indeterminate is truthful current uncertainty, not an excuse for an unsuitable provider. No mandatory second read for every write or universal proof threshold is imposed.
Native schemas, IDs, revisions and correlation support the governed reconstruction and identity/version obligations without replacing them. The physical contract need not be IU-shaped. Search, transactions, indexes, traversal, bulk, history or other capabilities may be additive and attach only to actual supporting PersistenceServices; no universal parity, fabricated search support or one Interaction per native verb is created.
GPF controls workflow; the adapter owns technology-specific execution/verification. Both contribute jointly to PersistenceService. For a given IU, eligible Mnemosyne instances reach the same logical authoritative engine, which may have physical replicas. This permits no independent authoritative histories or transfer of IU-instance concurrency from Mneme.
### Incorporation standing
Accepted parent DRP semantics, incorporated under the operative Task for 1.1.23/001. Actual resulting candidate confirmation remains pending. Earlier component/source qualifications remain independently in force.

element.name: Information Exchange - Assessments
element.documentation:
This existing element is a **SolutionFacet**, a specialisation of native **Grouping**. The [governed definition](../../governance/continuum-representation.md#solutionfacet-classification--1119-candidate) distinguishes accessible solution classification from Capability, responsibility and ownership. Its canonical identity, G01–G18 context, existing Composition and separately established Home assertions are preserved.
Native Grouping originally authored as `Interoperability-and-Integration.Information-Exchange.Assessments` in the retained 004 export, incorporated under the Solution Architect's Subject Grouping hierarchy Task. It groups the source-qualified `Assessments` concern within the existing **Information Exchange** SolutionFacet (G05.03). Its earlier authored name above is retained as provenance; current names follow the explicit properties in the 1.1.19 submission. That earlier incoming record has no Documentation or authored Properties; no normative definition, native statement, classification of individual statements, or additional responsibility is invented to complete that absence.
The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. These are distinct assertions. Neither diagram membership nor the Grouping's label alone establishes another Home or a statement allocation. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.
Source Exchange identifier: `id-00f9c244941c4c36ae47791075061c5a`. View placement corroborates the authorised containing SolutionFacet; the exact correspondence is retained in the iteration's folder/Grouping inventories. Existing canonical identities and all pre-existing architectural assertions retain their standing. Archi visual acceptance and HCRL closure remain separate.

element.name: PractitionerCapacity
element.documentation:
For a Practitioner, the available PractitionerCapacity set is constrained by the practitioner's governed profile and applicable operational context. The Practitioner selects **one active PractitionerCapacity** for the applicable session/operational or roster context. It supplies operational context used by Themis when deriving effective authorisation; **it does not itself confer authority**. Selection UI and the exact PractitionerCapacity ↔ FHIR PractitionerRole mapping remain deferred.
> **Authentication establishes who the Individual is. PractitionerCapacity > establishes the capacity in which a Practitioner is currently acting. Themis > establishes what that Identity, acting in that capacity, may do.**
```mermaid graph TD Auth["Authenticated Practitioner"] --> Eligible["Eligible PractitionerCapacity set"] Profile["Governed practitioner profile"] --> Eligible Context["Applicable operational / roster context"] --> Eligible Eligible -->|"Practitioner selects ONE"| Capacity["Active PractitionerCapacity: context, no authority by itself"] Capacity -->|"authorisation context"| PDP["Themis: resolve governed Criteria / assignments / policy state"] PDP --> Criteria["Identity-specific precomputed PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context"] Criteria --> PEP["Constrained local Themis PEP"] Capacity -.->|"operational responsibility context"| Responsibility["Agora: membership intent; detailed context use deferred"] ```
Themis answers **“May this Identity perform this action on this information?”** Future Agora collaboration detail concerns **“Is this Practitioner currently responsible for receiving/responding to this operational activity?”** These are separate responsibilities even where they consume the same PractitionerCapacity. Receipt of an escalation or approval notification grants no information access. Following it into Iris or another application surface requires normal Themis PEP enforcement using current valid PEP-Criteria. U16 establishes [Agora control and Omilia operations](../application-component/d1c4053e68384080b8eb79d2008632ba.md); detailed membership, escalation and approval-routing mechanics remain deferred.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Device Utilisation Support
element.documentation:
Enable and support otherwise appropriately authorised users to use the particular device safely and effectively.
Clinical Device Utilisation Support helps otherwise appropriately authorised users use a particular device safely and effectively. It represents the device-specific enablement needed beyond general professional qualifications. Within technology management it addresses the practical support for use, without making that support the clinical action performed with the device.
**Boundary**
Professional qualification or privilege alone does not establish device-specific enablement; enablement does not confer clinical authority.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Access Monitoring
element.documentation:
Evaluate actual organisational access/handling practice, including controls, accessibility, compartments, classification and physical/printed handling.
Health Information Access Monitoring evaluates actual access and handling practice across organisational circumstances. Digital audit information can contribute, but so can physical access, printed handling, compartments and classification practice. Its purpose is to understand what is happening in use rather than merely observe software events or assume configured controls describe reality.
**Boundary**
Evidence supply does not transfer business accountability, and observation is not automatically independent assurance.

element.name: REQ-FND-001: Durable Ingress Acceptance Boundary
element.documentation:
### Normative Requirement Statement > **Harmonia shall not positively acknowledge acceptance of an incoming event until responsibility for that event has crossed the required durable acceptance boundary.**
### Architectural Intent & Rationale This requirement eliminates the critical vulnerability identified in [Silent Data Loss via False Acceptance](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/assessments.md). When an upstream external system transmits a clinical event (such as an emergency admission, critical lab result, or medication order), it remains the responsibility of that upstream sender until Harmonia has durably secured the event.
Releasing an upstream sender from responsibility (by returning a positive transport acknowledgement) before the event is committed to durable storage creates a vulnerable window where gateway crashes, memory exhaustions, or hardware reboots cause silent, unrecoverable data loss.
### Protocol-Neutral Delineation & Downstream Realisations - **Normative Rule**: The requirement mandates that the durable acceptance boundary must be crossed before positive acknowledgement. It is completely protocol-neutral. - **Downstream Realisations**: - In HL7 v2 over MLLP integration (owned by Domain 06 Integration Architecture), this rule is realised by forbidding an `MSA-1 = AA` (Application Accept) acknowledgement until downstream persistence or queue publication succeeds. If persistence fails, the gateway MUST return `MSA-1 = AE` (Application Error) to trigger upstream sender retry. - In FHIR RESTful APIs, this rule is realised by returning `201 Created` or `200 OK` only after transactional database commitment, returning `202 Accepted` only when durable asynchronous queueing is verified, and returning `500 Internal Server Error` or `503 Service Unavailable` on durable failure. - In Ingress Dual-Write safety (`REC-001`), this rule enforces that in-memory active caching alone is insufficient to satisfy positive acceptance.
- **Primary Motivation**: [Silent Data Loss via False Acceptance](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/assessments.md), [Continuous Clinical Service Availability](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/drivers.md) - **Governing Principles**: [AX-05 (State Separation)](../principle/0412a2084f0145babc4f022c71fea65f.md), [AX-10 (Failure as Normal Condition)](../principle/0d9673833eb840eab03804aa076c1b0c.md), [AX-15 (Explicit Representation of Uncertainty)](../principle/ef8abbaec37e4890ad78b9f263e67906.md) - **Historical Identifier Reference**: `REQ-INGRESS-001`

element.name: Multi-Source Clinical Information → Coherent Clinical Picture
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Purpose & Value Focus
Modern healthcare delivery is chronically fragmented across acute facilities, primary care practices, diagnostic laboratories, imaging centres, and community services. Clinical information arrives across disjointed standards (HL7 v2, CDA, FHIR), disparate identifier namespaces, and isolated episodes of care.
The strategic value created by **VS-01** is **not** merely the technical transit of electronic messages between systems. The authentic clinical and enterprise value is that **clinically relevant information from heterogeneous sources is unified into a coherent, longitudinal, patient-centred clinical picture**, enabling clinicians to make timely, well-informed, and safer care decisions.
```mermaid graph LR S1["S1: Clinically Relevant Info Available"] --> S2["S2: Identity & Context Established"] S2 --> S3["S3: Meaning Established & Preserved"] S3 --> S4["S4: Information Integrated Longitudinally"] S4 --> S5["S5: Coherent Understanding Available"] ```
#### Value Transformation Stages
1. **S1 — Clinically Relevant Information Available**: - *Stakeholder State*: Clinical observations, pathology reports, diagnostic imaging results, medication orders, discharge summaries, or encounter notes occur across distributed care settings and become accessible for integration. - *Value Generated*: Clinical events are no longer trapped within isolated source silos; they enter the integration sphere where their clinical significance can be recognized. 2. **S2 — Identity & Clinical Context Established**: - *Stakeholder State*: Subject-of-care identity is established to the level required for safe association of the information, preserving source identifiers, provenance, confidence, and ambiguity where applicable; relevant encounter, episode, service, and care-delivery context is associated. - *Value Generated*: Clinical facts are safely bound to the correct individual and operational care context without masking identity ambiguity or making premature, unsafe identity conflations. 3. **S3 — Meaning Established & Preserved**: - *Stakeholder State*: Clinical concepts, classifications, and terminologies are mapped to canonical standards (e.g., SNOMED CT-AU, AMT) while strictly preserving original source clinical intent, qualifiers, and provenance. - *Value Generated*: Clinical data is semantically unambiguous across organisational boundaries while ensuring that the originating practitioner's original meaning and expression remain unaltered. 4. **S4 — Information Integrated Longitudinally**: - *Stakeholder State*: Disparate episodic facts, temporal observations, diagnostic series, and encounter histories are synthesized into a cumulative, longitudinal patient-centred record. - *Value Generated*: Clinical interactions are connected across time and specialty, moving beyond episodic snapshots to reveal patient trajectories, trends, and clinical history. 5. **S5 — Coherent Patient-Centred Understanding Available**: - *Stakeholder State*: The longitudinal clinical picture is made accessible in a contextual, consumable representation, structured for clinical review, clinical decision support, or standards-compliant query. - *Value Generated*: Treating clinicians and multidisciplinary care teams gain holistic, trusted situational awareness, reducing diagnostic errors, preventing duplicate testing, and improving patient outcomes.
#### Clinical Authority Boundary Guardrail
Harmonia provides **governed, vendor-neutral longitudinal clinical representation and preservation**. Harmonia does **not** claim originating clinical authority for source clinical facts. The originating EMR, laboratory information system, or practitioner retains source clinical authority; Harmonia is authoritative for its governed longitudinal aggregation, contextual relationships, and verifiable provenance trail.
#### Representative Strategic Traceability
| Traceability level | Current architectural standing | | :--- | :--- | | Motivation | Unresolved: the retired block does not establish a replacement stream-specific axiom set or current named Driver/Goal relationship. | | Current Business Capability contribution | **Unresolved / not presently established.** The superseded BC relationships are retired; no relationship to BC-01 through BC-18 is supplied by identifier position or similarity. | | Current Business Enabling contribution and contextual view | **Unresolved / not presently established.** Old view ordinals and meanings are retired; no enabling-capability or Feature relationship is inferred. | | Existing current Enterprise Capability contributions | **Established, partial:** [EC-02 — Context Management](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-02-context-management); [EC-07 — Provenance & Traceability](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-07-provenance--traceability). These previously documented contributions retain their canonical meanings. Other current contributions are unresolved; the retired EC labels do not establish replacements. |
- **Strategic Courses of Action**: `COA-01` (Boundary Membrane Sovereignty), `COA-02` (Distinct Management and Durable Preservation), `COA-03` (Meaning-Centric Provenance and Traceability).
### 1.1.21 Journey incorporation
This existing Value Stream is reused as a Journey with the same canonical and Exchange identities, names, original definition and standing. Its source-defined transformations are represented by independently identifiable constituent Journeys. The added Aggregation relationships express reusable structure; Triggering expresses meaningful progression with its stated conditions. Neither creates runtime orchestration. New, explicitly qualified capability contributions supplement the predecessor traceability account; the original unestablished relationships and qualifications above are not retrospectively rewritten or declared accepted.

element.name: [CT2] Compliance Governance
element.documentation:
Define how adherence to the authoritative WHAT will be determined, checked and reported.
Compliance Governance defines how adherence to established obligations, authorities and constraints will be determined. Assessment Definition specifies the evidence and basis for evaluation; Reporting & Checkpoint Definition specifies where adherence is checked and what must be communicated. This makes the compliance test explicit without treating the design of a test as its successful execution.
**Intent**
Provide a defensible basis for checking and reporting whether the governing envelope has been respected.
**Boundary**
Defining assessment arrangements does not perform assurance or manage the governed activity. The obligations being assessed retain their authoritative source.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: Unqualified Information → Governed, Consumable Information
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Purpose & Value Focus
Information arriving at the healthcare enterprise boundary is frequently incomplete, syntactically inconsistent, ambiguous in authority, or lacking explicit privacy controls. Consuming or publishing unverified information risks clinical misinterpretation, privacy violations, and regulatory breach.
The strategic value created by **VS-02** is the progressive **qualification, governance, policy attachment, and durable integrity assurance of information**, transforming raw external data into trusted, policy-governed assets that can be safely published across enterprise boundaries.
```mermaid graph LR S1["S1: Unqualified Information"] --> S2["S2: Qualified / Structured Info"] S2 --> S3["S3: Governed / Controlled Info"] S3 --> S4["S4: Durably Available Info"] S4 --> S5["S5: Published / Consumable Info"] ```
#### Value Transformation Stages
1. **S1 — Unqualified Information**: - *Stakeholder State*: Raw, unvalidated data streams, documents, or transactions arrive at the enterprise membrane with unverified structural conformance, incomplete provenance, and unverified authority. - *Value Generated*: Ingress boundaries accept external input safely without allowing malformed or unauthorized data to compromise internal environments. 2. **S2 — Qualified / Structured Information**: - *Stakeholder State*: Data structures are validated against canonical schemas, syntactically parsed, and reconciled into well-defined, verifiable information models. - *Value Generated*: Syntactic and structural ambiguity is eliminated; information adheres to predictable, conformant architectural structures. 3. **S3 — Governed / Controlled Information**: - *Stakeholder State*: Information is evaluated against security policies, organizational authority boundaries, consent directives, and confidentiality classifications under default-deny governance (`Themis`). - *Value Generated*: Information carries explicit, enforceable access policies and privacy guardrails, ensuring that sensitive healthcare data cannot be disclosed without legitimate authority. 4. **S4 — Durably Available Information**: - *Stakeholder State*: Information is preserved with verifiable integrity, non-destructive versioning, and comprehensive provenance, remaining resiliently queryable and recoverable. - *Value Generated*: Stakeholders are assured that information is protected against unauthorised alteration or loss, establishing an enduring, verifiable and auditable history of care information. 5. **S5 — Published / Consumable Information**: - *Stakeholder State*: Governed information is projected into standards-compliant external representations (such as FHIR R5 Core and Australian profiles) across explicit egress boundaries. - *Value Generated*: External consumers and presentation layers receive trusted, standards-conformant information tailored to their authorised scope without exposing internal platform mechanics.
#### Enabling Behavioural Pattern (Subordinate to Value Stream)
The progression through VS-02 is supported internally by an established architectural behavioural pattern:
$$\text{Aggregation} \longrightarrow \text{Processing} \longrightarrow \text{Persistence} \longrightarrow \text{Publishing}$$
**Crucial Distinction**: This behavioural pattern describes the internal activity contributing to the transformation. It must **not** be substituted for the value stream stage names. The value stream expresses the *evolving state and value of the information*; the behavioural pattern describes the underlying operational mechanics that support it.
#### Representative Strategic Traceability
| Traceability level | Current architectural standing | | :--- | :--- | | Motivation | Established existing constraints: [AX-05 — Active State and Authoritative Durable State Are Distinct](../../motivation/principle/0412a2084f0145babc4f022c71fea65f.md) and [AX-07 — Security Is Intrinsic to Managed Operations](../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md). Current named Driver/Goal relationships and a replacement for the retired axiom meanings remain unresolved. | | Current Business Capability contribution | **Unresolved / not presently established.** The superseded BC relationships are retired; no relationship to BC-01 through BC-18 is supplied by identifier position or similarity. | | Current Business Enabling contribution and contextual view | **Unresolved / not presently established.** Old view ordinals and meanings are retired; no enabling-capability or Feature relationship is inferred. | | Existing current Enterprise Capability contributions | **Established, partial:** [EC-02 — Context Management](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-02-context-management); [EC-06 — Policy & Control](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-06-policy--control); [EC-07 — Provenance & Traceability](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-07-provenance--traceability). These previously documented contributions retain their canonical meanings. Other current contributions are unresolved; the retired EC labels do not establish replacements. |
- **Strategic Courses of Action**: `COA-01` (Boundary Membrane Sovereignty), `COA-02` (Distinct Management and Durable Preservation), `COA-03` (Meaning-Centric Provenance and Traceability), `COA-06` (Collaborative Reusable Capability Realisation).
### 1.1.21 Journey incorporation
This existing Value Stream is reused as a Journey with the same canonical and Exchange identities, names, original definition and standing. Its source-defined transformations are represented by independently identifiable constituent Journeys. The added Aggregation relationships express reusable structure; Triggering expresses meaningful progression with its stated conditions. Neither creates runtime orchestration. New, explicitly qualified capability contributions supplement the predecessor traceability account; the original unestablished relationships and qualifications above are not retrospectively rewritten or declared accepted.

element.documentation:

**Overview**
Evaluate the operation, effectiveness, appropriateness and conformance of the assurance service itself through independent review. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Evaluate the operation, effectiveness, appropriateness and conformance of the assurance service itself through independent review.
**Boundary**
Evaluation concerns operation, effectiveness, appropriateness and conformance of the assurance service; it is not execution of assurance against a subject.

element.name: [Feature] Clinic Session Tracking
element.documentation:
Ingest and track clinic operating session start, delay, and completion states.
Clinic-session tracking records the operating session's start, delay and completion as service-level context. It is distinct from an individual patient's queue state: knowing where one patient is waiting does not establish whether the clinic session is running as planned.

element.name: AX-05 Active State and Authoritative Durable State Are Distinct
element.documentation:
#### Axiom
Mneme owns Harmonia's application-facing access to managed information and the distributed active-state representation, observation and coordination required to use that information safely.
Mnemosyne owns Harmonia's authoritative durable representation of managed information. It atomically establishes authoritative state and authoritative version progression and persists the durable management metadata required to interpret that state.
Mneme manages active use; Mnemosyne establishes durable truth.
#### Rationale
Distributed availability and authoritative persistence are different responsibilities.
Conflating them makes cache state authoritative, persistence state application-facing, or both.
#### Consequences
Mneme MAY reject or coordinate a proposed state progression before persistence.
Only Mnemosyne can establish a new authoritative durable state.
Following authoritative commit, Mneme SHALL converge its active representation toward the authoritative state.
Loss of Mneme SHALL NOT cause process-local or cached state to become authoritative.
Loss of Mnemosyne SHALL NOT cause Mneme to promote its active representation into authoritative durable state.
Mneme active state SHALL be reconstructable from authoritative state where applicable.
**This does not mean:**
- Every Mneme operation requires a database operation. - Mnemosyne is exposed as an application database API. - Mneme and Mnemosyne must use the same version or concurrency mechanism.
Mneme active-state generation SHALL represent successfully established active state. A valid active-state token SHALL identify an observed generation of that state.
Failed or degraded convergence following authoritative state progression SHALL NOT establish or advance a valid active-state generation. Where the active representation cannot be successfully converged, its coordination state SHALL be treated as untrusted until reconciled with authoritative state.
Mneme active-state generation and Mnemosyne authoritative version SHALL remain distinct concurrency domains. Neither SHALL be inferred from, substituted for, or treated as an alias of the other.

element.name: [CT2] Individual Health Assessment
element.documentation:
The capability to establish an understanding of an individual's current health state through the collection, consideration and evaluation of relevant clinical, health and contextual information.
Assessment establishes what is currently known about an individual's health through history, examination and measurement. Within Individual Care Delivery it supplies assessed findings, including findings obtained directly from the person rather than retrieved from an existing record. Its three children distinguish ways of establishing knowledge, rather than professions, clinical specialties or locations.
**Intent**
Give subsequent clinical interpretation a defensible account of the person's current state and relevant history.
**Boundary**
Finding an abnormal measurement is distinguishable from deciding what it means clinically. Diagnosis, prognosis, selection of care and performance of care belong to adjacent abilities.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Qualification Administration
element.documentation:
Administer organisation clinical certification/compliance information and provider qualification evidence with its externally established standing.
**Overview**
Administer organisation clinical certification/compliance information and provider qualification evidence with its externally established standing.
**Intent**
Administer organisation clinical certification/compliance information and provider qualification evidence with its externally established standing.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Clinical Qualification Management checks professional and clinical qualification or competency context before specialised operational work is dispatched. It makes relevant standing available at the point where an operational action must respect it. The approved rename preserves the professional responsibility while distinguishing it from operational badges and physical access credentials.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
The historical name Clinical Credential Management is an alias only for this element. It is not equivalent to Credential Management, and role resolution alone establishes neither clinical nor operational privilege.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Qualification context materially constrains legitimate dispatch without making Harmonia the originating professional regulator or training authority.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/04-health-service-operations.md` — entry lines 292-292. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.
- **Owning Capability**: `Clinical Qualification Management`.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [5fea7aaac4384245b1f08a3d8a076bd9](5fea7aaac4384245b1f08a3d8a076bd9.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.
## ARB source correspondence
Scope/anti-responsibility and clinical/operational meaning establish the responsible Capability; descriptive ledger/registry/asset labels do not establish a separately bounded formal Information Concept. Preserve non-transfer and source authority.
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/information-responsibility/information-responsibility.md` — information responsibility row 24. Standing: Established Business responsibility only; formal information identity/lifecycle not inferred.
```text | **Clinical Qualification Management** | **Qualification/Competency Checkpoint Outcome & Work Context** | Verification of active clinical credentials and required competency certificates before specialised work dispatch, derived from `FEAT-HSO-23`. | Does not originate qualifications or confer clinical privileges; source facts retain their authority. Clinical Privilege and Operational Privilege remain distinct; physical badge/access Credential Management is separate. | ```
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B08.02`; additional scope correspondences: `B08.03`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Knowledge Information Formulation
element.documentation:
Formulate explicit reusable knowledge, including applicability, qualifications, rationale and evidence relationships.
This capability expresses reusable clinical knowledge with its applicability, qualifications, rationale and evidence relationships. It moves beyond extracted material by making the knowledge claim and its limits explicit. That formulation supports later review and use while retaining the distinction between a proposed knowledge expression and one approved for a governed purpose.
**Boundary**
Formulation does not approve knowledge, govern terminology or define health-information structures.

element.name: Reduced Clinical Risk from Unavailable, Fragmented or Incorrectly Associated Information (O1)
element.documentation:
### Outcome Definition Patients experience significantly safer care and reduced preventable harm across the regional healthcare network, achieved through the elimination of clinical data blind spots, the prevention of erroneous subject associations, and the provision of coherent longitudinal patient records.
### Clinical & Operational Value - **Prevention of Adverse Medical Events**: Clinicians have point-of-care access to complete allergy lists, current medications, and past medical histories, preventing severe adverse drug events and contraindicated treatments. - **Elimination of Diagnostic Blind Spots**: Hospital emergency departments can immediately view recent laboratory results and diagnostic imaging reports performed at external facilities, avoiding redundant radiation exposure and delays in critical therapy. - **Accurate Subject Attribution**: Clinical records are referentially validated, ensuring that test results and treatment orders are never erroneously attributed to the wrong patient.
### Direct Contributing Goals - [Vendor-Independent Longitudinal Clinical Information Coherence](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) (Thread 2) - [Reliable Subject Identity and Referential Integrity](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) (Thread 5)

element.name: [Feature] Next-of-Kin & Guardian Association
element.documentation:
Associate nominated emergency contacts, legal guardians, and care agents with the client record.
This Feature records the nominated people and capacities through which a client can be contacted or represented. Association preserves who the contact or guardian is in relation to the client; it does not make every nominated person an unrestricted recipient of clinical information.

element.name: [Feature] Temporal Event Correlation
element.documentation:
Correlate incoming clinical events with scheduled appointments and operational calendar milestones.
Temporal correlation relates incoming events to the relevant appointment or calendar milestone. Association provides context for interpretation and coordination without assuming that temporal proximity proves attendance, fulfilment or the clinical outcome expected at that time.

element.name: [CT2] Specialist Clinical Context Integration
element.documentation:
Integrate specialist assessment, investigation and therapeutic information with longitudinal and episode context.
**Overview**
Integrate specialist assessment, investigation and therapeutic information with longitudinal and episode context. Its constituent abilities distinguish Clinical Assessment; Diagnostic Services; Therapeutic Services; Medication Therapy; Allied Health; Rehabilitation.
**Intent**
Keep specialised clinical context connected to the wider record while retaining the specialist source of clinical judgement.
**Boundary**
A clinical specialty is evidence for integration purpose, not authority to invent a specialist engine, clinical decision or duplicated general capture function.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Medication Compounding & Preparation
element.documentation:
Prepare or compound a clinically required medication formulation under the applicable professional and product-governance mandate.
**Overview**
Prepare or compound a clinically required medication formulation under the applicable professional and product-governance mandate. The proposed decomposition separates this outcome from the other responsibilities within Medication & Pharmacy Services.
**Intent**
Provide the required medication formulation when ordinary supply alone does not satisfy the authorised preparation need.
**Boundary**
Preparation differs from dispensing and administration; this proposal assigns no compounding activity to Harmonia.

element.name: [Topic] ServiceAssurance
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing the assurance context associated with a healthcare service, including the evidence or determination that its provision satisfies applicable expectations, requirements or obligations.
- **Semantic Classification**: `Accountability / Audit Record` - **Definition**: The formal retrospective quality evaluation, clinical audit, accreditation review, or funding/billing reconciliation assessed against delivered services and outcomes. - **Architectural Scope & Ownership Assessment**: Evaluates single service deliveries or aggregated cohorts across an episode of care. Because Harmonia's core operational capabilities do not claim R1 architectural ownership for statutory health insurance billing reconciliation or external accreditation governance, `AssuredHealthcareService` is designated as a **Reference / Contextual Concept** where Harmonia consumes or supports assurance interfaces without owning the external statutory authority.
Source standing: Established Package1 conceptual information meaning; residual qualifications in selected section remain unchanged.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Data Retrieval
element.documentation:
Obtain identified information under an applicable authorised request/context.
Health Information Data Retrieval obtains identified information under an applicable authorised request and context. It supplies the content whose existence may already be known through a catalogue or index. The distinction matters because locating an item, obtaining it and presenting it to a person each establish different outcomes.
**Boundary**
Retrieval does not itself grant permission, provide participant communication or confer authority over the retrieved facts.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: [CT3] Health Privacy Safeguard Management
element.documentation:
Establish organisational safeguards and assurance processes concerning privacy consequences of information supply, exposure or use.
This capability establishes safeguards and assurance arrangements concerning the privacy consequences of supplying, exposing or using information. It focuses on the effect on people and legitimate information use, distinguishing that concern from protection of the information estate itself. Technical access restrictions may contribute without exhausting the organisational privacy responsibility.
**Boundary**
Privacy safeguards do not replace broader estate resilience, access decisions or originating consent authority.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [Topic] TaskOutcome
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing the governed resolution of a Task, including its completion disposition, resulting information and applicable outputs.
> **TaskOutcome is the governed resolution of an ActionableTask according to > that ActionableTask's explicitly defined outcome policy.**
TaskOutcome belongs to and resolves the ActionableTask. It does not independently belong to a FulfillmentTask. Conceptually it:
- **references FulfillmentTask [0..*]**: identifies the undertaking or undertakings that participated in establishing the outcome, as determined by `OutcomeConcurrency.Mode`; - **contains Task Completion Metadata**: Harmonia-governed information concerning resolution/completion of the ActionableTask; no complete metadata schema is defined here; and - **contains / represents Task.Output(s)**: the resulting ActionableTask output established from the participating undertakings' outputs according to `Outcome.OutputRules.Mode`.
The encapsulated domain content of a `Task.Output` may remain semantically opaque to Harmonia. Neither output information nor TaskOutcome becomes the physical, clinical or other phenomenon represented. No detailed Task.Output payload structure is established here.
**Recursive TaskOutcome containment is excluded from this model.** Multiple execution results are represented through references from the single governed TaskOutcome to the relevant participating FulfillmentTask undertakings, rather than through recursive outcome aggregation hierarchies. Aggregate participation does not imply recursive composition. The remaining questions in §5 remain unresolved.
Source standing: Bounded adjudicated conceptual Task meaning; section 5 reservations, including runtime TaskOutcome identity/lifecycle, remain unresolved.
Under [AX-17](../../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md), the following remaining Task / Work matters require subsequent architectural adjudication or separately governed detailed definition:
- TaskOutcome identity rules; - detailed cardinalities beyond the established relationships, including whether an outcome is mandatory; - detailed TaskOutcome lifecycle/state semantics; - detailed Task Completion Metadata and Task.Output payload structures, and their representation mechanisms; - detailed finishing/qualification rules, assignment mechanisms and concurrency execution mechanics; and - task-specific explicit output rules and their downstream execution mechanisms.
Outcome ownership, participation modes, output-rule modes, their orthogonality and exclusion of recursive TaskOutcome composition are adjudicated above; they SHALL NOT be presented as still provisional or unresolved. This refinement allocates no previously unestablished archetype-authoring or outcome-authority owner.
**ReportedTask remains unresolved.** Its existing intersection with Definition → Contextualisation → Fulfilment → Outcome → Accountability does not reaffirm its previous definition or require a separate accountable report. Its necessity and semantics may overlap accountability, assurance, audit, historical representation and evidence, and require separate adjudication. It is neither removed nor normalised into one of those concerns here. No ReportedTask relationships, identity, immutability or lifecycle are settled.
The metamodel, reusable pattern and general lifecycle/containment guidance SHALL NOT be used to fill these reserved questions by inference. The bounded semantics above are established; the remaining Task / Work family and Domain04 are not declared complete.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Knowledge Context Extraction
element.documentation:
Extract relevant material while preserving its source/context relationship.
Clinical Knowledge Context Extraction selects relevant material while retaining its relationship to the source and context. Its purpose is to make potential knowledge material available without stripping away the circumstances needed to understand it. Extracted material remains distinguishable from the reusable knowledge subsequently formulated from it.
**Boundary**
Extraction does not establish approval or turn source information into an individual clinical conclusion.

element.name: [CT3] Care Eligibility Determination
element.documentation:
Determine whether applicable eligibility conditions for care access are satisfied.
Care Eligibility Determination establishes whether the conditions governing access to applicable care are met. It contributes a qualified access decision alongside intake and referral, so that an identifiable request can be distinguished from one that satisfies the relevant criteria. Its purpose is eligibility in the applicable context rather than clinical diagnosis or service allocation.
**Boundary**
Eligibility alone does not reserve capacity, allocate a care place or deliver care.

element.name: Retrieve Health Information
element.documentation:
Fetches discrete clinical observations and original attachments.
Feature association not established: FEAT-ISE-09 — Access-Controlled Information Filtering requires access-controlled disclosure/filtering; retrieval of discrete information alone does not materially realise that responsibility. No replacement Feature is assigned.
Retrieval obtains discrete clinical information or attachments under the owning access responsibility. It is distinct from applying the access-qualified filtering required by FEAT-ISE-09. A shared owner and related data do not justify making that unresolved realisation association authoritative.

element.name: Mneme-Workflow-Cache
element.documentation:
Mneme's transient materialised processing-cache responsibility, realised by **embedded Infinispan LOCAL inside each applicable Ponos, DigitalTwin and Dokimasia execution JVM**. It stores the full/resolved working manifestation required by governed context loading. It is local per JVM, not a site-wide shared cache, remote Server cache, Hot Rod near cache or distributed L1 hybrid. No inter-JVM/site replication, ownership/affinity registry or cache-recovery subsystem is introduced.
Common Ergon owns context loading/unloading, checkpointing and execution recovery; Behaviour and Dokimasia Ergon reuse these facilities. GovernedReader attempts Content materialisation through Mneme/Mnemosyne (large-binary pass-by-reference exception retained). A summary alone does not establish materialised external Content. Concurrent executions may independently materialise the same immutable .input(); their outputs remain governed by existing Pragma/Praxis/Ergon rules. Existing DigitalTwin sequential Behaviour execution is unchanged.
Entries are bounded/transient under context validity, Themis isolation and Mneme operational Version/Active Generation semantics. Cache copies/instances and generations are not new authoritative IUs, Content versions or representations. New authoritative versions do not retroactively rewrite an executing version-specific immutable input. Context-save changes go through governed Mneme/full Writer, not raw write-through or SummaryWriter UPDATE.
After eviction, JVM/cache/site loss, common execution recovery reconstructs necessary context from authoritative information and durable work/checkpoints at the existing boundary. Do not resume inside a failed Ergon. Lost cache entries need not themselves be recovered; accepted work and acknowledged information must remain preserved. A checkpoint in a transient cache does not prove durability.
### Retained MC-01–MC-07 qualifications
- **MC-01:** Standard-Cache multi-site topology and active/active consistency need evidence; synchronous distribution/cross-site backup is not native linearizability or safe independent-cluster same-key concurrency. - **MC-02:** Owner count/site placement, majority/partition/failover and continued governed work after one site loss remain unproved; Mneme retains state-transition concurrency obligations beyond cache operations. - **MC-03:** Per-JVM memory bounds, safe eviction/lifetime relative to context load/unload/checkpoint and security isolation remain solution/deployment policy under existing Ergon semantics. - **MC-04:** Durable propagation does not prove immediate replica read visibility. Exact-version/currentness, read-after-write and wait/fail/Indeterminate behaviour use Mneme–Mnemosyne and PersistenceService contracts; no cache affinity mechanism is invented. - **MC-05:** Active/active N+1 (N > 0) is an architectural target, not a verified product guarantee. With only two physical sites, loss of one prevents **new multi-site durable write Success** without another eligible durable site or explicit owning NFR/persistence disposition. Never weaken Success or claim unqualified N+1 write continuity. Three-plus sites alone do not prove quorum/failover correctness. - **MC-06:** Five-service reconciliation is deterministically incorporated: historical GovernedSearch identity is reused as sole GovernedSummarySearch, Summary Reader/Writer added, full Reader/Writer retained; no independent Summary IU or sixth method. - **MC-07:** Existing capability/Feature contributions are reused. Physical remote-client/embedded ownership, observation, deployment and as-built integration remain downstream; no new module or implementation framework is selected.
### Incorporation standing
Accepted complete Final.001 DRP semantics; authorised 1.1.24 ADD; actual incorporated candidate awaiting Solution Architect confirmation. Authority: operative Solution Architect Task and HCRL 1.1.24/001; input approval is distinct from result acceptance.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Logistics Coordination
element.documentation:
Coordinate specimen metadata and specimen movement traceability across responsible collection, courier and diagnostic services.
**Overview**
Coordinate specimen metadata and specimen movement traceability across responsible collection, courier and diagnostic services.
**Intent**
Coordinate specimen metadata and specimen movement traceability across responsible collection, courier and diagnostic services.
**Boundary**
Includes specimen metadata and specimen movement traceability. Supply/materiel movement belongs to Health Materiel Traceability Administration.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Clinical Logistics Coordination integrates the movement and custody context of clinical material, notably specimen pickup, transport conditions and laboratory delivery. It keeps a material's journey connected to the fulfilment context requiring it. This enables clinical logistics to be followed without reducing specimen integrity to a delivery timestamp alone.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Tracking material movement does not perform diagnostic interpretation or establish general enterprise supply-chain ownership.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Custody and transport information materially support diagnostic continuity and appropriate interpretation of specimen handling.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.
| Source predicate | Target element | Source standing / currentness | ARB native treatment | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Context Management](3cfd3e56c23a4943bd1b476ec248ac49.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-8c6915926bdd51d98f8e890771efb770` | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Activity & Execution](e5ff80e655084524a8dcee8e4ded788a.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-0aab5c340160565087c2ee753c10e1a8` | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Operational Assurance](938cd44380ab431fa8dae13c702d83c1.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-790a814f8096553283c2ee7706a55d59` |
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/04-health-service-operations.md` — entry lines 264-264. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.
- **Owning Capability**: `Clinical Logistics Coordination`
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [90a782ff2d004fa984ae0465528b2253](90a782ff2d004fa984ae0465528b2253.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.
## ARB source correspondence
Scope/anti-responsibility and clinical/operational meaning establish the responsible Capability; descriptive ledger/registry/asset labels do not establish a separately bounded formal Information Concept. Preserve non-transfer and source authority.
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/information-responsibility/information-responsibility.md` — information responsibility row 26. Standing: Established Business responsibility only; formal information identity/lifecycle not inferred.
```text | **Clinical Logistics Coordination** | **Specimen Manifest & Chain-of-Custody Register** | Pathology bio-specimen courier manifests, temperature compliance logs, courier custody signatures, and laboratory delivery receipts. | Does not own pathology diagnostic results. | ```

element.documentation:
Adopt applicable information models, including intrinsic assessment of adoption impacts.
Information Model Adoption establishes the organisation's use of an applicable information model, including consideration of the consequences of adopting it. It gives a discovered model an organisational standing distinct from mere availability. The intrinsic impact consideration helps adoption remain a business governance responsibility rather than a mechanical import of definitions.

Adoption does not perform every education, compliance or governance-oversight responsibility associated with subsequent use.

element.name: [CT2] Policy & Control
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Evaluate and enforce security, consent, privacy, and regulatory policies including authority, access control, and information handling rules. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Executing impartial, default-deny policy evaluations for all integration transactions. - Enforcing Role-Based and Attribute-Based Access Control (RBAC/ABAC) policies. - Evaluating patient consent directives and privacy restrictions at boundary and query checkpoints. - Enforcing statutory information disclosure boundaries (e.g., mental health, VIP records). - **Collaborative Nature**: Evaluated across boundary gateways, internal bus dispatch, storage interfaces, and presentation layers.
Policy & Control supplies the reusable evaluation and enforcement of authority, consent, privacy and handling constraints. Its purpose is consistent governed action across ingress, information access, execution and presentation boundaries. Default-deny evaluation preserves the need for established authority rather than treating a caller's intent or a technically valid request as permission.
**Boundary**
Participation at multiple enforcement points does not distribute policy ownership or turn operational security context into persistent clinical content.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E05.06`; additional scope correspondences: `E05.03`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [Feature] Document Metadata Indexing
element.documentation:
Index clinical document metadata (author, specialty, encounter, date, confidentiality) for rapid discovery.
Metadata indexing makes documents discoverable by clinically and operationally relevant attributes. It describes content for search without making the index the document itself or granting access merely because a matching record can be located.

Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Service Offering Readiness Coordination
element.documentation:
Assemble the dependency evidence needed to determine and communicate whether a defined service offering is operationally ready in a particular context.
**Overview**
Collective readiness depends on suitable workforce, spaces, equipment, materials and supporting services. This proposal evaluates their joint availability for an offering without treating one available bed, an operating-hours declaration or aggregate capacity as service readiness.
**Intent**
Distinguish collective service deliverability from nominal availability or readiness of any single dependency.
**Boundary**
Contributing capabilities retain source readiness and resource management. Clinical go/no-go decisions and service governance are not granted by this information-based coordination.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B07.04.01`; additional scope correspondences: . Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Information Protection - Assessments
element.documentation:
This existing element is a **SolutionFacet**, a specialisation of native **Grouping**. The [governed definition](../../governance/continuum-representation.md#solutionfacet-classification--1119-candidate) distinguishes accessible solution classification from Capability, responsibility and ownership. Its canonical identity, G01–G18 context, existing Composition and separately established Home assertions are preserved.
Native Grouping originally authored as `Security-and-Authorisation.Information-Protection.Assessments` in the retained 004 export, incorporated under the Solution Architect's Subject Grouping hierarchy Task. It groups the source-qualified `Assessments` concern within the existing **Information Protection** SolutionFacet (G03.04). Its earlier authored name above is retained as provenance; current names follow the explicit properties in the 1.1.19 submission. That earlier incoming record has no Documentation or authored Properties; no normative definition, native statement, classification of individual statements, or additional responsibility is invented to complete that absence.
The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. These are distinct assertions. Neither diagram membership nor the Grouping's label alone establishes another Home or a statement allocation. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.
Source Exchange identifier: `id-f1c6f7c28e7b4d9d9a6f0441e9817406`. View placement corroborates the authorised containing SolutionFacet; the exact correspondence is retained in the iteration's folder/Grouping inventories. Existing canonical identities and all pre-existing architectural assertions retain their standing. Archi visual acceptance and HCRL closure remain separate.

element.name: [Feature] Ward Care Capacity Management
element.documentation:
Represent ward care capacity in relation to staffing, care-place suitability and patient dependency.
**Overview**
A clean bed can remain unusable when staffing or patient needs constrain the ward; source clinical facts remain attributed.
**Boundary**
Local responsibility retains its capacity meaning; Service Capacity Management consumes it without acquiring ownership or imposing one common capacity model.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: [CT3] Standards Adoption
element.documentation:
Adopt applicable standards within the organisation.
Standards Adoption establishes which applicable standards the organisation adopts. It gives standards an intentional place in organisational practice rather than allowing familiar products or conventions to define requirements by default. The business responsibility concerns adoption in context, including standards whose effects extend beyond information representation.
**Boundary**
Adoption does not establish a complete standards lifecycle taxonomy or perform the distinct identification of broader standards impacts.

element.name: AX-10 Distribution, Load and Failure Are Normal Operating Conditions
element.documentation:
#### Axiom
Harmonia SHALL be designed on the assumption of distributed deployment, sustained processing load and failure or degradation of individual runtime components.
Loss or degradation of implementation machinery SHALL NOT silently alter the authoritative, security, governance or information-authority semantics of managed information.
#### Rationale
Distribution and failure are not exceptional architectural cases for Harmonia. They are part of its normal operating environment.
#### Consequences
Work that has crossed an explicit durable processing boundary SHALL be recoverable according to that boundary's contract.
Processing pressure SHOULD preferentially be represented as bounded, durable backlog rather than unbounded growth of JVM heap, threads, database connections or volatile work.
Failure SHALL be visible rather than silently replaced by semantically weaker local behaviour.
**This does not mean:**
- Every component must be independently distributed. - Every operation must be asynchronous. - Every internal Java boundary should become a network boundary.

element.name: CST-EXT-001: Applicable Health-Information Privacy and Data-Protection Obligations
element.documentation:
### Categorical Definition > **Harmonia must operate within the health-information privacy, confidentiality, disclosure, retention, and data-protection obligations applicable to the jurisdiction and deployment context.**
### Context & Architectural Boundary Health data is categorized as hypersensitive personal data across all legal jurisdictions. Wherever Harmonia is deployed, it is bound by the statutory data protection regime governing that region. The platform must be architecturally designed to satisfy these obligations without requiring bespoke rewrites of core domain logic.
### Representative Instances & Examples - **Australia**: The *Privacy Act 1988 (Cth)*, the Australian Privacy Principles (APPs), the *My Health Records Act 2012*, and state-based health records legislation (e.g., *Health Records Act 2001 (Vic)*). - **United States**: The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Security and Privacy Rules. - **European Union**: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and European Health Data Space (EHDS) regulations.
### Direct Architectural Impacts - Requires downstream security architecture to govern access to protected health information and enforce applicable access controls ([`SEC-001 / SEC-002`](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/requirements-constraints/master-requirements-catalogue.md)). - Requires downstream operational logging policies and guardrails to protect health information from unauthorized exposure in diagnostic telemetry ([`SEC-010`](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/requirements-constraints/master-requirements-catalogue.md)). - Requires platform communications and stored data representations to apply appropriate protection mechanisms according to deployment risk and statutory requirements. - Informs audit and provenance requirements for demonstrating authorized handling of health information ([`PROV-001`](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/requirements-constraints/master-requirements-catalogue.md)). - Bounds Platform Driver: [Statutory Health Information Privacy & Protection](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/drivers.md).

element.name: [CT2] Interoperability & Exchange
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Resolve destinations, transform schemas, route, transport, deliver, acknowledge, and coordinate standards-based information exchange across enterprise boundaries. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Providing multi-protocol boundary adaptation for healthcare standards (HL7 v2, FHIR REST, DICOM, secure messaging). - Executing bidirectional structural and semantic transformations between legacy formats and canonical representations. - Ensuring reliable addressed delivery and fan-out distribution to external clinical endpoints. - Processing and distinguishing technical delivery acknowledgements from business acknowledgements. - **Boundary Rule**: Egress terminates Harmonia management of the emitted representation (Axiom AX-13).
Interoperability & Exchange moves information across participating boundaries through destination resolution, transformation, delivery and acknowledgements. It preserves the difference between technical transmission and the recipient's business response so that an exchange can be understood under its actual contract. Standards govern the external representation while internal management semantics remain private.
**Boundary**
Egress ends Harmonia management of the emitted representation. Retained delivery evidence does not extend control over an external recipient or transfer payload authority.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E03`; additional scope correspondences: . Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [UserStory] Legitimate patients regain access to services
element.documentation:
Independent stakeholder need, expectation or desired outcome:
> Reinstate a suspended Patient identity after investigations are completed so that legitimate patients regain access to services.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.
### Reconciled source contributions
- `UC-DepartmentalOfficer-Identity-11` — Identity Reactivation; Scope - Patient / Related Person Identity; [source](../../../../../openspec/specs/patient-identity-management/uc-departmentalofficer-identity-11-identity-reactivation/spec.md).
Source-specific access conditions, supporting actors, alternative outcomes, verification and data-authority rules remain distinct in their cited source contributions. Legacy claims that each statement is a business capability are not adopted: this instance has native Requirement semantics. Source target-state scope is not a software delivery commitment for 1.1.21. Historical assessment findings remain recoverable and do not establish current coverage.

element.name: [UseCase] End Care Team Participation
element.documentation:

The interaction is directed towards the source purpose: my ongoing access can be reviewed
Source primary actor: External ClinicianProvider (Rehabilitation Provider)

element.name: Praxis
element.documentation:
- **Role/ownership:** higher-order operational construct defining expected/permitted context and the operational/assurance envelope. **Energeia C39 owns Praxis** and provides **Praxis Management Services F11** under [U06](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u06). It is not another execution engine or necessarily an independent component. - **Fulfilment semantics:** Pathway defines the conceptual Ergo sequence; Praxis defines how it is fulfilled: applicable Context definitions required by the Ergo framework, segment criteria/outcomes, continuation derivation semantics and other Praxis-level housekeeping. Ponos/Ergo performs output processing and routing. Context requirements are concrete in R1.x/R2.x; criteria-driven dynamic Context and dynamically configured reusable/generic Ergo remain deferred R3.x direction, without an AI-driven selection/configuration mechanism. - **Information/relationships:** candidate interface configuration, Topic exclusions and potentially inclusions, operational constraints/configuration and assurance rules. **Aggregation: Pathway [0..1]**; working **Aggregation: Journey** with cardinalities unresolved. No Composition or shared lifecycle is inferred. Praxis may exist without a Pathway for Publish/Subscribe activity. The specialised [Digital Twin Behaviour pattern](../application-component/a26f06d66bec4981b266e202c46a9afb.md) uses a Pathway with exactly one Ergo; it retains full Praxis semantics and does not change the general Aggregation cardinality. - **Management/persistence:** Mneme manages governed representations; Mnemosyne **C&G** provides durable persistence responsibility. Ponos consumes Praxis for execution and Dokimasia uses it as the primary normative assurance basis; neither use nor persistence transfers application ownership. - **Retained detail:** schema, lifecycle/versioning, activation/deactivation, replacement/retirement and in-flight effects remain CDG-01/06. Historical TaskSequence/PraxisDefinition/PraxisImplementation and A04 actual-assurance- activity descriptions do not establish equivalence or a definition-to-instance model. U06 supersedes the earlier wholly unresolved broader-Praxis standing. - **Logical boundary:** [Praxis.Horos C46](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#c46), with IngressHoros/EgressHoros, names the Praxis boundary. EgressHoros hands interaction state/outcome back before Ergo.ContextUnloader completes; it is not a technical endpoint. - **Exclusions:** Praxis is not Pathway, Route, a sequence of Ergo/Ergon, an orchestrator, choreographer, runtime engine or Pub/Sub graph. Mneme semantic selection, Petasos concrete persistent handoff and Ponos execution remain distinct. No detailed Praxis schema is invented.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md` — ## Praxis: operational context and assurance basis. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
**Praxis is the higher-order operational construct establishing the operational and assurance envelope within which Harmonia activity occurs.** The conversational description “super Pathway/Journey” identifies its higher-order context; it establishes neither a supertype nor an execution engine. Praxis defines expected or permitted operational context, including candidate externally visible interface information, overall Topic exclusions and potentially inclusions, operational configuration/constraints and assurance rules/expectations.
**Pathway defines the conceptual Ergo sequence; Praxis defines how that Pathway is fulfilled.** Praxis manages the definition of Context required by the Ergo framework, expected criteria/outcomes for Pathway segments, output-to-next-input continuation semantics and other Praxis-level fulfilment housekeeping. Ponos/Ergo performs governed execution, output processing and routing using those semantics; **Praxis is neither an orchestrator nor a choreographer**.
The [U19 Digital Twin Behaviour pattern](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md) is a genuine one-Ergo Praxis: Digital Twin → Behaviour [1..*] → Praxis → Pathway → Ergo [exactly 1]. Required Context, criteria/outcomes, fulfilment and housekeeping still apply. This specialised realisation does not alter the general Praxis → Pathway Aggregation [0..1]. Energeia and Ponos are peer application components; Praxis's semantic/operational envelope does not structurally contain Ponos. Behaviour sequencing is not Pathway orchestration.
**Energeia owns the Praxis application responsibility** and SHALL provide the candidate **Praxis Management Services** responsibility set:
- definition and registration; - discovery and retrieval; - operational configuration and externally visible interface configuration; - Topic inclusion/exclusion policy; - Pathway relationship/aggregation management; - applicable Context definitions, segment criteria/outcomes and continuation semantics; - assurance-rule association and other Praxis-wide operational constraints.
These responsibilities are not yet decomposed into separate Application Features, Application Services, internal constructs or subordinate Software Components. Topic inclusion's necessity, the interface model and assurance-rule attachment contract remain unresolved. Managing interface configuration does not transfer Pylai's external contract/publication responsibility to Energeia; Praxis Topic policy does not transfer Mneme's Publishing/Subscription/Pattern selection.
| Architectural relationship | Established meaning and limit | | :--- | :--- | | Energeia → Praxis | Application ownership/management through Praxis Management Services. Mneme manages its governed information; Ponos uses it for execution; Dokimasia uses it as assurance basis. | | Praxis → Pathway | **Aggregation [0..1]**. Praxis may exist without a Pathway because activity may proceed through Publish/Subscribe. | | Praxis → Journey | Working **Aggregation** of relevant observed progression; exact cardinalities and association contracts remain unresolved. No Composition or shared lifecycle is inferred. | | Journey → contributing information/evidence | Semantic **Aggregation/reference** without transfer of originating ownership or indiscriminate duplication. |
Praxis is not equivalent to Pathway, Route, a sequence of Ergo/Ergon, a runtime engine or a Pub/Sub graph. Historical blueprint/composition/execution descriptions are retained provenance, not competing current definitions. Detailed Praxis representation and lifecycle remain [CDG-01/06](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md): versioning, activation/deactivation, replacement, retirement and treatment of in-flight activity following change are deliberately unestablished.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Pragma-Outputs-and-Pathway-Continuation.md` — ## 2. Pathway and Praxis. Standing: Architecturally adjudicated U18; candidate scope and representation deferrals retained.
**A Pathway defines the conceptual sequence of Ergo through which execution progresses.** Established PathwayEndpoints, PathwaySegments and Routes express the controlled interactions available along that sequence; their existing meanings remain intact.
**A Praxis defines how that Pathway is to be fulfilled**, including:
- the Context definitions applicable to execution; - expected criteria/outcomes associated with Pathway segments; - the semantics required to process one segment's result into the input required by the next; and - other Praxis-level housekeeping required for fulfilment.
Praxis manages the definition of Context required by the Ergo framework. Mneme manages Context materialisation and use; the framework applies the applicable definitions. The existing non-exhaustive likely resource set identified by an Ergo and supported bounded Adhoc access remain compatible with that division.
This clarifies fulfilment semantics within Praxis's established operational and assurance envelope. It preserves Praxis Aggregation of Pathway [0..1], including the established possibility of Pub/Sub activity without a predefined Pathway. It does not make Praxis an orchestrator, choreographer or execution engine.

Detailed Praxis-to-activity relationships and definition-to-instance model remain CDG-01/06; no Composition inferred. |``.
