element.name: [BusinessObject] Information Unit
element.documentation:
An Information Unit is Harmonia's **indivisible unit of governed information**: one persistent IU identity, **exactly one InformationRepresentation [1..1]** and accepted-state integrity/consistency. Its governed boundary associates represented information and its management concerns. Atomicity does not prescribe one physical write, row, Java object, cache instance, file or transport operation.
The conceptual and [logical Calliope Class](../../application/data-object/class/74ec609de1ae498fbf9d13e4ef8c6cbe.md) describe the same IU, not independently governed entities. IU identity consists of its persistent UUID and its own Topic name `harmonia.mneme.iu.<hex-string-of-compressed-uuid>`. The UUID encoding is deterministic/reversible; its exact algorithm is not chosen. IU identity is distinct from represented-information/entity identity, native Content versions, coordinate/security/content-structure Topics and provider/transport IDs.
The accepted conceptual form is **Identity / Metadata / InformationRepresentation**. Metadata distinguishes ManagementContext, InformationCoordinates, SecurityContext and LifecycleContext, with optional supplied relationships [0..*]. The singular representation distinguishes ContainerMetadata, ContentMetadata (including Content Structure Topic and Content Structure Version) and Content (native instance version only where supported). [Information Unit Metadata](../../application/data-object/c05b7e37278141488ecc90b9a9ef96eb.md) and [InformationRepresentation](../../application/data-object/b9891b88150840ada3daefdec6f26c35.md) detail the logical allocation without requiring one implementation Class per concern or creating nested independently governed IUs. Unit Structure, Content Structure and Content Format remain distinct.
Mneme manages active access and operational Version/individual Active Generation; Mnemosyne establishes authoritative durable state/version. These remain different concurrency domains under AX-05. The retained generation guardrails below concern successfully established manifestations and governed information progression; their 'Version' does not redefine Mneme's operational Version. Failed/degraded convergence establishes no valid generation or durable truth. A failed subsequent manifestation does not, by itself, invalidate an existing successful generation.
Transformation to another governed representation creates another IU. The IU owns no transformation management, reverse-transformation guarantee, automatic reciprocal relationship maintenance or universal lifecycle. Creators/updaters supply optional references; Mneme validates local acceptability and preserves remote references without validating external existence/availability/correctness. Provenance remains distinct from such references; Kleio audit and Dokimasia Provenance/assurance remain their specialised responsibilities. Operational owner/location grants no access.
The IU is foundational across the accepted Capability hierarchy, not owned by one Capability or by Mneme, Mnemosyne, Themis, a database or a transport. Information Container remains a retired proposed name; no PetasosParcel identity mapping is introduced. Search Result Sets remain metadata-reference collections. Native standards semantics, originating authority and existing security/preservation obligations remain intact. The IU implements no audit or lifecycle orchestration.
### Bounded supersession of the prior conceptual partition
------- Legacy Content - Superseded ------- Start ------ Superseded by: accepted Information Unit DRP §§2–9,13–19 and the current definition above; logical [InformationUnit](../../application/data-object/class/74ec609de1ae498fbf9d13e4ef8c6cbe.md). Only the old definition, partition and concern allocation enclosed here are superseded. Original content follows unchanged. Established generation/failure guardrails and other source contributions retain their applicable standing. ---------------------------------------------------------
> **An Information Unit is the governed boundary within which Harmonia associates a Governed Representation with its Management Context.**
An Information Unit is bounded, governed and a unit of Harmonia-managed information. It is **not necessarily atomic**: boundedness does not imply indivisibility. An Information Unit MAY contain structured, composite or related information according to its defined Information Unit structure.
**Information Unit** is the canonical term for this concept. **Information Container** is retired as its proposed name; legitimate technology or application uses of container and the existing containment pattern retain their meaning. No architectural mapping to `PetasosParcel` is established. Any future implementation mapping must be derived downstream.
### 6.1 Conceptual Partition
```text Information Unit │ ├── Identity │ ├── Metadata │ ├── Content │ └── Context ```
| Conceptual partition | Meaning | | :--- | :--- | | **Identity** | Identifies the Information Unit. | | **Metadata** | Describes how Harmonia recognises and manages the Information Unit. | | **Content** | Contains the represented information and its representation characteristics. | | **Context** | Contains the management context governing the information over time. |
These are conceptual partitions, **not a final schema**. They SHALL NOT be interpreted as requiring four implementation objects, database structures, Java classes or serialised elements. The partition does not prescribe a physical separation or a complete allocation of management concerns to implementation representations.
All dotted notation below is illustrative conceptual notation only. It SHALL NOT establish final attribute names, datatypes, identifier schemes, cardinalities or implementation representations, and does not enumerate complete structures.
### 6.2 Identity
> **Identity identifies the Information Unit itself.**
Illustrative notation: `InformationUnit.Identity.InstanceId`.
Information Unit identity, the identity of the represented information, and the identity of a real-world entity represented by that information are potentially distinct architectural concerns. None SHALL be inferred to be another merely because an implementation or external representation uses a common identifier. The Information Concept's [Identity & Reference characteristics](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#31-identity--reference) remain distinct from this Information Unit identity. The complete Identity structure is not established here.
### 6.3 Metadata
> **Metadata describes the Information Unit and the characteristics required for Harmonia to recognise and manage that Information Unit.**
Illustrative notation: `InformationUnit.Metadata.StructureId`. This MAY conceptually identify the defined Information Unit structure/type to which the Information Unit conforms. It concerns the **Unit structure**, not the semantic structure/model of the information represented within it. The complete Metadata attribute set, naming, cardinality and representation are not established here.
### 6.4 Content
> **Content contains the information represented by the Information Unit together with the representation characteristics necessary to interpret that content.**
Illustrative notation:
```text InformationUnit.Content.Data InformationUnit.Content.StructureId InformationUnit.Content.Format ```
**Content Structure** conceptually identifies the semantic/structural definition to which the represented content conforms. **Content Format** conceptually identifies the concrete representation or encoding of that content.
Downstream architecture might, for example, distinguish a semantic structure, profile or model from JSON, XML, a binary representation or a media type. These examples are non-normative: no supported model, format, mapping or mandatory attribute is established by them. Concrete encoding/format SHALL NOT be treated as equivalent to semantic information structure.
| Illustrative notation | Distinct architectural concern | | :--- | :--- | | `InformationUnit.Metadata.StructureId` | The structure/type of the Information Unit. | | `InformationUnit.Content.StructureId` | The semantic structure/model of the represented information within Content. | | `InformationUnit.Content.Format` | The concrete representation or encoding of that Content. |
Unit Structure, Content Structure and Content Format SHALL remain distinct. Sharing a notation suffix or a downstream representation does not collapse these concerns.
### 6.5 Context
> **Context contains the management context through which Harmonia governs, understands and safely manages the represented information over time.**
The complementary [Metabolē pattern](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/metabole.md) defines bounded progression of one or more Information Units, with applicable Context, provenance/derivation and accumulated outputs. Its conceptual [ActivityContext](c34b4929f71946708d37dbe6c1da920a.md) classifies the broad activity; it neither replaces this Unit Management Context nor equates it with Mneme's loaded-value Context or Themis PEP-Context.
The following are currently identified **conceptual management concerns**. They are not a final attribute list or schema, nor a mandatory populated field bundle.
| Concern | Conceptual meaning and boundary | | :--- | :--- | | **Provenance** | Where/how information arose or was established. | | **Authority** | Whose assertion, relationship or determination is authoritative within the applicable context. | | **Version** | Identifies a governed progression of an Information Unit's representation. | | **Lifecycle** | The applicable information lifecycle and its governance; no universal lifecycle or new state set is defined. | | **Temporal Context** | The temporal context needed to understand and manage the represented information; no new temporal model is defined. | | **Relationships** | Applicable relationships relevant to management and interpretation; no new relationship taxonomy is defined. | | **Active Generation** | Identifies a particular valid manifestation of an Information Unit established for active management or use. |
**Provenance and Authority SHALL NOT be collapsed.** The source supplying information is not necessarily the originating authority for every assertion or relationship represented by it. The existing granular assertion/relationship authority and provenance distinctions remain applicable; this model does not complete the wider authority/credibility vocabulary or evidence/retention model.
**Version and Active Generation SHALL NOT be collapsed.** Under [AX-05](../../motivation/principle/0412a2084f0145babc4f022c71fea65f.md), authoritative durable progression and valid active managed-state generation remain distinct concurrency domains. Mnemosyne establishes authoritative durable state/version; Mneme manages active representation and coordination. Failed or degraded convergence SHALL NOT establish or advance a valid active-state generation; untrusted active coordination requires reconciliation with authoritative state. Neither domain may substitute for the other or promote cached/process-local state to durable authority. This preserves the established boundary without completing the managed-state model or prescribing concurrency mechanisms.
Management Context does not imply that every management concern is durable resource content. [AX-07](../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md) preserves security context as operational context without automatic persistence as information content; [AX-08](../../motivation/principle/21d6864657964ba5b03e3f6b5eb29cd5.md) and [AX-09](../../motivation/principle/9a5cb9e8876844e58e660f909f7df9fc.md) distinguish meaningful durable evidence from transient operational state. No retention or security representation mechanism is inferred here.
------- Legacy Content - Superseded ------- Finish ----
### Retained governed progression and generation semantics
The sections below retain their original wording. Their establishment/failure constraints remain binding. Earlier statements leaving component/context allocation for downstream work are superseded only to the bounded extent now established by the accepted IU Framework; no concurrency or lifecycle mechanism is inferred.
#### 6.5.1 Version and Active Generation
> **Version identifies a governed progression of an Information Unit's representation.**
> **Active Generation identifies a particular valid manifestation of an Information Unit established for active management or use.**
These definitions are complementary and identify different semantic dimensions: **Version concerns governed information progression. Active Generation concerns active manifestation.**
**Multiple Active Generations MAY derive from the same Version. A change of Active Generation does not, by itself, indicate a change of Version.**
```text Information Unit │ ├── Version V7 │ ├── Active Generation G21 │ ├── Active Generation G22 │ └── Active Generation G23 │ └── Version V8 └── Active Generation G24 ```
The labels are illustrative only; they establish no identifier syntax, sequence mechanism or numbering scheme. The model also permits a Version with no current Active Generation. It establishes no maximum number of Generations.
Version and Active Generation remain conceptual concerns within Information Unit Context. Their inclusion in Context does not require simple scalar fields and defines no canonical Version or Generation attributes. The architecture establishes semantics, not schema.
#### 6.5.2 Observability and Manifestation
Independent processes/functions may act upon manifestations of the same Information Unit Version established at different observable points. For example, Process A may act upon G21, Process B upon G22 and Process C upon G23, with all three manifestations derived from V7:

The arrows illustrate which manifestations the processes act upon; they do not define Generation creation, assignment or ownership. The processes can therefore share governed information progression while acting against different active manifestations. Version alone cannot express that distinction.
**Active Generation identifies the manifestation, not the process acting upon it.** Multiple processes/functions MAY legitimately act upon the same Active Generation. The example requires neither a separate Generation for each process nor any process-to-Generation cardinality or affinity.

> **Active Generation is not a timestamp or measure of time.**
Temporal Context may help explain when a manifestation was established, applicable or observed, but Temporal Context and Active Generation are distinct Information Architecture concerns. A single Active Generation may remain valid across an interval. Different Active Generations need not be distinguished by wall-clock time. No timestamp, clock, sequence counter or temporal implementation mechanism is established.
```text Version change = governed information progression Active Generation change = different valid active manifestation ≠ necessarily information progression ```
Active Generation SHALL NOT be treated as another form of Version. A difference in active manifestation does not, by itself, establish authoritative information progression.

The distinction does not determine whether retrieval manifests a Generation or how returned Units or result sets are manifested. #### 6.5.6 Establishment and Semantic Indivisibility
> **Active Generation is a successful-state concept. An unsuccessful attempt to manifest an Information Unit does not create an invalid Active Generation; it fails to establish an Active Generation.**
> **Active Generation establishment is semantically indivisible. Partial, degraded or incomplete manifestation SHALL NOT constitute an Active Generation.**
The manifestation must be successfully established in full according to the applicable governed architecture; otherwise no Active Generation is established by that attempt.
```text Manifestation Attempt │ ├── successfully established in full │ └── Active Generation established │ └── otherwise └── No Active Generation established by this attempt ```
There is no partially valid, degraded, incomplete or half-established Active Generation. Runtime work may pass through partial, intermediate, degraded or failed conditions while attempting manifestation. These examples define no implementation state names, attributes or schema. > **Harmonia SHALL support a bound set of Information Unit structures for each architectural release. **The semantic space supported by a release is explicitly governed and bounded.** Bound does not mean that all Information Units have identical populated attributes, that every conceptual element is mandatory, that the model can never evolve, or that the supported set is permanently closed.

> **Evolution between release-bound Information Unit models is explicit architectural evolution, not uncontrolled schema drift.**
```text Harmonia │ ├── R1.x │ └── Bound Information Unit Model │ ├── R2.x │ └── Bound Information Unit Model │ └── R3.x └── Bound Information Unit Model ```

Information Unit establishes the governed boundary through which Harmonia manages represented information; it is not an Information Concept synonym or a new semantic category. | | **Information Relationship** | Retains its governed source/target/type, qualification and role distinctions. Relationships may be relevant to represented information and Management Context without being replaced by the Information Unit boundary. | | **Information Assembly** | Retains its meaning as a governed semantic composition of independently meaningful Information Concepts. Composite Content is permitted, but Information Unit does not redefine Assembly or establish Assembly-to-Unit equivalence. | | **Information View** | Retains its purpose/consumer-oriented projection meaning. Presentation or a contextual view does not by itself establish an Information Unit or acceptance of management responsibility. | | **Authority, Custody and Provenance** | Retain their existing distinctions. Establishing a managed boundary does not originate represented facts, transfer their authority or equate custody with management acceptance. Provenance remains distinct from Authority. | | **Lifecycle, Temporal Context and Managed State** | Remain governed concerns within applicable context. The conceptual partitions establish neither a universal lifecycle nor the complete managed-state/history model. Durable Version remains distinct from Active Generation. | | **FHIR Resource / Standards Model** | A FHIR Resource MAY eventually be used as, or within, the representation of Content according to downstream architecture. Information Unit is not a FHIR Resource; no one-to-one equivalence or mapping is established. Native standards representations remain applicable under AX-03. | | **Digital Twin** | Remains an active management construct associated with a real-world entity, coordinating information and operational activity. The Twin SHALL NOT be modelled as an Information Unit. Its information relationships/structures remain downstream questions, not a Unit mapping established here. |
See the [Assembly/View definitions](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/assemblies-views/assemblies-and-views.md#1-information-assembly-vs-information-view), [relationship pattern](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/information-relationships.md), [lifecycle principles](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/information-lifecycle.md) and [Strategy Digital Twin definition](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/strategic-views/logical-component-responsibilities.md#component-7-digital-twin-entity-centred-operational-coordination-construct) for their established meanings. [AX-03](../../motivation/principle/e99a4e2bf99f476d876394300d6b9c3d.md) and [AX-12](../../motivation/principle/ce85889bd9b34f79a53d4c907ceb19d4.md) preserve appropriate native standards models and fluent access to information; the conceptual Unit boundary does not require replacement models or an implementation wrapper.

Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md` — ## 9. Platform / Framework Obligations. Standing: Established Information Unit boundary; unresolved downstream realisation preserved.
> **Harmonia capabilities/services concerned with persistence, security, provenance or transport SHALL recognise and support both the Information Unit itself and the information represented within the Information Unit.**
An Information Unit is not an incidental implementation wrapper that infrastructure services may ignore. Persistence, security, provenance and transport SHALL be capable of respecting the Information Unit boundary and its applicable management semantics, as well as those of the represented information.
This obligation defines required semantic support. It allocates no Application Component and prescribes no encryption mechanism, database schema, ACL structure, serialisation protocol, message header, cache layout or other implementation mechanism. It is consistent with [AX-04](../../motivation/principle/54508cda80484a6caf95b901780eaf7d.md): Harmonia owns semantics while engines provide suitable machinery.
Recognition by transport does not require external parties to understand private Information Unit management semantics. [AX-02](../../motivation/principle/eee8c3783d964d18a7f9dcea85fcd4cf.md) governs standards-facing contracts, and [AX-13](../../motivation/principle/b6a55decfeec4f1bb3d7f18534a2ffea.md) terminates Harmonia management of the emitted representation at external egress. Retained internal information and provenance do not extend operational control beyond that boundary. No external Unit envelope or transport mapping is defined.

Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md` — ## 10. Information Unit Guardrails. Standing: Established Information Unit boundary; unresolved downstream realisation preserved.
These G1–G8 identifiers are local to the Information Unit model and supplement the existing [sixteen core modelling guardrails](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/guardrails/modelling-guardrails.md).
| Guardrail | Required boundary | | :--- | :--- | | **G1 — Managed Does Not Mean Originated** | Harmonia management responsibility does not establish originating information authority. | | **G2 — Managed Does Not Mean Domain Authority** | Managing information concerning an activity does not confer authority to determine or manage the underlying domain activity; AX-18 applies. | | **G3 — Information Unit Is Not Necessarily Atomic** | Boundedness does not imply indivisibility. | | **G4 — Unit Structure and Content Structure Are Distinct** | The structure/type of an Information Unit and the semantic structure of its Content are different architectural concerns. | | **G5 — Format and Semantic Structure Are Distinct** | Concrete encoding/format SHALL NOT be treated as equivalent to semantic information structure. | | **G6 — Release Models Are Bound** | Within a release, supported Information Unit structures and semantics SHALL be explicitly governed. | | **G7 — Evolution Is Explicit** | Change between release-bound Information Unit models is architectural evolution, not uncontrolled schema drift. | | **G8 — Implementation Does Not Invent Information Unit Semantics** | New Information Unit structures SHALL NOT arise merely because an implementation component requires a convenient wrapper, envelope, DTO, cache object or transport object. |

Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md` — ## 11. Downstream Derivation and Retained Questions. Standing: Established Information Unit boundary; unresolved downstream realisation preserved.
This conceptual model does **not yet establish**:

### 11.1 Adjudicated Search Management Boundary
The 2026-10-10 [two-case search adjudication](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/search-results.md) resolves the former generic search-management question:
- **Harmonia-managed search** produces a managed metadata-based **Search Result Set**, governed within its own Information Unit boundary. Membership references the Information Unit Versions comprising that result, without copying their content, creating new Versions of them or another authority. - **External search** is intentionally performed within an **Ergo activity**. Returned information is acquired and persisted within that activity's governed context and applicable Information Unit boundary; no additional generic management-acceptance transition is required because the origin is external.
Search metadata categories and `0..*` Version-reference membership establish information meaning, not a complete schema. API/result representation, reference encoding, storage/cache and manifestation mechanics remain downstream. Snapshot/export and detailed Audit / Assurance remain separate concerns. Result encoding, projection or cache treatment SHALL NOT redefine this boundary. [AX-17](../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) preserves genuinely unestablished details without retaining the resolved generic acceptance question.

Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/information-lifecycle.md` — ## 1. Rejection of Universal Lifecycles. Standing: Canonical information governance; concept-specific lifecycles retained.
A foundational principle of the Harmonia Information Architecture is the explicit rejection of an artificial, universal lifecycle applied indiscriminately across all information assets:
> **Harmonia does NOT impose a single universal lifecycle across Information Concepts. Lifecycles are concept-specific and governed by the business meaning and responsibilities of the owning Capability.**
Different categories of healthcare and operational information progress through fundamentally different states: - A **Catalogue Definition** progresses through publication and versioning lifecycles (*Draft* $\to$ *Active* $\to$ *Deprecated* $\to$ *Retired*). - A **FulfillmentTask** represents a particular undertaking and carries applicable execution progression (illustratively, *Proposed* $\to$ *Accepted* $\to$ *In-Progress* $\to$ *Completed* / *Failed*). This is not a universal transition model; multiple/concurrent undertakings may exist for one ActionableTask where its work semantics allow them. - A **Clinical Document** progresses through legal authoring states (*Draft* $\to$ *Preliminary* $\to$ *Final* $\to$ *Amended* $\to$ *Superseded*). This is a scoped lifecycle illustration: `Final ≠ automatically Final Signed`. Signing, finalisation, authorship, attestation, approval, authentication, verification, authority and legal qualification remain distinct; locally established signing requirements are preserved without making them universal. Amendment and supersession are not mandatory for every document, and consumer processing does not define originating validity or authority. - A **Clinical Assertion / Finding** progresses through epistemic verification (*Suspected* $\to$ *Confirmed* $\to$ *Refuted* / *Entered-in-Error*). - An **Encounter** progresses through admission, movement, and discharge stages (*Planned* $\to$ *Arrived* $\to$ *In-Care* $\to$ *Discharged*).
```mermaid graph TD subgraph DefLC ["Definition Lifecycle"] D1["Draft"] --> D2["Active"] --> D3["Deprecated"] --> D4["Retired"] end
subgraph TaskLC ["FulfillmentTask Execution — Illustrative"] T1["Proposed"] --> T2["Accepted"] --> T3["In-Progress"] --> T4["Completed"] T3 --> T5["Failed"] end
subgraph DocLC ["Clinical Document Lifecycle"] DC1["Draft"] --> DC2["Preliminary"] --> DC3["Final"] --> DC4["Amended"] --> DC5["Superseded"] end
subgraph AssertLC ["Assertion Verification Lifecycle"] A1["Suspected"] --> A2["Confirmed"] A1 --> A3["Refuted"] A2 --> A4["Entered-in-Error"] end ```
The [bounded Task / Work model](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/task-work.md) separates the archetype, work instance, undertaking and governed ActionableTask resolution. An undertaking has its own execution state and may produce output; it does not independently own TaskOutcome. Completion alone does not inherently satisfy its parent: the ActionableTask's explicit outcome policy governs participation and resulting outputs. ExecutionConcurrency, OutcomeConcurrency.Mode and Outcome.OutputRules.Mode remain orthogonal and SHALL NOT be collapsed into a single lifecycle, state or concurrency mechanism. This lifecycle guidance does not adjudicate TaskOutcome lifecycle/identity or the unresolved ReportedTask meaning.

Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/information-lifecycle.md` — ## 2. Lifecycle Transition Governance. Standing: Canonical information governance; concept-specific lifecycles retained.
Where an Information Concept is stateful, transitions between states are **governed semantic events**:
```mermaid graph LR S1["Prior State (S1)"] -->|"Transition Event<br/>+ Triggering Activity<br/>+ Authorising Authority<br/>+ Provenance & Timestamp<br/>+ Justification / Reason"| S2["Target State (S2)"] ```
### 2.1 Transition Requirements Every material lifecycle transition SHALL support: 1. **Triggering Context**: The business interaction, clinical activity, or workflow rule that initiated the transition. 2. **Authorising Authority**: The clinician, system, or administrative authority empowered to effect the change. 3. **Transition Provenance**: Timestamp, location, and non-repudiation audit capture. 4. **Justification / Reason**: Explicit rationale, especially for abnormal, exceptional, or erratum transitions (e.g. *Entered-in-Error*, *Emergency Cancellation*).
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/information-lifecycle.md` — ## 3. Immutability of History & Non-Destructive Progression. Standing: Canonical information governance; concept-specific lifecycles retained.
In accordance with healthcare safety and legal compliance: - **No Physical Destruction / Deletion**: Information Concepts, once asserted or recorded into durable truth, are never subjected to physical destructive deletion. - **State Invalidation via Explicit Supersession / Error Status**: Corrections and retractions are represented as new, append-only assertion events (*Superseded*, *Entered-in-Error*, *Refuted*) that preserve the historical record alongside the rationale for correction. - **Bi-Temporal Integrity**: Information architecture supports reconstructing what was known at any specific past historical point in time (*as-of query*), distinguishing when an event occurred from when it was recorded or amended.

Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/information-lifecycle.md` — ## 4. Information Unit Context and Managed-State Boundary. Standing: Canonical information governance; concept-specific lifecycles retained.
Lifecycle and Temporal Context are conceptual management concerns within an [Information Unit's Context](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#65-context). The Unit boundary does not impose a universal lifecycle, new lifecycle states or temporal model. Authoritative representation/Version progression remains distinct from valid Active Generation under AX-05. Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/authority-custody-provenance.md` — ## 6. Information Unit Management Boundary. Standing: Canonical information governance; originating authority preserved.
The [canonical Harmonia-managed information definition](10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md) concerns explicit responsibility to maintain a governed representation and its management context over time. This acceptance remains distinct from originating information authority, domain authority, custody, persistence, transport, presentation and consumption. Externally originated information may be managed without transferring its originating authority to Harmonia; AX-18 applies.

A supplying source need not be the originating authority of every represented assertion/relationship. The wider evidence/retention and authority vocabulary questions remain for separate reconciliation.

Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/guardrails/observable-information-and-domain-meaning.md` — ## 2. Observability and Encapsulated Domain Meaning. Standing: Adjudicated observable-information boundary; runtime AI optional.
Harmonia's concept of reality is bounded by its observability of that reality through the information available to it. Observation and management of information do not imply semantic comprehension of all encapsulated domain content. Missing observation supplies neither a domain fact nor a certain operational outcome; [AX-15](../../motivation/principle/ef8abbaec37e4890ad78b9f263e67906.md) continues to govern operational uncertainty.
Harmonia may observe, carry, associate, apply, append, transform, persist, route, forward and respond to information according to explicitly established models, rules, Behaviours, Praxis and developer-defined logic without independently deriving the domain meaning of that information.
**Harmonia is not intrinsically an inferential agent.** Meaning acted upon is supplied through established models, explicit rules/behaviour, developer-defined processing or intentionally invoked services. The Harmonia Platform does not independently infer that meaning, nor intrinsically require comprehension of encapsulated business, clinical or other domain content.
This boundary does not remove Harmonia's own semantics. Harmonia necessarily understands the governed architectural semantics required to manage its own information and execution constructs, including authority, lifecycle, security, provenance and work/undertaking distinctions. Established semantic models, terminology rules and conformance responsibilities remain applicable; their existence does not make the Platform intrinsically comprehend every content item it carries.
For the [bounded Task model](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/task-work.md), an `ActionableTaskArchetype` can establish content expectations without specifying the content's structural representation or requiring domain comprehension. The domain content of `Task.Output(s)` contained / represented by `TaskOutcome` may remain semantically opaque while the governed ActionableTask resolution and its undertaking references remain explicit. The ActionableTask's `Outcome.OutputRules.Mode = Derived` applies explicitly defined rules to participating outputs without requiring Harmonia to infer their domain meaning. This information semantic prescribes no derivation implementation mechanism and does not make runtime AI intrinsic to Harmonia.

element.name: GovernedWriter
element.documentation:
### Approved 1.1.24 incorporation — resulting candidate pending
Full GovernedWriter conveys authorised CREATE, UPDATE and governed RETIRE of the full IU. RETIRE preserves governed history, retention, immutable versions and evidence; provider-native DELETE is not automatic physical destruction authority. Original MI-07 retains this mapping subject.
Persist/manage actual Content through the applicable PersistenceService, obtain its opaque reference, establish/update that reference in ContentMetadata and durably establish the corresponding Summary as **one coherent authoritative IU/version** (FC-01/04). Native Content-only or Summary-only partial/orphaned effects are not a successful full write. Responsible persistence workflow/adapter handles them under existing recovery rules. Logical atomicity does not mandate one native transaction, physical store or exact call order. There is no SummaryWriter UPDATE.
A directed/forced write never destructively overwrites preserved immutable history. An absent requested version may be established; an identical preserved state may already satisfy it. When integrity requires, Mnemosyne may establish a higher actual IU version, including a greater increment, and **returns the actual authoritative version on Success**. This changes neither Content Structure Version nor native payload version and transfers no per-IU concurrency from Mneme (AV-04).
Multi-site durable completion is required synchronously on Success (AV-03/04). Lost response/Indeterminate is investigated through authoritative GovernedReader(version=*) plus sufficient submitted-write correspondence and durability evidence; newer version alone is not proof (MI-06). Explicit version reads remain exact. No new seam transaction identifier, independent version counter or Mnemosyne-to-Mnemosyne IU arbitration is introduced.
Mneme reconciles Standard-Cache Summary and appropriate active manifestations with the actual outcome. It may safely refresh/invalidate caches but must preserve an executing Ergon's immutable version-specific input. Cache updates do not prove persistence.
All five contracts are synchronous governed request/response, with Calliope-owned factual Outcome (closed Success / Failure / Indeterminate and governed closed Reason vocabulary/extensions). Exact Reason members and stage codes remain deferred. Mnemosyne reports facts; Mneme determines consumer disposition without rewriting them. Transport/session timeout is not a factual operation Failure. Receipt, work acceptance, authoritative effect and end-to-end completion remain distinct.
Authentication and Themis policy apply: Readers require ACCESS + READ, SummarySearch invocation ACCESS + SEARCH and disclosed candidates ACCESS + READ, Writers CHANGE with the requested information operation. Protect identity, metadata, counts, pagination and other existence disclosures as well as Content. RequiredIU/SupportedIU capability matching grants no permission. Preserve source-near audit/provenance, Kleio mandatory capture authority/fail-closed obligations and Dokimasia/Provenance allocations; no blanket candidate event catalogue is promoted. Native database/query/provider values stay below the seam.
Every authoritative full or Summary mutation Success requires the applicable multi-site durable authoritative operation and actual resulting IU version, never cache success, local commit, replication queued or transport ACK. Immutable historical versions are preserved. Mneme retains individual-IU concurrency; eligible Mnemosyne instances must expose one coherent authoritative logical history or factual uncertainty. No extra seam transaction identifier or second version axis is introduced.

Only the enclosed predecessor wording is superseded; source history is unchanged. ---------------------------------------------------------
The established Harmonia-owned contract conveys CREATE, UPDATE and DELETE authoritative persistence requests and their governed state/version and Outcome results from Mnemosyne to Mneme. Accepted active-cache activity, transport/native receipt and authoritative durable acceptance remain distinct. Mneme coordinates individual IU changes; Mnemosyne establishes authoritative durable state/version atomically under AX-05 and applicable persistence constraints.
GPF controls workflow and the Persistence Adapter executes/verifies; the Façade preserves the boundary. Applicable security, audit/provenance, retention holds, governed identity and reconstruction remain effective. Provider-native DELETE is not automatic Harmonia retirement/disposition authority. Unknown effect remains Indeterminate and cannot justify blind repeated mutation.
This accepted parent meaning supplies no exact proof/correlation envelope, method signature, protocol, lifecycle state machine or independent acceptance of the neighbouring interaction draft.

element.name: [CT3] Assurance Conclusion Determination
element.documentation:
Establish the legitimately supported conclusion, including insufficiency, qualification and unresolved concerns where applicable.
Assurance Conclusion Determination establishes what confidence is legitimately supported by the assessment. It preserves qualifications and unresolved concerns rather than forcing incomplete evidence into a positive or negative result. Within Assurance Evaluation it is the responsibility that gives the conclusion its standing, distinct from gathering or assessing the supporting material.
**Boundary**
Insufficiency proves neither assurance nor non-assurance, and the conclusion does not manage the subject's operational response.

element.name: Specimen Transport Process
element.documentation:
• Owning Capability: Clinical Logistics Coordination
• Process Purpose: Governs the physical courier chain-of-custody, transport, and delivery of pathology bio-specimens, blood products, and surgical biopsies.
• State Progression Lifecycle: Specimen Packaged → Courier Dispatched → Chain-of-Custody Signed → In-Transit (Monitored) → Lab Ingress Received → Specimen Accepted
• Key State Dispositions:
• Specimen Packaged: Clinical unit packages bio-sample with barcode manifest.
• Courier Dispatched: Courier route assigned for pickup.
• Chain-of-Custody Signed: Courier scans barcode and accepts legal custody.
• In-Transit (Monitored): Specimen in transit under temperature/time constraints.
• Lab Ingress Received: Central pathology specimen reception logs physical receipt.
• Specimen Accepted: Specimen integrity verified and passed to analytical track.
---
## History
### Process Overview — predecessor explanation
Specimen transport preserves the movement and custody account connecting collection context with laboratory receipt. It makes the journey of the material explainable rather than reducing it to a sent/received pair. Delivery remains distinct from specimen acceptance, diagnostic performance and the eventual professional interpretation of its evidence.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md` — entry lines 248-261. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.

\texttt{\seqsplit{Chain-of-Custody Signed}}: Courier scans barcode and accepts legal custody.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Transit (Monitored)}}: Specimen in transit under temperature/\allowbreak{}time constraints.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Lab Ingress Received}}: Central pathology specimen reception logs physical receipt.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Accepted}}: Specimen integrity verified and passed to analytical track.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

element.name: [CT1] Health Service Assurance
element.documentation:
Establish and maintain justified confidence that health services can be, and are being, delivered in accordance with applicable expectations, obligations, constraints and required levels of performance.
Health Service Assurance establishes justified confidence in the ability to deliver health services appropriately. Specification defines how confidence will be established; evaluation determines what the available evidence supports. Its subject is macro-level service delivery, with workforce, clinical, information, security and other concerns contributing evidence or criteria without becoming separate assurance trees.
Where independent governed assurance is required, the subject cannot control its own evaluation or conclusion. Independence concerns control of the assurance judgement rather than requiring a separate organisation or technology installation.
**Intent**
Distinguish justified confidence, qualified conclusions and insufficient evidence so that assurance communicates what is actually supported.
**Boundary**
Assurance manages its own evaluation and does not assign, remediate or progress the subject activity. Harmonia does not thereby assume responsibility for clinical adequacy or professional practice.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Approved independent governed assurance materially supports service confidence. The three established assurance BECs provide bounded support; they are not remapped to the newer BC descendants and are not assigned implementation components.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT3] Care Appointment Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage a scheduled opportunity for care.
Care Appointment Management establishes a scheduled opportunity for care and maintains that opportunity as arrangements change. Within scheduling and capacity it supplies the temporal commitment around which participants can organise, while leaving the actual availability of places and resources distinguishable. A scheduled opportunity is useful coordination information even before attendance or care occurs.
**Boundary**
A booking does not establish attendance, intervention performance or satisfaction of diagnostic-service-specific scheduling constraints.

element.name: [CT2] Organisation Administration
element.documentation:
Organisation Administration maintains the identity, profiles, structural relationships and contact context of participating healthcare organisations. It enables a legal or operational entity to be distinguished from a department, network relationship or communication channel. This supports consistent interpretation of providers and destinations across information flows rather than allowing each interface to create an incompatible organisational account.
**Overview**
Organisation Administration maintains the identity, profiles, structural relationships and contact context of participating healthcare organisations. It enables a legal or operational entity to be distinguished from a department, network relationship or communication channel. This supports consistent interpretation of providers and destinations across information flows rather than allowing each interface to create an incompatible organisational account.
**Intent**
Organisation Administration maintains the identity, profiles, structural relationships and contact context of participating healthcare organisations. It enables a legal or operational entity to be distinguished from a department, network relationship or communication channel. This supports consistent interpretation of providers and destinations across information flows rather than allowing each interface to create an incompatible organisational account.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Representing organisational structure does not acquire corporate authority or ownership of every service offered by the organisation.

element.name: [CT2] Work Allocation & Dispatch
element.documentation:
Work Allocation & Dispatch progresses authorised operational work from a recognised requirement through matching, dispatch, acknowledgement and oversight. It distinguishes an instantiated work item from its assignment and from evidence of performance, allowing stalled activity to be identified and escalated. Examples such as cleaning or transport concern real-world support work, not technical message queues.
**Overview**
Work Allocation & Dispatch progresses authorised operational work from a recognised requirement through matching, dispatch, acknowledgement and oversight. It distinguishes an instantiated work item from its assignment and from evidence of performance, allowing stalled activity to be identified and escalated. Examples such as cleaning or transport concern real-world support work, not technical message queues.
**Intent**
Work Allocation & Dispatch progresses authorised operational work from a recognised requirement through matching, dispatch, acknowledgement and oversight. It distinguishes an instantiated work item from its assignment and from evidence of performance, allowing stalled activity to be identified and escalated. Examples such as cleaning or transport concern real-world support work, not technical message queues.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Intent — predecessor explanation
Make operational work progression accountable from requirement to reported outcome within applicable policy and role constraints.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
This assignment responsibility does not confer clinical work allocation, qualification or privilege. A technical receipt has only its interaction contract's meaning.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Governed operational work progression is a substantive platform responsibility supporting the Core classification.
## Qualified relationship assertions

element.name: [CT3] Care Intake Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage the intake context through which an individual seeks or enters care.
Care Intake Management establishes the access context through which a person seeks or enters care. It makes the entry circumstance manageable without assuming that every intake follows a referral or already satisfies eligibility conditions. Within Care Access Management, intake is the responsibility for entry context rather than a decision that all subsequent care arrangements are complete.
**Boundary**
An intake record does not establish acceptance of a referral, care responsibility or delivery of care.

element.name: [CT1] Governed Information Operations
element.documentation:
Maintain identifiable, meaningful, context-qualified and retrievable information through valid state progression.
**Overview**
Entity integrity, context, lifecycle, information maintenance, discovery and semantic conformance are constituent reusable abilities; none is an implementation subsystem.
**Intent**
Keep information identity, meaning, context, state and retrieval compatible across diverse healthcare uses.
**Boundary**
Information management and semantic governance do not grant originating domain authority or erase active/durable state separation.

Information Model Compliance addresses conformity to applicable model requirements. It makes actual organisational use accountable to the adopted semantic frame rather than treating model availability or user education as proof of conformity. Within standards governance it concerns the requirements for use, not the separate task of discovering or adopting models.
**Boundary**
Conformity does not redefine the model or absorb governance oversight of the wider adoption arrangements.

element.name: Provenance Client Library
element.documentation:
Dokimasia provides this reusable architectural library responsibility for use by Harmonia components and execution activities. It performs the common work of Provenance creation, capture of relevant information/activity/context references, and reporting or publishing Provenance into the Provenance Management framework. The originating component generates Provenance through the library; Dokimasia retains ownership of the framework and management/lifecycle of resulting information.
This is a logical ApplicationComponent representing the agreed reusable library, not an implementation-level Java class/interface, additional execution framework, runtime service or deployment boundary. Provision by Dokimasia asserts no runtime containment, Java dependency or particular contract/transport. Existing Ponos, Ergo/Ergon and governed information-management facilities remain in use.
Provenance references relevant InformationUnits, Pragma instances, execution activities and associated Context without requiring embedded contents. Existing identity/version/reference/governance semantics remain unchanged. Management uses Mneme and authoritative durable persistence uses Mnemosyne; the library establishes no independent storage and does not make publication success equivalent to persistence or Assurance. It grants no assured component control over Assurance conclusions. Kleio's Audit capture contract/library and AuditEvent responsibilities remain separate.
**Standing:** Candidate under HCRL 1.1.19-001 DR-18, with DR-19 Assurance constraints; agreed intent is not formal candidate acceptance. Original versus linked new retry Pragma, attempt representation, synchronous/asynchronous publication, acknowledgement/ recovery, Provenance schemas/cardinalities/lifecycle states and detailed client-library contracts/deployment remain unresolved. No implementation is authorised.
Canonical ADD references: [Provenance](../data-object/e282811b51274649816566aac7edeb8a.md); [Provenance Client Library](171f05d188384cedb7d5c493eeaee519.md).

element.name: [CT2] Care Coordination & Transition
element.documentation:
Coordinate care participation, actual responsibility transition and discharge.
Care Coordination & Transition supports continuity by keeping participation, actual responsibility assumption and discharge progression distinct. Care teams may collaborate while responsibility is shared or changes, but physical transit and information exchange do not themselves establish who has accepted care. The capability therefore addresses continuity of accountable participation as well as the practical circumstances of departure.
**Intent**
Avoid gaps in care continuity caused by treating a movement or communication as an accepted responsibility transition.
**Boundary**
Harmonia may assemble handover information without managing clinical handover. Arrival, discharge readiness and physical departure are not equivalent to responsibility acceptance.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT3] Semantic Mapping Governance
element.documentation:
Govern mappings between applicable semantic artefacts without collapsing their source meanings or authorities.
Semantic Mapping Governance maintains mappings between applicable semantic artefacts while preserving the meaning and authority of each side. Its purpose is intelligible correspondence rather than assumed equivalence. A governed mapping can support exchange or interpretation without suggesting that the mapped artefacts have become the same concept or share one authority.
**Boundary**
A mapping does not erase source distinctions or give a consuming system authority to redefine either source.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Device Lifecycle Management
element.documentation:
Govern introduction, continued service, review, replacement, withdrawal, decommissioning and retirement within the overall device estate.
Clinical Device Lifecycle Management governs whether devices enter, remain in or leave the managed estate. Introduction, review, replacement, withdrawal and retirement concern the device's overall service disposition. This gives technology management a longer-lived responsibility than the device's current loan, release or data-exchange session.
**Boundary**
Lifecycle disposition differs from monitoring and restoring device condition; the maintenance-membership discrepancy remains unresolved.

element.name: [Topic] ReferralOutcome
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing the outcome or resolution of a Referral, including the resulting disposition and relevant information returned to participants involved in the referral.
**Status: RESOLVED — APPROVED. G2-Q01 is resolved; G2 remains open.**
Referral Disposition is **not retained as an independent Information Concept**. The assurance and governance requirement previously represented by that B candidate is instead represented by **Referral Outcome**.
> **Referral Outcome is the governed information concerning what ultimately became of a Referral, sufficient to support assurance, governance and traceability over the Referral and its progression.**
**Semantic classification:** Outcome; provenance-bearing information with Assertion characteristics where a source reports what became of the Referral. This is not ServiceOutcome equivalence or a downstream representation category.
Referral Outcome exists principally to support the ability to account for Referrals within the applicable governance/assurance scope. Where established and appropriate, it may include the resulting outcome, basis/reason, source/originator, authority, temporal context and relationships to relevant resulting activity or information. No canonical Referral Outcome value set is established.
```text Referral ≠ Referral Progression Event ≠ Referral Outcome Referral Outcome ≠ Responsibility Assumption ≠ Transfer of Care ≠ HealthcareServiceDelivery ≠ ServiceOutcome Referral information semantics ≠ Referral Administration workflow progression ```
Referral Outcome may reference or relate to those Concepts where appropriate; its existence establishes none of them. Recording that a Referral was accepted, progressed or otherwise reached an outcome does not itself prove that care responsibility was actually assumed or transferred. G1 K1's intent/disposition/responsibility/Transfer of Care distinctions remain intact. Outcome is not equated with acceptance.
**Referral Progression Event:** Retained as historical information concerning significant occurrences in the administrative/business progression of a Referral. Not every Event represents a Referral Outcome, and the historical progression record is not collapsed into the final/current Outcome.
**Assurance / governance coverage — RF-IR5:** Harmonia must support assurance that Referrals within the applicable governance scope can be accounted for through sufficient progression and outcome information to establish what became of them. This requirement is applied to established Referral Administration / Manage Referral Progression / Referral Status & Outcome Service responsibility without allocating a new owner, Feature, Service or Collection.
```text Referral population within governance scope → progression/outcome evidence → assurance coverage ```
An inability to establish what became of a Referral is itself an assurance gap. No Referral Outcome is manufactured to make coverage appear complete. Where the outcome is not known, its absence is preserved explicitly.
**Workflow closure / finalisation:** This belongs to the progression of the Business Process / Referral Administration activity, not intrinsic Referral disposition information. The workflow may reach a state in which no further Referral Administration activity is required. This does not require a Referral Finalisation or Referral Closure Information Concept, a terminal state intrinsic to Referral, or Referral Outcome to double as workflow state. No workflow terminal states are defined and the Business Process state machine is not reproduced as the Information Concept lifecycle.
**Authority, temporal meaning and provenance:** Harmonia governs the outcome information for assurance and traceability; it does not infer substantive authority from recording or possessing it. Outcome may require provenance sufficient to establish what outcome was understood, source/originator, authority where relevant, when established/effective, and rationale/qualification where relevant. These are not all universally mandatory attributes. Detailed governance-scope criteria, evidence sufficiency, authority eligibility and contextual provenance/temporal qualification remain unestablished where existing architecture supplies no detail.
**Review history and consequence:** Q01 retains its original B question. The former Referral Disposition candidate proposed an independent Assertion for an attributable decision/reported disposition, with acceptance, decline, redirection and context-specific waitlisting examples. Architectural review rejects that separate Concept and reframes its assurance/governance purpose as Referral Outcome. Recipient-decision meanings and the canonical upstream Referral Disposition Log label are not erased. Q01 is resolved, without answering acceptance's clinical responsibility effects or the precise Referral–delivery/outcome relationships under Q05. Responsibility Assumption Assertion remains a non-authoritative D suggestion.
**Persistence boundary:** Only the Referral family, this review record and the necessary Referral navigation text are reconciled. Q02–Q07 and the complete G2-D01–D03 record remain unchanged. Frozen upstream architecture, Foundation, Package1 and initial historical report/diff are not modified. No other G2 question, G3, later Package2 family, FHIR mapping or downstream representation is commenced. G1 remains CLOSED; G2 is not CLOSED.
Source standing: Explicitly APPROVED G2-D04; no promotion of Referral family/package or independent Referral Disposition.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Rostering
element.documentation:
Clinical Rostering provides the Adjacent context of planned workforce availability. It is distinct from consuming roster projections for operational views or resolving who is currently on call. The present architecture retains the context without establishing a Harmonia Feature decomposition for authoring or managing the authoritative roster.

element.name: [UserStory] Systems can access the data securely
element.documentation:
Independent stakeholder need, expectation or desired outcome:
> As an Integration Administrator, I want the Provider Directory to expose provider data via an API so that systems can access the data securely.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.
### Reconciled source contributions
- `SR-40` — Expose Provider Data via an API; Additional Source Requirements – SR-26 to SR-58; [source](../../../../../openspec/specs/provider-directory-integration/sr-40-expose-provider-data-via-an-api/spec.md).
Source-specific access conditions, supporting actors, alternative outcomes, verification and data-authority rules remain distinct in their cited source contributions. Legacy claims that each statement is a business capability are not adopted: this instance has native Requirement semantics. Source target-state scope is not a software delivery commitment for 1.1.21. Historical assessment findings remain recoverable and do not establish current coverage.

element.name: Petasos
element.documentation: - **Role/responsibility:** **Harmonia's durable message/event queue-management component**, a first-class shared messaging/event capability. Petasos manages creation, operation and operational state/status of its durable queues. [U09](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u09) extends the U05 handoff boundary, preserving AX-10. - **Purpose-defined queues:** purposes include inter-Ergon information flow, defined communication/event sharing, notification/event sharing and other architecturally established Harmonia event-sharing services. Queue purpose is architecturally defined; queues are not arbitrary generic queues. Final taxonomy, names, registration/configuration and topology remain unresolved. - **Features:** queue management and durable Parcel communication/event handling; persistent handoff obligations, bounded backlog, destination mechanics and handoff redelivery/recovery/dead-letter and designated replay responsibilities remain. Detailed delivery/ordering/duplicate/replay/recovery contracts are not newly selected; CDG-16/17/19/34/37/44 retain uncertainty. #### PetasosParcel and information ownership Every Petasos queue carries the single common datatype **PetasosParcel**. It represents the queued Harmonia communication/event and is conceptually analogous to **FHIR Communication**, without established literal equivalence. No schema or mapping to historical PetasosMessage/ErgonEvent is inferred. ```text PetasosParcel pass-by-value; the queued communication/event Referenced Information predominantly pass-by-reference; remains managed by its authoritative component ``` **PetasosParcel is passed by value.** Petasos does not transport only references and does not duplicate all associated information into the Parcel. Petasos owns Parcel messaging/event semantics and queue operations; references confer no ownership of the referenced information. For the **ActionableTask handoff special case**, ActionableTask/Pragma and payload remain managed through Mneme. A Parcel may reference that ActionableTask and is itself queued by value. Petasos does not transport another consumer's FulfillmentTask; each consumer undertaking the ActionableTask establishes its own distinct FulfillmentTask. The established no-payload-copy rule for this case does not make all Parcels reference-only. [Handoff view](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md#persistent-handoff). - **Persistence:** durable queues/Parcels and handoff recovery state are Petasos responsibility; referenced managed-information durable establishment remains Mnemosyne. Queue persistence mechanisms are not selected and queues do not become automatically permanent audit evidence. - **Operational observation:** Petasos owns queue operational state/status. Energeia may **observe/report** relevant state, without acquiring queue management or autonomous queue control. Detailed metrics/state structures remain unresolved. - **Themis collaboration:** for a governed FORWARD action, Petasos is the host/ enforcement location because it controls the queue operation. Applicable enforcement SHALL use **Themis-owned PEP capability** and relevant **PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context**. Themis owns authorisation/enforcement semantics; Petasos owns the operation. Detailed protocol remains unresolved. - **Other collaborations/exclusions:** serves Ergon, ingress, execution, publication, Agora and architecturally established communication/notification services. It is not subordinate to Ponos, ActionableTask-only, a reference transport helper or merely a generic enterprise broker abstraction. Mneme owns Publishing/Subscription/Pattern semantic selection; Ponos owns execution. - **Standing:** U09 resolves queue responsibility and common datatype/pass semantics; [CDG-44](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#petasos-detailed-contracts) retains schema, queue and interaction detail. Internal middleware remains Domain05; external protocols remain Domain06. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md` — ## Persistent handoff without information ownership. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. > **Mneme determines semantic eligibility and eligible recipient/consumer > relationships under Publishing, Subscription and Pattern semantics. Petasos > establishes and manages the concrete persistent handoff obligation to the > destination and reliably effects that handoff. Ponos manages execution.** Eligible consumer relationships express semantic selection. They do not assign queue binding, destination mechanics or concrete handoff state to Mneme. Petasos is Harmonia's durable message/event queue-management component. It creates, operates and owns the operational state/status of **purpose-defined queues** for inter-Ergon flow and other architecturally established communication, notification and event sharing. Every queue carries **PetasosParcel by value**; associated information is predominantly by reference to governed information managed elsewhere. Parcel is conceptually analogous to FHIR Communication; literal equivalence and detailed schema are not established. For the ActionableTask handoff special case, governed ActionableTask/Pragma and Information Unit payload remain managed through Mneme. A by-value Parcel may carry references and communication/handoff metadata required for resolution and recovery. Petasos acquires no management authority over the referenced information and does not copy the managed ActionableTask payload in this pattern. ```text Mneme manages ActionableTask / Pragma and payload --> semantic selection / eligibility Petasos persistently manages handoff obligation --> queues PetasosParcel by value, referring to ActionableTask Consumer resolves governed information through Mneme --> establishes its own distinct FulfillmentTask undertaking Ponos manages execution / progression --> Ergon supplies bounded behaviour within Ergo's contract ``` **Petasos distributes the opportunity to undertake work, not another consumer's FulfillmentTask**, in this pattern. Each consumer undertaking the ActionableTask establishes a distinct FulfillmentTask; no undertaking is transported on its behalf. The Ergo framework works with **Mneme Context Load** to materialise anticipated values before **Context Loader** exposes them to business logic. **Context Unloader** returns changed working values and new Content as **Pragma Output** across that boundary; **Mneme Context Save** manages subsequent consequences. The Unloader is not persistence. Bounded Adhoc Resource Access/Search remains supported; Mnemosyne establishes/reports durable state. [U10/U11 lifecycle](49c9eb2bef0c47b8b5328621d5fc5479.md). Handoff acceptance, information commit, undertaking completion, work resolution and external acknowledgement remain distinct. ActionableTask handoff is one Petasos use case. Communication/Notification Events and other established event-sharing purposes use the common PetasosParcel datatype without becoming ActionableTasks or losing their own semantics. The no-payload-copy rule above SHALL NOT be generalised to reference-only Petasos transport or to copying all referenced information into every Parcel. Final purpose taxonomy, names, Parcel schema and detailed delivery contracts remain [CDG-44](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#petasos-detailed-contracts). Petasos owns queue operational state/status; Energeia may observe/report it, without acquiring queue management or autonomous control. For governed FORWARD, Petasos hosts enforcement because it controls the operation, using **Themis-owned PEP capability and relevant PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context**. Themis owns semantics; Petasos owns the queue operation. Detailed protocols/state metrics remain unresolved. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md` — ## Distinct state and recovery responsibilities. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. | State / concern | Responsibility and boundary | | :--- | :--- | | **Pragma / managed-information state** | Governed information managed through Mneme; authoritative durable establishment/preservation through Mnemosyne. May record a governed observation concerning delivery without owning the handoff obligation. | | **Petasos queue/handoff/delivery state** | Queue operational state/status and operational state of a particular persistent handoff obligation, including delivery attempt, redelivery/recovery and dead-letter handoff semantics. | | **FulfillmentTask undertaking state** | Information representing a particular identifiable undertaking, distinct from ActionableTask and other undertakings. Consumer establishment and Mneme Context/Pragma management do not collapse into runtime execution state. | | **Pylai Diadromí interaction state** | Transient and non-recoverable; loss terminates the interaction and appropriate client retry creates a new Diadromí. Controller keeps no recoverable state. Retained observations/evidence do not restore it or prove earlier effects did not occur. | | **Ponos execution/progression state** | Runtime execution, scheduling/concurrency, execution failure and execution retry/re-attempt or activity progression semantics. | | **Digital Twin input/Behaviour progression** | U19: at most one input at a time; interested Behaviours execute sequentially with the applicable sequence stable for that input. Sequence changes apply to subsequent inputs. ContinueBehaviourOnFailure contains failure to the current execution, leaving the Behaviour active and other interested Behaviours and queue processing unaffected. StopBehaviourOnFailure stops the failing Behaviour immediately, lets remaining interested Behaviours complete the current input, then halts the Twin. StopDigitalTwinOnFailure terminates the failing Behaviour and halts the Twin immediately, preventing remaining current-input and subsequent queued processing. Stopped Twins retain queued inputs pending governed administrative resume; generic retry/redelivery does not automatically resume them. Stopped-Behaviour recovery remains deferred. | Pragma “destination-specific delivery observations” means governed information recording observations concerning delivery. **Operational ownership of the delivery/handoff obligation remains with Petasos.** REC-002 destination granularity is preserved; the exact relationship among Petasos observations, Pragma/checkpoints, Task outputs and parent progression remains unresolved. No observation is silently treated as a completion or TaskOutcome algorithm. Ponos execution retry and Petasos handoff redelivery are different operations. Detailed acknowledgements, retry/recovery, duplicates, replay, ordering and continuation contracts remain unresolved. An uncertain previous effect remains uncertain under AX-15; technical failure alone proves neither success nor non-occurrence. No safe re-attempt algorithm is invented here. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md` — ## Fan-out: established principle and retained detail. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. The supplied Publish/Subscribe DesignNote §§11–13/21 **partially adjudicates** the fan-out question: - A single Pragma may match multiple Subscriptions. The common managed Pragma and payload remain within Mneme; Petasos may manage multiple independent handoff obligations/queue entries carrying PetasosParcels by value, referring to it. Payload duplication is not inherently required. - For ActionableTask processing, each consumer that undertakes the work creates/morphs its **distinct FulfillmentTask**. Selection or handoff alone does not establish an undertaking. This preserves Domain04's [ActionableTask → FulfillmentTask [0..*] distinction](../data-object/topic/30f4deffcd694f07bf54b2b192695d4f.md). Semantic interest fan-out and execution concurrency are orthogonal. Multiple independent **Ergon types** interested in an ActionableTask each receive a separate FulfillmentTask. Separately, **ActionableTask.ExecutionConcurrency** may permit multiple instances of the **same Ergon type** to undertake it concurrently, each through its own FulfillmentTask. This does not change outcome participation or TaskOutcome ownership. Twin input interest matching analogously produces an identifiable **BehaviourStimulus / BehaviourEffector per interested Behaviour**, without establishing inheritance, identical information types or execution through ActionableTask/FulfillmentTask. Interested Behaviours execute sequentially within one Twin; concurrency is across independent Twins. Each loads its Praxis-defined Context fresh after the preceding Behaviour completes/saves. [U19](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u19). **Detailed fan-out identity/lifecycle semantics remain unresolved:** reference, copy and version binding; exact morph/derivation mechanics; Pragma identity for undertaking representations; targetDestination and per-consumer processing state; concurrent processing and mutable-state isolation; lineage/causation; Journey correlation/reconstruction and assurance. No copy-per-subscriber or shared mutable processing-state model follows. Domain04 execution concurrency, outcome participation, output rules and TaskOutcome ownership remain unchanged. [CDG-37](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#pubsub-fanout) retains the remaining question. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F13 | Durable message/event queue creation, operation and status; persistent handoff/backlog/recovery | [Petasos C10](component-register.md#c10), first-class shared messaging/event capability for architecturally defined purposes | Every queue carries PetasosParcel by value; associated information predominantly by reference. ActionableTask Parcel references Mneme-managed work; each undertaking establishes its own FulfillmentTask | U05/U09, AX-10. Inter-Ergon, communication/notification and other established event sharing; no final taxonomy or broker topology. Petasos owns queue state; Energeia observes/reports. Governed FORWARD uses local Themis PEP/PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context. Detail CDG-16/19/34/37/44. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. | F13 | Durable message/event queue creation, operation and status; persistent handoff/backlog/recovery | [Petasos C10](195e5f10db8e419391354197b5d7a8cc.md), first-class shared messaging/event capability for architecturally defined purposes | Every queue carries PetasosParcel by value; associated information predominantly by reference. ActionableTask Parcel references Mneme-managed work; each undertaking establishes its own FulfillmentTask | U05/U09, AX-10. Inter-Ergon, communication/notification and other established event sharing; no final taxonomy or broker topology. Petasos owns queue state; Energeia observes/reports. Governed FORWARD uses local Themis PEP/PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context. Detail CDG-16/19/34/37/44. | ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F14 | Designated deliberate replay | Petasos transition anchor and governed executing activity; Kleio evidence where policy requires | New linked processing attempt; original transition remains unchanged | L13 ADR-015. Replay/redelivery/reprocessing/result redelivery distinct; operational tool terminology CDG-17. |``. Governed observations in Pragma or Task do not own that obligation | U05 preserves REC-002; exact observation relationships, durable recording and parent progression remain CDG-18/34/38.
