element.name: [Topic] Order
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing a formal request for a service, activity or other fulfilment to be performed, including its subject, requester, intent and requested outcome. Harmonia enforces an essential architectural rule regarding clinical requisitions and service delivery: $$\text{Order} \neq \text{Healthcare Service}$$ ```mermaid graph TD ORDER["Order
(Authoritative Requisition / Directive)"] DELIV["DeliverableHealthcareService
(Bound Service Context)"] DELIVERY["HealthcareServiceDelivery
(Information Referring to Service Execution)"] DELIV -.->|"may be requested / directed via"| ORDER ORDER -.->|"requests / directs"| DELIVERY DELIV -->|"fulfilled by"| DELIVERY ``` ### Key Semantics & Invariants 1. **Associated Request Mechanism**: An `Order` is an authoritative clinical requisition, directive, or prescription requesting the delivery of a service. It is **NOT** a mandatory lifecycle stage of `Healthcare Service`. 2. **Delivery Without an Order**: Service delivery may legitimately occur without an `Order` where business or clinical semantics permit (e.g. *Emergency Resuscitation*, *Triage Assessment*, *Direct Routine Nursing Care*, *Scheduled Facility Maintenance*). 3. **Independent Lifecycles**: An `Order` possesses its own lifecycle states (*Requested*, *Accepted*, *In-Progress*, *Completed*, *Discontinued*), owned by `Order Administration`, distinct from the lifecycle of the service delivery itself. Source standing: Established Package1 conceptual information meaning; residual qualifications in selected section remain unchanged. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/order.md` — ### 3.1 Order — A; existing Concept reused. Standing: G2 candidate contribution with only the explicitly recorded decisions approved; semantic classifications and residual questions remain qualified. - **Semantic Classification**: Assertion / Request / Direction. - **Definition**: The independently identifiable clinical requisition, directive or prescription requesting bounded activity/service fulfilment for a stated subject and purpose. - **Necessity**: OR-IR1 requires the requested work to be understood and OR-IR3 requires returned facts to correlate with the same originating Order. Package1 already establishes Order as an associated direction mechanism; this family elaborates its information responsibility rather than creates a duplicate request Concept. - **Boundary**: The Order's directive standing is attributable to its originator/context; ingestion does not certify that every submitted Order is clinically valid. Order does not establish receipt, acceptance, execution or delivery. Requested clinical responsibility for bounded work does not by itself distinguish every assessment Order from Referral; G1 U1 remains. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/order.md` — ## 1. Purpose & Semantic Boundary. Standing: G2 source-qualified boundary and unresolved questions; no whole-family approval. Order Administration needs to understand an attributable request/direction for bounded clinical activity or service fulfilment, determine its destination, coordinate routing, track a closed loop, coordinate requested modification/cancellation and associate returned outcomes. Diagnostic, medication and procedural orders remain in scope; the local diagnostic Process does not delimit the entire family. ```text Order ≠ Referral ≠ HealthcareServiceDelivery ≠ ServiceOutcome Dispatch ≠ receipt ≠ acknowledgement ≠ acceptance Modification/cancellation requested ≠ modification/cancellation effected Order closure / requester acknowledgement ≠ diagnostic-content verification ``` Reuse the [Healthcare Service semantic chain](2a791e0e1f6b45c0a57fb8233f73faa5.md): DeliverableHealthcareService → optional Order → HealthcareServiceDelivery → ServiceOutcome. These arrows distinguish meanings and evidenced associations, not mandatory states of a single lifecycle. Delivery may occur without an Order; an Order may remain unfulfilled. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/order.md` — ## 6. Temporal & Lifecycle Characteristics. Standing: G2 source-qualified boundary and unresolved questions; no whole-family approval. Closed-loop progression requires requested/issued and received time where available, dispatch time, recipient-reported occurrence/disposition time, association time and Harmonia recorded time to be distinguished. Requested timing, imaging scheduled timing and actual execution timing apply only where supplied/evidenced. A cancellation/modification request's time is distinct from an established effect time; a response delay does not determine whether the effect occurred. The local diagnostic/procedural Process preserves signed requisition, specimen/scheduling, preliminary/final result binding and requester acknowledgement/closure requirements. It does not establish a universal signature state, specimen stage or result lifecycle for medication or every Order. Its Order Dispatched compound checkpoint contains routing and recipient acceptance facts; Behaviour Received is not mapped to it without evidence (G1 U8). Foundation's illustrative independent Order states remain guidance, not an exhaustive universal state machine. Order information progression, actual service execution, returned-information lifecycle and Process checkpoint progression remain distinct. Closed / Verified concerns requester acknowledgement and Order closure; it does not establish diagnostic-content verification, approval or incorporation. G1 U2's signing/finality/legal criteria and U5's business-acceptance criteria remain unresolved. Foundation correction/provenance principles apply; the Closed-Loop Tracking Ledger label does not independently establish exhaustive retention policy. No cancellation race-resolution, retry protocol, order-entry workflow or universal completion rule is added. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/order.md` — ## 8. Explicit Boundaries, Unresolved Semantics & Downstream Realisation. Standing: G2 source-qualified boundary and unresolved questions; no whole-family approval. G2-Q07 retains who may request/authorise changes, the meaning of performing-system response and when modification/cancellation takes effect. Candidate assembly boundaries remain G2-Q06. Exact diagnostic authority/finality/legal criteria are consumed only within established local requirements, never resolved by Order Administration. No Order subtype taxonomy, universal healthcare request superclass, order-entry system, clinical verification system or unsupported Service dependency is designed. Order Outcome association has no allocated Feature identity. The assessment Referral/bounded Order semantic boundary remains unresolved rather than merged. No FHIR/resource/profile mapping, Java/application representation, schema, persistence/cache model, API, integration message, topic or implementation allocation is created. [AX-17](../../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) governs all candidate and unestablished derivation links.

element.name: [CT3] Operational Fulfilment Definition
element.documentation:
Define the context requirements, expected outcomes and housekeeping of an operational undertaking.
**Overview**
The semantic execution envelope applies to one-step and multi-step activity and stays distinct from dispatch and supervision.
**Intent**
Keep the semantic promise of an undertaking separate from the machinery that executes it.
**Boundary**
A fulfilment definition does not execute, orchestrate or choreograph its activity.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Risk Mitigation Management
element.documentation:
Manage prospective/preventative measures reducing identified risk likelihood, exposure or consequence.
Clinical Risk Mitigation Management addresses prospective measures intended to reduce an identified risk's likelihood, exposure or consequences. It gives prevention a distinct responsibility alongside risk characterisation and active response. Required measures can involve other capabilities without transferring the ownership of their actions or information to safety management.
**Boundary**
Mitigation differs from containing or remediating a concern that has materialised or requires active intervention.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [0bd3311d89af45bb935fde20e719369c](0bd3311d89af45bb935fde20e719369c.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.

element.name: [CT3] Remote Patient Monitoring
element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Remote & Virtual Care integrates remotely obtained observations and associates virtual consultations with their patient and episode context. It distinguishes a telemetry contribution from the encounter in which a practitioner may interpret it. The enabling responsibility concerns information continuity across delivery modes, preserving the setting-independent meaning of the Business care capabilities.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Telemetry acquisition is not clinical monitoring judgement or treatment; session association does not establish clinical adequacy.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Remote data and virtual-session context materially extend information continuity across care locations and modes.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.documentation:
Administer batch/lot, serial, supplier, manufacturer, receipt/delivery and relevant movement/provenance information concerning health materiel.
**Overview**
Administer batch/lot, serial, supplier, manufacturer, receipt/delivery and relevant movement/provenance information concerning health materiel.
**Intent**
Administer batch/lot, serial, supplier, manufacturer, receipt/delivery and relevant movement/provenance information concerning health materiel.

Materiel traceability does not make Harmonia a procurement, stock-control or supply-chain manager; specimen movement remains Clinical Logistics Coordination.

element.name: [CT3] Closed-Loop Order Progression
element.documentation:
Administer the traceable progression of an order from request through destination, delivery, acknowledgement, fulfilment and outcome association.
**Overview**
Administer the traceable progression of an order from request through destination, delivery, acknowledgement, fulfilment and outcome association. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Administer the traceable progression of an order from request through destination, delivery, acknowledgement, fulfilment and outcome association.
**Boundary**
Information administration and coordination preserve the authority of the responsible source, clinical actor and governed domain; they confer no additional real-world management authority.

element.name: [CT3] Health Service Financial Management
element.documentation:
Establish the service’s fit within funding, financial and charging arrangements without absorbing enterprise finance/accounting.
Health Service Financial Management establishes how the service fits applicable funding, financial and charging arrangements. It connects service viability with its surrounding financial context without attempting to become the enterprise finance function. The responsibility is service-specific alignment rather than the production of all financial transactions associated with care.
**Boundary**
Financial fit does not confer pricing, accounting, billing or enterprise revenue-management authority.

element.name: Assurance Process Reporting / Communication
element.documentation:
• Canonical Name: Assurance Process Reporting / Communication.
• Owning Capability: Governed Assurance (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#governed-assurance).
• Process Purpose: Communicates applicable established Assurance Findings and Conclusions to legitimate recipients according to their responsibilities, authority and information requirements, without altering the established assurance outcome or assuming responsibility for the recipient's subsequent action.
• Starting Basis: An already established Assurance Finding / Conclusion. This Process does not perform assessment or adjudication, alter or reinterpret the established outcome.
• Communication Participation: Service Guardian participates through Service Assurance Outcome Communication (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md#service-assurance-outcome-communication), associated with Communicate Service Assurance Outcome (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#communicate-service-assurance-outcome). No additional Function is introduced to populate this Process.
• Boundary: Reporting / Communication is not limited to documentary report production; an appropriate Business Interaction may communicate the outcome without a report document. It assumes no operational response, remediation, escalation, policy/compliance response, process improvement, clinical management, clinical judgement or other recipient action. Detailed communication progression and completion semantics remain unresolved.
---
## History
### Process Overview — predecessor explanation
This Process starts from an established finding and communicates it to legitimate recipients without altering the outcome. Communication need not create a report document, and it does not repeat assessment or adjudication. Recipients retain authority and responsibility for any clinical, operational, policy or improvement action they take in response.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md` — entry lines 389-396. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.

This Process does not perform assessment or adjudication, alter or reinterpret the established outcome. - **Communication Participation**: Service Guardian participates through [Service Assurance Outcome Communication](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md#service-assurance-outcome-communication), associated with [Communicate Service Assurance Outcome](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#communicate-service-assurance-outcome). No additional Function is introduced to populate this Process. - **Boundary**: Reporting / Communication is not limited to documentary report production; an appropriate Business Interaction may communicate the outcome without a report document. It assumes no operational response, remediation, escalation, policy/compliance response, process improvement, clinical management, clinical judgement or other recipient action. Detailed communication progression and completion semantics remain unresolved.

\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Assurance Process Reporting / Communication}}.



\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#governed-assurance}{Governed Assurance}.



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Communicates applicable established Assurance Findings and Conclusions to legitimate recipients according to their responsibilities, authority and information requirements, without altering the established assurance outcome or assuming responsibility for the recipient's subsequent action.



\item 
\textbf{Starting Basis}: An already established Assurance Finding /\allowbreak{} Conclusion. This Process does not perform assessment or adjudication, alter or reinterpret the established outcome.



\item 
\textbf{Communication Participation}: Service Guardian participates through \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md\#service-assurance-outcome-communication}{Service Assurance Outcome Communication}, associated with \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#communicate-service-assurance-outcome}{Communicate Service Assurance Outcome}. No additional Function is introduced to populate this Process.



\item 
\textbf{Boundary}: Reporting /\allowbreak{} Communication is not limited to documentary report production; an appropriate Business Interaction may communicate the outcome without a report document. It assumes no operational response, remediation, escalation, policy/\allowbreak{}compliance response, process improvement, clinical management, clinical judgement or other recipient action. Detailed communication progression and completion semantics remain unresolved.



\end{itemize}

element.documentation:
Track surgical case state transitions (CALLED → IN_THEATRE → ANAESTHETISED → INCISION → CLOSED → RECOVERY).

element.name: [CT3] Operational Care Capacity Management
element.documentation:
Understand and manage the service’s usable capacity to accommodate care in its current operational context.
Operational Care Capacity Management establishes and manages the service's usable ability to accommodate care under current conditions. It considers capacity as a service-level concern rather than a simple count of staff, devices or vacant beds. This supports decisions grounded in what can actually be accommodated, while keeping current capacity distinct from plans for future provision.
**Boundary**
Resource availability, strategic capacity requirements and collective service readiness are distinct; the latter's placement remains unresolved.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B07.03.02`; additional scope correspondences: . Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Calliope-Models
element.documentation:
### Accepted common Outcome model ownership — 1.1.23/001
Calliope owns the generic Harmonia Outcome model and its common closed Status/Reason semantics, including governed closed domain-specific Reason extensions. Calliope model ownership remains the default across Harmonia; operation execution does not confer ownership of the models used. The logical Outcome DataObject defines exact Success/Failure/Indeterminate status semantics without inventing Reason members, Java types, a runtime data store or physical packaging. Models and mutable governed DataSets retain their accepted separate responsibilities.
### Accepted Information Unit Framework incorporation — 1.1.22
Calliope-Models defines the shared [logical InformationUnit](../data-object/class/74ec609de1ae498fbf9d13e4ef8c6cbe.md) and common Topic/TopicMask semantics. Definition responsibility does not confer runtime information ownership, matching execution, Themis policy evaluation or persistence management. The IU's metadata and representation structures are logical DataObjects, not inferred Java Classes or new build/dependency/deployment boundaries. Existing Calliope-DataSets runtime responsibilities remain distinct.
Distinct Calliope design/build-time submodule: Models, Metadata Types, Criteria Definitions, Topics, Filter Types/Elements, core element libraries and security/ assurance nomenclature definitions. Design → Code → Build → Test → Release → Deploy. Provides structural access contracts and useful development representations of known runtime DataSets as normal library dependencies; those representations do not establish current membership. Models' pure-library dependency semantics remain. Definition ownership is not runtime operational ownership. [U13 lifecycle and authority](307b3440a507403f8bc214d290bffb6a.md).
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md` — ## Calliope-Models. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
Calliope-Models is the foundational design/build-time library of:
- Models and Metadata Types; - Criteria Definitions and Topic definitions; - Filter Types and Filter Elements; - Core Harmonia Element Libraries; - Security and Assurance nomenclature definitions.
Its governed lifecycle is:
```text Design → Code → Build → Test → Release → Deploy ```
Criteria Definitions, Topics, Filter Types and Filter Elements are **development/build-time definitions**. Runtime uses of these definitions do not make the definitions runtime-mutable DataSets. Models supplies structural contracts consumed by Themis, Mneme, Mnemosyne, Ponos, Petasos, Kleio and other components; physical packaging and distribution remain implementation concerns.
> **Definition ownership does not imply runtime operational ownership.**
| Calliope-Models definition | Runtime use and responsibility | | :--- | :--- | | Criteria Definition | Themis runtime Criteria / PEP-Context; policy association, resolution, compilation and enforcement remain Themis-owned. | | Topic Definition | Metadata on Pragma / Content; Topic is classification, not a queue or destination. | | Filter Type / Filter Element | Runtime Pattern evaluated/matched through Mneme's Publishing/Subscription semantics. |
Calliope SHALL NOT become the runtime executor of the constructs it defines. Mneme retains runtime Pattern management/matching and Themis retains the [Identity/Authorisation Model](899d34ec491948b68aad09e507dea6d1.md). Reusable converter support does not move interface-specific semantic processing out of [developer-defined Ergo.BusinessLogic](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pylai-external-interoperability.md#pylai-pathway-ingress). The remaining general converter/activity allocation questions stay in CDG-05.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F01 | Design/build-time models, Metadata Types, Criteria Definitions, Topics, Filter Types/Elements and core element libraries | [Calliope-Models C41](component-register.md#c41); Themis and Mneme own applicable runtime use | Structural contracts, security/assurance definitions and useful human/IDE/AI development representations of known runtime datasets | U13/U15; normal development/build-time library dependency, Design → Code → Build → Test → Release → Deploy. Build knowledge is not current membership authority; no runtime structural bootstrap. Mechanisms CDG-49. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
| F01 | Design/build-time models, Metadata Types, Criteria Definitions, Topics, Filter Types/Elements and core element libraries | [Calliope-Models C41](307b3440a507403f8bc214d290bffb6a.md); Themis and Mneme own applicable runtime use | Structural contracts, security/assurance definitions and useful human/IDE/AI development representations of known runtime datasets | U13/U15; normal development/build-time library dependency, Design → Code → Build → Test → Release → Deploy. element.name: [Feature] Event-Driven Syndication
element.documentation:
Publish clinical and directory change events to subscribed systems matching interest filters.
Syndication connects published changes with subscribers whose registered interests match them. It differs from named-recipient distribution in how consumers are selected, while retaining governed delivery and the distinction between notification and the subscriber's eventual business action.

element.name: [Feature] Diagnostic Request Correlation
element.documentation:
Correlate diagnostic test orders with collected clinical specimens and patient encounters.
Diagnostic request correlation connects the order with its specimen and encounter context. It helps distinguish evidence belonging to the intended fulfilment from superficially similar results, without treating association as proof of specimen suitability or diagnostic interpretation.

element.documentation:
Resolve local clinical codes against standard terminologies (SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD-10).

element.name: [Topic] TaskFulfillment
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing an identifiable undertaking performed toward completion of a Task, allowing the work performed and its relationship to the originating Task to be represented.
**FulfillmentTask** represents an identifiable undertaking of an `ActionableTask`: doing or attempting to do that particular work. It carries the execution-related information necessary to represent the undertaking, including, where applicable:
- performer / executing actor and execution context; - commencement and timing; - progression and execution state; - completion, failure, suspension or other applicable execution information; and - other execution metadata/scaffolding needed to represent the undertaking.
It has its own execution state and may produce output. It does **not independently own TaskOutcome**. One or more undertakings may contribute to resolution of the parent ActionableTask according to that ActionableTask's explicitly defined outcome policy.
An `ActionableTask` may have **zero, one or multiple `FulfillmentTasks`**. Multiple undertakings MAY execute concurrently where the ActionableTask's `ExecutionConcurrency` permits them. Execution state SHALL NOT be collapsed into `ActionableTask` on the assumption that each work instance has exactly one execution.
Completion of one `FulfillmentTask` does **not inherently establish satisfaction or completion of its parent `ActionableTask`**. Satisfaction depends on the definition and context of the work, with outcome resolution governed by the ActionableTask's explicit outcome policy. No universal execution state machine or satisfaction rule is established here. Information representing an undertaking remains distinct from the undertaking itself.
Source standing: Bounded adjudicated conceptual Task meaning; section 5 reservations, including runtime TaskOutcome identity/lifecycle, remain unresolved.

element.name: [Feature] Standards-Based Boundary Exchange
element.documentation:
Provide standards-conformant boundary exchange for healthcare messaging and resource representations.
---
## History
### Feature Overview — predecessor explanation
Boundary exchange preserves the standards contract understood by the external participant. Harmonia's internal management metadata must not leak into that contract, and publication must construct an allowed external representation without destructively changing the internally managed information.

element.name: Clinic / Operational Queue Progression Process
element.documentation:
• Owning Capability: Clinic & Practice Operations
• Process Purpose: Governs the movement and state tracking of outpatients through an ambulatory specialty clinic session.
• State Progression Lifecycle: Scheduled → Patient Arrived → Checked-In → Roomed / Pre-Consult → Consultation In-Progress → Consultation Concluded → Departed
• Key State Dispositions:
• Scheduled: Appointment booked on session list.
• Patient Arrived: Patient enters waiting area.
• Checked-In: Reception verifies demographics and marks patient ready.
• Roomed / Pre-Consult: Nursing staff record baseline vitals and room patient.
• Consultation In-Progress: Clinician actively conducting consultation.
• Consultation Concluded: Clinical discussion finished; follow-up orders placed.
• Departed: Patient checks out and departs clinic facility.
This Process follows an individual's operational passage through the clinic. Waiting, rooming, consultation and departure have different implications for flow and communication, while the clinic's overall session has its own state. The progression is therefore patient-specific operational context rather than a complete account of clinic capacity or clinical priority.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md` — entry lines 187-201. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.

element.name: Healthcare Delivery Organizations
element.documentation:
### Profile & Role Healthcare Delivery Organizations (HDOs) encompass the institutional entities providing clinical care across the region: acute public hospitals, private hospital networks, primary health clinics, specialist outpatient centers, and diagnostic pathology and medical imaging facilities.
### Core Responsibilities - Providing direct patient care across emergency, inpatient, ambulatory, and diagnostic settings. - Generating, maintaining, and ingesting operational clinical transactions (admissions, transfers, discharges, orders, results, clinical notes) through local hospital information systems (HIS), patient administration systems (PAS), and laboratory information systems (LIS). - Maintaining local boundary integration gateways and adhering to regional messaging protocols.
### Principal Architectural Concerns - **Reliable Ingress & Egress Integration**: Guaranteeing that clinical messages dispatched to Harmonia are reliably accepted and preserved without silent loss or unhandled dropouts. - **Low Latency & High Throughput**: Fast turnaround times for critical pathology results, radiology reports, and patient admission feeds without queuing delays. - **Standards-Compliant Boundary Interoperability**: Seamless support for legacy messaging standards (HL7 v2.x via MLLP) alongside modern FHIR RESTful interactions, avoiding disruptive upgrades to legacy hospital software. - **Clear Demarcation of Responsibility**: Explicit integration boundaries defining where the delivery organization's operational responsibility ends and Harmonia's management begins.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Device Administration
element.documentation:
Clinical Device Administration represents device types, identifiable instances, patient or location associations and communication endpoints. This lets device-originated information be interpreted in relation to the actual device and care context, rather than merely a network address. Type, instance, assignment and connectivity each answer a different question about the source of device data.
**Overview**
Clinical Device Administration represents device types, identifiable instances, patient or location associations and communication endpoints. This lets device-originated information be interpreted in relation to the actual device and care context, rather than merely a network address. Type, instance, assignment and connectivity each answer a different question about the source of device data.
**Intent**
Clinical Device Administration represents device types, identifiable instances, patient or location associations and communication endpoints. This lets device-originated information be interpreted in relation to the actual device and care context, rather than merely a network address. Type, instance, assignment and connectivity each answer a different question about the source of device data.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Device registration is not maintenance, release management or clinical interpretation. An endpoint credential does not by itself authorise clinical use of the device.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [UserStory] Newly created patient identities can be synchronised with connected systems
element.documentation:

> Receive new patient registration events so that newly created patient identities can be synchronised with connected systems.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.

element.name: [CT1] Trust, Accountability & Assurance
element.documentation:
Make governed activity permissible, attributable, operationally dependable and independently assessable.
**Overview**
Policy, evidence, resilience and independent assurance contribute to confidence through different responsibilities. Keeping them as peers prevents technical success or recorded evidence from becoming a business assurance conclusion.
**Intent**
Keep permission, attribution, operational integrity and independent confidence distinguishable and usable together.
**Boundary**
Cross-cutting participation does not distribute semantic ownership, mandate centralisation or authorise the assured subject to determine its own conclusion.
## Capability model replacement history

Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [Feature] Work Item Instantiation
element.documentation:
Instantiate operational units of work from clinical triggers (e.g., bed cleaning required, specimen transport required).
Work-item instantiation gives an authorised operational requirement an identifiable unit of work. It distinguishes recognising that support activity is needed from assigning it, dispatching it and recording its completion; a clinical trigger does not make the resulting support item clinical work authority.

element.name: [CT3] Ward Logistics Coordination
element.documentation:
Coordinate ward patient flow, handover context and ward-specific operational logistics and capacity information.
**Overview**
Coordinate ward patient flow, handover context and ward-specific operational logistics and capacity information. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Coordinate ward patient flow, handover context and ward-specific operational logistics and capacity information.

element.name: [Feature] Procedural Documentation Ingestion
element.documentation:
Ingest operative reports, anesthesia records, and post-procedure summaries.
Procedural documentation ingestion preserves the operative, anaesthetic and post-procedure account supplied by the clinical service. It connects performed-care documentation with the wider record without giving the integration process authority to originate or judge the clinical findings.

element.name: Practitioner Verification Process
element.documentation:
• Owning Capability: Provider Administration
• Process Purpose: Governs the lifecycle of validating, certifying, and periodically re-verifying a healthcare practitioner's professional credentials, registration status, and clinical scope of practice.
• State Progression Lifecycle: Verification Initiated → Regulatory Registry Queried → Credentials Validated → Privileges Endorsed → Active Verified → Expired / Suspended
• Key State Dispositions:
• Verification Initiated: New practitioner registration or periodic re-credentialing triggered.
• Regulatory Registry Queried: Real-time query executed against national registry (e.g., AHPRA).
• Credentials Validated: Primary qualifications, specialist endorsements, and sanctions checked.
• Privileges Endorsed: Health service medical administration endorses admitting/procedural scope.
• Active Verified: Practitioner verified for clinical ordering and electronic communication.
• Expired / Suspended: Verification lapses or regulatory sanction triggers privilege suspension.
Verification progresses from checking the recognised professional source to the locally applicable endorsement and continuing verification status. The distinction matters because a nationally identifiable practitioner is not automatically privileged for every service activity. The illustrated progression retains the health service's endorsement responsibility rather than letting directory ingestion grant clinical authority.
## Source-qualified contribution

element.name: Unmonitored Destination Failure / Fan-Out Divergence
element.documentation:
### Assessment Summary Broadcasting clinical events across multiple downstream destination systems without tracking granular, per-destination delivery status leads to silent divergence between destination systems and fractured clinical state.
### Operational Hazard A single clinical event often requires distribution to multiple disparate destinations (fan-out). For example, an HL7 `ADT^A08` (Update Patient Information) or `ADT^A02` (Transfer Patient) may need to update: 1. The regional clinical data repository. 2. The local pharmacy dispensing system. 3. The radiology information system (RIS). 4. The hospital billing and claims engine. 5. An external primary health network notifications feed.
If the integration platform considers the parent activity "completed" merely because the message was posted to an internal dispatch mechanism, failures at individual destination endpoints go unmonitored: - The clinical repository is updated, but the pharmacy feed times out. - The parent workflow reports success. - The pharmacy continues operating on obsolete patient medication allergy data. - Systemic clinical state diverges silently across the healthcare network.
### Architectural Implication & Response - Operational workflows must track explicit progression state per destination. - Parent activities must maintain fine-grained sub-status across the entire fan-out lifecycle until every individual destination delivery is deterministically confirmed or explicitly flagged as failed/indeterminate. - **Related Driver**: [Coordinated Operational Activity and Entity State](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/drivers.md) - **Target Goal**: [Coordinated Progression of Operational Activities & Associated Entity State](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) - **Governing Axiom**: [AX-16 (Operational Activity & Entity State Progress Together)](../principle/de7e90f46127455a9ec9ad3b9b48ba54.md) - **Foundational Requirement**: [`REQ-FND-002` Operational Activity Progression State](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/requirements-constraints/foundational-requirements.md)

element.name: Harmonia.Omilia.Client
element.documentation:
- **Role/responsibility:** Harmonia collaboration client providing the associated collaboration user experience; communicates with Omilia.Server using Matrix protocol. Presentation does not confer information or collaboration-control authority. - **Provenance/standing:** derived from Element; U16 adjudicated candidate. Detailed modifications and human-experience integration remain deferred; Iris has no direct Agora/Omilia interaction (U19).
## ARB DesignNote assertion contributions
These bounded source assertions are reconciled under the cited U-decisions and ARB release Praxis. They retain the source's candidate, scope and detailed-design qualifications. They do not accept the whole Domain05 candidate or create a new element per paragraph. Later-corrected assertions are retained in the disposition evidence instead of being restored here.
### DesignNote-Agora-Controlled-Collaboration-and-Omilia-Realisation — original lines 133-134
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Agora-Controlled-Collaboration-and-Omilia-Realisation.md`; U16/U17/U19; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
Omilia.Client is the Harmonia-specific collaboration client derived from Element.
### DesignNote-Agora-Controlled-Collaboration-and-Omilia-Realisation — original lines 136-137
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Agora-Controlled-Collaboration-and-Omilia-Realisation.md`; U16/U17/U19; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
It provides the collaboration user experience associated with the Omilia collaboration environment.
### DesignNote-Agora-Controlled-Collaboration-and-Omilia-Realisation — original lines 139-146
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Agora-Controlled-Collaboration-and-Omilia-Realisation.md`; U16/U17/U19; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
[U19](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u19) establishes that **Iris does not directly interact with Agora or Omilia**. Detailed Omilia.Client responsibilities and human-experience integration remain later design matters within that boundary. Administrative intent through Omilia → Agora proceeds to an Administrative Function implemented by specialised Administrative Ergon; Iris uses its separate Iris-BackEnd path. Neither presentation/collaboration channel directly resumes or manipulates a Digital Twin. Normal authorisation, Context, execution, Petasos handoff and Kleio audit controls apply; this adds no direct Agora-to-Ponos dependency.

element.name: [ArchitecturalAxiom] Three-Generation Release Compatibility
element.documentation:
Harmonia release N shall support concurrent operation with either release N−1 or release N+1 against the same governed information environment.Three-generation compatibility window N−1/N/N+1; N runs concurrently with either N+1 or N−1, not necessarily all three. General-purpose rollback and reversible database migration not required.
Source entry: **NFR-132 — Three-Generation Release Compatibility**. Primary subject: `G10.05`.
The source classification is Principle «ArchitecturalAxiom». The source identifier is a scoped register reference and does not determine architectural type. Applicability, release scope and unresolved thresholds remain as stated above.

element.name: [UseCase] Maintain Provider Directory Reference Data
element.documentation:
Recognisable interaction: **Maintain Provider Directory Reference Data**.
The interaction is directed towards the source purpose: Enable the Provider Directory to maintain controlled reference data used by Provider Directory processes. This supports the target-state objective that uc-13 is implemented as a governed business capability rather than as an isolated technical function. The intended outcome is that provider information is captured and interpreted consistently using governed reference values.
Source primary actor: Provider Directory Administrator
The interaction retains its source context and conditions. It is not a Journey, Capability or claim of implementation satisfaction.

element.name: [ArchitecturalAxiom] Information Residency Governance

Source entry: **NFR-155 — Information Residency Governance**. Primary subject: `G02.05`.
The source classification is Principle «ArchitecturalAxiom». The source identifier is a scoped register reference and does not determine architectural type. Applicability, release scope and unresolved thresholds remain as stated above.

element.name: [Feature] Activity Outcome & Continuation Rules
element.documentation:
Define how output roles, expected outcomes and continuation conditions are interpreted for an undertaking.
**Overview**
An output may contribute to completion, subsequent activity or retained evidence under different rules. Those meanings need to be specified rather than inferred from a returned payload.
**Boundary**
Completion policy is not business outcome truth; uncertain effects remain explicit.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E06.01.04`; additional scope correspondences: `E06.02.01`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Dokimasia Ergon
element.documentation:
- **Role/features:** discrete Ergon specialisation representing a bounded assurance activity executed within a Dokimasia workflow. Reuses normal Ergo/Ergon execution, Context Loading/Unloading, process-management, integration, checkpoint, logging/observability and reporting contracts. [U02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u02). - **Information/persistence/collaboration:** uses governed assurance input, applicable basis and evidence, and may produce assurance information through Mneme Pragma Management. No detailed schema, evidence-access API, storage or additional Information Resource is inferred. Executed through Dokimasia's specialised Ponos model. - **Standing/exclusions:** discrete candidate component responsibility established; subject to [Dokimasia terminal constraints](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#dokimasia-terminal-boundaries). AI Assurance Ergon C27 specialises this component. Other potential assurance classifications, including deterministic/human subclasses, require adjudication.

element.name: [Feature] Pathology Specimen Transport Tracking
element.documentation:
Track pickup, custody chain, transport conditions, and laboratory delivery of clinical specimens.
Specimen transport tracking retains pickup, custody and condition context through laboratory delivery. It supports interpretation of the material's journey without treating a delivered package as proof of specimen suitability, completed analysis or an authorised diagnostic report.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B09.05.03.F02`; additional scope correspondences: . Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [UserStory] Authorised systems can retrieve current provider information using a reusable machine-to-machine interface
element.documentation:

> As the Provider Directory, I need to make provider information available through a governed API, so that authorised systems can retrieve current provider information using a reusable machine-to-machine interface.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.
### Reconciled source contributions
- `UC-9` — Supply Care Provider Details via an API; Additional Source Use Cases and System Requirements; [source](../../../../../openspec/specs/provider-directory-integration/uc-9-supply-care-provider-details-via-an-api/spec.md).
Source-specific access conditions, supporting actors, alternative outcomes, verification and data-authority rules remain distinct in their cited source contributions. Legacy claims that each statement is a business capability are not adopted: this instance has native Requirement semantics. Source target-state scope is not a software delivery commitment for 1.1.21. Historical assessment findings remain recoverable and do not establish current coverage.

Its earlier authored name above is retained as provenance; current names follow the explicit properties in the 1.1.19 submission. That earlier incoming record has no Documentation or authored Properties; no normative definition, native statement, classification of individual statements, or additional responsibility is invented to complete that absence.
The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. These are distinct assertions. Neither diagram membership nor the Grouping's label alone establishes another Home or a statement allocation. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.

element.documentation:
First-class observational construct / candidate Application Data Object: governed observed progression reconstructed from available execution evidence, whether Pathway-controlled, Pub/Sub or mixed. It may be graph-shaped and have no Pathway. Primary reporting, analysis and assurance subject; Dokimasia may interpret it under applicable basis without replacing observations with inference. **Energeia owns Journey and Journey Management Services F38** under U06. Mneme manages governed information; Mnemosyne **O&A** provides durable persistence responsibility. Journey aggregates/references observations/information from Mneme, Petasos, Ponos, Ergon, DigitalTwin and other components/evidence mechanisms where appropriate, retaining their ownership. Comparatively small discrete Journey information may describe substantial activity/evidence: aggregate semantically, without indiscriminate duplication. Detailed representation/construction, lifecycle, retention, graph/evidence/causal/correlation/reference schema and inference contracts remain unresolved ([CDG-38](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#journey-contracts)); Journey is not a shard key. Journey is neither an engine, AI narrative nor automatic permanent AuditEvent. For Pathway-based Praxis fulfilment, continuation-Pragma lineage provides an important observable progression thread. **Journey lineage is not complete Pragma provenance**: independent outputs may establish their own activity, Pub/Sub interactions, Praxes and Journeys. Mneme may manage richer relationships. Journey is not a complete provenance graph, execution log, audit trail or Petasos queue history. [U18 reconciliation](359b901df27f4b43b5a2ff14a8484e34.md).
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md` — ## Journey: common observation and assurance subject. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
> **Journey is the governed representation of meaningful observed progression > of information and activity in fulfilment of a Praxis, reconstructed from > available execution evidence and forming the primary subject of reporting, analysis and > assurance, irrespective of whether that progression arose through > Pathway-controlled routing, Publish/Subscribe processing, or a combination > of both.**
Journey C35 is a first-class observational construct / candidate Application Data Object, not an execution engine or merely a telemetry report. A Journey may exist without a corresponding Pathway and may be graph-shaped because observed progression can branch, fan out, converge or combine mechanisms. Pathway controls permitted progression; Journey represents observed progression.
For a Praxis with a Pathway, Journey observes meaningful fulfilment against that Pathway. **Pathway-continuation Pragma lineage is an important observable thread; Journey lineage is not complete Pragma provenance.** Independently resulting Pragma may establish their own activity, Pub/Sub interactions, Praxes and Journeys. Common origin does not automatically include all that subsequent processing in the originating Journey. Mneme may manage richer Pragma relationships/provenance than that Journey represents. Journey remains neither a complete graph of information provenance, execution log, audit trail nor Petasos queue history. Detailed correlation remains open; graph-shaped observation does not imply complete provenance.
**Energeia owns Journey as an application responsibility** and SHALL provide candidate **Journey Management Services**. These manage the governed representation of observed progression and its semantic aggregation/references, supporting operational reporting and assurance consumption. The detailed service and construction contracts remain unresolved. Mneme remains the **Context and Pragma Manager**; Mnemosyne **Harmonia Operations & Assurance** provides durable persistence responsibility. Application ownership does not make Energeia a persistence owner or owner of all referenced information.
Journey is expected to hold comparatively little discrete information while aggregating/referencing potentially substantial distributed activity/evidence. **Aggregate semantically; do not duplicate governed information indiscriminately.** Efficient Journey reconstruction/use is an architectural objective, not a graph schema, correlation/causal algorithm, retention period or shard-key decision.
```mermaid flowchart LR Praxis["Praxis: fulfilment / Context definitions / continuation semantics / assurance"] -->|Aggregation: 0..1| Path["Pathway / Route: conceptual Ergo sequence / defined control"] Path --> Exec["Ponos / Ergon: execution"] Pub["Publishing / Subscription: dynamic selection through Mneme"] --> Exec Exec -->|governed execution observations| Journey["Journey: observed progression"] Mneme["Mneme: selection observations"] --> Journey Petasos["Petasos: handoff observations"] --> Journey Twin["DigitalTwin and other governed contributors"] -->|operational observations / evidence references| Journey Energeia["Energeia"] -->|application management: Journey Management Services| Journey Energeia -->|application management: Praxis Management Services| Praxis Praxis -.->|Aggregation: cardinality unresolved| Journey Journey --> Reporting["Energeia R1.x/R2.x: Observe → Report"] Journey -->|observed evidence subject| Assurance["Dokimasia: governed interpretation"] Praxis -->|assurance basis; Pathway may contribute expectations| Assurance Assurance --> Finding["Assurance finding / result"] ```
Labelled arrows distinguish application management, Aggregation and evidence contribution/use. Detailed Journey representation/construction, reference/evidence schema, causal/correlation/reconstruction algorithms and lifecycle/retention remain [CDG-38](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#journey-contracts); Energeia ownership is resolved by U06.
| Contributing responsibility | Examples of available governed observations | | :--- | :--- | | **Mneme** | Publishing permitted/blocked; Subscription matched; Pattern condition matched; eligible consumer selected. | | **Petasos** | Handoff established; destination identified; delivery attempted; delivery succeeded/failed or uncertain; redelivery/recovery observations. | | **Consumer / Ponos / Ergon** | Undertaking established; execution attempted/occurred; activity result; checkpoint and progression observations. | | **Pylai** | Applicable successful logical business interaction or technology/interoperability failure within the governed Journey; no universal Journey, fabricated Praxis or per-network-event AuditEvent requirement. | | **DigitalTwin / other components / assurance-evidence mechanisms** | Governed operational observations or references where appropriate, preserving originating responsibility and Dokimasia terminal rules. |
These contributions can distinguish selection without handoff, handoff without observed execution, and execution with failure or unexpected results. An absent observation does not prove non-occurrence. Available evidence bounds the Journey; missing or uncertain evidence remains distinguishable from established fact.
Reporting, analysis and Dokimasia assurance SHALL be capable of operating against Journey. **Praxis is the assurance basis; Journey is the evidence subject.** A Pathway/Route may contribute normative expectations as part of the applicable Praxis; Pathway alone is not the general assurance basis. Possible interpretation includes progression, branching and convergence, conformance to applicable Praxis expectations, missing or unexpected activity, failure/incomplete progression, information exposure, policy/security anomalies, relationships between apparently separate activities and significance in context. These are possible uses, not mandatory algorithms. Praxis provides the operational and assurance envelope even where activity uses Publish/Subscribe without a Pathway.
```text Praxis: expected / permitted context Journey: observed progression assurance rules evidence \ / +------------+----------------+ v Dokimasia v Assurance Finding / Result ```
```text What Harmonia observed --> Journey --> what Harmonia can reason from those observations --> Dokimasia / governed AI Assurance activity --> what Harmonia concludes: Assurance Finding / Result ```
Journey is factual with respect to available governed observations/evidence. Inferred relationships SHALL remain distinguishable from directly observed relationships. Deterministic or AI interpretation cannot replace underlying observations with inferred fact or turn Journey into an AI-generated narrative. The inference/evidence representation and detailed Journey model are unresolved. Evidence contribution, operational observation, AuditEvent and assurance finding remain distinct; not every Journey observation becomes a permanent AuditEvent (AX-08/09). Dokimasia's [terminal constraints](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#dokimasia-terminal-boundaries) and operational independence remain intact.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md` — ## Journey and authoritative Audit Capture. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
Journey represents governed observed activity/progression; AuditEvent represents an authoritative significant auditable occurrence. Journey is an important audit source, **not the audit boundary**. A Journey may relate to many AuditEvents and an AuditEvent may exist without Journey participation. **Journey participation SHALL NOT be a prerequisite for Audit Capture.**
Kleio may consume Journey and Dokimasia outputs and provide historical audit context back to Dokimasia. Audit is neither Governance nor Assurance; derived/ correlated/prepared historical views remain distinguishable from authoritative evidence. Dokimasia's terminal rules continue to prohibit a separate own-execution AuditEvent and recursive assurance; output consumption does not introduce either.
Client components report significant occurrences through Kleio's contract; Kleio constructs immutable FHIR AuditEvent. Required authoritative durable audit capture is a precondition of Harmonia operation, independent of Journey availability or later reconstruction. [Kleio's history/availability rules](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#auditability-and-availability) and O&A independent-target/harmonisation-SEP release boundary apply.
U15 establishes [Kleio-specific mandatory capture authority](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#kleio-capture-authority) under Harmonia security policy. The audited Identity remains evidence, not the authority persisting its mandatory AuditEvent; its PEP-Criteria is not borrowed. Insufficient capture authority fails the governed operation closed. This supplies no equivalent intrinsic authority to Journey, Energeia or other components.

## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Pragma-Outputs-and-Pathway-Continuation.md` — ## 5. Journey consequence. Standing: Architecturally adjudicated U18; candidate scope and representation deferrals retained.
Journey represents meaningful observed progression in fulfilment of a Praxis against its Pathway. The lineage of Pathway-continuation Pragma therefore provides an important observable thread for Journey progression.
**Journey lineage is not equivalent to complete Pragma provenance.** Independent Pragma created from the same Ergon outputs may establish their own subsequent activity, Pub/Sub interactions, Praxes and Journeys. Their common origin alone does not make all subsequent activity progression of the originating Praxis.
Mneme may manage richer Pragma relationships and provenance than the Journey associated with the originating Praxis represents. This does not transfer Journey management from Energeia or authoritative audit responsibility from Kleio. Journey may reference relevant governed observations without becoming a complete information-provenance graph, execution log, audit trail or Petasos queue history. Existing Pub/Sub-only and mixed, potentially graph-shaped Journeys remain valid; this note does not require every Journey to have a Pathway or prescribe correlation or reconstruction algorithms.

Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Pragma-Outputs-and-Pathway-Continuation.md`; U18; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
Journey represents meaningful observed progression in fulfilment of a Praxis against its Pathway. The lineage of Pathway-continuation Pragma therefore provides an important observable thread for Journey progression.
### DesignNote-Pragma-Outputs-and-Pathway-Continuation — original lines 116-119
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Pragma-Outputs-and-Pathway-Continuation.md`; U18; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
**Journey lineage is not equivalent to complete Pragma provenance.** Independent Pragma created from the same Ergon outputs may establish their own subsequent activity, Pub/Sub interactions, Praxes and Journeys. Their common origin alone does not make all subsequent activity progression of the originating Praxis.
### DesignNote-Pragma-Outputs-and-Pathway-Continuation — original lines 121-128
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Pragma-Outputs-and-Pathway-Continuation.md`; U18; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
Mneme may manage richer Pragma relationships and provenance than the Journey associated with the originating Praxis represents. This does not transfer Journey management from Energeia or authoritative audit responsibility from Kleio. Journey may reference relevant governed observations without becoming a complete information-provenance graph, execution log, audit trail or Petasos queue history. Existing Pub/Sub-only and mixed, potentially graph-shaped Journeys remain valid; this note does not require every Journey to have a Pathway or prescribe correlation or reconstruction algorithms.
### DesignNote-Pylai-External-Interoperability-Architecture — original lines 262-262
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Pylai-External-Interoperability-Architecture.md`; U14/U15; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
**Journey:** records architecturally meaningful observed progression. At the Pylai boundary it may report successful business transaction progression at the applicable logical boundary, or a technology failure that prevented progression. Journey is factual observation, not AI interpretation.
### DesignNote-Pylai-External-Interoperability-Architecture — original lines 264-264
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Pylai-External-Interoperability-Architecture.md`; U14/U15; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
**Audit:** every architecturally meaningful interoperability **transaction** is auditable. This does not mean every low-level network or Camel activity becomes an AuditEvent. Pylai identifies/reports the auditable transaction; Kleio constructs and manages the authoritative AuditEvent.
### DesignNote-Pylai-External-Interoperability-Architecture — original lines 266-266
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Pylai-External-Interoperability-Architecture.md`; U14/U15; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
**Technical failures:** detailed Pylai communication failures and diagnostics are principally IT/Operations concerns. They may nevertheless provide evidence relevant to Dokimasia assurance activity.

element.name: [CT2] Scheduling Administration
element.documentation:
Scheduling Administration integrates appointment information established by departmental scheduling systems. It receives scheduled events and propagates cancellation, rescheduling and attendance changes so that care-coordination contexts do not diverge. Its concern is the coherence of scheduling information across participants rather than originating every booking decision.
**Overview**
Scheduling Administration integrates appointment information established by departmental scheduling systems. It receives scheduled events and propagates cancellation, rescheduling and attendance changes so that care-coordination contexts do not diverge. Its concern is the coherence of scheduling information across participants rather than originating every booking decision.
**Intent**
Scheduling Administration integrates appointment information established by departmental scheduling systems. It receives scheduled events and propagates cancellation, rescheduling and attendance changes so that care-coordination contexts do not diverge. Its concern is the coherence of scheduling information across participants rather than originating every booking decision.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
A synchronised booking does not prove attendance, service capacity or delivered clinical care.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Timely appointment changes materially support coordination across systems without giving Harmonia the scheduler's clinical or departmental authority.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/02-service-administration.md` — entry lines 48-48. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.
- **Owning Capability**: `Scheduling Administration`
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [1a6630940ffb44fcad4543b93a367b67](1a6630940ffb44fcad4543b93a367b67.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.
## ARB source correspondence
Scope/anti-responsibility and clinical/operational meaning establish the responsible Capability; descriptive ledger/registry/asset labels do not establish a separately bounded formal Information Concept. Preserve non-transfer and source authority.
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/information-responsibility/information-responsibility.md` — information responsibility row 12. Standing: Established Business responsibility only; formal information identity/lifecycle not inferred.
```text | **Scheduling Administration** | **Appointment Synchronisation State** | Ingested appointment booking milestones, schedule change events, and consolidated patient appointment timeline caches. | Does not own host PAS booking engines or master clinic slots. | ```
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B07.03.03`; additional scope correspondences: `B07.03.04`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Knowledge Concept Association
element.documentation:
Associate knowledge with applicable governed clinical concepts without acquiring concept authority.
Clinical Knowledge Concept Association relates reusable knowledge to the governed clinical concepts relevant to its meaning. It makes the semantic context of the knowledge intelligible without allowing local association to redefine the referenced concepts. The association assists interpretation while preserving the distinction between knowledge authority and concept authority.
**Boundary**
Associating knowledge with a terminology concept does not acquire terminology governance or establish approval of the knowledge.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Workforce Capability Monitoring
element.documentation:
Monitor supplied information about the clinical capability available from the workforce without acquiring employment or clinical allocation authority.
**Overview**
Monitor supplied information about the clinical capability available from the workforce without acquiring employment or clinical allocation authority.
**Intent**
Monitor supplied information about the clinical capability available from the workforce without acquiring employment or clinical allocation authority.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Clinical Workforce Management is retained as an Adjacent operational context for the workforce on which services depend. The current enabling catalogue does not assign an atomic Feature set. Its presence allows workforce constraints to be recognised without treating integration of workforce facts as authority to govern employment, coverage or clinical allocation.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
No new workforce system responsibility or complete CT ancestry is inferred from this contextual entry.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Adjacent standing reflects contextual participation rather than management of the workforce itself.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [24c015676c254e2e82e8e4287c295179](24c015676c254e2e82e8e4287c295179.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.

Primary replacement catalogue identity `B08.02`; additional scope correspondences: `B08.04`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Harmonia.Omilia.Server
element.documentation:
- **Role/responsibility:** owns/performs underlying Room/Space, user, membership, dialogue/message, collaboration-event and applicable collaboration-media operations. Exposes the **Application Services API** for Agora operation requests and dialogue/activity delivery from Agora-managed Rooms/Spaces. - **Boundary:** operational worker, not owner of Harmonia collaboration semantics, membership intent or originating clinical/operational information. Agora owns native collaboration information; AX-05 durable-state responsibility remains. - **Provenance/standing:** derived from Matrix Synapse; U16 adjudicated candidate. API technology, modifications and persistence mechanics are deferred, not inferred from historical Synapse deployment/configuration.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/agora-omilia-collaboration.md` — ## Application Services API. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
Omilia.Server exposes an **Application Services API** used by Agora both to request collaboration operations and to receive managed-Room dialogue/activity.
```mermaid flowchart LR Agora["Harmonia.Agora: collaboration control"] -->|"Application Services API: operation requests"| Server["Harmonia.Omilia.Server: collaboration operations"] Server -->|"Application Services API: managed-Room dialogue / activity"| Agora Client["Harmonia.Omilia.Client: collaboration experience"] <-->|"Matrix protocol"| Server ```
Agora decides to create/change a managed Room/Space, add/remove a participant or publish information; Omilia.Server performs the operation. Room activity returns through the same architectural boundary. The exact API contract, technology and mapping to upstream Matrix interfaces remain deferred. Historical Admin, Client-Server and AS-transaction endpoints do not define this new contract.
Workflow/execution collaboration continues through Petasos with **no direct Agora-to-Ponos dependency**. Matrix DTO encapsulation, Themis default-deny governance and zero-PHI Room aliases/names/topics remain repository constraints. Membership or receipt of a notification does not confer information-access rights.
[U19](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u19) establishes the administrative interaction boundary: Administrator → Omilia → Agora → Administrative Function → specialised Administrative Ergon → governed subsystem operation. Stopped-Twin resumption uses this pattern, with normal authorisation, Context, execution and Kleio audit controls; Agora and Omilia do not directly resume or manipulate the Twin. The arrows describe semantic progression and retain Petasos execution handoff and Agora's no-direct-Ponos-dependency rule. Iris provides a separate path through Iris-BackEnd and does **not** directly interact with Agora or Omilia. Broader Administrative Function reconciliation is [deferred](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#administrative-function-finding).
Identity mapping/provisioning is collaboration integration, not authentication authority. Existing isolation constraints are not relaxed; detailed security, privacy and external/federated interactions remain deferred.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F23 | Bidirectional collaboration operations/activity boundary; historical transaction deduplication intent | Omilia.Server Application Services API: Agora requests operations and receives dialogue/activity in all managed Rooms; Petasos mediates wider execution collaboration | Operation intent/results, Room activity and collaboration transaction information | U16 settles owners and direction, not exact API or Matrix endpoint mapping. Historical AS transaction ID/status mechanisms remain L12; partial publication, marker failure and uncertain effects CDG-19; storage/API detail CDG-22/52. No exactly-once claim. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
| F23 | Bidirectional collaboration operations/activity boundary; historical transaction deduplication intent | Omilia.Server Application Services API: Agora requests operations and receives dialogue/activity in all managed Rooms; Petasos mediates wider execution collaboration | Operation intent/results, Room activity and collaboration transaction information | U16 settles owners and direction, not exact API or Matrix endpoint mapping. Historical AS transaction ID/status mechanisms remain L12; partial publication, marker failure and uncertain effects CDG-19; storage/API detail CDG-22/52. No exactly-once claim. |

Server derived from Matrix Synapse; Client from Element. Lineage is provenance; API, modifications, storage and Client/Iris detail deferred CDG-52. |``. element.name: [CT3] Practitioner Engagement & Privilege Management
element.documentation:
Manage practitioners as service participants, their roles/capacities, applicable privileges and qualification context above ordinary HR employment administration.
This capability manages how practitioners participate in services and the privileges applicable to that participation. It connects professional standing with roles and permitted capacities in the service context, beyond ordinary employment administration. Separating engagement and privilege from qualification makes it possible to recognise a qualified practitioner who is not authorised for a particular service activity.
**Boundary**
Representation or consumption of privilege information does not transfer the underlying workforce decision authority to Harmonia.

element.documentation:

Source entry: **NFR-124 — Credential and Grant Revocation**. Primary subject: `G03.03`.
The source classification is Principle «ArchitecturalAxiom». The source identifier is a scoped register reference and does not determine architectural type. Applicability, release scope and unresolved thresholds remain as stated above.

element.name: [Feature] Service-Location-Provider Binding
element.documentation:
Correlate which organization provides a named health service at which physical location with which practitioner roles.
Service-location-provider binding explains which participant provides an identifiable service in which place and acting capacities. The mapping associations belong to Health Service Administration, while the organisations, locations and practitioner entities retain their own information responsibility.
