element.name: Communicate Service Assurance Outcome
element.documentation:
• Canonical Name: Communicate Service Assurance Outcome.
• Definition: Communicates applicable established Assurance Findings and Conclusions to authorised recipients according to their responsibilities, authority and information requirements.
• Approved Potential Recipients: Care Coordinator, Service Coordinator, Regulator, Policy Authority, System Steward.
• Associated Interaction: Service Assurance Outcome Communication (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md#service-assurance-outcome-communication), with Service Guardian and one or more authorised recipient Roles.
• Process Relationship: Exposes the communication behaviour of Assurance Process Reporting / Communication (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md#assurance-process-reporting-communication), beginning from an already established finding/conclusion. It does not perform assessment or adjudication or alter/reinterpret the established outcome. A documentary report is not required.
• Recipient Boundary: No mandatory broadcast is established. A particular outcome may be communicated to one, some or all legitimate recipients according to applicability, authority, responsibility and information requirements. Requester, status consumer and outcome recipient need not be the same Role. Communication does not transfer responsibility for recipients' interpretation within their authority, operational/clinical management, remediation, escalation, policy/compliance response, process improvement or other subsequent action to Service Guardian.
---
## History
### Service Overview — predecessor explanation
Outcome communication exposes already established findings to applicable authorised recipients from the approved roles. It preserves the adjudicated meaning and does not require a broadcast to every possible recipient. Receipt does not transfer the recipient's subsequent clinical, governance or operational action to Service Guardian.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.
| Source predicate | Target element | Source standing / currentness | ARB native treatment | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | exposes_process | [Assurance Process Reporting / Communication](../business-process/2fc0b626577b43feb050bcd91ac2b0a9.md) | established / preserved historical assertion | Serving (reverse) — `id-19a64370784357b0bd2a034f4c64b298` |
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md` — entry lines 195-195. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.
- **Process Relationship**: Exposes the communication behaviour of [Assurance Process Reporting / Communication](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md#assurance-process-reporting-communication), beginning from an already established finding/conclusion. It does not perform assessment or adjudication or alter/reinterpret the established outcome. A documentary report is not required.

element.name: Clinicians & Care Teams
element.documentation:
### Profile & Role Clinicians and Care Teams represent the front-line healthcare workforce: medical practitioners, nurses, clinical specialists, allied health professionals, pharmacists, and multi-disciplinary care coordinators operating at the direct point of care.
### Core Responsibilities - Diagnosing clinical conditions, formulating treatment plans, and administering patient care. - Ordering diagnostic investigations, prescribing medications, and documenting clinical findings. - Reviewing historical health records, previous test results, and discharge summaries to inform clinical decision-making.
### Principal Architectural Concerns - **Timely Information Availability**: Point-of-care access to complete, up-to-date clinical information without lag or missing historical encounters. - **Semantic Fidelity & Clinical Context**: Clinical observations, units of measure, reference ranges, and diagnostic notes must be preserved without lossy truncation, confusion of normal/abnormal flags, or distortion of clinical nuance. - **Elimination of Data Fragmentation**: Synthesized, longitudinal patient views that reduce duplicate diagnostic testing and eliminate dangerous blind spots. - **Explicit Information Authority**: Clear visual and semantic distinction between authoritative hospital-validated records and preliminary, informational, or anecdotal patient-reported data.

element.name: Iris backend-for-frontend mediation
element.documentation: - **Role/features:** decoupled presentation service mediation and clinical versus operations request separation; telemetry aggregation and provider contracts. [L11/L21/L23](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#l11). - **Information/contained constructs:** projected resources, task/sequence views, subsystem status, dependency/queue/gateway observations and alert diagnostics; operations aggregator and health-provider support, not a new information authority. - **Persistence/collaboration:** uses Mneme-facing governed access, Themis and approved execution requests; backend/presentation state is not durable truth. Documented raw Hot Rod/cache paths remain conflicting (CDG-11). **Iris-BackEnd** mediates administrative intent into governed Administrative Function/Administrative Ergon execution. It does not directly resume a stopped Twin or provide a privileged subsystem backdoor (U19). - **Exclusions/standing:** no direct JPA/PostgreSQL or server-side registry governance. Candidate mediation component; ports/server frameworks/provider class catalogues are support details, and telemetry persistence/provenance remains CDG-28.

element.documentation:
Maintain governed longitudinal synthesis and the associations needed to use its constituent clinical information safely.
**Overview**
Maintain governed longitudinal synthesis and the associations needed to use its constituent clinical information safely. Its constituent abilities distinguish Patient Clinical Record.
**Intent**
Make the integrated clinical account usable while keeping its source assertions and associated content attributable.
**Boundary**
The synthesis preserves what Harmonia received or managed without becoming the originator of the clinical facts.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Device Data Integration
element.documentation:
Acquire, exchange or convey device data through established integration capability.
Clinical Device Data Integration acquires, exchanges or conveys device data using an established integration capability. It represents actual information participation rather than the prior configuration enabling it. The distinction makes it possible to preserve the device and care context of received data while retaining separate responsibility for its subsequent interpretation.
**Boundary**
Data movement does not confer clinical meaning, originating authority or device-maintenance responsibility.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). element.name: Manage Clinic & Practice Capacity
element.documentation:
Understands and manages available, committed and utilised clinic/practice capacity in relation to practitioner availability, sessions, rooms, appointments and patient demand.
Responsibility boundary: Operating-session tracking and individual queue progression contribute to this responsibility; neither alone expresses overall service capacity. Capacity coordination does not own source bookings, clinical decisions or practitioner rostering.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Determination
element.documentation:
The capability to interpret assessed health information and establish clinically meaningful conclusions about an individual's health state, condition, risk or prognosis.
Clinical Determination turns assessed findings into clinically interpreted understanding of a person's condition, risk or prognosis. It represents the professional responsibility for deciding what the findings mean in the individual's clinical context, including the significance of changes identified through monitoring. This is the interpretive responsibility within Individual Care Delivery, rather than another method of collecting evidence.
**Intent**
Establish clinical conclusions on which an intended response can be based.
**Boundary**
Determining clinical meaning does not itself select the care response. No CT3 taxonomy has been adjudicated; diagnosis and prognostic judgement illustrate this responsibility without becoming additional catalogue elements.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [Topic] Episode
element.documentation:
**Status: RESOLVED — APPROVED, with explicit unresolved association/responsibility details.**
**Description** Information describing a longitudinal context that relates healthcare activity over time for one or more health problems or conditions, providing continuity across relevant Encounters and other care interactions.
**Definition** Episode is a longitudinal information context representing the treatment of one or more Problems or Conditions across a related series of Encounters, providing a coherent perspective for assurance, workflow and financial purposes.
Episode is now an independently meaningful Information Concept. The former non-authoritative Episode Context suggestion is promoted to Episode with this definition; its original rationale and standing remain historical in §7.
- Episode is not merely a Collection of Encounters. Encounter association contributes to longitudinal treatment context but does not define its complete meaning. - Episode relates one or more Problems/Conditions [1..*] to a longitudinal course of treatment and may relate to multiple Encounters [0..*]. Not every Encounter for a healthcare subject necessarily belongs to a particular Episode. - Encounter-association mechanisms/rules, detailed identity, originating authority, Harmonia information-responsibility allocation and temporal/lifecycle semantics remain unresolved. The decision allocates no reverse cardinality, upstream owner, Feature or Service. - No Episode ownership of related Encounters is inferred; the association is not implementation containment. Assurance/workflow/financial perspective is not an allocation of authority for those activities. - This architecturally approved meaning stands independently of representation. No FHIR EpisodeOfCare derivation, mapping or equivalence is established.
**Review consequence:** G2-Q04 no longer asks whether Episode exists or what its basic meaning is; only genuinely unresolved details remain. No Problems/Conditions family is derived.
Source standing: Explicitly APPROVED G2 decision only; G2 remains candidate/open and all residual qualifications remain unresolved.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/episode-encounter.md` — ### 3.5 Episode — APPROVED (G2-D01). Standing: Approved G2-D01 meaning only; remaining family review open.
- **Semantic Classification**: Longitudinal Information Context. It is not merely a Collection of Encounters; no additional metamodel kind or implementation aggregate is assigned by this decision. - **Definition**: Episode is a longitudinal information context representing the treatment of one or more Problems or Conditions across a related series of Encounters, providing a coherent perspective for assurance, workflow and financial purposes. - **Architectural authority**: Explicitly approved in [G2-D01](3927d161556d48f4b2cc57bd46ab785d.md), superseding the former non-authoritative Episode Context suggestion while retaining its review history. This meaning is independent of downstream representation and is not derived from FHIR EpisodeOfCare. - **Necessity**: EC-IR5 now has this explicit approved longitudinal treatment meaning. Problems/Conditions and related Encounters contribute to the treatment context; Encounter association does not define Episode's complete meaning. These are boundary references, not derivation of a later clinical family. - **Relationships and boundary**: Episode relates one or more Problems/Conditions [1..*] to a longitudinal course of treatment and may relate to multiple Encounters [0..*]. Not every Encounter for the subject necessarily belongs to a particular Episode. No Encounter-association rules, reverse cardinality, Encounter ownership or implementation containment are established. - **Remaining uncertainty**: Originating authority, Harmonia information-responsibility allocation, detailed identity, association evidence/rules and temporal/lifecycle details remain unresolved under G2-Q04. Assurance/workflow/financial perspective does not confer performance, billing or assurance authority.

element.name: [CT3] Credential Management
element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Credential Management concerns operational badges and physical-access credentials used in authorised operational participation. It retains a distinct Domain03 responsibility even though Strategy has no matching catalogue entry. This prevents the word credential from merging physical-access context with the professional qualifications and competency evidence checked by Clinical Qualification Management.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
No Strategy correspondence or Feature association is inferred from name similarity. Operational credentials do not themselves establish professional clinical qualification or privilege.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Relevance remains Unresolved. Established operational behaviour provides context for possible enablement but does not authorise a formal classification.

element.name: [CT3] Governed Operational Activity Design
element.documentation:
Define the information context, expected outcomes, continuation conditions and housekeeping of governed operational activity.
**Overview**
An activity needs a fulfilment definition even when only one bounded execution unit is involved. This capability specifies its semantic envelope while execution and event delivery remain separate responsibilities.
**Intent**
Make the expected information and fulfilment basis of an undertaking explicit before it executes.
**Boundary**
An activity definition is neither an orchestrator nor a choreographer. It does not choose clinical care or dynamically invent execution logic.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT3] Terminology Localisation
element.documentation:
Manage controlled local responses where adopted terminology does not meet legitimate organisational semantic requirements.
Terminology Localisation manages controlled local responses where adopted terminology does not satisfy legitimate organisational semantic needs. It makes the local variation explicit rather than allowing ad hoc usage to conceal a gap or change in meaning. Within clinical-semantics governance, this preserves a distinction between governed local adaptation and uncontrolled drift.
**Boundary**
The established localisation responsibility concerns terminology; no corresponding Classification Localisation capability is inferred.

The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. These are distinct assertions. Neither diagram membership nor the Grouping's label alone establishes another Home or a statement allocation. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.

element.name: [CT3] Operational Work Assignment & Dispatch Coordination
element.documentation:
Coordinate qualified operational work assignment, dispatch, acknowledgement, progression and escalation within assigned authority.
**Overview**
Coordinate qualified operational work assignment, dispatch, acknowledgement, progression and escalation within assigned authority. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Coordinate qualified operational work assignment, dispatch, acknowledgement, progression and escalation within assigned authority.
**Boundary**
Information administration and coordination preserve the authority of the responsible source, clinical actor and governed domain; they confer no additional real-world management authority.

element.name: [Feature] Operation-Bound Authorisation Enforcement
element.documentation:
Apply effective policy at the governed action boundary and reject actions lacking sufficient authority.
**Overview**
Consistent enforcement is required across mutation, access, execution and administration rather than relying on each caller to voluntarily invoke a check.
**Boundary**
Consumes trusted identity and criteria; it does not authenticate or establish clinical privilege from directory roles.

element.name: Distributed Clinical Knowledge → Informed Clinical Collaboration
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Purpose & Value Focus
Healthcare is inherently collaborative. Complex patient care requires continuous multidisciplinary interaction among medical specialists, nursing staff, allied health professionals, pharmacists, and community care providers. However, clinical communication is frequently disconnected from the longitudinal patient record, leading to ungrounded decisions, fragmented care plans, and clinical risk.
The strategic value created by **VS-04** is the **synthesis of distributed clinical knowledge into contextually relevant information supporting informed multidisciplinary collaboration**. It enables care teams to communicate, consult, and coordinate in the direct presence of verified longitudinal clinical facts without altering source clinical truth.
```mermaid graph LR S1["S1: Distributed Clinical Knowledge"] --> S2["S2: Relevant Info Discovered"] S2 --> S3["S3: Access Appropriately Governed"] S3 --> S4["S4: Clinical Context Established"] S4 --> S5["S5: Info Presented in Context"] S5 --> S6["S6: Informed Clinical Collaboration"] ```
#### Value Transformation Stages
1. **S1 — Distributed Clinical Knowledge**: - *Stakeholder State*: Clinically relevant information, historical observations, diagnostic findings, care history, and other governed clinical knowledge exist across the healthcare ecosystem. - *Value Generated*: Ecosystem knowledge is recognized as an active collective resource rather than isolated data fragments. 2. **S2 — Relevant Information Discovered**: - *Stakeholder State*: Authorized queries, alerts, and subscriptions discover clinical facts pertinent to an active patient problem, clinical event, or multidisciplinary consultation. - *Value Generated*: Practitioners are spared manual cross-system searching; relevant clinical facts are brought forward based on active clinical need. 3. **S3 — Access Appropriately Governed**: - *Stakeholder State*: Participant identities, clinical roles, care team relationships, consent policies, and default-deny governance rules are evaluated prior to disclosing clinical information. - *Value Generated*: Patient privacy and sensitive clinical data are rigorously safeguarded; collaboration proceeds within legitimate clinical relationships. 4. **S4 — Clinical Context Established**: - *Stakeholder State*: Longitudinal patient timeline context, active problems, current medication regimens, allergies, and relevant diagnostic findings are bound to the collaborative space. - *Value Generated*: Clinical discussions are anchored directly in objective patient history rather than fragmented recollection or unverified hearsay. 5. **S5 — Information Presented in Context**: - *Stakeholder State*: Verified clinical summaries, trends, and diagnostic reports are rendered seamlessly alongside collaborative communication channels without exposing internal platform mechanics. - *Value Generated*: Care team members share an identical, high-fidelity clinical picture, eliminating misunderstandings and information asymmetry. 6. **S6 — Informed Clinical Collaboration**: - *Stakeholder State*: Treating clinicians and multidisciplinary care team members engage in timely, context-rich deliberation, arriving at informed, coordinated clinical care decisions. - *Value Generated*: Care plans are coordinated rapidly, multidisciplinary consultation is streamlined, and patient safety is significantly enhanced.
#### Boundary Guardrail: Clinical Authority & Expertise in Collaboration
Harmonia establishes the governed information context in which clinical collaboration occurs. Harmonia explicitly maintains the following boundaries: 1. **Harmonia is not an Electronic Medical Record (EMR)**: It does not replace source departmental or enterprise EMRs. 2. **Harmonia is not the clinical decision-maker**: Clinical responsibility and decision-making authority rest entirely with the attending clinicians and care teams. 3. **Harmonia does not originate clinical assertions during collaboration**: Collaborative dialogue (e.g., in Matrix/Agora channels) does not automatically become an authoritative clinical record. Clinical practitioners bring their expertise to the collaboration; Harmonia provides the governed clinical context in which that expertise is exercised. 4. **Clinical statements require source attribution**: Any clinical order or diagnostic finding resulting from collaboration must be explicitly committed through governed clinical workflows with source practitioner attribution.
#### Representative Strategic Traceability
| Traceability level | Current architectural standing | | :--- | :--- | | Motivation | Established existing constraint: [AX-07 — Security Is Intrinsic to Managed Operations](../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md). Current named Driver/Goal relationships and a replacement for the retired axiom meanings remain unresolved. | | Current Business Capability contribution | **Unresolved / not presently established.** The superseded BC relationships are retired; no relationship to BC-01 through BC-18 is supplied by identifier position or similarity. | | Current Business Enabling contribution and contextual view | **Unresolved / not presently established.** Old view ordinals and meanings are retired; no enabling-capability or Feature relationship is inferred. | | Existing current Enterprise Capability contributions | **Established, partial:** [EC-02 — Context Management](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-02-context-management); [EC-06 — Policy & Control](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-06-policy--control). These previously documented contributions retain their canonical meanings. Other current contributions are unresolved; the retired EC labels do not establish replacements. |
- **Strategic Courses of Action**: `COA-01` (Boundary Membrane Sovereignty), `COA-03` (Meaning-Centric Provenance and Traceability), `COA-06` (Collaborative Reusable Capability Realisation).
### 1.1.21 Journey incorporation
This existing Value Stream is reused as a Journey with the same canonical and Exchange identities, names, original definition and standing. Its source-defined transformations are represented by independently identifiable constituent Journeys. The added Aggregation relationships express reusable structure; Triggering expresses meaningful progression with its stated conditions. Neither creates runtime orchestration. New, explicitly qualified capability contributions supplement the predecessor traceability account; the original unestablished relationships and qualifications above are not retrospectively rewritten or declared accepted.

element.name: [CT2] General Collaboration
element.documentation:
General Collaboration provides secure operational messaging for departmental, administrative and facility-support participants. It gives non-clinical coordination an interaction context without assuming every discussion requires a patient-linked clinical workspace. Its role is communication enablement rather than ownership of the support activity being discussed.
**Overview**
General Collaboration provides secure operational messaging for departmental, administrative and facility-support participants. It gives non-clinical coordination an interaction context without assuming every discussion requires a patient-linked clinical workspace. Its role is communication enablement rather than ownership of the support activity being discussed.
**Intent**
General Collaboration provides secure operational messaging for departmental, administrative and facility-support participants. It gives non-clinical coordination an interaction context without assuming every discussion requires a patient-linked clinical workspace. Its role is communication enablement rather than ownership of the support activity being discussed.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Conversation does not assign operational authority, complete work or become an authoritative record merely through retention.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Operational messaging materially enables coordination while the participants' business responsibilities remain external to the collaboration mechanism.

element.name: [CT3] Provider Relationship
element.documentation:
Managing organizational affiliations and multidisciplinary team relationships.
**Overview**
Effective affiliations explain which practitioner or team participates with which organisation. These relationships support collaboration and routing while each participating identity keeps its own responsibility owner.
**Intent**
Preserve which affiliations apply when interpreting provider participation.
**Boundary**
Affiliation records do not transfer the participating organisations or practitioner identities to this capability.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: [Feature] Outpatient Appointment Capacity Management
element.documentation:
Represent usable outpatient session capacity from booking, staffing and local flow information.
**Overview**
The projection distinguishes scheduled slots from currently usable care capacity without taking source booking authority.
**Boundary**
Local responsibility retains its capacity meaning; Service Capacity Management consumes it without acquiring ownership or imposing one common capacity model.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B07.03.03.F03`; additional scope correspondences: . Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Assurance Process Execution
element.documentation:
• Canonical Name: Assurance Process Execution. • Owning Capability: Governed Assurance (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#governed-assurance). • Process Purpose: Performs defined assurance for an identifiable governed subject in accordance with an applicable Assurance Definition and establishes an Assurance Finding / Conclusion from applicable trustworthy evidence. • Principal Performing Role: Service Guardian (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md#service-guardian). • Participating Functions: Establish Assurance Context (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#establish-assurance-context), Assess Assurance Evidence (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#assess-assurance-evidence) and Adjudicate Assurance Assessment (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#adjudicate-assurance-assessment), all retaining Governed Assurance ownership. • Conceptual Basis and Output: Applicable Assurance Definition plus identifiable governed subject; Assurance Finding / Conclusion established through adjudication where sufficient trustworthy evidence permits. Correct execution with insufficient evidence does not imply satisfaction or non-satisfaction or force a conclusion. • Boundary: Function completion does not define Process lifecycle states. No Context Established, Evidence Assessed, Adjudicated or Concluded states are inferred. Detailed lifecycle states, transitions and initiation mechanics remain unresolved. Requesting this Process does not grant control of evidence assessment, adjudication or the resulting finding/conclusion. Correct execution with insufficient evidence remains different from execution failure and from a positive or negative conclusion about the subject. element.name: [CT3] Bed & Care-Place Turnover Coordination
element.documentation:
Coordinate the operational transition of a released care-place through cleaning, preparation and readiness notifications.
**Overview**
Coordinate the operational transition of a released care-place through cleaning, preparation and readiness notifications. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Coordinate the operational transition of a released care-place through cleaning, preparation and readiness notifications.
**Boundary**
Information administration and coordination preserve the authority of the responsible source, clinical actor and governed domain; they confer no additional real-world management authority.

element.name: [CT2] Diagnostic Administration
element.documentation:
Diagnostic Administration correlates requests with specimens and encounters and integrates diagnostic reports into their request context. It connects the laboratory or imaging contribution with the participants expecting an outcome, preserving report identity and standing as updates occur. Its enabling role differs from performing the diagnostic procedure or professionally interpreting evidence.
**Overview**
Diagnostic Administration correlates requests with specimens and encounters and integrates diagnostic reports into their request context. It connects the laboratory or imaging contribution with the participants expecting an outcome, preserving report identity and standing as updates occur. Its enabling role differs from performing the diagnostic procedure or professionally interpreting evidence.
**Intent**
Diagnostic Administration correlates requests with specimens and encounters and integrates diagnostic reports into their request context. It connects the laboratory or imaging contribution with the participants expecting an outcome, preserving report identity and standing as updates occur. Its enabling role differs from performing the diagnostic procedure or professionally interpreting evidence.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
The finalised-report distribution Feature retains its narrower scope. Broader Domain03 behaviour covering preliminary, corrected or addendum information does not silently expand that Feature.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Request, specimen and report correlation and governed distribution are substantive information-integration responsibilities.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [Feature] Mobile Visit Status Tracking
element.documentation:
Ingest arrival, visit progression, and safety check-in milestones from roving staff.
Mobile visit tracking receives arrival, progression and safety checkpoints from roving workers. It makes reported activity visible in the wider operational context without originating the clinical visit, deciding its clinical content or assuming that a checkpoint proves the intended clinical outcome.

element.name: [CT2] Context Management
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Establish, validate, propagate, and preserve the execution, clinical, security, and administrative context within which information and activities have meaning. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Binding the subject of care, encounter, ordering provider, and healthcare service context to in-flight messages and transactions. - Propagating tamper-evident, attributable security context across asynchronous, multi-hop operational boundaries. - Ensuring context preservation during cross-protocol transformations across disparate healthcare exchange formats and protocols. - Detecting and rejecting requests where mandatory operational or clinical context is missing or inconsistent. - **Collaborative Nature**: Bounded reusable context responsibility may be realised through participation across gateways, activity execution and information-access boundaries. Participation does not transfer semantic ownership.
Context Management preserves the circumstances in which information and activity have meaning as they cross processing boundaries. Subject, encounter, provider, service and security context must remain attributable and consistent rather than be reconstructed from convenient local assumptions. Its reuse is especially significant in multi-hop activity where a syntactically valid message can otherwise lose the context required for legitimate interpretation.
**Boundary**
Context participation does not transfer semantic ownership. Generic context management and assurance-specific context semantics contribute together without allocating a new central Context Service.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E06.06`; additional scope correspondences: `E07.04`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Establish, validate, propagate, and preserve the execution, clinical, security, and administrative context within which information and activities have meaning.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Binding the subject of care, encounter, ordering provider, and healthcare service context to in-flight messages and transactions.



\item 
Propagating tamper-evident, attributable security context across asynchronous, multi-hop operational boundaries.



\item 
Ensuring context preservation during cross-protocol transformations across disparate healthcare exchange formats and protocols.



\item 
Detecting and rejecting requests where mandatory operational or clinical context is missing or inconsistent.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Bounded reusable context responsibility may be realised through participation across gateways, activity execution and information-access boundaries. Participation does not transfer semantic ownership.



\end{itemize}

element.name: [Feature] Demographic Context Governance
element.documentation:
Manage essential demographic attributes (date of birth, sex, vital status) with full provenance and timestamping.
Demographic governance retains the provenance and temporal context of attributes used to interpret the subject of care. A changed date, status or demographic assertion can therefore be understood as sourced information rather than an unexplained overwrite of previously known context.

element.name: [CT3] Identity Qualification Control
element.documentation:
Determine whether presented identity characteristics, provenance and assurance quality are sufficient for its intended context.
Identity Qualification Control evaluates whether presented identity characteristics, provenance and assurance are sufficient for the intended context. It adds a contextual judgement beyond whether the actor can be authenticated. This permits an identity adequate for one purpose to remain insufficient for another without claiming that the identity is necessarily false.
**Boundary**
Identity qualification does not establish practitioner clinical qualification or a general permission to act.

element.name: Durable Clinical Information Independence
element.documentation:
### Context & Pressure Clinical information must remain intelligible, authoritative, and actionable across a patient's entire lifetime (often 80+ years). In contrast, commercial Electronic Medical Record (EMR) software products, proprietary database schemas, and integration broker technologies have commercial lifecycles of only 5 to 10 years.
When healthcare networks store longitudinal patient data exclusively inside proprietary EMR schemas, they suffer severe vendor lock-in, exorbitant data extraction fees, and the perpetual risk of data obsolescence during vendor transitions.
### Architectural Imperative Harmonia must establish durable clinical information independence. Patient health data managed by Harmonia must exist as a vendor-neutral, sovereign regional asset. The clinical representation must outlive the commercial life of any individual software vendor, database engine, or middleware framework.
- **Primary Stakeholders**: [Clinicians & Care Teams](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md), [Healthcare Delivery Organizations](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md) - **Associated Goal**: [Vendor-Independent Longitudinal Clinical Information Coherence](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) - **Governing Axioms**: [AX-01 (Health-Information Centricity)](../principle/e9bd61acaaea4577bc4086a5639e52c3.md), [AX-06 (Explicit Information Authority)](../principle/952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md)

element.name: [CT2] Clinic & Practice Operations
element.documentation:
Clinic & Practice Operations tracks operating sessions and the operational progression of people through the clinic environment. It makes delays, waiting and completion context visible alongside service-specific capacity responsibilities. This is real-world clinic operation, distinct from the technical queueing machinery that might realise the information flow.
**Overview**
Clinic & Practice Operations tracks operating sessions and the operational progression of people through the clinic environment. It makes delays, waiting and completion context visible alongside service-specific capacity responsibilities. This is real-world clinic operation, distinct from the technical queueing machinery that might realise the information flow.
**Intent**
Clinic & Practice Operations tracks operating sessions and the operational progression of people through the clinic environment. It makes delays, waiting and completion context visible alongside service-specific capacity responsibilities. This is real-world clinic operation, distinct from the technical queueing machinery that might realise the information flow.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Operational queue progression does not determine clinical priority or own the clinician's worklist.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Session and flow information materially supports clinic coordination while the clinic retains its contextual capacity responsibility.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT3] Screening and Immunisation Enablement
element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Preventive Care enables information flows around immunisation and screening recall. Administration records can be conveyed to national registers, while established reminders can reach designated providers. This Service Delivery context supplies bounded information enablement; it does not replace the broader Business Capability Preventative Health or its programme and cohort responsibilities.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Submission does not perform immunisation, and a recall notice does not determine individual clinical eligibility or complete screening.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Register integration and recall distribution materially connect preventative activity across participants.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: Service Guardian
element.documentation: - **Canonical Name**: `Service Guardian`. **Element Type**: Business Role. Canonical ID remains unresolved. The previous assurance-role name collision is [resolved in §3.6](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md#36-assurance-role-naming--resolved); the care-support Guardian under Representative is unchanged. - **Definition**: A Business Role responsible for independently evaluating governed activity, information, state or outcomes against applicable assurance criteria and establishing assurance findings and conclusions from sufficient trustworthy evidence. - **Derivation**: [REQ-FND-005](../../motivation/requirement/bbb7438e78604308abba93afc14f4e2e.md), [BC-18 Health Service Assurance](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-capabilities.md#18-health-service-assurance) and [Governed Assurance](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#governed-assurance) establish the independent evaluation/conclusion responsibility documented in the [bounded Domain03 assurance derivation](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md). The shared name is intentional: **EC-14 Service Guardian is an Enterprise Capability; Service Guardian here is a Business Role.** Neither is a software component. - **Performed Business Functions**: [Establish Assurance Context](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#establish-assurance-context), [Assess Assurance Evidence](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#assess-assurance-evidence) and [Adjudicate Assurance Assessment](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#adjudicate-assurance-assessment), all owned by Governed Assurance. Context establishment includes evidence assembly; adjudication includes establishment of findings/conclusions. No separate evidence-assembly, conclusion-establishment or reporting Function is added. - **Approved Process / Interaction Participation**: Principal performing Role for [Assurance Process Execution](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md#assurance-process-execution); communicates established outcomes through [Assurance Process Reporting / Communication](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md#assurance-process-reporting-communication). Participates in [Service Assurance Request, Status and Outcome Communication](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md#5-approved-service-assurance-interactions) with the approved requesting/status/recipient Roles. This adds no Function or Collaboration and does not make status an assurance conclusion. - **Management Boundary**: Service Guardian may manage progression of its own assurance activity but does not thereby manage, perform, remediate, assign, delegate or operationally escalate the subject being assured. Findings may cause another responsible party to initiate operational response; responsibility for that response remains with its applicable operational capability and authority. - **Clinical Boundary**: Service Guardian confers no clinical authority and does not establish clinical adequacy, clinical correctness or professional clinical judgement, replace clinical peer review or clinical governance, or assume Clinical Services Delivery Assurance. Clinical review and clinical assurance remain with their applicable clinical processes and authorities. Information and behaviour concerning clinical activity may be subject to Guardianship where an explicit applicable governed requirement establishes that concern; this does not transfer clinical responsibility. - **Conclusion Boundary**: Evidence assessment remains distinct from adjudication. Adjudication determines the finding or conclusion from assessed evidence and applicable criteria. Where evidence is insufficient to conclude with the required confidence, insufficiency remains explicit and implies neither satisfaction nor non-satisfaction. This is distinct from execution failure or uncertainty about whether assurance activity occurred. - **Allocation Boundary**: The Role performs independent assurance within Governed Assurance. It does not inherently approve governing requirements, Assurance Definitions or Assurance Criteria, or acquire modelling, clinical review or operational-response responsibility. Detailed Actor eligibility/mandates beyond the approved Role relationships, further Interactions and Collaborations remain unresolved. It has no application, runtime or implementation allocation.

element.name: [CT1] Connected Health Services
element.documentation:
Exchange health information appropriately and provide digitally mediated communication, notifications and collaborative interaction between health-service participants.
Connected Health Services represents the organisation's ability to exchange health information and communicate digitally between health-service participants. Its two children distinguish exchange of health-information artefacts from participant communication, notification and collaboration. Both support connected care, but a user viewing information through a screen is not thereby participating in a communication channel.
**Intent**
Enable appropriate information movement and interaction between otherwise separate participants and services.
**Boundary**
This organisational capability is not defined by an interface engine or messaging product. General presentation remains a separate enabling concern.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Information exchange and digitally mediated interaction are direct platform responsibilities within their assigned contracts, supporting the Core classification without transferring payload or clinical authority.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [48f01ef8b0e6431c85cf4f40cf8f94c3](48f01ef8b0e6431c85cf4f40cf8f94c3.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E03`; additional scope correspondences: `B05`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: DigitalTwin
element.documentation:
### Approved 1.1.24 incorporation — resulting candidate pending
Each applicable execution JVM hosts the common Mneme-Workflow-Cache capability using **embedded Infinispan LOCAL**, holding authorised materialised IU working information. This is per JVM, not a shared site cache or distributed L1/near cache. Common Ergon context loading/unloading, checkpoints and execution recovery remain intact; specialised execution reuses them. Immutable inputs may have independent working manifestations, with no automatic mutation on newer authoritative versions. Existing sequencing, assurance independence and failure boundaries remain unchanged. After loss/eviction, reconstruct through governed Mneme/Mnemosyne acquisition and durable work at the existing recovery boundary; do not resume inside a failed Ergon or treat cache state as checkpoint authority. Memory/security/lifecycle/packaging policy is MC-03/07; no new execution/recovery subsystem is created.
- **Role/features:** specialised Ponos-based execution component for entity-specific operational coordination associated with Energeia. [U02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u02) establishes specialisation/reuse, not containment by a Ponos runtime. The Digital Twin responsibility in [A02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#a02) remains controlling: entity-related execution SHOULD use the Twin unless explicitly justified otherwise. - **Twin-specific execution:** one input queue containing Stimulus and Effector. At most one queued input is processed at a time; interested Behaviours execute **sequentially**, subject to the failure dispositions below. Each receives its own BehaviourStimulus/BehaviourEffector and fresh Praxis-defined Context after its predecessor's completion/save on the normal path. No shared immutable input-level Context. [U19 serialisation and lifecycle](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md). Bounded resources service runnable pending work; stopped Twins retain pending inputs. Concurrency is across independent Twins, without a thread per Twin. - **Sequence/failure/recovery:** R1.x/R2.x framework loads/exposes Behaviours and provides/maintains the sequencing API; developer configuration supplies policy. Without it, order is unspecified. The applicable sequence remains stable for the current input; changes apply to subsequently processed inputs. `ContinueBehaviourOnFailure` contains failure to the current execution while keeping the Behaviour active and other interested Behaviours and queue processing unaffected. `StopBehaviourOnFailure` stops the failing Behaviour immediately, lets remaining interested Behaviours finish the current input, then halts the Twin. `StopDigitalTwinOnFailure` terminates the failing Behaviour and halts the Twin immediately, preventing remaining current-input and subsequent queued processing. Stopped Twins do not automatically resume: authorised administrative input through Iris/Iris-BackEnd or Omilia/Agora leads to Administrative Function → Administrative Ergon → governed Twin operation. Neither channel directly manipulates the Twin. Detailed recovery of a stopped Behaviour remains deferred (CDG-54). - **Information:** uses context drawn from governed entity information and relationships; entity/resource/Twin identity are not aliases. Historical patient, practitioner, wardsperson, organisation, care-team, ward and bed examples are illustrative archetypes, not an approved exhaustive component catalogue. - **Persistence/significant information:** definition/configuration is a C&G classification candidate; operational state/activity is an O&A candidate under U06. Detailed coordination-state Data Objects, activation/deactivation, preservation and transient/durable qualification remain CDG-07. A Twin is not inherently a permanent object, table or FHIR resource. - **Collaboration/exclusions:** executes Behaviour C25, which specialises Ergon and retains all common Ergo/Ergon facilities. Uses Mneme Pragma Management and candidate Stimulus/Effector specialisations; Ponos supplies common execution, Petasos supplies messaging/recoverable handoff. Follows the [specialisation principle](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/README.md#specialisation-principle); adds genuinely Twin-specific semantics instead of parallel platform mechanisms. Not a second engine, unmanaged persistent actor, separate policy/search service or authority over originating clinical facts/clinical work. - **Standing:** U02 specialisation and U19 Behaviour execution semantics established; representation/runtime details remain CDG-07/54. DigitalTwin and Dokimasia are sibling Ponos specialisations; neither contains the other or manages Pragma by execution.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Digital Twin Behaviour Context lifecycle. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
[U19](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u19) specialises the normal lifecycle for [Digital Twin Behaviour execution](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md). Each Behaviour has its own Praxis-defined Context requirements, interpreted relative to the singular represented entity. Interested Behaviours execute sequentially, with **fresh Context Load → Execute → Context Save for each** on the normal path. Normal progression loads the next Behaviour's Context only after its predecessor has completed and saved its information consequences; failure progression follows the [three failure dispositions](a26f06d66bec4981b266e202c46a9afb.md). Later Behaviours may therefore observe authoritative consequences established by earlier ones; there is no single immutable Context snapshot shared by all Behaviours for an input.
Mneme retains Context materialisation/save and Pragma management; Mnemosyne alone establishes authoritative durable state. This ordering grants neither cache authority nor an automatic commit guarantee and does not replace exceptional harmonisation or AX-15 uncertainty handling. Detailed continuation when a Behaviour cannot establish its save outcome remains [open](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#digital-twin-execution-contracts).
Behaviour outputs can enter normal governed processing. Twin-relative references may require resolution/dereferencing for the receiving context; sufficiently explicit outputs need no transformation. Same-Twin Stimulus/Effector outputs join its normal queue without interrupting the current input.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F32 | Entity-relative Behaviour execution and single-input serialisation | [DigitalTwin C19](component-register.md#c19) specialises Ponos; Behaviour [1..*], each through Praxis → Pathway → exactly one Ergo; Mneme manages Context/Pragma | One Stimulus/Effector queue; identifiable BehaviourStimulus/BehaviourEffector per interested Behaviour; sequential execution with fresh Context after predecessor completion/save on the normal path; open governed outputs | U02/U19 preserve A02 entity boundary. Developer sequencing policy through framework API; unspecified order without configuration. Applicable sequence stable for each input; changes apply to subsequent inputs. ContinueBehaviourOnFailure contains failure to the current execution, leaving the Behaviour active and other interested Behaviours and queue processing unaffected. StopBehaviourOnFailure stops the failing Behaviour immediately, lets remaining interested Behaviours complete the current input, then halts the Twin. StopDigitalTwinOnFailure terminates the failing Behaviour and halts the Twin immediately, preventing remaining current-input and subsequent queued processing. Queued inputs remain pending authorised Administrative Function/Ergon resume; stopped-Behaviour recovery deferred. Concurrency across independent Twins, no thread per Twin. [DesignNote](design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md); detail CDG-07/54/55. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
| F32 | Entity-relative Behaviour execution and single-input serialisation | [DigitalTwin C19](3f64d339648246e99e8866c8089f8960.md) specialises Ponos; Behaviour [1..*], each through Praxis → Pathway → exactly one Ergo; Mneme manages Context/Pragma | One Stimulus/Effector queue; identifiable BehaviourStimulus/BehaviourEffector per interested Behaviour; sequential execution with fresh Context after predecessor completion/save on the normal path; open governed outputs | U02/U19 preserve A02 entity boundary. Developer sequencing policy through framework API; unspecified order without configuration. Applicable sequence stable for each input; changes apply to subsequent inputs. ContinueBehaviourOnFailure contains failure to the current execution, leaving the Behaviour active and other interested Behaviours and queue processing unaffected. StopBehaviourOnFailure stops the failing Behaviour immediately, lets remaining interested Behaviours complete the current input, then halts the Twin. StopDigitalTwinOnFailure terminates the failing Behaviour and halts the Twin immediately, preventing remaining current-input and subsequent queued processing. Queued inputs remain pending authorised Administrative Function/Ergon resume; stopped-Behaviour recovery deferred. Concurrency across independent Twins, no thread per Twin. [DesignNote](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md); detail CDG-07/54/55. |
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md` — ## 1. Purpose and architectural boundaries. Standing: Agreed A4.7 decisions U19; whole-candidate acceptance and deferred mechanisms unchanged.
Capture Digital Twin Behaviour structure, entity-relative execution, input serialisation, Context lifecycle, sequencing, outputs, failure and authorised administrative resumption. This is a semantic contract, not a new execution engine, runtime topology or information schema.
| Relevant authority | Consistency of this decision | | :--- | :--- | | AX-04, AX-10, AX-12 | Harmonia defines serialisation, sequencing and failure meaning; common execution and durable handoff facilities remain reusable. No thread, queue product or runtime mechanism is prescribed. | | AX-05, AX-06, AX-11 | Mneme manages Context/Pragma and their consequences; Mnemosyne establishes authoritative durable state. Loaded or changed values do not themselves establish authority. | | AX-07, AX-08, AX-09 | Behaviour execution and administrative work remain authorised and auditable through normal boundaries. Operational state is not automatically durable audit evidence. | | AX-14, AX-15 | Interest fan-out, execution concurrency, input completion, failure disposition and uncertain effects remain distinct. Failure does not prove that no information consequences occurred. | | AX-16, AX-18 | Twin-relative operational activity progresses with the represented entity without acquiring authority over originating clinical facts or externally governed clinical work. | | AX-17 | The explicit decisions below settle bounded semantics; unestablished representations and deferred mechanisms are not inferred. A4.7 acceptance remains human adjudication. |
Energeia owns/manages **Praxis and Journey**. Ponos owns **governed execution**; Energeia and Ponos are peer application components. Praxis supplies a semantic and operational execution envelope and does not structurally contain Ponos. Existing [specialisation/reuse relationships](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-system-map.md#specialisation-and-reuse) remain intact: DigitalTwin specialises/reuses Ponos and Behaviour specialises/ reuses Ergon, without mandating implementation inheritance.
Mneme owns **Context and Pragma management**; Mnemosyne owns **authoritative persistence management**. Petasos owns **durable purpose-defined handoff and queueing**. Themis authorises/enforces; Kleio owns authoritative audit information. Iris provides general human interaction; Agora owns collaboration control and semantics; Omilia provides collaboration operations and experience. Iris does not directly interact with Agora or Omilia. Administrative access confers no privileged route into subsystem internals.

A Digital Twin establishes an execution reference frame relative to the singular real-world entity it represents. A Patient Twin executes relative to one Patient, a Practitioner Twin to one Practitioner, and a Bed Twin to one Bed. ## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md` — ## 4. One input queue and Behaviour-specific information. Standing: Agreed A4.7 decisions U19; whole-candidate acceptance and deferred mechanisms unchanged.
Each Digital Twin maintains a **single input queue containing Stimulus and Effector**. On dequeue, the framework determines which Behaviours have registered interest in that input and creates a discrete, identifiable information unit for each interested Behaviour:
```text Stimulus Effector ├── BehaviourStimulus → A ├── BehaviourEffector → A ├── BehaviourStimulus → B ├── BehaviourEffector → B └── BehaviourStimulus → C └── BehaviourEffector → C ```
**BehaviourStimulus:** an identifiable Behaviour-specific instance derived from a Stimulus and presented to the ingress of a Behaviour that has registered interest in that Stimulus.
**BehaviourEffector:** an identifiable Behaviour-specific instance derived from an Effector and presented to the ingress of a Behaviour that has registered interest in that Effector.
These terms replace working terminology such as `ActionableStimulus` and `FulfillmentStimulus`. They establish semantic information units, not a physical schema, new Domain04 Information Resource or implementation inheritance hierarchy. Existing candidate Stimulus/Effector Pragma specialisation standing remains; this note does not settle those representation contracts.
### Normal Ergon and Digital Twin processing
Ordinary Ergon processing matches semantic interest in an ActionableTask and establishes a separate FulfillmentTask for each interested Ergon undertaking. Twin processing analogously matches Behaviour interest and derives the corresponding BehaviourStimulus or BehaviourEffector.
```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Normal["Normal Ergon processing"] AT["ActionableTask"] --> Match["Semantic interest matching"] Match --> FT1["FulfillmentTask A"] --> ErgonA["Ergon type A"] Match --> FT2["FulfillmentTask B"] --> ErgonB["Ergon type B"] end subgraph Twin["Digital Twin processing: interested Behaviours execute sequentially"] Input["Stimulus / Effector"] --> Interest["Behaviour interest matching"] Interest --> IU1["BehaviourStimulus / BehaviourEffector A"] Interest --> IU2["BehaviourStimulus / BehaviourEffector B"] IU1 --> BA["Behaviour A"] --> PA["Praxis A"] --> PathA["Pathway A"] --> EA["Ergo [exactly 1]"] IU2 --> BB["Behaviour B"] --> PB["Praxis B"] --> PathB["Pathway B"] --> EB["Ergo [exactly 1]"] end ```
**Diagram A:** fan-out shows semantic interest and Behaviour realisation, not concurrent execution. The equivalence is semantic and architectural. It implies neither inheritance nor identical information types, and does not establish Stimulus/Effector processing through ActionableTask/FulfillmentTask.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md` — ## 5. Interest fan-out and execution concurrency. Standing: Agreed A4.7 decisions U19; whole-candidate acceptance and deferred mechanisms unchanged.
For ordinary Ergon processing, multiple independent **Ergon types** may register interest in the same ActionableTask; each receives a separate FulfillmentTask. Separately, **ActionableTask.ExecutionConcurrency** may permit multiple instances of the **same Ergon type** to undertake that ActionableTask concurrently, each through its own FulfillmentTask instance. Interest fan-out and execution concurrency are orthogonal. Existing Domain04 outcome participation, output and TaskOutcome semantics remain unchanged.
For Twin processing, multiple Behaviours may register interest in one Stimulus or Effector and each receives its own Behaviour-specific information unit. Those interested Behaviours execute **sequentially** within that Twin. Concurrency is expected **across independent Digital Twins**, rather than between Behaviours within one Twin. The runtime/threading mechanism remains deferred; there is no requirement for a thread per Twin.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md` — ## 6. Digital Twin serialisation invariant. Standing: Agreed A4.7 decisions U19; whole-candidate acceptance and deferred mechanisms unchanged.
> **A Digital Twin processes at most one queued Stimulus or Effector at a time.**
Interested Behaviours process their respective BehaviourStimulus or BehaviourEffector **sequentially**, subject to the [failure dispositions](a26f06d66bec4981b266e202c46a9afb.md). With no failure, processing completes after the interested Behaviour sequence completes. Failure may stop the failing Behaviour or halt the Twin, including immediately interrupting the current input. The Twin may commence the next queued input only after current input processing completes and no Twin halt applies. An empty queue or a stopped Twin does not imply that an input is executing.
```mermaid flowchart TB Queue["Single Twin queue: S1, E1, S2"] --> Input["Dequeue current Stimulus / Effector; applicable Behaviour sequence remains stable"] Input --> Match["Match registered Behaviour interest"] Match --> Create["Create Behaviour-specific information units"] Create --> Behaviour["Next interested Behaviour: fresh Context Load / Execute / Context Save on normal path"] Behaviour --> Outcome{"Behaviour outcome / failure disposition"} Outcome -->|"No failure"| More{"Remaining interested Behaviours?"} Outcome -->|"ContinueBehaviourOnFailure"| Continue["Failure contained to current execution; Behaviour remains active"] Continue --> More Outcome -->|"StopBehaviourOnFailure"| StopBehaviour["Stop failing Behaviour immediately; Twin halt due after current input"] StopBehaviour --> More Outcome -->|"StopDigitalTwinOnFailure"| Immediate["Terminate failing Behaviour; halt Twin immediately; no remaining Behaviours process current input"] Immediate --> Stopped["STOPPED; queued inputs pending; authorised administrative recovery required"] More -->|"Yes"| Behaviour More -->|"No"| Complete["Current input processing complete"] Complete --> Halt{"Twin halt due?"} Halt -->|"No"| Next["May commence next queued input"] Next --> Queue Halt -->|"Yes"| Stopped ```
**Diagram B:** order is established through developer configuration, or is unspecified when none is supplied; the applicable sequence remains stable for the current input. Failure disposition applies at the failing Behaviour: `StopDigitalTwinOnFailure` bypasses remaining current-input processing, while `StopBehaviourOnFailure` halts the Twin after the remaining interested Behaviours complete. Load / Execute / Save shows the normal path, not further processing after an immediate stop. Context Save denotes Mneme management of consequences, not a new persistence mechanism or automatic proof of authoritative commit.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md` — ## 11. Authorised administrative recovery. Standing: Agreed A4.7 decisions U19; whole-candidate acceptance and deferred mechanisms unchanged.
A Twin halted by `StopBehaviourOnFailure` or `StopDigitalTwinOnFailure` **does not automatically resume**. Queued Stimulus and Effector inputs remain pending. Resumption requires authorised administrative input initiated through an appropriate human interaction channel, such as Iris or Omilia:
```mermaid flowchart TB Admin["Administrator"] --> Iris["Iris"] Admin --> Omilia["Omilia"] Iris --> BackEnd["Iris-BackEnd"] Omilia --> Agora["Agora"] BackEnd --> Function["Administrative Function"] Agora --> Function Function --> Ergon["Administrative Ergon"] Ergon --> Governed["Governed Digital Twin operation"] Governed --> Resume["STOPPED → RUNNING"] ```
The two human-interaction branches are alternatives, not a direct Iris/Agora/ Omilia integration. Iris and Omilia do not directly manipulate or resume the Twin; Iris-BackEnd and Agora also provide no privileged subsystem backdoor. Agora's execution handoff retains Petasos and its prohibition on direct Ponos dependency. Arrows show semantic progression, not new synchronous APIs or dependencies.
The Administrative Function is executed through specialised Administrative Ergon under normal authorisation, Context management, execution and Kleio audit controls. This establishes authorised resume only; retry/replay/skip operations and recovery-console semantics are not designed here. The detailed treatment of a Behaviour stopped by `StopBehaviourOnFailure`, including whether/how it is reset, resumed, replaced or otherwise recovered, remains deferred to the Administrative Function/recovery design.

element.name: Embedded Infinispan LOCAL — Workflow Cache
element.documentation:
Selected embedded Infinispan LOCAL machinery resident **inside each applicable Ponos, DigitalTwin and Dokimasia execution JVM**, supporting Mneme-Workflow-Cache and common Ergon context use. Local instances have no inter-JVM replication, distributed owner lookup, Hot Rod round trip, global key affinity or cross-site L1 coherence.
Serving relationships record this local machinery/use allocation; they do not imply Ponos structurally contains DigitalTwin/Dokimasia, shared physical cache instances or an independent deployment unit. No new JVM Node is needed to duplicate the existing executor identities. Exact memory/lifecycle/security configuration and library-versus-WildFly-subsystem packaging remain MC-03/07; the LOCAL/residency commitment is fixed.
### Retained MC-01–MC-07 qualifications
- **MC-01:** Standard-Cache multi-site topology and active/active consistency need evidence; synchronous distribution/cross-site backup is not native linearizability or safe independent-cluster same-key concurrency. - **MC-02:** Owner count/site placement, majority/partition/failover and continued governed work after one site loss remain unproved; Mneme retains state-transition concurrency obligations beyond cache operations. - **MC-03:** Per-JVM memory bounds, safe eviction/lifetime relative to context load/unload/checkpoint and security isolation remain solution/deployment policy under existing Ergon semantics. - **MC-04:** Durable propagation does not prove immediate replica read visibility. Exact-version/currentness, read-after-write and wait/fail/Indeterminate behaviour use Mneme–Mnemosyne and PersistenceService contracts; no cache affinity mechanism is invented. - **MC-05:** Active/active N+1 (N > 0) is an architectural target, not a verified product guarantee. With only two physical sites, loss of one prevents **new multi-site durable write Success** without another eligible durable site or explicit owning NFR/persistence disposition. Never weaken Success or claim unqualified N+1 write continuity. Three-plus sites alone do not prove quorum/failover correctness. - **MC-06:** Five-service reconciliation is deterministically incorporated: historical GovernedSearch identity is reused as sole GovernedSummarySearch, Summary Reader/Writer added, full Reader/Writer retained; no independent Summary IU or sixth method. - **MC-07:** Existing capability/Feature contributions are reused. Physical remote-client/embedded ownership, observation, deployment and as-built integration remain downstream; no new module or implementation framework is selected.
### Incorporation standing
Accepted complete Final.001 DRP semantics; authorised 1.1.24 ADD; actual incorporated candidate awaiting Solution Architect confirmation. Authority: operative Solution Architect Task and HCRL 1.1.24/001; input approval is distinct from result acceptance.
