element.name: GovernedReader
element.documentation:
### Approved 1.1.24 incorporation — resulting candidate pending
An explicit IU identity/version read returns that exact version or its factual absence/denial/failure/uncertainty; it never silently substitutes an older/newer version. version=* expresses version selection and is different from an exact-version request (AV-01).
Full GovernedReader obtains authoritative Summary, resolves the opaque ContentMetadata reference with InformationCoordinates through the applicable PersistenceService, **attempts Content materialisation**, and assembles the same complete IU/version. Preserve the established large-binary/media pass-by-reference exception. External Content retrieval is an attempt, not a reachability guarantee; failure/denial/unavailability produces its own read Outcome and does not invalidate earlier Summary CREATE.
Mneme client cacheBehaviour USE_AVAILABLE / RELOAD_FOR_AUTHORITATIVE and persistenceBehaviour NO_WAIT / WAIT_FOR_ACTIVE / WAIT_FOR_AUTHORITATIVE are orthogonal consumer decisions. Version/currency constrains acceptable information; wait behaviour constrains the awaited condition. NO_WAIT can return Failure when no acceptable information is immediately available; ordinary synchronous processing is not zero elapsed time. These conceptual options/defaults/types belong to Mneme's API, not extra inter-component methods. Existing Themis constraints are non-optional.
Following a lost/Indeterminate write, authoritative **GovernedReader(version=*)** may inspect a potentially higher actual persisted version. Sufficient correspondence with the submitted write and required durability evidence must establish reconciliation; a newer version alone, a locally visible record or absence of the requested version does not prove success/failure. Insufficient evidence preserves Indeterminate (MI-06); no supplementary transaction ID.
The IU Summary is the projection of the same accepted InformationUnit excluding **exactly InformationRepresentation.Content**. It retains Identity, applicable Metadata (ManagementContext, InformationCoordinates, SecurityContext, LifecycleContext and optional Relationships), ContainerMetadata and ContentMetadata. A Content reference belongs in ContentMetadata and is opaque to Mneme; Mnemosyne/PersistenceService resolve it with InformationCoordinates. ContentReference is illustrative vocabulary, not a prescribed field encoding. Summary projection does not promote transient ManagementContext data to mandatory durable metadata, create a second IU/InformationRepresentation, independent metadata authority or Summary version lineage. Logical separate Content addressability does not require separate physical databases or a particular native transaction.
All five contracts are synchronous governed request/response, with Calliope-owned factual Outcome (closed Success / Failure / Indeterminate and governed closed Reason vocabulary/extensions). Exact Reason members and stage codes remain deferred. Mnemosyne reports facts; Mneme determines consumer disposition without rewriting them. Transport/session timeout is not a factual operation Failure. Receipt, work acceptance, authoritative effect and end-to-end completion remain distinct.
Authentication and Themis policy apply: Readers require ACCESS + READ, SummarySearch invocation ACCESS + SEARCH and disclosed candidates ACCESS + READ, Writers CHANGE with the requested information operation. Protect identity, metadata, counts, pagination and other existence disclosures as well as Content. RequiredIU/SupportedIU capability matching grants no permission. Preserve source-near audit/provenance, Kleio mandatory capture authority/fail-closed obligations and Dokimasia/Provenance allocations; no blanket candidate event catalogue is promoted. Native database/query/provider values stay below the seam.
Every authoritative full or Summary mutation Success requires the applicable multi-site durable authoritative operation and actual resulting IU version, never cache success, local commit, replication queued or transport ACK. Immutable historical versions are preserved. Mneme retains individual-IU concurrency; eligible Mnemosyne instances must expose one coherent authoritative logical history or factual uncertainty. No extra seam transaction identifier or second version axis is introduced.
The established Harmonia-owned contract supplies authoritative acquisition of governed IU information from Mnemosyne to Mneme. Established absence remains distinguishable from denial, failure, stale/qualified information and uncertainty where the operation contract requires. A successful lookup establishing absence may be Success with an applicable governed reason; this defines no particular Reason enumeration member.
Mnemosyne's Façade participates in the contract; IU governance, conformant construction and persistence execution retain the five-tier allocation. Mneme retains application-facing meaning and post-outcome disposition. The accepted parent DRP establishes this contract's purpose without incorporating or completing the neighbouring interaction draft or selecting a wire/Java/provider interface.
### Incorporation standing
Accepted parent DRP semantics, incorporated under the operative Task for 1.1.23/001. Actual resulting candidate confirmation remains pending. Earlier component/source qualifications remain independently in force.

element.name: [CT2] Information Management
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Validate, represent, persist, retrieve, version, and manage governed clinical, administrative, and operational information assets. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Validating inbound information structures against canonical information constraints. - Providing authoritative durable persistence for historical health records and administrative registries. - Managing active distributed working memory representations for low-latency retrieval. - Governing document versioning, supersession, amendments, and retractions without data loss. - **Architectural Principle**: Enforces the foundational separation between *active distributed state access* and *authoritative durable state preservation* (Axiom AX-05).
Information Management provides the recurring ability to represent and maintain governed information through validation, preservation, retrieval and versioned change. It accommodates both responsive active use and authoritative durable preservation while keeping those responsibilities separate. This distinction allows availability and working state to support care without turning a cache into durable truth.
**Boundary**
Engine capabilities provide machinery under Harmonia semantics. Persistence success does not establish information authority or make the platform the originator of the represented facts.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E01`; additional scope correspondences: `E02.01`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [Feature] Dispense Event Tracking
element.documentation:
Ingest medication dispense verification records from pharmacy management systems.
Dispense tracking receives the pharmacy's evidence that medication was supplied under the applicable context. It connects supply with the medication account without inferring that the patient received a dose or that Harmonia performed the professional dispensing activity.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B06.02.01`; additional scope correspondences: `E06.01.02`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: National Clinical Terminology Assets (SNOMED CT-AU / AMT)
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Definition **National Clinical Terminology Assets** comprise the authoritative, governed clinical vocabularies, concept identifiers, descriptions, and semantic relationships used to capture clinical meaning unambiguously across healthcare systems.
#### Enduring Strategic Role Harmonia requires authoritative clinical vocabularies to govern semantic meaning during data ingestion, correlation, and egress: - **SNOMED CT-AU**: The Australian extension to SNOMED CT, providing the clinical concept reference hierarchy for clinical findings, diagnoses, procedures, and body structures. - **Australian Medicines Terminology (AMT)**: The national standard terminology for medicinal products, supporting unambiguous medication reconciliation, prescribing concepts, and dispensing data.
These terminology assets enable Harmonia to evaluate clinical semantic equivalence, enforce conformance rules, and execute meaning-preserving transformations without corrupting clinical intent.
*(Note on LOINC: While Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC) is a recognised international standard for laboratory and diagnostic observations, its formal admission as an enduring foundational resource is governed by jurisdictional adoption and is not pre-empted ahead of explicit canonical scope).*
#### Traceability - **Architectural Axioms**: `AX-04` (Own Semantics / Use Machinery), `AX-08` (Meaning over Machinery), `AX-14` (Preserve Distinctions). - **Enterprise Capabilities**: `EC-13` (Semantic Governance & Conformance). - **Courses of Action**: `COA-03` (Meaning-Centric Provenance and Traceability).

element.name: [UserStory] My healthcare records can be accurately matched
element.documentation:
Independent stakeholder need, expectation or desired outcome:
> Link my recognised healthcare identifier to my patient profile so that my healthcare records can be accurately matched.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.
### Reconciled source contributions
- `UC-Participant-Identity-13` — Link My Healthcare Identifier; Scope - Identity; [source](../../../../../openspec/specs/patient-identity-management/uc-participant-identity-13-link-my-healthcare-identifier/spec.md).
Source-specific access conditions, supporting actors, alternative outcomes, verification and data-authority rules remain distinct in their cited source contributions. Legacy claims that each statement is a business capability are not adopted: this instance has native Requirement semantics. Source target-state scope is not a software delivery commitment for 1.1.21. Historical assessment findings remain recoverable and do not establish current coverage.

element.name: External Interoperability Service
element.documentation:
> **Pylai is Harmonia's External Interoperability Service, responsible for enabling > and managing system-to-system communication between Harmonia and external systems > and clients, irrespective of communication style, protocol, standard or technology.**
Pylai may support asynchronous messaging, synchronous or asynchronous remote method invocation (RMI), APIs, files, polling and other external interoperability mechanisms. RMI is an architectural interaction concept; it does not mean Java RMI. HL7/FHIR gateway slices are examples, not the complete Pylai architecture. Apache Camel or another integration framework may realise external connectors/ technical endpoints; it is a candidate implementation mechanism, not Pylai itself.
External representations conform to their applicable interoperability contracts. Publication SHALL be non-destructive and fail-closed: only permitted information/ extensions may leave. Harmonia-private authority, security-context, cache, persistence, governance and concurrency metadata are not automatically exportable. Egress terminates management of the emitted representation (AX-02/13); retained provenance does not extend control over the external copy.
The [Strategy/Terma reconciliation](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#pylai-strategy-conflict) distinguishes external communication mechanics from Harmonia application meaning and generic network/infrastructure management.

element.name: REQ-FND-003: Subject Referential Integrity
element.documentation:
### Normative Requirement Statement > **Harmonia shall preserve and validate the integrity of subject references and associations used within managed information, preventing known-invalid or internally inconsistent associations from being silently treated as valid.**
### Architectural Intent & Rationale Clinical records derive their entire medical validity from their association with the correct human patient subject. In regional health networks, patient identifiers arrive from disparate sources (national IHIs, regional MRNs, local facility patient numbers). Mismatched or corrupted subject references lead directly to patient harm.
Harmonia mandates that any subject reference attached to a managed clinical event must be structurally validated, referentially verified, and checked for internal consistency. Known-invalid identifiers (e.g., failed check-digits, malformed namespaces, or conflicting patient identifiers within a single clinical bundle) must be rejected or explicitly flagged rather than silently propagated as valid.
### Explicit Boundary: Non-MPI Demarcation - **Not a Master Patient Index (MPI)**: This requirement does **not** establish Harmonia as an MPI or enterprise demographic matching engine. - **Not a Golden-Record Determiner**: Harmonia does not execute probabilistic matching or merge patient demographics into a synthetic "golden record." - **Intent**: Preserving the referential integrity, authenticity, and provenance of subject identifiers without performing lossy or speculative demographic unification.
- **Primary Motivation**: [Patient Safety & Identity Integrity](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/drivers.md) - **External Constraint**: [Applicable National / Jurisdictional Healthcare Identifier Obligations](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/requirements-constraints/external-constraints.md) - **Governing Principles**: [AX-06 (Explicit Information Authority)](../principle/952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md), [AX-14 (Preservation of Semantic Distinctions)](../principle/d3fc6025dc7646d1b2020b51f7a44bfa.md) - **Historical Identifier Reference**: `REQ-IDENT-001`

element.name: [Topic] ServiceOffering
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing a healthcare service that an organisation or provider makes available, including its nature, characteristics and conditions of availability.

element.name: [CT2] Health Information Control
element.documentation:
Govern patient health-information restrictions, filtering and disclosure using established information-access authority, client privacy/consent determinations and applicable security controls.
**Overview**
Govern patient health-information restrictions, filtering and disclosure using established information-access authority, client privacy/consent determinations and applicable security controls.
**Intent**
Govern patient health-information restrictions, filtering and disclosure using established information-access authority, client privacy/consent determinations and applicable security controls.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity. Client consent directives remain owned by Client Privacy Guardrail Management (FEAT-EM-09); this capability references and respects those determinations without defining a second consent owner.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Health Information Control establishes the policy and security basis for governed information operations. Default-deny authority evaluation, consent constraints, security-context propagation and security-significant evidence have distinct purposes: deciding permission, retaining restrictions, carrying attributable operational context and preserving required evidence. The capability makes security intrinsic to the operation rather than optional presentation behaviour.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Security context is operational context and does not automatically become resource content. Security-context validation has no invented one-to-one mapping to propagation, and audit recording is not an assurance conclusion.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Assigned policy enforcement and attributable context are substantive Core responsibilities across managed operations.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.
| Source predicate | Target element | Source standing / currentness | ARB native treatment | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Policy & Control](0c5d986cc948421a8bebcab3b74d108f.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-af61b94f09e6524dbc1c27fc72ab7933` | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Context Management](3cfd3e56c23a4943bd1b476ec248ac49.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-53d4444f6115541b8cde2374f1ead72e` | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Provenance & Traceability](68a0755aa4e14a509ac5e6c0bbcff3e7.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-a3593aca31005063a81f775ccc8e41ba` | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT3] Governed Activity Audit Evidence](c8d93ddc5aa84960964b78345fff1b29.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-1342550f91de5150aa87c01701dc8e02` |
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/05-intrinsic-enablement.md` — entry lines 104-104. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.
- **Owning Capability**: `Health Information Control`
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [a3196aef21d443519de874c24f64a185](a3196aef21d443519de874c24f64a185.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.
## ARB source correspondence
Scope/anti-responsibility and clinical/operational meaning establish the responsible Capability; descriptive ledger/registry/asset labels do not establish a separately bounded formal Information Concept. Preserve non-transfer and source authority.
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/information-responsibility/information-responsibility.md` — information responsibility row 30. Standing: Established Business responsibility only; formal information identity/lifecycle not inferred.
```text | **Health Information Control** | **Security Context & Policy Ruleset** | Authorisation policy definitions (RBAC/ABAC rules), security context tokens, consent restriction matrices, and tamper-evident security audit trails. | Does not own patient demographic or clinical data. | ```
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E05.02`; additional scope correspondences: `E05.03`, `B10.04`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Durable Acceptance and Preservation of Clinical Events
element.documentation:
### Goal Statement Harmonia shall ensure that once an incoming clinical event is accepted by the platform, that event is guaranteed to be durably preserved and cannot be silently lost due to subsequent crashes, power interruptions, hardware faults, or transient network partitions.
### Rationale & Context Clinical events—such as patient admissions, pathology test orders, critical laboratory alerts, and clinical discharge summaries—carry direct patient safety implications. The platform must eliminate the critical vulnerability identified in [Silent Data Loss via False Acceptance](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/assessments.md), ensuring that acceptance at the ingress membrane is backed by authoritative durability before responsibility is released.
### Architectural Boundary - This goal defines the requirement for durable boundary crossing. - It does **not** mandate a specific storage technology (such as a relational database, append-only log, or distributed file system). - Downstream realization is governed by [`REQ-FND-001` Durable Ingress Acceptance Boundary](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/requirements-constraints/foundational-requirements.md).

element.name: [CT3] Classification Governance
element.documentation:
Govern applicable classification definitions and their organisational standing.
Classification Governance establishes the definitions and organisational standing of applicable classifications. In this governed context, classification concerns sensitivity and the consequences of exposure or mishandling, rather than the clinical meaning supplied by terminology. Its outcome supplies a basis for consistent application and protection considerations.
**Boundary**
Classification is orthogonal to contextual compartment membership and does not by itself determine an access decision.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E04.02`; additional scope correspondences: `E04.05`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Manage Outpatient Capacity
element.documentation:
Understands and manages available, committed and utilised outpatient capacity through clinic/session, practitioner and room availability, appointment demand, patient arrival/waiting and operational progression. Retains specialty room allocation and clinician arrival tracking.
Exposure qualification: Query behaviour and Outpatient Operations ownership remain established; a meaningful outside consumer/mandate is not identified by the current description. That exposure relationship remains unestablished rather than populated with an inferred Actor, Role or Capability.
Capacity boundary: Operational coordination does not acquire authoritative booking/rostering or clinical-work management. Room-occupancy query remains narrower than the capacity responsibility; no enlarged exposure or new named Service is inferred.

element.name: [Topic] ServiceDelivery
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing the actual provision of a healthcare service within a particular subject, provider, place and delivery context.
- **Semantic Classification**: `Activity / Fulfilment` - **Definition**: An Information Concept referring to the real-world execution or performance of a healthcare service for a specific target subject (or facility target) at a concrete point in time. It represents information about the activity rather than becoming the activity or implying that Harmonia performs it. - **Key Characteristics**: Actual start/end timestamps, performing practitioners, delivery location, executing devices/equipment, and execution status progression. - **Healthcare Subject Invariant**: While clinical service deliveries typically associate with a `Healthcare Subject Context`, broader service semantics (e.g., *Facility Sanitisation*, *Water Quality Testing*, *Equipment Calibration*) do not universally require a Healthcare Subject.

element.name: Calliope
element.documentation: ### Accepted common Outcome model ownership — 1.1.23/001 Calliope owns the generic Harmonia Outcome model and its common closed Status/Reason semantics, including governed closed domain-specific Reason extensions. Calliope model ownership remains the default across Harmonia; operation execution does not confer ownership of the models used. The logical Outcome DataObject defines exact Success/Failure/Indeterminate status semantics without inventing Reason members, Java types, a runtime data store or physical packaging. Models and mutable governed DataSets retain their accepted separate responsibilities. - **Role/responsibility:** management/governance of foundational models, definitions and mutable datasets, including first-class Security and Assurance Nomenclature and authoritative review of ontology sets for Harmonia use. [U13](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u13), [canonical Calliope view](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md). - **Distinct submodules:** **Calliope-Models C41** supplies design/build-time Models, Metadata Types, Criteria Definitions, Topics, Filter Types, Filter Elements, core Harmonia element libraries and security/assurance definitions. **Calliope-DataSets C42** manages runtime mutable ValueSets, CodeSets, Structured Metadata and applicable governed ontology content. No common lifecycle or undifferentiated metadata repository is inferred. - **Authority:** development representations support type-safe human/IDE/AI-assisted programming; current membership/content uses runtime authority. Models/build definitions establish structural access contracts; DataSets do not bootstrap them. Definition ownership confers neither runtime execution nor originating clinical authority. - **Persistence/collaboration:** DataSets uses established Mneme/Mnemosyne responsibilities; Calliope is not a Persistence Manager. Governed workflow may reuse Ponos/Ergo/Praxis, without another engine or detailed management UI. Themis decides/enforces, Dokimasia assures and Kleio audits. - **Standing:** U13 settles the two responsibilities, not their packaging, runtime ontology boundary or representation/workflow mechanisms (CDG-24/49). Existing pure-library dependency constraints apply to Models; U15 resolves the [realisation boundary](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md#calliope-realisation). General converter-support versus activity allocation remains CDG-05; no terminology product is selected. #### Controlled authorisation nomenclature [U12](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u12) establishes these **release-bounded ValueSets**: | ValueSet | Architectural shorthand / meaning | | :--- | :--- | | `Application.Function.AuthorisationPoint.Names` | **Function.Name**: architecturally significant application AuthorisationPoints at which enforcement is meaningful. An AuthorisationPoint identifies a governed function; it is not itself a permission. | | `Application.Function.AllowedAction.Names` | **Function.Scope**: the bounded set of actions applicable at AuthorisationPoints. Existing concepts include **ACCESS**, **CHANGE** and **FORWARD**; these are not asserted to be the complete final ValueSet. | | `Information.Compartments` | Governed information compartments; an applicable dimension is expressed as **Information.Compartment**. | | `Information.Classification` | Governed information classifications. | `Application.Function.AuthorisationPoint.Names` SHALL be comprehensive enough to satisfy business security requirements for the release while constrained enough to avoid unnecessary management, development and support burden. Complete release-specific contents remain [deferred](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#identity-deferred-design). **Calliope defines/governs the nomenclature. Themis owns policy association, resolution and enforcement.** ValueSet membership alone grants no authority and does not establish every Cartesian combination as meaningful or permitted. The controlled vocabularies fall within [Calliope-DataSets](466ad8f75a954c0581b5bba090443849.md); their structural definitions/contracts belong to Calliope-Models. This allocation does not reopen U12 or permit unrestricted runtime changes to release-bounded content; detailed release/change rules remain deferred. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Calliope and Pylai use of established responsibilities. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. [Calliope-DataSets](53bf6815c7a54ed0abde9b1aad311843.md) owns governed mutable content and uses established Mneme/Mnemosyne access/persistence; this adds no persistence manager or Mneme service. Models/build definitions supply structural contracts independently of runtime DataSet availability. [PylaiServer READ/SEARCH](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pylai-external-interoperability.md#pylai-server-controller) uses Diadromí-Controller → Mneme Adhoc Resource Access / Adhoc Search → Mnemosyne as needed. Mneme remains the Context and Pragma Manager with four exposed services, not a generic Information Manager or external interoperability service. No ActionableTask/Praxis/Ergon is fabricated for this read-oriented pattern. [PylaiPathway ingress](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pylai-external-interoperability.md#pylai-pathway-ingress) establishes initial Task.input/Context through a specialised Ergo ContextLoader; semantic mapping remains in BusinessLogic. EgressHoros returns communication state/outcome before ContextUnloader completes. Neither Loader/Unloader nor Pylai establishes durable truth. Protocol success, engine success and authoritative Harmonia persistence outcome remain distinct, including uncertainty. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md` — ## Responsibility and decomposition. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. Calliope manages and governs Harmonia's foundational Models, Metadata Types, Criteria Definitions, Topics, Filter Types, Filter Elements, ValueSets, CodeSets, Structured Metadata, core Harmonia element libraries, and Security and Assurance Nomenclature. It also owns authoritative review/governance of ontology sets for Harmonia use. That review does not make Harmonia the originating authority for externally governed ontologies. The B1 conceptual [`Metabolē.Context.ActivityContext` vocabulary](../../business/business-object/c34b4929f71946708d37dbe6c1da920a.md) is governed consistently with this shared definition/model/nomenclature responsibility. It classifies the broad activity, separately from a request action or authorisation permission. The initial examples are not an exhaustive enum; this establishes no physical Models/DataSets allocation. Runtime policy resolution, authorisation decisions and enforcement remain Themis responsibilities. ```text Calliope +-- Calliope-Models design/build-time governed knowledge `-- Calliope-DataSets runtime management of mutable governed content ``` These are distinct logical submodules with different lifecycles and dependency characteristics. They SHALL NOT be collapsed into one undifferentiated metadata repository. Their names establish no Maven artefacts, processes, databases or deployment boundaries. The [realisation boundary](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md#calliope-realisation) separates Models' library dependencies from DataSets' runtime collaboration. ### Library dependency and runtime management > **Calliope-Models provides development/build-time library dependencies. > Calliope-DataSets provides runtime management and authoritative access to > mutable governed datasets.** The existence of DataSets does not alter Models' library/dependency semantics and does not make Calliope a persistence manager. Repository pure-library and zero-higher-layer-dependency constraints apply to Models; they do not restrict all logical Calliope responsibilities to libraries. DataSets collaborates through established Mneme/Mnemosyne access and persistence. No new static dependency or physical allocation is inferred from that runtime collaboration. ```text Calliope +-- Calliope-Models | design / code / build-time model and library dependency `-- Calliope-DataSets runtime governed dataset management / authoritative content access ↓ Mneme / Mnemosyne access and persistence Concept / structural contract → Calliope-Models Current governed membership/content → Calliope-DataSets ``` > **Build-time representation and runtime authority are complementary, not > competing, responsibilities.** Strategy's library/local-evaluation statements concern Models. Calliope is not a mandatory mediator of every runtime transaction; current governed content may require DataSets runtime resolution. Such representations can support type safety, code completion, documentation, static analysis and testing, with stable identity, meaning, constraints, known build-time values and runtime-resolution contracts. > **Development-time knowledge SHALL NOT be treated as authoritative evidence of > current runtime membership or content.** > **Development-time representation SHALL NOT require developers to sacrifice > normal type-safe/code-assisted programming merely because a dataset is runtime > mutable.** A runtime value is not invalid merely because an earlier build did not know it. Validation/membership uses current governed runtime authority; the generated-code, IDE, AI-tooling and runtime access mechanisms remain deferred. Structural contracts for accessing/managing DataSets SHALL derive from Calliope-Models and the software build/deployment lifecycle. element.name: [CT3] Healthcare Organisation Identity & Structure Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage identity and structural relationships of participating organisations and organisational units.
This capability establishes the identity and structural relationships of participating organisations and organisational units. It provides the business account of who the participants are and how they relate, which directory representations can then convey. The distinction matters because a represented hierarchy should not create organisational authority merely through document or interface nesting.
**Boundary**
Organisation identity does not substitute for location, practitioner or material Healthcare Service context.

That earlier incoming record has no Documentation or authored Properties; no normative definition, native statement, classification of individual statements, or additional responsibility is invented to complete that absence.
The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.

View placement corroborates the authorised containing SolutionFacet; the exact correspondence is retained in the iteration's folder/Grouping inventories. Existing canonical identities and all pre-existing architectural assertions retain their standing. Archi visual acceptance and HCRL closure remain separate.
Current naming follows the [final naming dispositions](../../governance/canonical-identity-and-naming.md#solutionfacet-naming-roles--dr-17-final-dispositions): friendlyName expresses verified Composition context; displayName supplies local presentation; canonicalName retains its independently governed value and existing qualification. element.name: [Feature] Operating Schedule Specification
element.documentation:
Define temporal availability, clinic operating hours, and on-call service windows.
Operating schedules make temporal availability and exceptions explicit for a service. They distinguish an existing offering from one available at the relevant time, while leaving actual resource readiness and operational capacity as separate concerns.

element.name: [Feature] Encounter Bed/Location Association
element.documentation:
Dynamically maintain the association between an encounter, care team, and physical bed or ward location.
Encounter association keeps the relevant place and care-team context aligned with the episode as the patient moves. Location changes are meaningful operational facts, but they do not themselves establish a transfer of clinical responsibility.

**Intent**
Establish and maintain governed information assets suitable for health-service planning, modelling and analysis.
**Boundary**
Observed utilisation, operational capacity and planned capacity are distinct; information provision does not commission services or allocate resources.

element.name: Omilia Application Services API
element.documentation:
Omilia.Server exposes an **Application Services API** used by Agora both to request collaboration operations and to receive managed-Room dialogue/activity.
```mermaid flowchart LR Agora["Harmonia.Agora: collaboration control"] -->|"Application Services API: operation requests"| Server["Harmonia.Omilia.Server: collaboration operations"] Server -->|"Application Services API: managed-Room dialogue / activity"| Agora Client["Harmonia.Omilia.Client: collaboration experience"] <-->|"Matrix protocol"| Server ```
Agora decides to create/change a managed Room/Space, add/remove a participant or publish information; Omilia.Server performs the operation. Room activity returns through the same architectural boundary. The exact API contract, technology and mapping to upstream Matrix interfaces remain deferred. Historical Admin, Client-Server and AS-transaction endpoints do not define this new contract.
Workflow/execution collaboration continues through Petasos with **no direct Agora-to-Ponos dependency**. Matrix DTO encapsulation, Themis default-deny governance and zero-PHI Room aliases/names/topics remain repository constraints. Membership or receipt of a notification does not confer information-access rights.
[U19](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u19) establishes the administrative interaction boundary: Administrator → Omilia → Agora → Administrative Function → specialised Administrative Ergon → governed subsystem operation. Stopped-Twin resumption uses this pattern, with normal authorisation, Context, execution and Kleio audit controls; Agora and Omilia do not directly resume or manipulate the Twin. The arrows describe semantic progression and retain Petasos execution handoff and Agora's no-direct-Ponos-dependency rule. Iris provides a separate path through Iris-BackEnd and does **not** directly interact with Agora or Omilia. Broader Administrative Function reconciliation is [deferred](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#administrative-function-finding).
Identity mapping/provisioning is collaboration integration, not authentication authority. Existing isolation constraints are not relaxed; detailed security, privacy and external/federated interactions remain deferred.

element.name: Ergon
element.documentation:
### Approved 1.1.24 incorporation — resulting candidate pending
The common framework owns context load/unload, checkpointing and recovery across ordinary Ergon, Behaviour and Dokimasia Ergon. Materialised IU working information may reside in its execution JVM's embedded LOCAL Mneme-Workflow-Cache; .input() is immutable and independent executions may materialise independent copies. Cache loss reconstructs context from authoritative information and durable work at the existing boundary, never by resuming inside a failed Ergon. Cache writes/checkpoints alone confer no durable authority. Outputs/context-save remain governed; local cache machinery creates no specialist recovery framework. Adjacent schedule/waitBefore/blockWaitBefore/new-Pragma deferral discussion retains execution-contract ownership and is not specified here as a new scheduling API.
- **Role/responsibility:** a single well-defined software component encapsulating a bounded fine-grained task-completion activity set within the Ergo contract, executed/managed through Ponos. [U01/U02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u02), [L03/L19](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#l03). - **Features:** specialised transformation/mapping, validation, identifier/reference checking, enrichment, routing, result processing, fan-out or registry-change behaviour. Reuses C05 common facilities; `ErgonBase` is historical contract support, not an architectural inheritance requirement. - **Information:** acts upon or generates Pragma, payload/resource information, outputs, checkpoints and observations through governed contracts. It primarily acts on loaded Context values, may change working values and may generate new Content as **Pragma Output**, distinct from Context mutation. Bounded **Adhoc Resource Access / Adhoc Search** remains permitted for emerging needs. **No discrete Information Architecture representation or Ergon Information Resource exists merely because the component is an Ergon.** Activity is not information about it. - **Output progression:** one or more execution outputs may yield multiple Pragma. The [Pathway-continuation role](../data-object/27ad143e7c784e378556af8a57c438f7.md) identifies information continuing the current Praxis; independently resulting Pragma remain available for governed use, without automatically advancing it. - **Persistence/collaboration:** requests governed information use/change through Mneme; does not own Pragma management or durable state. Erga collects components; Ponos executes them; Petasos effects persistent handoff. Every Ergon exposes IngressEndpoint and EgressEndpoint C29; traversal does not expose internal logic. Praxis relationship detail remains open. The originating Ergon owns no persistence mechanics, shard/database transactions or generic conflict resolution; exceptional harmonisation is new governed work under U10. - **Specialisations:** Behaviour C25, Dokimasia Ergon C26 and, through the latter, AI Assurance Ergon C27. They retain normal Ergo/Ergon facilities, constrained by the specialised role and Dokimasia's terminal rules where applicable. - **Standing/exclusions:** bounded behaviour established for the candidate; competing atomic/pure/idempotent/branching claims remain CDG-05. An ordinary Ergon may intentionally invoke an AI service internally as an implementation choice without becoming AI Assurance Ergon or transferring authority.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Expected resource set and the Ergon information boundary. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
**Praxis manages the definition of Context required by the Ergo framework** for fulfilment of its Pathway. In R1.x/R2.x these requirements are concretely defined. During development/definition, an **Ergo identifies the resource set it is most likely to access**, within the applicable Context definitions. The set is deliberately **not exhaustive**. The Ergo framework applies those definitions and works with Mneme to efficiently load anticipated values before Ergon Business Logic executes; preloading every conceivably accessible resource is not required.
```text Praxis Context definitions / Ergo likely resource declaration ↓ Expected / Likely Resource Set ↓ Mneme Context Load ↓ Context Loader ↓ Ergon Business Logic ↓ Context Unloader ↓ Mneme Context Save ```
| Boundary | Responsibility | | :--- | :--- | | **Mneme Context Load** | Locate/acquire, map, establish authoritative state/version basis, apply controls and compose values to materialise the managed Context. | | **Ergo Context Loader** | Ordinarily exposes the **already-loaded Context** to Ergon Business Logic, without taking over Mneme resource acquisition. U14's [special Pylai ingress](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pylai-external-interoperability.md#pylai-pathway-ingress) instead establishes initial Context/Task.input from Communication Information through established Mneme/persistence responsibilities; it performs no semantic mapping. | | **Ergon Business Logic** | Perform bounded activity, primarily reading and acting upon values within its Context, with governed Adhoc acquisition where required. | | **Context Unloader** | Bring resulting bounded processing back across the business-logic boundary, preserving resulting Context state and Pragma Outputs. It is **not a persistence mechanism**. | | **Mneme Context Save** | Resume Mneme management of resulting Context state and the subsequent information consequences of Pragma Outputs; determine appropriate normal or exceptional handling. |
Context Load is the **preferred, performance-optimised common path**. Ergon Business Logic SHOULD primarily use loaded values. It MAY use **Adhoc Resource Access** and **Adhoc Search** where bounded activity requires runtime acquisition, particularly for interaction with external systems, deep interrogation outside reasonably known boundaries, or dynamically emerging information requirements. Adhoc access may be materially more expensive than Context Load; it remains legitimate. External interactions retain Pylai's established boundary.
Bounded Adhoc acquisition does not establish criteria-driven dynamic Context determination. That direction, together with dynamically configured reusable/ generic Ergo, remains **deferred R3.x direction**; no mechanism or AI-driven selection/configuration is introduced by [U18](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u18).
The originating Ergon SHALL NOT be responsible for persistence mechanics, database/shard selection, transactions, persistence tagging/indexing or generic conflict resolution. No exact loader/unloader API, acquisition/batching strategy, query language, locking/MVCC or Context concurrency algorithm is selected.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/search-results.md` — ## 3. External Information Search within an Ergo Activity. Standing: Adjudicated search boundary; exact source qualifications retained.
> **An external search performed by Harmonia is intentionally undertaken > within an Ergo activity. Information returned by that search is acquired > and persisted within the governed context of that activity and does not > require a separate generic management-acceptance transition.**
For the architecture currently in scope, Harmonia does not randomly or autonomously search external sources. The Ergo activity intentionally invokes the search and provides the governed context in which the returned information is obtained and persisted as activity information. Management responsibility attaches within that activity's governed information context and applicable Information Unit boundary; it is not a new acceptance decision merely because the source is external. This establishes no universal Unit per returned item, per external result or per activity.
```text Ergo Activity | +-- intentionally invokes External Search | | | v | Returned Information | | +--------+ | v Governed Ergo Activity / Context | v Persisted Activity Information ```
This is an intentional governed acquisition, not a rule that arbitrary observation, storage or consumption establishes management. The generic `Observed -> Accepted Into Management` transition is unnecessary for this case. Originating authority remains source-qualified; acquisition confers no authority over the underlying domain activity. The diagram expresses information meaning, not proof that every invocation succeeds or persistence has completed; AX-15 continues to preserve uncertain operational outcomes.
### 3.1 External Content and Semantic Opacity
Returned domain content may remain semantically opaque to Harmonia. Ergo logic may inspect, apply, associate, transform, route, persist or otherwise act upon it according to explicitly established behaviour. This does not imply that Harmonia independently infers the content's domain meaning.
The established [observable-information and governed Ergo logic boundary](49c9eb2bef0c47b8b5328621d5fc5479.md) continues to apply. No new execution allocation, intrinsic inference or runtime-AI responsibility is established.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/guardrails/observable-information-and-domain-meaning.md` — ## 3. Governed Ergo Logic Boundary. Standing: Adjudicated observable-information boundary; runtime AI optional.
The Harmonia Platform is responsible for the governed execution boundary around developer-defined Ergo business logic:
```text Context Loading | v Ergo Logic Process | v Context Unloading ```
This is a conceptual boundary, not a new component allocation, interface, runtime topology or definition of loading/unloading machinery. It does not redesign Ergo/Ergon, Praxis, Pragma, Ponos or Digital Twin.
Developer-defined Ergo logic may understand or deliberately interpret known content sufficiently to perform its intended function. It may inspect content, apply rules, transform or map information, append information to a model, invoke terminology or other domain services, invoke an AI agent/service, calculate results and produce outputs. Such intentional interpretation belongs to that defined logic or invoked service; it does not imply intrinsic domain comprehension by the Harmonia Platform. Platform governance and the applicable work, information and domain-authority boundaries remain in force.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F07 | Reusable activity contract, bounded transformation/validation/enrichment and meaningful collections | Praxis manages concrete R1.x/R2.x Context definitions; Ergo C05 declares likely resource set; Mneme Context Load materialises; Ergo Loader exposes Context; Ergon C23 acts; Unloader returns results to Mneme Context Save; Erga C24 assembles/manages/observes | Loaded resource values, changed working values and new Content as Pragma Output remain distinct; output processing may yield multiple independent/continuation Pragma; bounded Adhoc acquisition supported | U10/U18 refine U01/U02/A05. Resource set non-exhaustive; Unloader is not persistence; originating Ergon owns no shard/transaction/generic conflict resolution mechanics. CDG-05/45/53; R3.x dynamic Context and dynamically configured reusable/generic Ergo deferred. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.

## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/guardrails/observable-information-and-domain-meaning.md` — ## 4. Runtime AI as an Optional Adjunct. Standing: Adjudicated observable-information boundary; runtime AI optional.
**Runtime AI is an adjunct execution capability intentionally invoked by developer-defined Ergo business logic.** It is optional: Ergo execution may use deterministic logic, rules/algorithms and governed information/services without AI. Invocation does not make AI intrinsic to Harmonia or imply that the Platform independently derives domain meaning.
Using an AI agent/service does not alter Ergo/Praxis/Digital Twin responsibility, authority, governance or execution semantics. Architectural responsibility remains with the governed Harmonia construct invoking the capability. Invocation alone does not make the AI a Digital Twin, Business Role, Service Guardian, governance authority, independent workflow authority or owner of business responsibility, and transfers no architectural authority to it. AI and assurance do not define Twin identity; the existing [Strategy Digital Twin boundary](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/strategic-views/logical-component-responsibilities.md#component-7-digital-twin-entity-centred-operational-coordination-construct) remains controlling.
This general position does not allocate an AI-backed assurance activity or a Dokimasia execution engine, or establish new AI governance, orchestration or implementation. Assurance-specific uses and downstream execution allocation are outside this bounded reconciliation; unestablished matters remain explicit under AX-17.
### 4.1 Runtime AI and AI-Assisted Development
**AI-assisted development** uses AI tooling to design, document, analyse, test or implement Harmonia. Using such tooling to build Harmonia does not make it a participant in runtime business execution.
**Runtime AI** is an AI agent/service intentionally invoked by runtime Ergo business logic to contribute to governed execution. The distinction concerns the purpose of invocation, not the product name. Neither development-time use nor runtime invocation establishes intrinsic Platform intelligence.

**Ergon** is a single, well-defined software component encapsulating a bounded, fine-grained task-completion activity set. It supplies specialised activity/business behaviour within the Ergo boundary and is executed/managed through Ponos. An Ergon has no discrete Information Architecture representation merely because it is an Ergon.
### DesignNote-Energeia-DigitalTwin-Dokimasia-Specialisation — original lines 25-25
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Energeia-DigitalTwin-Dokimasia-Specialisation.md`; U02/U06/U19; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
**Erga** is a meaningful collection of Ergon for: (a) collating components into executable hubs; (b) capturing/observing activity where multiple concurrent Ergon, including instances of the same type, may execute; and (c) libraries of conceptually related Ergon suitably constrained for coherent change-management, testing, versioning and release. Erga is not merely an informal plural or List<Ergon>.

A **Dokimasia Ergon** is an Ergon specialisation representing a bounded assurance activity executed within a Dokimasia workflow. It inherits standard Ergo/Ergon execution, context, integration, reporting and process-management contracts, subject to Dokimasia constraints.

An **AI Assurance Ergon** is a candidate Dokimasia Ergon specialisation representing AI-based processing as an explicit governed activity within a Dokimasia assurance workflow. This is architecturally distinct from an ordinary Ergon internally calling an AI service as an implementation choice.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Classification Assurance
element.documentation:
Assure appropriate classification according to sensitivity and potential consequences of exposure/mishandling.
This capability evaluates whether classification is appropriate to information sensitivity and the consequences of exposure or mishandling. It examines the application of classification rather than merely the presence of a label. The responsibility supports protection decisions while retaining the distinction between the classification basis and the control applied to a particular request.
**Boundary**
Classification assurance does not define compartment membership or grant permission to access classified information.

element.name: [CT2] Health Information Protection
element.documentation:
Govern privacy consequences and adequate protection of the information estate and its environment.
Health Information Protection governs the consequences of information exposure and the safeguards protecting information and its operating environment. Privacy safeguards, estate protection, access-practice monitoring, compartment assurance and classification assurance address different questions. Together they distinguish appropriate arrangements from evidence of how information is actually handled, including physical and printed handling.
**Intent**
Protect information and the people affected by its use, with an intelligible basis for evaluating protective arrangements.
**Boundary**
Compartment assurance does not decide access. Subject-specific protection assurance does not create additional macro-level Health Service Assurance trees.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Material Logistics Coordination
element.documentation:
Coordinate clinically relevant material movement, custody, availability or disposition needed for care or diagnostic fulfilment.
This capability coordinates clinically relevant material movement and the custody, availability or disposition needed for care or diagnostic fulfilment. It makes the material's operational journey intelligible while retaining why the material matters to the clinical activity. The responsibility differs from moving a patient and from managing the diagnostic meaning of information derived from a specimen.
**Boundary**
Bounded clinical-material logistics does not establish a general procurement, supply-chain or enterprise inventory architecture.

element.name: [CT2] Theatre Operations
element.documentation:
Theatre Operations integrates surgical case progression and the operational consequences relevant to portering, sterilisation and recovery participants. It gives reported milestones an operational coordination context without originating the surgical acts they describe. Theatre-specific capacity remains a business responsibility even when shared information machinery supports several service contexts.
**Overview**
Theatre Operations integrates surgical case progression and the operational consequences relevant to portering, sterilisation and recovery participants. It gives reported milestones an operational coordination context without originating the surgical acts they describe. Theatre-specific capacity remains a business responsibility even when shared information machinery supports several service contexts.
**Intent**
Theatre Operations integrates surgical case progression and the operational consequences relevant to portering, sterilisation and recovery participants. It gives reported milestones an operational coordination context without originating the surgical acts they describe. Theatre-specific capacity remains a business responsibility even when shared information machinery supports several service contexts.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.

element.name: Distinct Management and Durable Preservation of Information and State
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Approach > **Maintain a clear separation between the governed management of Harmonia information and state and its durable preservation and recovery, allowing runtime management and persistence concerns to evolve independently without compromising information integrity.**
This course of action establishes that: - Runtime management of information, active relationships, context, and state is an operational governance concern requiring high availability, concurrent access, and responsive query navigation. - Authoritative durable state establishment, preservation and recovery atomically establish authoritative state and authoritative version progression, preserve the durable management metadata required to interpret that state, and ensure historical retention, immutability, and state reconstruction. - The distinction is strictly one of **architectural responsibility**, not a crude division between "ephemeral data" and "durable data". Information managed at runtime frequently represents durable healthcare concepts, but runtime management and durable preservation fulfill distinct architectural purposes.
#### Motivational Grounding & Traceability - **Architectural Axioms**: - `AX-05` (Active vs Durable State): Application-facing active state access/coordination and authoritative durable state/version establishment remain separate architectural concerns. - `AX-09` (Ephemeral Operational State): Transient execution states are reconstructable and decoupled from durable health records. - `AX-11` (High Availability & Responsiveness): Information access must not be blocked by backend persistence latencies or recovery locks. - `AX-14` (Preserve Distinctions): Preserve the boundary between runtime information governance and storage mechanics. - **Strategic Drivers & Goals**: 24/7 Clinical Operational Continuity, High-Throughput Access, Authoritative Preservation.
#### Capability Realisation & Configuration - **Primary Capabilities**: Shapes `EC-03` (Managed State & Lifecycle) and `EC-04` (Information Management). - **Component Boundary Impact**: Explicitly establishes the seam between **Mneme** (application-facing access and active information/state management) and **Mnemosyne** (authoritative durable state/version establishment, preservation and recovery). Neither component subsumes the other; Mnemosyne does not own operational activity progression, workflow execution, active distributed state, Digital Twin coordination, or application-facing query interfaces. Mneme may reject or coordinate a proposed state progression before persistence; only Mnemosyne establishes the new authoritative durable state. Following authoritative commit, Mneme converges its active representation toward that state. Mneme active-state generation and Mnemosyne authoritative version remain distinct concurrency domains (`AX-05`).
#### Downstream Direction (Domains 03–13) - Application Architecture (Domain 05) must forbid direct presentation/application access to database/JPA layers (enforcing Invariant 8). - Technology Architecture (Domain 07) must allow distributed in-memory data fabrics (for runtime state) and durable relational/document stores (for preservation) to be configured and scaled independently.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Catalogue and Index Management
element.documentation:
Manage descriptive catalogues/indexes through which information existence and location can be established.
This capability maintains the descriptive aids through which information existence and location can be established. It makes information discoverable without equating the catalogue entry with the content it describes. Within information management it answers where relevant information may be found before the separate question of obtaining it under an authorised context.
**Boundary**
Discoverability does not authorise access, retrieve the content or communicate it to a recipient.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E02.02.01`; additional scope correspondences: `E02.02.02`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Terminology Utilisation Oversight
element.documentation:
Oversee actual terminology/reference-set use and identify inappropriate, inconsistent or drifting usage.
Terminology Utilisation Oversight considers how terminology and reference sets are actually used. It identifies inappropriate application, inconsistency or semantic drift that the existence of an approved terminology does not prevent. Its purpose is to preserve coherent use without making each consuming capability the owner of terminology meaning.
**Boundary**
Use oversight does not redefine terminology or automatically authorise a local semantic variation.

element.documentation:
Establish population-health state, patterns and change over time from applicable evidence.
This capability establishes population-health state, patterns and change over time from relevant evidence. It interprets information at a population scope rather than treating a collection of individual observations as a population conclusion by itself. Its longitudinal purpose makes the temporal and population basis important to the meaning of the assessment.

Population assessment is not preventative-programme performance, an individual health conclusion or a service-demand decision.

element.name: Healthcare Interoperability Standards and Specifications
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Definition **Healthcare Interoperability Standards and Specifications** comprise the external, open, normative specifications governing healthcare data structures, clinical resource models, exchange semantics, and conformance criteria across enterprise and regional boundaries.
#### Enduring Strategic Role Harmonia is architected to facilitate vendor-neutral health data exchange across acute, primary, community, and diagnostic healthcare systems. This interoperability cannot be accomplished using proprietary vendor protocols. Harmonia depends directly on consensus-based, open standards to establish: - Standardised structural and semantic representations for clinical entities (encounters, observations, conditions, medications, diagnostic reports). - Conformance validation frameworks to assert that emitted and ingested payloads comply with normative specifications. - Standards-conformant external interaction contracts across the Harmonia boundary.
#### Current Strategic Instance - **HL7® FHIR® Release 5 Core & Australian Profile Specifications**: The principal contemporary instance of this resource is HL7 FHIR Release 5, alongside Australian jurisdictional profile specifications (AU Base and AU Core). - **Technology Independence**: The strategic resource is the **specification and standard itself**, not any specific implementation framework or runtime library (such as HAPI FHIR). The strategic dependency endures regardless of which runtime software serialises or deserialises the specifications.
#### Traceability - **Architectural Axioms**: `AX-02` (Boundary Membrane), `AX-03` (Native Standards), `AX-13` (Explicit Management Boundary). - **Enterprise Capabilities**: `EC-08` (Interoperability & Exchange), `EC-13` (Semantic Governance & Conformance). - **Courses of Action**: `COA-01` (Boundary Membrane Sovereignty).

element.name: [CT1] Diagnostic, Therapeutic & Clinical Support Services
element.documentation:
The specialised clinical services that support direct patient care, including pathology and laboratory testing, diagnostic imaging (radiology), pharmacy and medication dispensing, and allied health therapies.
Specialised services contribute evidence, professional interpretation, medication provision and therapeutic support to individual care. The established decomposition distinguishes diagnostic provision from medication and pharmacy services, while retaining wider therapeutic and allied-health scope as enterprise context. The catalogue deliberately explains the modelled branches without presenting them as an exhaustive inventory of clinical support.
**Intent**
Provide the specialised contributions that treating participants need to assess and care for individuals.
**Boundary**
Producing diagnostic evidence, authorising a report, dispensing medication and administering treatment establish different outcomes and authorities.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Requests, specimen associations, reports and medication events require reliable correlation and exchange. Supporting those information flows does not make Harmonia the diagnostic practitioner, pharmacy or therapy provider.

element.name: [CT3] Care-Place Readiness Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage whether a particular care place is ready for allocation or use.
Care-Place Readiness Management establishes whether a particular place can be allocated or used in its operational context. It connects the place's condition with its intended use so that vacancy can be distinguished from readiness. This is a place-specific responsibility within scheduling and capacity, supporting credible allocation rather than merely counting physical spaces.
**Boundary**
Readiness of one place does not establish collective readiness or usable capacity of the whole service.

element.name: [Topic] Practitioner
element.documentation:
**Definition**: An identifiable individual healthcare workforce or professional entity.
**Description**: Information describing an individual participating professionally in healthcare, independent of a particular organisational position, assignment or service context.
**Semantic Classification**: `Entity`
**Architectural Scope**: Represents the individual professional independently of statutory registration status. A `Practitioner` may be known to Harmonia prior to verification, when registration is pending or not applicable (e.g. unregistered healthcare workers, support staff), or when registration is externally authoritative.
**Boundary Rule**: $\text{Practitioner} \neq \text{Professional Registration}$. Registration is a governed assertion concerning a Practitioner, not the definition of the Practitioner entity itself.
Source standing: Established Package1 conceptual information meaning; residual qualifications in selected section remain unchanged.

element.name: [Feature] Outpatient Arrival Registration
element.documentation:
Ingest self-service check-in and clinic arrival events, notifying treating clinicians.
Outpatient arrival registration connects a check-in event with the treating context and required notification. Approved reusable composition supplies this integration responsibility; it does not require a specialised arrival Function or prove that a consultation has begun or finished.

element.name: [CT2] Interaction & Experience
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Provide contextual interaction between human actors, Harmonia, and enterprise presentation services, including visualization, alerting, and collaboration integration. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Mediating presentation interactions via dedicated backend-for-frontend gateways decoupled from internal databases. - Rendering clinical timelines, provider directory management interfaces, and operational console dashboards. - Providing contextual notifications and alerts to human users across web and mobile channels. - Projecting longitudinal record context into secure multidisciplinary collaboration spaces. - **Boundary Note**: Does not absorb the healthcare semantics of Clinical Collaboration or medical documentation. Consumes established identity and security context; does not own authentication, consent, or clinical truth.
Interaction & Experience makes contextual information and governed actions available to human participants through presentation and collaboration integration. Clinical timelines, directory administration and operational dashboards have different purposes, but share a need to retain established identity, security and information context. The recurring responsibility is usable interaction within those boundaries.
**Boundary**
Presentation does not own consent, authentication or clinical truth, and collaboration projection does not absorb clinical documentation semantics.

element.name: Centralised Synchronous Persistence Can Constrain Concurrent Processing
element.documentation:
### Assessment Summary Requiring central synchronous persistence interaction for every unit of active processing can introduce contention, latency, unnecessary I/O and coordination bottlenecks that limit concurrent throughput and scalability.
### Operational Hazard In a high-volume regional integration hub, thousands of clinical messages arrive concurrently from emergency rooms, pathology analyzers, and patient portals. If the architecture forces every active query, routing step, and transient coordination check to execute synchronous disk I/O and transactional row locking against a single central database: - Transaction lock contention and wait states escalate as concurrency increases. - Increased I/O wait times can cause ingress queues to fill and upstream connections to time out. - High-priority emergency point-of-care clinical queries become stalled behind long-running background batch imports. - Scalability is constrained to the physical I/O limits of the central persistence appliance.
*Note on Technology Neutrality*: This assessment diagnoses the fundamental hazards of synchronous persistence contention, latency, and coordination bottlenecks. It is an architectural evaluation of concurrency dynamics; it does not mandate any specific product, cache, database, or queueing technology.
### Architectural Implication & Response - The architecture must decouple active operational coordination from authoritative durable persistence. - High-frequency operational checks and client-facing queries must be served through responsive, concurrent access paths without imposing transactional lock contention on authoritative storage. - **Related Driver**: [Continuous Clinical Service Availability](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/drivers.md) - **Target Goal**: [Responsive Access to Managed Information](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) - **Governing Axioms**: [AX-11 (Responsive & Resilient Information Access)](../principle/8a1e995f16954484a78ae1c5c114d546.md), [AX-05 (Active Coordination ≠ Authoritative State)](../principle/0412a2084f0145babc4f022c71fea65f.md), [AX-09 (Default Ephemerality of Operational State)](../principle/9a5cb9e8876844e58e660f909f7df9fc.md)

Project qualified observed demand, capacity and utilisation for authorised planning consumers.
**Overview**
Comparisons need service, temporal and context qualifiers so that planned future capacity is not confused with present operational capacity.
**Boundary**
Projection does not establish a planning conclusion or allocate services and staff.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT3] Health Service Distribution Planning
element.documentation:
Determine the distribution of planned capacity across a geographical, organisational, site or service-network footprint.
Health Service Distribution Planning determines how planned capacity should be distributed across a geographical, organisational or service-network footprint. It addresses the placement of the planned response rather than only its aggregate scale. This allows the planning context to distinguish enough total capacity from capacity positioned where it is needed.
**Boundary**
A planned footprint does not establish recognised location records, identifiable offerings or actual resource deployment.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). element.name: [Feature] Emergency Treatment Capacity Management
element.documentation:
Represent current emergency treatment capacity under space, staffing and acuity constraints.
**Overview**
Bay state and length of stay contribute evidence but do not alone establish the ability to accept another care demand.
**Boundary**
Local responsibility retains its capacity meaning; Service Capacity Management consumes it without acquiring ownership or imposing one common capacity model.

element.name: Collaborative Reusable Capability Realisation
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Approach > **Realize bounded reusable platform capabilities (context, policy, provenance, EC-12 Operational Assurance) collaboratively across participating components rather than through centralized, bottlenecked runtime services.**
Harmonia requires pervasive platform capabilities—such as security policy evaluation, contextual propagation, operational assurance, and provenance tracking—across all transactions. This course of action establishes that: - **Reusable Capability $\neq$ Centralised Service (Guardrail G1)**: The existence of a reusable enterprise capability does not imply that a single monolithic service must execute it centrally. - Reusable capabilities define bounded responsibilities and common semantic rules. Participating components consume or enforce them through governed contracts without acquiring shared semantic ownership. **Distributed participation does not imply distributed responsibility. Cross-cutting concern does not imply cross-cutting responsibility.** - Centralized choke points and synchronous runtime bottlenecks are strictly avoided, ensuring horizontal scalability and fault isolation.
#### Motivational Grounding & Traceability - **Architectural Axioms**: - `AX-04` (Own Semantics / Use Machinery): Maintain sovereign capability rules while delegating execution across components. - `AX-07` (Intrinsic Security): Security and policy evaluation must be pervasive and intrinsic to all operations, not an external proxy. - `AX-11` (High Availability & Responsiveness): Eliminate single points of congestion and failure across the integration fabric. - **Strategic Drivers & Goals**: High Scalability, Fault Tolerance, Zero Bottleneck Architecture, Decentralised Resilience.
#### Capability Realisation & Configuration - **Primary Capabilities**: Shapes `EC-02` (Context Management), `EC-06` (Policy & Control), `EC-07` (Provenance & Traceability), and `EC-12` (Operational Assurance). Assurance here means the established EC-12 operational contribution; no independent Governed Assurance or EC-14 relationship is established. - **Component Boundary Impact**: Prevents components like **Themis** (Policy & Control) from becoming synchronous network choke points for every micro-operation; policy contracts are distributed and evaluated collaboratively.
#### Downstream Direction (Domains 03–13) - Application Architecture (Domain 05) and Technology Architecture (Domain 07) realise reusable responsibilities through governed contracts while preserving bounded ownership, scalability and fault isolation. Existing `themis-api` and `petasos-api` packages are illustrative downstream traceability only; Strategy does not mandate API packaging, local embedding, frameworks or deployment choices.
