Acknowledgement tracking associates delivery and read evidence with the communication transaction. Each receipt retains its contractual meaning; neither delivery nor reading alone proves business acceptance, clinical review, approval, finality or originating authority.

element.name: [CT2] Provenance & Traceability
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Preserve required origin attribution, meaningful transformation history, significant execution checkpoints, tamper-evident audit evidence and end-to-end traceability. Harmonia SHALL preserve provenance, audit and operational evidence where required by governing obligations, architectural significance, accountability, reconstruction, security or assurance needs. Routine technical activity SHALL NOT automatically require durable evidentiary recording. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Recording attributable, verifiable origin metadata for information sources, authors, and timestamps. - Tracking information-significant transformation history and required mapping checkpoints as information crosses system seams. - Capturing non-PHI operational and security audit trails for regulatory compliance (HIPAA, GDPR). - Supporting end-to-end transaction tracing across asynchronous processing pipelines. - **Collaborative Nature**: Participating elements preserve required provenance and audit context according to policy. Telemetry, operational facts, provenance, audit and assurance evidence remain distinct. Being evidence is contextual, not an intrinsic property of every recorded fact; preservation does not establish an assurance conclusion.
Provenance & Traceability preserves the meaningful attribution and history needed to explain information and significant activity. It connects source, transformation and required checkpoints without making every internal mechanism permanent evidence. Its recurring contribution supports accountability, reconstruction and assurance use while retaining the context that makes a recorded fact evidentially relevant.
**Boundary**
Telemetry, provenance, audit and assurance evidence remain distinct. Recording evidence neither establishes an assurance conclusion nor automatically requires retention of routine technical activity.

element.name: [UserStory] Failed communications are reduced
element.documentation:
Independent stakeholder need, expectation or desired outcome:
> Validate provider endpoints before sending information so that failed communications are reduced.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.
### Reconciled source contributions
- `UC-Integration-ProviderDirectory-23` — Validate Provider Endpoint Availability; Scope - Electronic Communication and Endpoint Management; [source](../../../../../openspec/specs/provider-directory-integration/uc-integration-providerdirectory-23-validate-provider-endpoint-availability/spec.md).
Source-specific access conditions, supporting actors, alternative outcomes, verification and data-authority rules remain distinct in their cited source contributions. Legacy claims that each statement is a business capability are not adopted: this instance has native Requirement semantics. Source target-state scope is not a software delivery commitment for 1.1.21. Historical assessment findings remain recoverable and do not establish current coverage.

element.name: [CT3] Governed Research Information Provision
element.documentation:
Provide existing health information for an authorised research purpose under applicable ethics, governance, privacy, consent, security and information-use constraints.
Governed Research Information Provision makes existing health information available for an authorised research purpose under its applicable constraints. It represents a substantive information contribution while keeping ethics, governance, consent, privacy, security and permitted use material to provision. The responsibility concerns supplying existing information legitimately, rather than running the research that uses it.
**Boundary**
Availability is not research authorisation. Trials, genomic analysis and research-governance responsibilities are not subsumed by this deliberately narrow capability.

element.name: [CT3] Entity-Relative Operational Progression
element.documentation:
Coordinate serial, entity-relative operational inputs and their interested behaviours.
**Overview**
Patient, practitioner and bed concerns recur across different business contexts; each can need a coherent progression frame without one central entity service.
**Intent**
Maintain a coherent operational reference frame as one entity reacts to successive inputs.
**Boundary**
Interest fan-out is distinct from intra-entity concurrency; entity progression does not acquire originating facts.

element.name: Bed Turnover Process
element.documentation:
• Owning Capability: Bed & Care-Place Management
• Process Purpose: Governs the rapid physical turnover, cleaning, sanitisation, and re-allocation of inpatient and emergency care-places.
• State Progression Lifecycle: Bed Vacated → Cleaning Dispatched → Sanitisation In-Progress → Terminal Cleaning Verified → Bed Ready / Available → Bed Allocated / Occupied
• Key State Dispositions:
• Bed Vacated: Prior patient discharged or transferred.
• Cleaning Dispatched: Cleaning job allocated to environmental services team.
• Sanitisation In-Progress: Ward cleaning or isolation decontamination underway.
• Terminal Cleaning Verified: Ward coordinator or supervisor verifies care-place readiness.
• Bed Ready / Available: Bed marked available for incoming patient allocation.
• Bed Allocated / Occupied: Incoming patient allocated and physically placed in bed.
Bed turnover connects the release of a care place with the operational work needed to return it to use. Its progression preserves the difference between vacancy, cleaning and readiness. A place can be empty while work remains outstanding, and a completed turnover does not by itself prove that the service has capacity for the next patient.
## Source-qualified contribution

Let authorised participants find and exchange the information their contract permits.
**Boundary**
Query execution, transaction coordination and boundary protocol mediation are separate responsibilities; none transfers content ownership.

element.name: [CT2] Search & Discovery
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Index, search, resolve, filter, and discover information assets, entities, directory endpoints, and healthcare services across the enterprise. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Providing multi-criteria indexed search across complex entity graphs (e.g., find active cardiologists at Location X accepting new referrals). - Resolving service and practitioner communication endpoints for addressed delivery. - Supporting bounded, paginated clinical queries across longitudinal patient records. - Applying dynamic security and consent filters to search results prior to egress. - **Anti-Responsibilities**: Does not dictate specific search engine indexes, inverted index implementations, or SQL query syntaxes.
Search & Discovery makes information, entities and service endpoints findable through governed criteria and bounded queries. It addresses the recurring need to locate relevant material or a destination before it can be used. Security-qualified results preserve the distinction between knowing that something exists and being entitled to obtain or disclose it.
**Boundary**
Discovery does not decide policy or prescribe a search engine, index format or query language.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E02.02`; additional scope correspondences: . Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [Feature] Bed Readiness Notification
element.documentation:
Notify bed allocation managers and clinical units when a cleaned bed achieves READY status.
Readiness notification exposes the established readiness of a care place to the responsible allocation participants. It makes a relevant transition actionable without deciding the clinical suitability of the next allocation or establishing whole-service readiness.

The client contract distinguishes confirmed capture from inability to capture, allowing required operations to fail closed.

The exposed boundary does not permit callers to assign themselves audit platform authority.

element.documentation:
Identify standards impacts across clinical/work practice, permitted medications, procedures, policy, safety, obligations and reporting as applicable.
Standards Impact Identification recognises the consequences of standards for relevant organisational activity. Impacts may concern clinical practice, medications, procedures, policy, safety, obligations or reporting, so the responsibility cannot be reduced to technical compatibility. It makes those consequences visible for the responsible capabilities to consider within their own authority.
**Boundary**
Identifying an impact neither adopts the standard nor acquires the operational authority needed to respond to it.

element.name: Service Assurance Status
element.documentation:
- **Canonical Name**: `Service Assurance Status`. - **Participants**: `System Steward`, `Service Guardian`. - **Purpose**: Enables the System Steward to obtain the current business progression state of an identifiable Service Assurance activity for stewardship purposes. - **Associated Business Service**: [Request Service Assurance Status](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#request-service-assurance-status). - **Boundary**: **Service Assurance Status concerns progression of the assurance activity and SHALL NOT constitute, imply or expose an unadjudicated Assurance Finding or Conclusion.** It supplies no provisional/predicted finding or incomplete assessment presented as a conclusion. Only System Steward consumes the associated Service; requesting assurance does not grant another Role access to status. Status taxonomy remains unresolved.
This Interaction is stewardship / management observation of assurance activity progression, not recursive assurance. Management Monitoring observes activity state to progress/manage activity; assurance evaluates a governed subject against governing criteria to establish a conclusion. Obtaining status is not itself assurance. The [non-recursion boundary](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#assurance-non-recursion-boundary) applies.

element.name: [CT3] Person Identity Administration
element.documentation:
Resolving, maintaining, and correlating identities and identifiers assigned to an individual across different authorities.
Definition — reviewed candidate
Resolve, maintain and correlate identities and identifiers assigned to a person across issuing authorities, retaining source-qualified correction history.
**Overview**
Resolve, maintain and correlate identities and identifiers assigned to a person across issuing authorities, retaining source-qualified correction history.
**Intent**
Resolve, maintain and correlate identities and identifiers assigned to a person across issuing authorities, retaining source-qualified correction history.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Person Identity resolves and correlates the identities and identifiers assigned to one individual by different authorities. It enables an incoming local identifier to be understood in its issuing namespace and related to other known identifiers without destructively replacing their history. Resolution, cross-authority correlation, alias association and governed correction preserve different aspects of that responsibility.
### Intent — predecessor explanation
Support reliable association of care information with the intended individual across participating systems.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Harmonia relies on authoritative upstream PAS/MPI information for R1/R2. Correlation and correction notifications do not establish an autonomous master-patient reconciliation engine.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Identity association is a direct platform concern because clinical records, orders and operational activity need an enduring subject context. Its Core standing does not imply originating master identity authority.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.
| Source predicate | Target element | Source standing / currentness | ARB native treatment | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Managed Entity & Relationship](910634fb1621416c818a022ab0b5d3a1.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-eae6d6072b4f58e1825337205605b9c2` | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Managed State & Lifecycle](6296abeee5074b9e80f21aea3a297e42.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-783e863158ec55c2b5c9a1648ba295d9` | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Search & Discovery](6a45701634f04b43919d9152a61e5f2e.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-7c25dc788ae3553d99771eff1152b612` | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Provenance & Traceability](68a0755aa4e14a509ac5e6c0bbcff3e7.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-76a2e24e2e935c9e91d0e8a6eb2f5c54` | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT2] Information Authority Qualification](cbba9984dd404deabed41fdcc96088b1.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-e64f76bbe27c530d8c8616059437de82` | | enterprise_enabled_by | [[CT3] Information Attribution & Lineage](8bc66c9bc1024a68a1bfd010b4dd1b79.md) | Proposed / current | Serving (reverse) — `id-f535f79890f9586a97dadb60c3ba83bf` |
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/01-entity-management.md` — entry lines 16-16. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.
- **Owning Capability**: `Person Identity` (under `Client Administration`)
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [7550fd5b17e643118fa76d2616e1ba20](7550fd5b17e643118fa76d2616e1ba20.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.
## ARB source correspondence
Scope/anti-responsibility and clinical/operational meaning establish the responsible Capability; descriptive ledger/registry/asset labels do not establish a separately bounded formal Information Concept. Preserve non-transfer and source authority.
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/information-responsibility/information-responsibility.md` — information responsibility row 1. Standing: Established Business responsibility only; formal information identity/lifecycle not inferred.
```text | **Person Identity** *(Client Administration)* | **Person Identity & Identifier Correlation Graph** | Ingested authoritative person identifiers and source-attributed identity information, namespace bindings, demographic traits, aliases, authoritative relationship correlations, and history of externally decided corrections/merge/unlink outcomes and their managed-state consequences. | Does not originate probabilistic matching, golden-record determination, authoritative master-person selection or person-merge decisions; does not own encounter registrations or clinical observations. | ```
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E05.07.07`; additional scope correspondences: `E05.07.02`, `B10.01.04`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Data Correlation
element.documentation:
Establish meaningful relationships between independently managed information items/sets.
Health Information Data Correlation establishes meaningful relationships between independently managed information items or sets. It helps information be understood together without requiring a merger of their identities, histories or originating authority. The responsibility is the association itself, rather than a clinical conclusion inferred from the associated content.
**Boundary**
Correlation does not establish person identity, clinical interpretation or ownership transfer between the related items.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Sharing Programme Management
element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
**Proposed overview**
Programme-level coordination supplies a plausible frame for the preserved name without replacing the established exchange abilities.
**Proposed definition**
Coordinate the governed scope, participants and change context of a health-information-sharing programme.
**Proposed boundary**
The element remains Candidate. The definition/placement elaboration is Proposed and does not adjudicate the unresolved RAD question or transfer source-domain authority.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
The RAD retains this named working concern while establishing only its corrected spelling. The name suggests an organised information-sharing context, but it does not provide enough governed meaning to decide what that programme manages or how it differs from the established exchange responsibilities. A fuller architectural overview would require inventing scope that the source has not supplied.
### Additional Notes / Unresolved Matters — predecessor explanation
Definition, tier and parent remain unresolved. This is an explicitly constrained description, not an approved programme-management responsibility or an allocated structural path.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Technology Management
element.documentation:
Manage clinical technology as a coherent business concern rather than only the device information Harmonia happens to use.
Clinical Technology Management treats a device as more than a data endpoint. Its responsibilities distinguish what device exists, what functionality and release it has, where and to whom it is deployed, how authorised users are supported, whether exchange is provisioned, what data is integrated and whether it should remain in service. These distinctions preserve the business meaning of the device estate beyond the subset of information used by Harmonia.
**Intent**
Maintain intelligible device capability, deployment and lifecycle context for clinical service use.
**Boundary**
Provisioning integration does not demonstrate that data has flowed. Monitoring, restoring device condition and deciding lifecycle disposition remain distinct; maintenance's tier membership requires adjudication.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [Feature] Order Cancellation & Modification Coordination
element.documentation:
Coordinate order cancellation and amendment requests, ensuring synchronization with performing systems.
Cancellation and amendment coordination carries a requested change into the performing-system context. It preserves the difference between asking to change an order and evidence that the change took effect, rather than silently rewriting the original request as though no prior intent existed.

Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Outcome
element.documentation:
The common Harmonia operation Outcome is a logical information model owned by Calliope under its default ownership of Harmonia models, including domain-specific models. It is not a Mnemosyne-private result, Strategy/Motivation Outcome, IU, native provider response or prescribed implementation Class.
Outcome contains status and reason. Status is the closed enumeration with exactly these accepted identifiers:
| Status | Meaning | | --- | --- | | Success | The reporter knows the specified operation succeeded according to that operation's contract. | | Failure | The reporter knows the specified operation failed according to that operation's contract. | | Indeterminate | The definitive outcome is not known at the time of reporting: “I don't know at this point.” |
Reason uses an agreed common closed vocabulary plus governed closed domain-specific extensions, including persistence reasons where required. Exact enumeration members are not adjudicated here; none are invented. Reason is operation-contextual and need not uniquely determine status. It is not an unrestricted free-text replacement for the governed vocabularies. Status and Reason are properties/semantics of this model, not mechanically allocated architectural elements.
The reported operation/stage must be clear: request receipt, accepted durable work, verified delegated execution, established authoritative persisted effect and remote/end-to-end completion are distinct. Timeout alone establishes neither success nor failure. Indeterminate does not excuse a provider unable to verify claimed operations, mandate later resolution or prescribe asynchronous reconciliation.
Mnemosyne reports its factual persistence Outcome; Mneme determines its subsequent consumer disposition. Treating an Indeterminate report as failure of Mneme's operation does not rewrite the persistence status. Safe retry and correlation follow owning contracts. This incorporation defines no Java/wire structure, model package, Reason members or provider completion-proof threshold.
### Incorporation standing
Accepted parent DRP semantics, incorporated under the operative Task for 1.1.23/001. Actual resulting candidate confirmation remains pending. Earlier component/source qualifications remain independently in force.

element.name: PHI Leakage through Operational Logging
element.documentation:
### Assessment Summary Emitting unmasked Protected Health Information (PHI) into operational diagnostic logs, monitoring systems, and tracing tools creates severe data breach exposures and violates statutory privacy obligations.
### Operational Hazard Software developers and integration engineers require diagnostic logging to troubleshoot routing errors, transform bugs, and network timeouts. A common developer practice is logging raw message payloads (e.g., logging an entire raw HL7 message string or complete FHIR resource JSON) at `DEBUG` or `INFO` levels.
In a healthcare environment, these logs are ingested into centralized search clusters, log forwarders, monitoring dashboards, and cloud observability tools: - Patient names, home addresses, phone numbers, Medicare numbers, and intimate clinical diagnoses become stored in unencrypted, broadly accessible log repositories. - Operational support personnel and external vendors gain unauthorized access to sensitive clinical data without clinical need-to-know authorization. - Routine log retention and aggregation triggers substantial statutory data breach notifications under national privacy legislation (e.g., the Australian *Privacy Act 1988* and Notifiable Data Breaches scheme).
### Architectural Implication & Response - Operational log streams must be structurally segregated from clinical data payloads. - Diagnostic logs must emit only non-sensitive operational metadata (transaction UUIDs, message control IDs, timestamps, masked identifiers) and strictly prohibit unmasked clinical observation values, demographic text, or free-text clinical notes. - **Related Driver**: [Statutory Health Information Privacy & Protection](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/drivers.md) - **Governing Axiom**: [AX-07 (Security Is Intrinsic to Managed Operations)](../principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md) - **Derived Guardrail & Requirement**: Classifies downstream as a mandatory Security Architecture requirement (`SEC-010` PHI-Safe Operational Logging), with formal governance guardrails owned under Domain 13.

element.name: CORE-001 — Information Authority Classification
element.documentation:
Harmonia shall support classification of information sources, ingress packets, and individual assertions as AUTHORITATIVE, INFORMATIONAL, or ANECDOTAL. Authority shall be contextual and independent of provenance, security classification, and access control. An authoritative classification shall express how Harmonia may treat an assertion within a defined information context and shall not independently assert clinical truth.
## ARB source correspondence
Same information-authority classification concern; source keeps downstream owning-domain reconciliation Candidate, independently of historical representation.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Safeguarding
element.documentation:
Ensure information and its operational environment are protected and resilient against loss, compromise, inappropriate access or operational failure.
Health Information Safeguarding protects information and its operational environment against loss, compromise, inappropriate access and operational failure. It frames resilience and protection as organisational outcomes, allowing physical controls, recovery arrangements and testing to contribute without defining the capability as a product. The concern is broader than any individual access transaction.
**Boundary**
Estate protection remains distinct from evaluating privacy consequences and from assurance conclusions about service delivery.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E05.05.02`; additional scope correspondences: . Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [Feature] Clinical Record Retrieval Mediation
element.documentation:
Mediate query-based retrieval requests across external and internal repositories.
Retrieval mediation connects a request with information held in participating repositories. It makes distributed retrieval possible without transferring repository authority, acquiring the clinical payload or treating a resolvable request as automatic permission to disclose.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E02.01.01`; additional scope correspondences: `E03.02.02`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Quality Reporting
element.documentation:
Communicate established clinical-quality measures, assessments, findings and conclusions to authorised consumers.
Clinical Quality Reporting communicates established quality measures, assessments and findings to authorised consumers. It makes the outcome of quality consideration usable beyond the assessment context while retaining its basis and standing. Reporting therefore represents a communication responsibility, not another opportunity to originate or silently change the reported judgement.
**Boundary**
Communicating a quality concern does not perform the operational or clinical improvement response.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [e5812fcdf3f5465b9b1d8ba536075c5f](e5812fcdf3f5465b9b1d8ba536075c5f.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.

element.documentation:
Ingest internal (portering) and external (ambulance, inter-hospital) patient transfer requests with clinical mobility requirements.

element.name: [CT3] Emergency Care Progression
element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Emergency Care integrates presentation and triage information and correlates it with recent admissions, summaries and known allergies. It supports a rapidly intelligible account of the patient arriving for emergency care without replacing the clinical triage decision. The context is valuable because the regional history may be distributed across participants outside the receiving department.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Ingested triage categories remain externally established clinical information; correlation does not confer emergency decision authority.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Cross-facility context and current presentation information materially support emergency care continuity.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: Discharge Progression Process
element.documentation:
• Owning Capability: Discharge Management
• Process Purpose: Governs the multidisciplinary coordination of patient discharge planning, pharmacy reconciliation, transport, and community handover.
• State Progression Lifecycle: Discharge Planning Initiated → Clinical Readiness Confirmed → Medications Reconciled → Transport & Services Booked → Discharge Summary Signed → Physically Departed (Illustrative preparation; publication, authorisation and exit distinct)
• Key State Dispositions:
• Discharge Planning Initiated: Estimated Date of Discharge (EDD) set on admission.
• Clinical Readiness Confirmed: Attending medical team declares patient fit for discharge.
• Medications Reconciled: Hospital pharmacy reconciles and dispenses discharge medications.
• Transport & Services Booked: Community nursing, home equipment, and patient transport booked.
• Discharge Summary Signed: Applicable signed summary is available/published and may be communicated before departure where the Business behaviour requires it; signing, finalisation, publication and discharge authorisation remain distinct.
• Physically Departed: Confirmed physical exit triggers departure notifications, updated bed-state communication and finalised-summary dispatch to external care providers under FEAT-HSO-29; care-place turnover follows its own responsibility.
• Timing reconciliation: Preparation, information availability/publication, applicable discharge authorisation and physical exit are distinct. Earlier preparation/communication is permitted; it does not realise a Feature triggered by confirmed exit. This illustrated local pathway establishes neither universal publication timing nor a universal discharge state machine, and adds no inferred publication event or authorisation state.
• Preserved uncertainty: Summary signing and finalisation are not universal equivalents. Detailed applicability, discharge-authority workflows and timing beyond the established preparation/confirmed-exit distinction remain unestablished.
Discharge progression coordinates the confirmations and practical requirements around leaving care. Clinical readiness, medications, destination arrangements and transport are related but distinct contributions, and the source progression retains its stated local applicability. Operational coordination does not originate the clinical discharge decision or prove that another provider assumed responsibility.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md` — entry lines 263-278. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.

Earlier preparation/communication is permitted; it does not realise a Feature triggered by confirmed exit. This illustrated local pathway establishes neither universal publication timing nor a universal discharge state machine, and adds no inferred publication event or authorisation state. - **Preserved uncertainty**: Summary signing and finalisation are not universal equivalents. Detailed applicability, discharge-authority workflows and timing beyond the established preparation/confirmed-exit distinction remain unestablished.

element.name: Receive Mobile Visit Progression
element.documentation:
Ingests arrival, visit-progression and safety check-in milestones from roving staff.
Derivation: FEAT-HSO-17 directly requires visit-specific milestone ingestion. It remains distinct from presence, capacity assessment and work-management integration. Received progression can inform mobile capacity without determining clinical work or clinical completion.

element.name: [CT3] Service Provision Relationship
element.documentation:
Binding health services to specific organizations, locations, and practitioner roles.
**Overview**
Service provision joins a named offering to the organisations, places and practitioner roles through which it is provided. The mapping is the owned concern; the identity and meaning of each mapped participant remain with its established capability.
**Intent**
Make it clear which provider delivers which service at which place and through which participating roles.
**Boundary**
Owns mapping associations, retaining the owners of each participating entity.
## Capability model replacement history

Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Assurance Design
element.documentation:
The capability to determine and define how satisfaction of a governed requirement, constraint or expected behaviour will be assured, including its assurance disposition, applicable criteria, required evidence and evaluation expectations.
Definition — reviewed candidate
Model how satisfaction of a governed subject or requirement will be assured, preserving applicable assurance dispositions and boundaries.
**Overview**
Model how satisfaction of a governed subject or requirement will be assured, preserving applicable assurance dispositions and boundaries.
**Intent**
Model how satisfaction of a governed subject or requirement will be assured, preserving applicable assurance dispositions and boundaries.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Assurance Design determines how satisfaction of a governed requirement or expected behaviour will be assured. It makes the disposition, criteria, evidence and evaluation expectations explicit alongside behaviour and failure/recovery design. Its output is a basis for assurance rather than proof that the implemented behaviour has satisfied the requirement.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Designing assurance does not confer approval authority, define the underlying obligation or allocate a runtime component. No Feature decomposition or CT ancestry is established.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Formal classification remains Unresolved. Its approved support to Health Service Assurance establishes purpose and Enterprise Capability contributions without adjudicating this separate relevance dimension.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT1] Security, Privacy & Digital Trust
element.documentation:
Establish adequate identity confidence, coherent access controls, privacy/protection safeguards, governed activity attribution and accountability for security-relevant activity and information use.
This capability establishes confidence in identity, coherent control of access, protection of information and accountability for its use. Its three branches distinguish identity/access governance, protection and privacy, and attribution/accountability. The scope includes physical and procedural arrangements as well as digital controls, preventing a software authorisation check from standing in for the organisation's whole trust responsibility.
**Intent**
Support information use and governed activity within legitimate identity, authority, privacy and protection constraints.
**Boundary**
Identifying an actor, permitting an action, recording participation and judging appropriateness are different outcomes. Evidence production is not itself independent assurance.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Security and governance are intrinsic to Harmonia-managed operations. The Core classification concerns assigned platform controls and evidence; it does not acquire every organisational security or privacy responsibility.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [b01441b2f5584fc2b9c3988643a7c93b](b01441b2f5584fc2b9c3988643a7c93b.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.

element.name: Governed Person Identity Correction Process
element.documentation:
• Owning Capability: Person Identity (under Client Administration)
• Process Purpose: Processes externally authoritative identity corrections and merge/unlink outcomes, applies their consequences to Harmonia-managed identity information and identifier associations, and communicates resulting changes with an audit history.
• Authority boundary: Person correction/merge decisions originate externally. Internal triage, evidence verification and approval concern applicability and governed processing of that authoritative outcome, not person matching, golden-record determination, master-person selection or originating merge adjudication.
• State Progression Lifecycle: Correction Requested → HIM Triage → Evidence Verified → Correction Approved → Merge/Unlink Executed → Change Broadcasted → Closed
• Key State Dispositions:
• Correction Requested: Externally authoritative correction or merge/unlink outcome received for governed application.
• HIM Triage: Health Information Manager reviews the received decision/outcome and its applicability.
• Evidence Verified: Authoritative source decision and supporting provenance/documentation verified.
• Correction Approved: Governed application of the externally authoritative outcome approved; this does not originate a person-merge decision.
• Merge/Unlink Executed: External merge/unlink consequences applied to Harmonia's managed identifier associations and audit history.
• Change Broadcasted: Downstream clinical systems notified of merged or rectified identity.
This Process governs the application of an externally authoritative correction rather than originating a person-merge judgement. Triage, evidence verification and approval establish that the received outcome should be applied to Harmonia's associations. The progression and change communication preserve why the managed identity account changed without making internal approval a master-person decision.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md` — entry lines 69-83. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.
### 2.1 Governed Person Identity Correction Process - **Owning Capability**: `Person Identity` (under `Client Administration`) - **Process Purpose**: Processes externally authoritative identity corrections and merge/unlink outcomes, applies their consequences to Harmonia-managed identity information and identifier associations, and communicates resulting changes with an audit history. - **Authority boundary**: Person correction/merge decisions originate externally. Internal triage, evidence verification and approval concern applicability and governed processing of that authoritative outcome, not person matching, golden-record determination, master-person selection or originating merge adjudication. - **State Progression Lifecycle**: $$\text{Correction Requested} \longrightarrow \text{HIM Triage} \longrightarrow \text{Evidence Verified} \longrightarrow \text{Correction Approved} \longrightarrow \text{Merge/Unlink Executed} \longrightarrow \text{Change Broadcasted} \longrightarrow \text{Closed}$$ - **Key State Dispositions**: - `Correction Requested`: Externally authoritative correction or merge/unlink outcome received for governed application. - `HIM Triage`: Health Information Manager reviews the received decision/outcome and its applicability. - `Evidence Verified`: Authoritative source decision and supporting provenance/documentation verified. - `Correction Approved`: Governed application of the externally authoritative outcome approved; this does not originate a person-merge decision. - `Merge/Unlink Executed`: External merge/unlink consequences applied to Harmonia's managed identifier associations and audit history. - `Change Broadcasted`: Downstream clinical systems notified of merged or rectified identity.

element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
**Proposed overview**
Maintenance/restoration is materially distinct from overall lifecycle disposition and monitoring; include the Candidate concern as a proposed eighth CT3.
**Proposed definition**
Maintain or restore acceptable device condition through testing, calibration, inspection, maintenance and repair.
**Proposed boundary**
The element remains Candidate. The definition/placement elaboration is Proposed and does not adjudicate the unresolved RAD question or transfer source-domain authority.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
This retained concern addresses maintaining or restoring acceptable device condition through testing, calibration, inspection, repair and related maintenance activity. Its purpose is distinguishable from observing device condition and deciding overall lifecycle disposition. The definition is useful architectural context, but the explicit seven-child device set omits this concern.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Membership, tier and ancestry require adjudication; this description does not establish an eighth Clinical Technology Management child.

**Intent**
Manage the identifying, descriptive, custody and relevant handling information needed to interpret a transported specimen.

element.name: Service Assurance Outcome Communication
element.documentation:
- **Canonical Name**: `Service Assurance Outcome Communication`. - **Participants**: `Service Guardian` and **one or more authorised recipient Roles** from `Care Coordinator`, `Service Coordinator`, `Regulator`, `Policy Authority`, `System Steward`. - **Purpose**: Communicates an established Assurance Finding or Conclusion to authorised Business Roles for use within their respective responsibilities. - **Associated Business Service**: [Communicate Service Assurance Outcome](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#communicate-service-assurance-outcome). - **Boundary**: The outcome is already established; communication does not assess/adjudicate, reinterpret or alter it. This Interaction is not necessarily a broadcast: one, some or all legitimate recipients may receive the applicable outcome according to authority, responsibility and information requirements. The requesting Role, status consumer and outcome recipient need not coincide. Communication need not require a documentary report.
Service Guardian does not become responsible for the recipient's interpretation within its own authority, management action, remediation, escalation, policy change, process improvement, clinical action or other subsequent response. Financial relevance does not establish Harmonia financial-governance responsibility; the [deliberate Financial Governance exclusion](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#financial-governance-exclusion) applies, with exact external recipients still unresolved.

element.name: [CT3] Policy / Obligation Governance
element.documentation:
Identify, interpret, establish and maintain authoritative legislative, regulatory, policy, standards, guideline, contractual and other obligations, attributable and traceable to source authority.
Policy / Obligation Governance establishes and maintains the authoritative requirements under which the organisation operates. It interprets applicable legislative, regulatory, contractual, policy and other sources while preserving traceability to their authority. The purpose is a legitimate account of what must be satisfied, rather than an operational choice about how to satisfy it.
**Boundary**
Interpreting obligations does not acquire the regulator's authority or determine operational means.

element.name: Work Order Progression Process
element.documentation:
• Owning Capability: Workflow & Activity Coordination
• Activity Archetype: Human Doing — physical or operational task executed by healthcare staff.
• State Progression Lifecycle: Created → Ready → Dispatched → Accepted → In-Progress → Completed / Failed / Cancelled
• Key State Dispositions:
• Created: Work order instantiated with scope, target, and required skills.
• Ready: Preconditions satisfied; available for assignment.
• Dispatched: Sent to target individual or worker group queue.
• Accepted: Worker claims task.
• In-Progress: Execution underway.
• Completed: Task finished with recorded completion telemetry.
---
## History
### Process Overview — predecessor explanation
Work Order progression describes a human undertaking physical or operational activity. Assignment, acknowledgement and outcome make the undertaking accountable without collapsing dispatch into completion. Its generic work meaning can support different operational contexts while leaving their domain authority and the clinical-work boundary intact.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md` — entry lines 282-295. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.

element.name: [Class] InformationUnit
element.documentation:
### Accepted Information Unit Framework incorporation — 1.1.22
This Calliope logical Class and [[BusinessObject] Information Unit](../../../business/business-object/10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md) represent the **same IU** at logical and conceptual levels. Its existing canonicalId, Class classification, Package Composition and names are preserved. No additional implementation Class is inferred from the semantic decomposition below.
```text InformationUnit ├── Identity: persistent UUID and its own Topic │ └── harmonia.mneme.iu.<hex-string-of-compressed-uuid> ├── Metadata │ ├── ManagementContext: operational Version; Active Generation │ ├── InformationCoordinates: PersistenceGateway; GatewayEndpoint; │ │ InformationLocation; InformationOwner (TopicIDs) │ ├── SecurityContext: IU-required Topics / TopicMasks │ ├── LifecycleContext: Mneme–Mnemosyne operational handshaking │ └── Relationships [0..*]: optional creator/updater-supplied references └── InformationRepresentation [1..1] ├── ContainerMetadata ├── ContentMetadata: Content Structure Topic; Content Structure Version └── Content: native information; native instance version only if supported ```
[Information Unit Metadata](../c05b7e37278141488ecc90b9a9ef96eb.md) and [InformationRepresentation](../b9891b88150840ada3daefdec6f26c35.md) define the two logical structures; their native Composition represents IU constituency, not separate governed nested IUs or a physical schema. Their internal concerns are documented in those structures rather than allocated a Class or Topic per property. [Topic](../9e2ffa9b4a1d4422a33c2a4bbcfc86ef.md) and [TopicMask](../bb489157a6bf48be926c5a601bb0a6c3.md) supply the common Topic/Mask semantics; existing named Topic instances retain identity.
The IU is **atomic as governed information**: one identity, exactly one governed representation and accepted-state consistency. Physical decomposition/references, multiple active manifestations and provider-native persistence remain permitted. A differently structured/formatted governed transformation result is a new IU; the transforming consumer owns fidelity and any reverse transformation. The IU does not manage alternative representations or relationship synchronisation.
Stable Feature-owned interfaces may expose characteristics without requiring clients to traverse internal metadata. No universal operation catalogue, additional exposed service, provider interface or mandatory attribute-population rule is introduced. The historical phrase 'Governed Representation with its Management Context' denotes this IU boundary; it is not a second independently governed context object.
The governed boundary associating a Governed Representation with its Management Context.

element.name: InformationUnit Constructor / Disassembler
element.documentation:
Mnemosyne's third responsibility tier decomposes governed IU structure into the logical pieces needed for persistence and reconstructs a conformant governed IU on acquisition. It preserves one atomic IU identity and exactly one InformationRepresentation, UUID/own Topic, applicable Metadata and Content, with no second governed IU merely for provider encoding.
The accepted 1.1.22 Information Unit Framework remains intact: Metadata separates ManagementContext, InformationCoordinates, SecurityContext and LifecycleContext; four coordinate references are TopicIDs. Operational Version and per-cache Active Generation remain Mneme ManagementContext concerns, authoritative durable progression remains Mnemosyne's AX-05 concern, Content Structure Version remains ContentMetadata, and optional native payload instance version remains Content. Provider-native keys/revisions never replace these meanings.
Not every transient ManagementContext field must persist. LifecycleContext supports Mneme–Mnemosyne handshaking. Physical decomposition must permit reconstruction of required governed attributes and unchanged native clinical/business Content. Native encoding/protocol details belong to the Persistence Adapter, and governed Content transformation remains creator/domain responsibility. Optional relationships retain local/remote validation limits, without inferred inverse links or universal graph synchronisation. Large binary pass-by-reference boundaries remain unchanged.
### Incorporation standing
Accepted parent DRP semantics, incorporated under the operative Task for 1.1.23/001. Actual resulting candidate confirmation remains pending. Earlier component/source qualifications remain independently in force.

element.name: [CT3] Preventative Health Education Services
element.documentation:
Provide education intended to prevent adverse health outcomes and influence preventative knowledge or behaviour.
Preventative Health Education Services provides education intended to influence knowledge or behaviour so that adverse health outcomes can be prevented. Its purpose distinguishes it from general organisational communication: the educational contribution is directed to a preventative-health need. It can support organised programme activity without being equivalent to programme management or clinical intervention.
**Boundary**
Communicating educational material does not establish individual clinical assessment, treatment or programme effectiveness.

element.name: Demonstrable Protection and Accountable Handling of Health Information (O3)
element.documentation:
### Outcome Definition Sensitive health information is demonstrably safeguarded across all integration operations, backed by default-deny authorization, zero-PHI diagnostic logging, and tamper-evident audit provenance that satisfies rigorous statutory data protection regimes.
### Clinical & Operational Value - **Patient Trust & Confidentiality**: Patients are assured that their intimate health data is protected from unauthorized access, eavesdropping, and accidental leakage into operational logs. - **Statutory Compliance & Legal Assurance**: The regional health network demonstrably complies with national privacy legislation (e.g., the Australian *Privacy Act 1988*, My Health Records Act, and Notifiable Data Breaches scheme), eliminating legal liability and multi-million-dollar breach penalties. - **Forensic Auditability**: Every state-changing clinical transaction maintains unambiguous, tamper-evident cryptographic provenance (who authorized it, what information was conveyed, when it occurred), enabling rigorous clinical incident retrospectives.
### Relationship to Motivational Principles Unlike Outcomes O1 and O2 (which receive direct handovers from specific strategic goals), Outcome O3 is an **intrinsic platform property**: - It is realized through the foundational architectural principles [AX-07 (Security Is Intrinsic to Managed Operations)](../principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md) and [AX-08 (Evidence Records Meaning)](../principle/21d6864657964ba5b03e3f6b5eb29cd5.md). - Security and privacy are enforced intrinsically across all governed ingress, processing, and egress paths rather than being isolated to a single integration workflow. - As established in the [Orientation View](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/orientation-view.md), AX-07 and AX-08 do not maintain causal arrows to outcomes; O3 acts as a common consequence sink for the entire platform.

element.name: [CT3] Client Privacy Guardrail Management
element.documentation:
Enforcing client-level privacy preferences, consent directives, and confidentiality markers.
Definition — reviewed candidate
Manage client-associated privacy constraints, preferences, permissions, restrictions and consent directives, and evaluate their applicability to information use.
**Overview**
Manage client-associated privacy constraints, preferences, permissions, restrictions and consent directives, and evaluate their applicability to information use.
**Intent**
Manage client-associated privacy constraints, preferences, permissions, restrictions and consent directives, and evaluate their applicability to information use.
**Boundary**
Owns client-associated constraints and consent directives; general enterprise privacy policy remains outside this capability.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Client Privacy applies client-level consent directives, confidentiality markers and privacy preferences to governed information use. It makes the person's restrictions operationally relevant at disclosure, query and presentation boundaries instead of leaving them as passive record annotations. Its responsibility complements the broader policy boundary while retaining the distinction between the directive and an action evaluated against it.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
A privacy flag does not become a caller-controlled grant of authority. Consent evaluation and information access must respect established policy ownership.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Consistent application of client restrictions across information pathways is a direct platform responsibility, supporting Core classification.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

- **Owning Capability**: `Client Privacy`.

element.name: [CT2] Calendar Management
element.documentation:
Calendar Management projects schedules and correlates events with temporal commitments. It brings rosters, on-call windows, facility calendars and appointment milestones into operational views without replacing their authoritative sources. This distinguishes the temporal context used for coordination from the business decisions that establish the schedule.
**Overview**
Calendar Management projects schedules and correlates events with temporal commitments. It brings rosters, on-call windows, facility calendars and appointment milestones into operational views without replacing their authoritative sources. This distinguishes the temporal context used for coordination from the business decisions that establish the schedule.
**Intent**
Calendar Management projects schedules and correlates events with temporal commitments. It brings rosters, on-call windows, facility calendars and appointment milestones into operational views without replacing their authoritative sources. This distinguishes the temporal context used for coordination from the business decisions that establish the schedule.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Projection does not author the roster or confer qualification, privilege or clinical assignment authority.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Consistent temporal projections and event correlation are direct platform coordination responsibilities.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/05-intrinsic-enablement.md` — entry lines 200-200. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.
- **Owning Capability**: `Calendar Management`
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [8b42aac6083441caa78b59f5e62eebd9](8b42aac6083441caa78b59f5e62eebd9.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.
## ARB source correspondence
Scope/anti-responsibility and clinical/operational meaning establish the responsible Capability; descriptive ledger/registry/asset labels do not establish a separately bounded formal Information Concept. Preserve non-transfer and source authority.
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/information-responsibility/information-responsibility.md` — information responsibility row 35. Standing: Established Business responsibility only; formal information identity/lifecycle not inferred.
```text | **Calendar Management** | **Projected Unified Temporal Timeline** | Composite chronological schedule projections, shift boundaries, and temporal activity correlation indices. | Does not own authoritative host rosters or booking slots. | ```
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B07.03.04`; additional scope correspondences: `E06.05`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Information Persistence - Constraints
element.documentation:
This existing element is a **SolutionFacet**, a specialisation of native **Grouping**. The [governed definition](../../governance/continuum-representation.md#solutionfacet-classification--1119-candidate) distinguishes accessible solution classification from Capability, responsibility and ownership. Its canonical identity, G01–G18 context, existing Composition and separately established Home assertions are preserved.
Native Grouping originally authored as `Information-Management.Information-Persistence.Constraints` in the retained 004 export, incorporated under the Solution Architect's Subject Grouping hierarchy Task. It groups the source-qualified `Constraints` concern within the existing **Information Persistence** SolutionFacet (G02.04). Its earlier authored name above is retained as provenance; current names follow the explicit properties in the 1.1.19 submission. That earlier incoming record has no Documentation or authored Properties; no normative definition, native statement, classification of individual statements, or additional responsibility is invented to complete that absence.
The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. These are distinct assertions. Neither diagram membership nor the Grouping's label alone establishes another Home or a statement allocation. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.
Source Exchange identifier: `id-9508b495e21740989bf5e86f7acecded`. View placement corroborates the authorised containing SolutionFacet; the exact correspondence is retained in the iteration's folder/Grouping inventories. Existing canonical identities and all pre-existing architectural assertions retain their standing. Archi visual acceptance and HCRL closure remain separate.

element.name: [Feature] Active Clinical Record Access
element.documentation:
Provide low-latency, active distributed access to consolidated patient clinical summaries.
Active access supports responsive use of consolidated clinical summaries in ongoing care. The working representation remains reconstructable active state; speed and availability do not promote it to authoritative durable truth when persistence or convergence is unavailable.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Knowledge Management
element.documentation:
Identify, extract, formulate, associate, govern and share reusable clinical knowledge.
Clinical Knowledge Management turns potentially useful source material into explicit reusable knowledge with an intelligible basis and governed standing. Context identification and extraction preserve where material came from; formulation expresses applicability and rationale; concept association supplies semantic context; review and publication govern its intended use. These responsibilities distinguish source information, formulated knowledge and approved knowledge without prescribing a compulsory workflow.
**Intent**
Make reusable clinical knowledge available with the qualifications and approval standing needed to judge its use.
**Boundary**
Publication does not establish applicability to an individual or a clinical decision. Concept association does not redefine terminology, and formulation does not constitute approval.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: Context Topic
element.documentation:
> **Context is a versioned, temporal load-snapshot composed from authoritative > resource values materialised for a Harmonia activity's anticipated information > requirements.**
Context contains **values, not merely references**. Each value represents the defined authoritative resource state/version actually materialised when it is incorporated. Loaded values are composed into the Context bucket:
```text Context — identity / Context version / temporal load basis └── Resource Bucket [Composition] ├── Resource Value A @ authoritative state/version ├── Resource Value B @ authoritative state/version └── Resource Value C @ authoritative state/version ```
**Composition** concerns loaded values belonging to the snapshot. The Context does not existentially own the underlying authoritative resources. This is distinct from the separately established Aggregation relationships for Praxis, Journey and PragmaFactory.
Context version and constituent resource authoritative state/version SHALL remain distinct. Neither is an alias for a valid active-state generation or security PEP-Context. Materialisation does **not** imply a globally transactionally consistent distributed snapshot or a universal frozen instant. Context is the Ergon's managed working information environment, not a closed universe of all information it may access or produce.
Authoritative constituent resource state may progress while an Ergon operates. Mneme needs sufficient state/version information to recognise delivery that cannot safely proceed normally; generic conflict handling remains outside the originating Ergon. No concurrency or conflict-detection algorithm is established here.
This activity Context does not redefine Domain04's Information Unit [Management Context](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#65-context). Their detailed mapping, physical bucket representation, Context identity/version mechanisms and concurrency algorithms remain unresolved under AX-17.
Source standing: Bounded adjudicated application information meaning; Domain05 remains the accepted candidate Step-B baseline, not final Solution Architecture. Detailed representation is deferred; only this defined logical object is projected.

They do not accept the whole Domain05 candidate or create a new element per paragraph. Later-corrected assertions are retained in the disposition evidence instead of being restored here.

Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md`; U19; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
Each Behaviour has its own **Praxis-defined Context requirements**. Mneme loads Context fresh when that Behaviour begins, and manages its Context Save:
### DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics — original lines 222-227
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md`; U19; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
On the normal path, Behaviour B's Context is loaded **after A has completed and saved its information consequences**; C's is loaded after B, and so forth. Progression after failure remains subject to section 10. Later Behaviours may therefore observe authoritative information consequences established by earlier Behaviours. There is **no single immutable input-level Context snapshot** shared by all interested Behaviours.
### DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics — original lines 229-235

Normal [Loader/Unloader versus Load/Save boundaries](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md#ergon-information-access) apply. Mnemosyne alone establishes authoritative durable state; working changes and Context Save invocation do not manufacture confirmed persistence outcomes. Existing exceptional harmonisation and AX-15 uncertainty semantics remain intact. This note adds no cross-Behaviour transaction, universal globally consistent snapshot or conflict-resolution mechanism.

Energeia had previously been useful as an architectural boundary around Harmonia execution constructs including Ponos, DigitalTwin, Dokimasia, Ergo, Ergon and Erga. That alone did not provide a sufficiently strong reason for Energeia to exist as a discrete Software Component rather than merely as a grouping or boundary.

element.name: [CT3] Governed Health Information Retrieval
element.documentation:
Retrieve and search health information and apply access-qualified result filtering under established access and consent determinations.
**Overview**
Retrieve and search health information and apply access-qualified result filtering under established access and consent determinations. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Retrieve and search health information and apply access-qualified result filtering under established access and consent determinations.
**Boundary**
Information administration and coordination preserve the authority of the responsible source, clinical actor and governed domain; they confer no additional real-world management authority.

element.name: [Feature] Medication Administration Record (MAR) Ingestion
element.documentation:
Ingest point-of-care medication administration events.
MAR ingestion captures source-reported point-of-care administration events. It preserves the crucial distinction between intended or supplied medication and an administration recorded as performed, without originating that bedside event or its clinical authority.

element.name: [Topic] CarePlace
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing the characteristics and intended healthcare function of a place in which care may be provided, independently of its transient operational state.
- **Semantic Classification**: `Definition` - **Definition**: The static engineering, physical infrastructure, and architectural specification of a bed bay or clinical treatment point. - **Key Characteristics**: Physical capacity, isolation classification (e.g. *Negative Pressure*, *Positive Pressure*, *Standard*), medical gas outlet provisions (e.g. *Oxygen*, *Suction*, *Medical Air*), emergency power backup, and fixed telemetry wiring. - **Architectural Boundary**: Captures what the physical care-place **is** built to support, independent of its transient operational occupancy.

element.name: [CT3] Care Resource Deployment
element.documentation:
Apply legitimately available and appropriately authorised resources to a current or planned operational care requirement, particularly using roster/on-call and service-coverage context.
Care Resource Deployment applies legitimately available resources to a current or planned care requirement. It considers coverage, role, qualification, engagement and privilege context to distinguish availability in principle from deployment to a particular need. Its contribution is the operational application of resources, without changing the authoritative facts that make their use legitimate.
**Boundary**
Deployment is neither roster authoring nor clinical work assignment and does not confer clinical authority or ownership of enterprise assets.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: [UserStory] Renewals can be obtained before expiry
element.documentation:
Independent stakeholder need, expectation or desired outcome:
> Identify clinicians with expiring registrations or licences so that renewals can be obtained before expiry.
