element.name: Themis
element.documentation: ### Accepted Information Unit Framework incorporation — 1.1.22 The protected [IU](../data-object/class/74ec609de1ae498fbf9d13e4ef8c6cbe.md)'s SecurityContext carries required Topics and/or shared TopicMasks. These are subject-side requirements, distinct from an authenticated Identity's effective Passport/AuthorisationMap and the established PEP-Criteria supplied through PEP-Context. A Themis-owned local PEP evaluates applicable requirements, valid Identity context and requested operation; a TopicMask match alone is no authorisation grant. InformationCoordinates owner/location/gateway supplies no permission. Existing action/compartment criteria are reused without a parallel taxonomy or mandatory unitCriteria/containerCriteria/contentCriteria Classes. Request/session security context is not automatically durable IU Content/Metadata. This adds no schema-level equivalence or replacement of PEP-Criteria/PEP-Context by a new Passport Class. - **Role/responsibility:** **Themis owns and manages Harmonia's Authorisation Model**, including PAP, PRP, PDP, Criteria/collections, AuthorisationRoles, Identity assignments, role/group resolution, Criteria compilation and the distributed PEP framework. Themis consumes trusted authenticated Identity; it does not authenticate that Identity. [U12](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u12) refines [U08](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u08) within [AX-07](../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md). - **PAP — Policy Administration Point:** administration and lifecycle management of the Themis-owned model. Management/review/approval activity uses [Ergo/Praxis and Iris](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#authorisation-administration); detailed Praxes/Erga, UI and versioning mechanisms remain deferred. No general-purpose policy language is implied by policy administration. - **PRP — Policy Repository Point:** authoritative repository semantics for the Authorisation Model. Durable persistence may be delegated through **Themis PRP → Mneme → Mnemosyne Harmonia Configuration & Governance**. This requires no dedicated Themis physical database and transfers no model ownership to persistence. - **PDP — Policy Decision Point:** resolves authoritative policy, authenticated Identity and applicable context into precomputed Identity-specific **PEP-Criteria**, supplied through **PEP-Context** for local enforcement. An immediate decision remains possible; it uses the same governed semantics. - **Governed actions:** **Can I ACCESS XYZ? Can I CHANGE ABC? Can I FORWARD DEF?** ACCESS, CHANGE and FORWARD are distinct; they SHALL NOT collapse into CRUD. FORWARD may depend on destination/context independently of ACCESS. Unauthenticated or unauthorised operations default to **DENY**; unavailable authoritative policy determination remains distinct from that decision. #### Identity.Authentication — separately provided trusted Identity **Identity.Authentication establishes WHO an Individual or System is. It is a Separately Provided Capability (SEP).** The primary pattern is standards-based OIDC/OAuth integration with an externally managed Identity Provider (IdP). Harmonia does not own or provide an identity-management, credential-management, password-management or MFA framework. > **Keycloak + PostgreSQL SHALL provide the default FOSS Identity Provider for > development, test and POC environments.** Keycloak remains an external, replaceable implementation component. Harmonia's Identity.Authentication architecture SHALL NOT acquire Keycloak-specific dependencies. This target does not prescribe a production IdP or an internal Harmonia credential store. Authentication establishes trusted Identity only; it SHALL NOT determine Harmonia Function permissions, Function.Scope or PEP-Criteria. **Identity.Authorisation** establishes what that authenticated Identity may do within Harmonia and is Themis-owned. The same authorisation model applies to human and system Identities; differing allowable assignments do not establish separate architectures. #### Identity and role terminology | Term | Candidate meaning and boundary | | :--- | :--- | | **Identity** | The authenticated Individual or System consumed by Themis. This use does not redefine Information Unit Identity or the Domain04 professional identifier assertions. | | **Practitioner** | The individual practitioner, retaining the [Domain04 workforce-entity meaning](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/practitioner.md#31-practitioner); registration status is a separate assertion. | | **FHIR PractitionerRole** | The formal practitioner role/service relationship represented through FHIR. | | **PractitionerCapacity** | The selected operational capacity in which a Practitioner is currently acting within Harmonia; it does not itself confer authority. | | **AuthorisationRole** | A named, governed, assignable collection of additive Themis Criteria and/or Criteria collections. It is distinct from PractitionerCapacity, FHIR PractitionerRole and a Domain03 Business Role. | | **Criterion / Criteria** | One governed permitted combination / multiple such combinations in the Themis Authorisation Model. | | **PEP-Criteria** | The precomputed, Identity-specific set of permitted combinations derived by Themis for constrained local enforcement. | | **PEP-Context** | The Themis-derived operational enforcement context for an authenticated Identity, through which applicable PEP-Criteria is supplied. It is distinct from the general Mneme working Context. | The [Domain04 Practitioner Role Binding](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/practitioner.md#36-practitioner-role-binding) and [Domain03 Business Roles](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md) retain their meanings. Neither lexical similarity nor FHIR convention establishes their mapping to PractitionerCapacity or AuthorisationRole. #### Criterion conjunction and additive grants A Criterion represents a **governed permitted combination** across applicable dimensions, using [Calliope-controlled nomenclature](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#authorisation-nomenclature): ```text Criterion = Information.Compartment AND Information.Classification AND Function.Name AND Function.Scope AND applicable Temporal constraints ``` The four principal dimensions describe **what** is authorised; applicable temporal constraints describe **when**. Within an individual Criterion, applicable dimensions are **conjunctive**. Between Criteria, grants are **additive / UNION**: each Criterion independently contributes its permitted combination. Only explicitly governed combinations have authorisation meaning. Absence of a matching effective Criterion results in **DENY**. **Explicit negative/DENY Criteria are not part of this Candidate Architecture.** Neither arbitrary Boolean policy expressions, deny-overrides semantics nor a general-purpose policy language is introduced by this model. #### Criteria containment, AuthorisationRoles and Identity assignments Criteria support containment, collection and nesting for management and reuse: ```text CriteriaCollection (conceptual label; final name unresolved) ├── Criterion ├── Criterion └── CriteriaCollection ├── Criterion └── Criterion ``` Flattening nested collections produces the same additive set of effective Criteria. Nesting creates no arbitrary Boolean semantics and requires no Role hierarchy. The exact implementation name/class hierarchy and representation remain deferred; this diagram establishes no lifecycle/ownership semantics beyond the stated management/reuse requirement. An **AuthorisationRole** is named, governed and assignable and contains Criteria and/or Criteria collections. Its contents are additive: ```text EffectiveCriteria(AuthorisationRole) = UNION(all contained Criteria) IdentityEffectiveCriteria = DirectCriteria UNION AuthorisationRole1.Criteria UNION AuthorisationRole2.Criteria UNION ... ``` An Identity may have directly assigned Criteria, one or more AuthorisationRoles, or both. This applies to human and system Identities. The UNION is of applicable grants, subject to governed assignments, temporal validity, revocation and applicable operational context; it does not remove a Criterion's conjunctions or require every contained Criterion to match simultaneously. #### Predetermined temporal validity and explicit revocation **Temporal validity** establishes predetermined applicability/validity bounds. Temporal constraints may apply to a Criterion, a direct Criterion assignment, an AuthorisationRole assignment and applicable operational context such as PractitionerCapacity. The exact temporal expression model remains deferred. **Revocation** withdraws an otherwise valid authorisation. It SHALL NOT be modelled merely as temporal expiry. Both concepts are required. Propagation of revocation and invalidation of already-issued PEP-Criteria/PEP-Context remain unresolved; no mechanism or continued validity after revocation is inferred. #### PractitionerCapacity and operational responsibility For a Practitioner, the available PractitionerCapacity set is constrained by the practitioner's governed profile and applicable operational context. The Practitioner selects **one active PractitionerCapacity** for the applicable session/operational or roster context. It supplies operational context used by Themis when deriving effective authorisation; **it does not itself confer authority**. Selection UI and the exact PractitionerCapacity ↔ FHIR PractitionerRole mapping remain deferred. > **Authentication establishes who the Individual is. PractitionerCapacity > establishes the capacity in which a Practitioner is currently acting. Themis > establishes what that Identity, acting in that capacity, may do.** ```mermaid graph TD Auth["Authenticated Practitioner"] --> Eligible["Eligible PractitionerCapacity set"] Profile["Governed practitioner profile"] --> Eligible Context["Applicable operational / roster context"] --> Eligible Eligible -->|"Practitioner selects ONE"| Capacity["Active PractitionerCapacity: context, no authority by itself"] Capacity -->|"authorisation context"| PDP["Themis: resolve governed Criteria / assignments / policy state"] PDP --> Criteria["Identity-specific precomputed PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context"] Criteria --> PEP["Constrained local Themis PEP"] Capacity -.->|"operational responsibility context"| Responsibility["Agora: membership intent; detailed context use deferred"] ``` Themis answers **“May this Identity perform this action on this information?”** Future Agora collaboration detail concerns **“Is this Practitioner currently responsible for receiving/responding to this operational activity?”** These are separate responsibilities even where they consume the same PractitionerCapacity. Receipt of an escalation or approval notification grants no information access. Following it into Iris or another application surface requires normal Themis PEP enforcement using current valid PEP-Criteria. U16 establishes [Agora control and Omilia operations](d1c4053e68384080b8eb79d2008632ba.md); detailed membership, escalation and approval-routing mechanics remain deferred. #### PEP-Context and distributed enforcement > **PEP-Context is the Themis-derived policy enforcement context established for > an authenticated Identity. It supplies the precomputed PEP-Criteria applicable > to that Identity that a Themis Policy Enforcement Point requires for local > enforcement decisions.** **PEP-Criteria is a precomputed, Identity-specific set of permitted combinations**, not a general-purpose executable policy language distributed to PEPs. Themis resolves direct Criteria, AuthorisationRole-derived Criteria, nested collections, applicable temporal constraints, PractitionerCapacity context where applicable and authoritative policy state. PEPs SHALL NOT receive the complete model merely because they need enforcement information. ```text Policy Authorisation Model managed by Themis Criteria governed permitted combinations in the Authorisation Model PEP-Criteria precomputed Identity-specific permitted combinations PEP-Context operational context supplying applicable PEP-Criteria Enforcement Decision local PEP determination for a particular proposed action ``` Enforcement occurs at the component capable of preventing the action. A PEP may be a Themis-provided library/framework element embedded within a host module. **The distributed PEP capability, implementation and enforcement semantics are Themis-owned/derived/built.** The host controls the actual operation; Themis supplies enforcement mechanism and semantics. Hosts SHALL NOT independently reinterpret the Authorisation Model in place of the Themis PEP. No separate central Policy Enforcement Software Component is created. A local PEP SHALL perform deliberately **constrained, deterministic enforcement** against authenticated Identity context, effective Information.Compartment and Information.Classification, Function.Name, Function.Scope, applicable temporal state and the Identity's valid PEP-Criteria. It SHALL NOT become a general-purpose policy interpreter. Themis SHALL retain sufficient provenance to explain effective PEP-Criteria derivation: authoritative Criteria, collections, direct/AuthorisationRole assignments and applicable policy state. Runtime PEP-Criteria need not carry the full derivation history; stable references may support it. No final wire/data structure, cache, refresh or distribution mechanism is prescribed. PEP-Context and existing security-context contracts are operational context; they do not automatically become persisted resource content. Their detailed relationship, schema and distribution mechanisms remain unresolved; PEP-Context is not silently equated with a historical class or transport carrier. #### Untagged information and effective security attributes > **Absence of explicit information security metadata does not imply absence > of security control. Untagged information is not unrestricted information.** Where required Information.Compartment and/or Information.Classification attributes are absent, effective values SHALL be established through governed, deterministic rules. If required effective attributes cannot be established, enforcement SHALL fail closed. Deriving effective attributes for an authorisation decision is distinct from persistently assigning/changing security metadata on an Information Unit. Themis enforces the resulting attributes; it is not assumed to own all semantic derivation rules. Exact derivation ownership and precedence, including possible context/containment relationships, remain [deferred](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#identity-deferred-design). Mnemosyne's established compartment validation/reapplication responsibility does not settle those semantic rules. #### Availability and delegation An in-flight activity with a **valid PEP-Context sufficient for its required enforcement decisions** may continue during temporary PDP unavailability. PDP availability is required for a **new, renewed or replacement PEP-Context**. If the PDP cannot establish that required context, the activity SHALL NOT proceed beyond the point requiring it and must wait. **PDP unavailability is not policy denial**: policy permits, policy denies, and authoritative policy determination cannot presently be established remain distinct. This grants no unauthenticated or unauthorised action permission and weakens no required audit-capture boundary. Detailed validity, timeout/retry, revocation and renewal mechanisms are unresolved. At this stage delegation is **Identity / PEP-Criteria pass-off (forwarding)**, subject to applicable **FORWARD** authority. Provenance SHALL preserve both the originating Identity and receiving/acting Identity; the receiver does not become the originator. No separate general-purpose delegation subsystem is introduced. Detailed forwarding lifecycle/representation, PDP interaction and governance mechanisms remain deferred; forwarding establishes no unrestricted impersonation or authority-broadening rule. #### Governed authorisation administration and target allocation Authorisation administration is governed Harmonia work. Criteria creation/change, collection management, AuthorisationRole management, direct Identity Criteria assignment, AuthorisationRole assignment, temporal changes and revocation SHALL be subject to appropriate governed management/review/approval processes through **Ergo/Praxis**, with **Iris** providing human interaction. Detailed PAP management Praxes/Erga and approval rules remain deferred; this does not make every change require an identical approval sequence. | Responsibility | Candidate target | | :--- | :--- | | Identity authentication | Keycloak / external OIDC IdP; SEP, Keycloak + PostgreSQL default for development/test/POC | | Controlled authorisation nomenclature | Calliope | | Authorisation model, Criteria/collections, AuthorisationRoles and Identity assignments | Themis-owned | | Role/group resolution | Themis-owned; no separate human/system authorisation architecture | | Criteria compilation | Themis-owned | | Policy repository | Themis PRP, persisted through Harmonia via Mneme / Mnemosyne C&G | | Policy administration | Themis PAP | | Governed management / review / approval workflows | Ergo/Praxis | | Administration UI | Iris; no authorisation-model ownership or detailed reusable-form design | | Runtime enforcement | Themis PEP library at action-controlling hosts | | Untagged information handling | Governed effective-attribute resolution; exact ownership/precedence deferred | Harmonia owns its authorisation semantics. **jCasbin, OPA, Cedar or another general-purpose policy framework is not an architectural dependency.** FOSS implementations may later supply implementation references where appropriate; their conceptual models SHALL NOT redefine Harmonia semantics. - **Collaboration/exclusions:** governed access, activity, publication and collaboration hosts use Themis-owned PEP capability. Petasos hosts governed FORWARD enforcement because it controls the queue operation. element.name: AX-11 Managed Information Access Is Highly Available and Responsive
element.documentation:
#### Axiom
Mneme SHALL provide highly available, responsive and load-tolerant access to Harmonia-managed active information.
Its architecture SHALL favour bounded resource consumption, distributed workload, reconstructable active state and graceful expression of processing pressure.
Availability SHALL NOT be achieved by weakening authoritative-state, concurrency, security, governance or information-authority guarantees.
#### Rationale
Mneme exists partly to prevent every application interaction from becoming an authoritative persistence interaction while still preserving Harmonia's correctness guarantees.
#### Consequences
Different categories of Mneme state MAY use different distribution and consistency strategies.
Small coordination state need not have the same topology as large resource caches.
Cache topology SHALL be selected according to the semantics and operational requirements of the managed state rather than applied universally.
**This does not mean:**
- Every cache should use REPL_SYNC. - Every managed resource must always reside in memory. - Cache availability is equivalent to authoritative information availability.

element.documentation:
Capturing referral criteria, catchment boundaries, and clinical eligibility.
**Overview**
Published catchment, referral and clinical eligibility conditions explain the intended audience and access constraints of an offering. Their representation supports responsible assessment without deciding acceptance or clinical priority.
**Intent**
Make the governed intake and catchment conditions available to the party responsible for access decisions.
**Boundary**
Represents governed eligibility criteria; it does not make clinical acceptance or triage decisions.

element.name: [CT3] Compliance Assessment Definition
element.documentation:
Define the evidence, measures, criteria, controls and assessment arrangements sufficient to evaluate compliance with established obligations, authorities and constraints.
Compliance Assessment Definition specifies the evidence, measures, criteria and arrangements sufficient to evaluate adherence. It makes the assessment basis explicit after obligations, authorities and constraints have been established. This preserves the distinction between defining what compliance means and determining whether the available evidence demonstrates it in a particular case.
**Boundary**
Assessment definition does not replace the authoritative obligation, perform assurance or establish a compliance finding.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Competency Administration
element.documentation:
Administer information about what clinical capability an organisation can provide and what a practitioner is competent to perform.
**Overview**
Administer information about what clinical capability an organisation can provide and what a practitioner is competent to perform.
**Intent**
Administer information about what clinical capability an organisation can provide and what a practitioner is competent to perform.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Clinical Competency Management is retained as a Reference context concerning practitioner competence. It is distinguishable from checking supplied qualification or competency evidence before specialised work. The model does not establish that representing evidence makes Harmonia the authority that assesses or grants competence.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
No atomic Features or competency-assessment authority are allocated to this context.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
The formal Reference classification remains separate from the relevance of operational qualification checking elsewhere.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [8a4b918e1c9d47bb99daf2b42008ab39](8a4b918e1c9d47bb99daf2b42008ab39.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.

element.name: [UserStory] External systems can consume standardised values
element.documentation:
Independent stakeholder need, expectation or desired outcome:
> As a Provider Directory Administrator, I want to expose reference data sets via an API, so that external systems can consume standardised values.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.
### Reconciled source contributions
- `SR-58` — Expose Reference Data Sets via an API; Additional Source Requirements – SR-26 to SR-58; [source](../../../../../openspec/specs/provider-directory-integration/sr-58-expose-reference-data-sets-via-an-api/spec.md).
Source-specific access conditions, supporting actors, alternative outcomes, verification and data-authority rules remain distinct in their cited source contributions. Legacy claims that each statement is a business capability are not adopted: this instance has native Requirement semantics. Source target-state scope is not a software delivery commitment for 1.1.21. Historical assessment findings remain recoverable and do not establish current coverage.

element.name: Theatre Case Progression Process
element.documentation:
• Owning Capability: Theatre Operations
• Process Purpose: Governs the perioperative operational milestones of a surgical procedure within the operating theatre suite.
• State Progression Lifecycle: Case Called → In Anaesthetic Bay → Anaesthesia Commenced → Patient in Theatre → Knife-to-Skin → Procedure Finished → In PACU Recovery → Ward Handover Complete
• Key State Dispositions:
• Case Called: Theatre team requests ward to send patient for surgery.
• In Anaesthetic Bay: Patient arrives in theatre holding and identity/consent verified.
• Anaesthesia Commenced: Anaesthetic induction underway.
• Patient in Theatre: Patient transferred onto operating table.
• Knife-to-Skin: Surgical incision initiated (operative start).
• Procedure Finished: Wound closure completed and dressings applied.
• In PACU Recovery: Patient monitored in post-anaesthesia care unit.
• Ward Handover Complete: Post-operative clinical handover to inpatient ward completed.
Theatre case progression follows reported milestones of the surgical encounter so that supporting participants can coordinate around the actual situation. The state account concerns what the clinical service reports has occurred. It does not make the integration mechanism the actor administering anaesthesia, performing surgery or managing clinical handover.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md` — entry lines 170-185. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.

element.name: [CT3] Information Authority Representation
element.documentation:
Represent the source, credibility and qualified authority standing of competing health-information assertions.
**Overview**
A persisted assertion may be authoritative, informational or anecdotal. This ability carries that standing into interpretation without treating transport reliability, freshness or successful commit as proof of credibility.
**Intent**
Keep an assertion technical acceptance separate from the standing of the source that asserted it.
**Boundary**
Classification does not originate clinical facts or universally adjudicate conflicts. Policy determines how qualified assertions are used.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT3] Community Care Coordination
element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Community Care integrates encounters, observations and plans across home, community and hospital outreach participants. It supports continuity where clinical activity occurs outside the hospital's immediate information environment. Receiving visit records and synchronising plan changes helps make community activity visible without turning the platform into the provider of that activity.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Plan synchronisation does not originate clinical intent, assign community work or establish that a visit occurred beyond its source evidence.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Cross-organisational encounter and care-plan information materially supports community care continuity.
## Qualified relationship assertions

element.name: [CT3] HIE Implementation Management
element.documentation:
Manage implementation information and progression for established exchange requirements, including submission, retrieval, distribution and syndication interactions.
**Overview**
Manage implementation information and progression for established exchange requirements, including submission, retrieval, distribution and syndication interactions. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Manage implementation information and progression for established exchange requirements, including submission, retrieval, distribution and syndication interactions.
**Boundary**
Information administration and coordination preserve the authority of the responsible source, clinical actor and governed domain; they confer no additional real-world management authority.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [a99b4119339545a89dc54ebb216ddb85](a99b4119339545a89dc54ebb216ddb85.md) has evolved correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E08.04.01`; additional scope correspondences: `E03.05`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. These are distinct assertions. Neither diagram membership nor the Grouping's label alone establishes another Home or a statement allocation. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.

element.name: [Feature] Collaboration Interaction Capture Qualification
element.documentation:
Qualify when a defined collaboration interaction creates a new governed information or activity consequence.
**Overview**
A message may convey existing information or an explicit interaction may derive a new managed consequence. The distinction preserves collaboration-native records while routing governed consequences to their accountable responsibility.
**Boundary**
Conversation presence, display or read receipt does not itself make a clinical decision, approval or final record.

**Overview**
Coordinate emergency-department bed/bay occupancy, operational waits, length-of-stay milestones and local capacity information. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Coordinate emergency-department bed/bay occupancy, operational waits, length-of-stay milestones and local capacity information.

Information administration and coordination preserve the authority of the responsible source, clinical actor and governed domain; they confer no additional real-world management authority.

element.name: [Feature] Binary Content Resolution & Assembly
element.documentation:
Resolve governed payload associations and retrieve or assemble the content required by a requesting information context.
**Overview**
A logical clinical item may reference externally held or multipart payloads. The Feature supplies a usable content result while retaining custody and missing-content standing.
**Boundary**
No assumption of local copying, shared storage, universal content retention or originating clinical authority.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: AI Assurance Ergon
element.documentation:
- **Role/features:** candidate Dokimasia Ergon specialisation where AI-based processing is itself an explicit governed participant in Dokimasia workflow. Its existence and discrete responsibility are established by [U02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u02); its detailed Information Systems architecture is not finalised. - **Distinction:** ordinary Ergon may call AI internally as an implementation choice. AI Assurance Ergon makes that AI activity an explicit governed assurance workflow activity. This allocates neither every use of AI to this component nor a mandatory AI step to every Dokimasia workflow. - **Information/persistence/collaboration:** inherits C26/C23/C05 contracts and common Pragma Management, process-management, platform integration and reporting. AI invocation confers no originating domain or assurance-determination authority on the service/model. Context, disclosure, results, provenance/evidence and detailed workflow interactions require [CDG-35 discovery](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#dokimasia-ai-discovery). - **Standing/exclusions:** established component boundary with candidate detailed design; no LLM, agent framework, SDK, model, provider or service technology selected. Discovery precedes final implementation modelling. Inherits both Dokimasia terminal rules; unresolved design does not invalidate its boundary.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F35 | Explicit governed AI participation within Dokimasia workflow | [AI Assurance Ergon C27](component-register.md#c27) candidate specialisation of Dokimasia Ergon, executed by Dokimasia with common platform contracts | AI activity's context/input, result and assurance evidence interactions require discovery | **Existence/discrete responsibility established by U02; detailed architecture candidate/discovery.** Distinct from ordinary Ergon invoking AI internally; not all AI use allocated here. CDG-35 discovery precedes final implementation modelling; no technology/provider selected; terminal rules apply. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
| F35 | Explicit governed AI participation within Dokimasia workflow | [AI Assurance Ergon C27](8fe50975372b4d399a4bcb9f3d9348f7.md) candidate specialisation of Dokimasia Ergon, executed by Dokimasia with common platform contracts | AI activity's context/input, result and assurance evidence interactions require discovery | **Existence/discrete responsibility established by U02; detailed architecture candidate/discovery.** Distinct from ordinary Ergon invoking AI internally; not all AI use allocated here. CDG-35 discovery precedes final implementation modelling; no technology/provider selected; terminal rules apply. |

element.name: [CT3] Device Association
element.documentation:
Associating clinical devices with patients, beds, or rooms.
**Overview**
A device can be associated with different patients and care places at different times. Qualified association and its lineage allow observations to be interpreted against the applicable binding rather than the current assignment alone.
**Intent**
Allow a device-originated item to be associated with the correct subject and place at the relevant time.
**Boundary**
Represents qualified device-to-subject/place association without owning those subjects or observations.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: Vendor-Independent Longitudinal Clinical Information Coherence
element.documentation:
### Goal Statement Harmonia shall establish and maintain a vendor-neutral, semantically coherent representation of a patient's longitudinal health record that outlives individual EMR software lifecycles and remains independent of proprietary vendor schemas.
### Rationale & Context Patient care spans decades across multiple disparate healthcare institutions. Commercial EMR platforms have short market lifecycles and store data in proprietary, closed schemas that create vendor lock-in. To ensure continuity of care, the regional health network requires an enduring clinical asset that preserves the semantic meaning, units of measure, clinical nuance, and temporal sequence of health events across disparate provider systems.
### Architectural Boundary - Governed by [AX-01 (Health-Information Centricity)](../principle/e9bd61acaaea4577bc4086a5639e52c3.md), [AX-02 (Standards at Boundary)](../principle/eee8c3783d964d18a7f9dcea85fcd4cf.md), and [AX-06 (Explicit Information Authority)](../principle/952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md). - Hands over directly to [Reduced Clinical Risk (O1)](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/business-outcomes.md) and [Continuous Regional Exchange (O2)](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/business-outcomes.md).

element.name: PEP-Context
element.documentation:
> **PEP-Context is the Themis-derived policy enforcement context established for > an authenticated Identity. It supplies the precomputed PEP-Criteria applicable > to that Identity that a Themis Policy Enforcement Point requires for local > enforcement decisions.**
**PEP-Criteria is a precomputed, Identity-specific set of permitted combinations**, not a general-purpose executable policy language distributed to PEPs. Themis resolves direct Criteria, AuthorisationRole-derived Criteria, nested collections, applicable temporal constraints, PractitionerCapacity context where applicable and authoritative policy state. PEPs SHALL NOT receive the complete model merely because they need enforcement information.
```text Policy Authorisation Model managed by Themis Criteria governed permitted combinations in the Authorisation Model PEP-Criteria precomputed Identity-specific permitted combinations PEP-Context operational context supplying applicable PEP-Criteria Enforcement Decision local PEP determination for a particular proposed action ```
Enforcement occurs at the component capable of preventing the action. A PEP may be a Themis-provided library/framework element embedded within a host module. **The distributed PEP capability, implementation and enforcement semantics are Themis-owned/derived/built.** The host controls the actual operation; Themis supplies enforcement mechanism and semantics. Hosts SHALL NOT independently reinterpret the Authorisation Model in place of the Themis PEP. No separate central Policy Enforcement Software Component is created.
A local PEP SHALL perform deliberately **constrained, deterministic enforcement** against authenticated Identity context, effective Information.Compartment and Information.Classification, Function.Name, Function.Scope, applicable temporal state and the Identity's valid PEP-Criteria. It SHALL NOT become a general-purpose policy interpreter.
Themis SHALL retain sufficient provenance to explain effective PEP-Criteria derivation: authoritative Criteria, collections, direct/AuthorisationRole assignments and applicable policy state. Runtime PEP-Criteria need not carry the full derivation history; stable references may support it. No final wire/data structure, cache, refresh or distribution mechanism is prescribed.
PEP-Context and existing security-context contracts are operational context; they do not automatically become persisted resource content. Their detailed relationship, schema and distribution mechanisms remain unresolved; PEP-Context is not silently equated with a historical class or transport carrier.

element.name: [CT2] Managed Entity & Relationship
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Identify, classify, relate, and maintain the structural integrity of managed healthcare and administrative entities throughout the enterprise landscape. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Uniquely identifying core domain entities (Persons, Practitioners, Roles, Organisations, Locations, Services, Devices). - Resolving and maintaining multi-authority identifier systems and aliases without destructive overwriting. - Representing and traversing multi-dimensional relationships (affiliations, organizational hierarchies, physical location trees, care team memberships). - Maintaining referential integrity across interconnected entity graphs. - **Anti-Responsibilities**: Does not own physical database relational tables or foreign key constraints (Domain 04/07).
This reusable capability keeps managed healthcare entities identifiable and their relationships structurally intelligible. It supplies common identity, alias and relationship behaviour recurring in persons, practitioners, organisations, locations and devices. Reuse concerns those architectural responsibilities, allowing the healthcare-specific meaning of each entity to remain with its governing context.
**Boundary**
Relationship integrity is not a physical database design. Correlating entities does not establish originating clinical identity authority or a new standalone Correlation capability.

{"ancestry_status":"proposed","architectural_status":"Canonical","baseline_description":{"Boundary":"Relationship integrity is not a physical database design. Correlating entities does not establish originating clinical identity authority or a new standalone Correlation capability.","Capability Overview":"This reusable capability keeps managed healthcare entities identifiable and their relationships structurally intelligible. It supplies common identity, alias and relationship behaviour recurring in persons, practitioners, organisations, locations and devices. Reuse concerns those architectural responsibilities, allowing the healthcare-specific meaning of each entity to remain with its governing context."},"baseline_placement":{"canonical_id":"EC-01","owner_key":null,"parent_key":null,"tier":null},"baseline_unresolved":[],"baseline_version":"0.1","canonical_id":"CT1-EC-GOVERNED-INFORMATION-OPERATIONS.CT2-EC-01","canonical_name":"Managed Entity & Relationship","category":"enterprise","confidence":"High","governed_definition_latex":"
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Identify, classify, relate, and maintain the structural integrity of managed healthcare and administrative entities throughout the enterprise landscape.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Uniquely identifying core domain entities (Persons, Practitioners, Roles, Organisations, Locations, Services, Devices).



\item 
Resolving and maintaining multi-authority identifier systems and aliases without destructive overwriting.



\item 
Representing and traversing multi-dimensional relationships (affiliations, organizational hierarchies, physical location trees, care team memberships).



\item 
Maintaining referential integrity across interconnected entity graphs.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not own physical database relational tables or foreign key constraints (Domain 04/\allowbreak{}07).



\end{itemize}

element.name: [UserStory] I can verify that updates are being distributed

Independent stakeholder need, expectation or desired outcome:
> As a Provider Directory Administrator, I want to monitor broadcast activity to Rhapsody, so that I can verify that updates are being distributed.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.
### Reconciled source contributions
- `SR-46` — Monitor Provider Update Broadcasts to Rhapsody; Additional Source Requirements – SR-26 to SR-58; [source](../../../../../openspec/specs/provider-directory-integration/sr-46-monitor-provider-update-broadcasts-to-rhapsody/spec.md).
Source-specific access conditions, supporting actors, alternative outcomes, verification and data-authority rules remain distinct in their cited source contributions. Legacy claims that each statement is a business capability are not adopted: this instance has native Requirement semantics. Source target-state scope is not a software delivery commitment for 1.1.21. Historical assessment findings remain recoverable and do not establish current coverage.

element.name: Capture Post-Clinic Follow-up Requirements
element.documentation:
Captures follow-up booking and diagnostic-order requirements generated at clinic completion.
Derivation: FEAT-HSO-10 directly establishes this capture responsibility. The Clinic queue Process's consultation-concluded checkpoint describes orders placed, not Outpatient Operations' capture of follow-up requirements. Capture does not authorise clinical orders, own authoritative bookings or establish a new Service dependency.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/04-health-service-operations.md` — entry lines 144-144. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged.
- *Function*: `Capture Post-Clinic Follow-up Requirements` — Captures follow-up booking and diagnostic-order requirements generated at clinic completion.

element.name: Clinical Interoperability Across Heterogeneous Standards
element.documentation:
### Context & Pressure Regional healthcare environments are characterized by decades of technical layering. Acute care hospitals, outpatient clinics, pathology laboratories, and diagnostic imaging centers operate software solutions spanning multiple technological eras: - Legacy hospital information systems communicating via HL7 v2.x pipe-and-hat (`ER7`) messaging over Minimal Lower Layer Protocol (MLLP). - Modern clinical repositories exposing HL7 FHIR RESTful APIs (R4/R5) using JSON and XML encodings. - Specialized imaging platforms exchanging DICOM objects. - Proprietary file drops, CSV exports, and ad-hoc database integrations.
### Architectural Imperative Harmonia must bridge these heterogeneous standards without forcing disruptive, multi-million-dollar system replacements across delivery organizations. The platform must accept standards-based messages natively at its integration membrane while maintaining canonical semantic coherence internally, preventing message corruption or loss of clinical intent during translation.
- **Primary Stakeholders**: [Regional Health Network Operator](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md), [Healthcare Delivery Organizations](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md) - **External Constraint**: [Mandated External Interoperability Contracts](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/requirements-constraints/external-constraints.md) - **Associated Goal**: [Vendor-Independent Longitudinal Clinical Information Coherence](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) - **Governing Axioms**: [AX-02 (Standards at Boundary)](../principle/eee8c3783d964d18a7f9dcea85fcd4cf.md), [AX-03 (Native Standards Representations)](../principle/e99a4e2bf99f476d876394300d6b9c3d.md)

element.name: [CT2] Care Support Logistics Management
element.documentation:
Coordinate bounded operational support needed for care access and fulfilment.
Care Support Logistics Management coordinates the bounded physical and operational support needed to fulfil care. Patient transit, clinical-material movement and authorised support work have different subjects and completion evidence, even when the same operational environment supports them. This capability provides their common care-support frame without absorbing every logistical activity of a healthcare enterprise.
**Intent**
Ensure necessary supporting activity can progress with the relevant patient, material and operational constraints visible.
**Boundary**
Assignment does not establish a worker's qualification or clinical authority. Enterprise supply chains, facilities and workforce governance retain their own responsibilities.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: Provider Registry solution collaboration
element.documentation:
- **Role/responsibility:** documented application solution for directory resources and governed changes across existing components, rather than a new enclosing platform component. [L15/L18](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#l15). - **Features/contained constructs:** synchronous read/search, request-for-change, per-resource validation/identifier uniqueness/reference checks, candidate automated approval, durable commit and observable task progress. Seven per-resource Ergon activities and a registry change sequence are documented behavioural specialisations; Erga supplies the distinct collection/assembly/library responsibility. - **Information:** Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, Location, HealthcareService, Endpoint and Group; change Pragma/input/output, errors and resulting versions. Endpoint and Group remain independently referenced resources. - **Persistence:** clinical/FHIR Mnemosyne slice; current-row versus history structures unclear. Iris is presentation-only; server-side governance remains with Mnemosyne Clinical, Ergon activities within Erga, and Themis under AGENTS Invariant 3. - **Collaboration/exclusions:** Pylai interaction, Themis, Petasos, Ponos/Praxis/Erga, Mneme/Mnemosyne and Iris Administration. Does not automatically own all provider, care-team or national-source facts, or imply an EMPI. - **Standing:** documented candidate domain solution, CDG-03/11/12/21/32/33. Direct persistence search and published async response claims are not approved external contracts by inclusion here.

element.name: [CT2] Operational Assurance
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Ensure concurrency integrity, system resilience, duplicate detection, exception handling, automated recovery, and operational telemetry across platform operations. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Enforcing sliding-window duplicate message detection and idempotent suppression. - Guaranteeing ingress dual-write safety (durable acceptance before emitting positive application ACK). - Managing structured failure recovery, exception escalation, and dead-letter isolation. - Emitting platform telemetry, operational health metrics, and queue processing metrics. - **Collaborative Nature**: Realized collaboratively across boundary gateways, messaging infrastructure, execution workers, and storage layers.
#### EC-12 / EC-14 Boundary
EC-12 retains the established scope and responsibilities above. It may contribute directly to generic operational/processing assurance, limited to that contribution in the [approved assurance matrix](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md#collaborative-enterprise-capability-contribution-matrix). It does not own the general semantics of assurance disposition, assurance-specific criteria applicability, evidentiary association, assessment against assurance criteria, adjudication, or independent assurance findings and conclusions. Those distinguishing responsibilities are introduced through EC-14 Service Guardian. Operational health and business-level processing assurance remain distinct; EC-12 is not expanded to absorb EC-14.
Operational Assurance preserves processing integrity under concurrency, duplicate delivery and failure. It brings together resilience, durable ingress acceptance, recovery and operational telemetry so that technical degradation does not silently weaken the managed operation's semantics. Its contribution is collaborative across operational boundaries while remaining a bounded architectural responsibility.
**Boundary**
Operational health is distinct from independent assessment of a governed subject. Assurance-specific criteria applicability, adjudication and conclusions belong to the established EC-14 contribution.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E08.04`; additional scope correspondences: `E08.06`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Diagnostic Specimen Management
element.documentation:
Maintain a specimen’s identity, integrity, suitability, custody and applicable lifecycle context.
Diagnostic Specimen Management preserves the specimen context needed to trust its use: which specimen it is, whether it remains suitable, and how integrity and custody are maintained. It concerns the physical diagnostic subject across its applicable lifecycle rather than only the results generated from it. This distinction protects the relationship between evidence and the material from which it arose.
**Boundary**
Specimen stewardship is separate from diagnostic-data management and interpretation of results.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

This existing element is a **SolutionFacet**, a specialisation of native **Grouping**. The [governed definition](../../governance/continuum-representation.md#solutionfacet-classification--1119-candidate) distinguishes accessible solution classification from Capability, responsibility and ownership. Its canonical identity, G01–G18 context, existing Composition and separately established Home assertions are preserved.
Native Grouping originally authored as `Architectural-Governance.Implementation-Strategy.Principles` in the retained 004 export, incorporated under the Solution Architect's Subject Grouping hierarchy Task. It groups the source-qualified `Principles` concern within the existing **Implementation Strategy** SolutionFacet (G01.03). Its earlier authored name above is retained as provenance; current names follow the explicit properties in the 1.1.19 submission. That earlier incoming record has no Documentation or authored Properties; no normative definition, native statement, classification of individual statements, or additional responsibility is invented to complete that absence.
The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. These are distinct assertions. Neither diagram membership nor the Grouping's label alone establishes another Home or a statement allocation. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.
Source Exchange identifier: `id-b67e6a308e864c5dbe522df87125fcb6`. View placement corroborates the authorised containing SolutionFacet; the exact correspondence is retained in the iteration's folder/Grouping inventories. Existing canonical identities and all pre-existing architectural assertions retain their standing. Archi visual acceptance and HCRL closure remain separate.

element.name: [CT3] Preventative Health Programme Monitoring
element.documentation:
Observe programme operation, reach, participation, coverage, progress and applicable performance.
This capability observes how a preventative programme is operating, including reach, participation, coverage and progress. It supplies an account of programme performance in the programme's own scope, rather than substituting population-health state for evidence of programme activity. That account can inform reporting or consideration of the programme without itself being an assurance conclusion.
**Boundary**
Programme monitoring is distinct from individual health monitoring, population assessment and independent assurance.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [e05f6310f6d544efaca5568604f27dd8](e05f6310f6d544efaca5568604f27dd8.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.

element.name: [CT3] Workflow & Activity Coordination
element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Workflow & Activity Coordination provides governed progression for three distinct work meanings: human operational Work Orders, human review or decision To Dos, and non-human Synthetic Tasks. It supports dispatch, state and deadline oversight without collapsing those meanings into a generic technical task. The common coordination responsibility makes progression visible while preserving who has authority to perform or decide the underlying activity.
### Intent — predecessor explanation
Keep assigned activity, acknowledgement, progress and outcome distinguishable across human and automated work.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Coordination does not confer clinical work ownership. Synthetic Tasks are not external clinical worklists, and the incomplete stalled/failed Process paths remain unresolved.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Governed activity progression is a substantive Core responsibility; information traceability preserves archetype, work and undertaking distinctions without transferring outcome authority.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: AX-06 Information Authority Is Explicit
element.documentation:
#### Axiom
Harmonia SHALL represent the authority and credibility of managed information independently of its technical transport, cache state, persistence state or concurrency state.
Harmonia SHALL support governed information-authority concepts including:
- Authoritative, - Informational, and - Anecdotal.
#### Rationale
Technical correctness and information credibility answer different questions.
A successfully persisted assertion is not necessarily authoritative. A stale assertion is not necessarily false. A technically reliable source is not necessarily the authoritative source for every fact it supplies.
#### Consequences
Concurrency determines whether information has changed.
Semantic analysis determines what changed.
Information authority and assurance describe the standing of competing assertions.
Policy determines what Harmonia does about them.
Calliope governs the semantics of information authority. Appropriate Harmonia processes and policies apply those semantics.
**This does not mean:**
- Authoritative information automatically wins every conflict. - Anecdotal information is discarded. - Persistence success establishes information authority.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Data Management
element.documentation:
Manage actual health-information content within applicable governed structures.
Health Information Data Management concerns the actual content maintained within applicable governed structures. It keeps the represented information distinct from definitions describing how that information should be organised and interpreted. Within Health Information Management, its responsibility is meaningful content rather than mere successful persistence of values.
**Boundary**
Managing content does not originate its clinical facts or acquire the authority of its semantic references.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: Service Assurance Modeller
element.documentation: - **Canonical Name**: `Service Assurance Modeller`. **Element Type**: Business Role. Canonical ID remains unresolved; the metamodel does not establish Role identifier tokens or structural context. - **Fundamental Responsibility**: Determine and model how satisfaction of a governed requirement, constraint or expected behaviour is to be assured. - **Responsibility Contexts**: [Assurance Design](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#assurance-design) and [Assurance Criteria Management](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#assurance-criteria-management). - **Performed Business Functions**: [Design Service Assurance](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#design-service-assurance), owned by Assurance Design; [Manage Assurance Criteria](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#manage-assurance-criteria), owned by Assurance Criteria Management. Role performance does not replace capability ownership. - **Principal Process Performance**: [Assurance Process Design](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md#assurance-process-design), owned by Assurance Design, with both established Functions participating without transferring Assurance Criteria Management ownership. Assurance Definition remains a conceptual output/boundary; its use by Service Guardian does not establish a Modeller-to-Guardian Interaction. - **Authority Boundary**: Modelling does not inherently confer authority to approve the governing requirement, Assurance Definition or Assurance Criteria. Governance Authority is exercised through existing mandated authority Roles as described in [§3.7](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md#37-governance-authority-and-assurance-modelling). - **Clinical and Operational Boundary**: The Role confers no clinical authority, clinical correctness or adequacy determination, professional clinical judgement, peer-review or clinical-governance authority, or Clinical Services Delivery Assurance. It does not manage, perform, remediate, assign, delegate or operationally escalate the subject activity merely because it models assurance concerning that activity. Explicitly required assurance concerning clinical information or behaviour does not transfer clinical responsibility. - **Allocation Boundary**: The Role models how satisfaction is assured; it does not perform the resulting independent assurance merely by fulfilling this Role. Detailed Actor eligibility, mandates, approval workflows, further Interactions and Collaborations remain unresolved. No application, runtime or implementation allocation is established.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Knowledge Publication & Sharing
element.documentation:
Make approved knowledge available to applicable authorised consumers and use contexts.
Clinical Knowledge Publication & Sharing makes approved knowledge available to applicable authorised consumers and contexts. It preserves the standing and limits under which knowledge was approved rather than reducing publication to unrestricted dissemination. Its contribution is availability for appropriate use, distinct from both approval and the individual clinical application that may follow.
**Boundary**
Published knowledge is not a patient-specific conclusion, decision or instruction merely because a clinician can access it.

element.name: [CT2] Service Delivery Preparedness Management
element.documentation:
Establish whether service offerings can be delivered in their intended operating contexts through the combined standing of their dependencies.
**Overview**
Preparedness asks whether the service as a whole can operate, distinct from scheduling capacity or readiness of a single place. This is a proposed missing business frame for the already identified readiness concern.
**Intent**
Recognise whether the whole service can actually operate in its intended context.
**Boundary**
Does not own the dependencies, their management or clinical execution.

element.name: [Feature] Remote Telemetry Ingestion
element.documentation:
Ingest home patient monitoring data, biometric telemetry, and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs).
Remote telemetry ingestion accepts measurements and patient-reported contributions from outside the usual care site. The information can inform subsequent monitoring and interpretation, but acquisition alone does not establish clinical significance or authorise an intervention.

Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Indeterminate Activity Outcome Reconciliation Process
element.documentation:
Order the observation, effect qualification and authorised disposition of a materially indeterminate operational outcome.
**Overview**
First inspect the governing handoff and available authoritative state; then reconcile observed effects; finally authorise a safe continuation, retry or retained uncertainty. Each participating Function keeps its responsibility owner.
**Boundary**
Not a universal lifecycle or automatic retry loop. A safe disposition may remain unresolved.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: Governed PHI Logging & Dual-Logger Privacy Controls
element.documentation: Operational log streams (INFO, WARN, ERROR) must remain strictly devoid of Protected Health Information (PHI), personally identifiable demographics, and security credentials under all conditions. element.name: [CT2] Care Resource & Capacity Coordination
element.documentation:
Relate operational care-place and equipment state to the coordinated view of service demand and capacity.
**Overview**
Relate operational care-place and equipment state to the coordinated view of service demand and capacity. Its constituent abilities distinguish Bed & Care-Place Management; Clinical Resource Management; Service Capacity Management.
**Intent**
Make resource-state contributions and coordinated capacity views usable without collapsing their different responsibilities.
**Boundary**
Bed/equipment availability is a contribution to capacity, not its definition. Higher-order capacity consumes local capacity without taking its ownership.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B07.03`; additional scope correspondences: `B09.06`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Preventative Health Cohort Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage the target population, inclusion/exclusion criteria, membership, stratification and applicable entry/exit context.
Preventative Health Cohort Management establishes who belongs to the population targeted for a preventative purpose. Inclusion, exclusion, stratification and entry or exit context make membership explainable rather than a list detached from its rationale. It provides a governed population context through which programme activity and reporting can be understood.
**Boundary**
A population at risk is not automatically a defined cohort, and cohort membership is not an individual clinical determination.
## ARB identity continuity

element.name: [CT3] Health Service Need Identification
element.documentation:
Establish an unmet health-service need requiring response.
Health Service Need Identification establishes the unmet service need for which an organisational response is being considered. It gives service modelling a reason grounded in what is missing rather than beginning with a predetermined solution. That identified need can then frame the abilities and resources required without assuming that a new offering has already been established.
**Boundary**
Identifying need does not define an offering, approve funding or determine the surrounding implementation arrangements.

element.name: [CT3] Diagnostic Report Management
element.documentation:
Establish and govern the authoritative expression of diagnostic findings, including applicable creation, review, amendment, verification, finalisation and authorisation/signing.
Diagnostic Report Management governs the authoritative expression of diagnostic findings. Creation, review, verification, amendment, finalisation and signing matter because they establish the standing of the report rather than merely its existence as data. The responsibility preserves a meaningful distinction between evidence, interpretation and the report that a service is prepared to authorise.
**Boundary**
Signing is behaviour within this capability, not another CT3. Sending a report does not establish its authorisation.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: Pylai.Diadromí Topic
element.documentation:
**Pylai.Terma** is the logical external interoperability interface/boundary. `Pylai.IngressTerma` and `Pylai.EgressTerma` specialise it where useful. Terma owns external communication mechanics: connection/session handling, listening, polling, transport/protocol interaction, framing, segmentation/reassembly, protocol acknowledgements, API/RMI/file interaction, interaction-local communication retry and external identity carriage. One Terma may use one or more technical endpoints/connectors; it is not reducible to a socket, URL, Camel endpoint or deployed adapter.
> **Pylai.Terma manages the communication stack; the applicable Harmonia > execution framework manages the application meaning.**
Terma owns the mechanics necessary to establish, conduct and complete an external communication interaction. It does not own the Harmonia application semantics of the information communicated. Application interpretation and processing use the applicable Harmonia execution framework, principally Praxis/Ergo/Ergon, except where an explicitly defined interaction pattern provides otherwise. The [Server READ/SEARCH pattern](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pylai-external-interoperability.md#pylai-server-controller) is such a defined pattern; it grants Terma no application/business interpretation responsibility.
```text External System → Pylai.Terma → Pylai.Diadromí → Praxis / Ergo / Ergon communication mechanics application interpretation, transformation / processing ```
Ingress/Egress describe **information direction**, irrespective of client/server role, who opened the connection or push/pull behaviour. An IngressTerma may poll; an EgressTerma may expose an external file interaction.
> **Pylai.Diadromí is the transient carriage and interaction context through which > a Pylai.Terma exchanges communication with its Harmonia-side participant for the > duration of an external interoperability interaction.**
> **Terma acts; Diadromí carries/represents transient interaction.**
A Diadromí may span multiple protocol exchanges, acknowledgements, retries within the active interaction and segmented communication. An intermediate protocol acknowledgement need not establish logical handover or authoritative Harmonia acceptance. Diadromí is neither an Ergon, Task/Pragma alias nor a durable queue. Its exact representation is unresolved.
**Pylai.Diadromí realises [Metabolē](../../business/business-object/c34b4929f71946708d37dbe6c1da920a.md)** for transient information progression through Pylai interoperability activity. This is genuine architectural Realisation, not analogy, synonymy with Metabolē or inheritance from Pragma. Pylai retains responsibility; Diadromí's transient, non-recoverable lifecycle does not acquire Pragma persistence or Mneme management requirements. Conceptual ActivityContext does not replace a specific interaction action or grant authorisation.
Source standing: Bounded adjudicated application information meaning; Domain05 remains the accepted candidate Step-B baseline, not final Solution Architecture. Detailed representation is deferred; only this defined logical object is projected.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md` — ### C44 — Pylai.Diadromí. Standing: Candidate — accepted Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
**Architectural Realisation:** Pylai.Diadromí realises [Metabolē](../../business/business-object/c34b4929f71946708d37dbe6c1da920a.md) for transient Pylai interoperability progression. Pylai retains responsibility; no common manager, inheritance or shared persistence/lifecycle with Pragma follows.
Transient carriage/interaction context between Terma and its Harmonia-side participant during an external interaction. May span segments, protocol exchanges, intermediate ACKs and active retries; it performs no Terma protocol logic. Lost or uncompletable interaction terminates; appropriate client retry creates a **new** Diadromí. No recoverable interaction state, Ergon/Task/Pragma equivalence or durable Petasos handoff semantics. Evidence may remain and uncertain effects remain AX-15. [Transience contract](978f5c2bd2d343ffaf3a13dff700c258.md).
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pylai-external-interoperability.md` — ## Transience, loss and recoverability. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
> **Pylai.Diadromí-Controller SHALL NOT maintain recoverable interaction state. > A Diadromí represents a transient interoperability interaction and, if that > interaction is lost or cannot be completed, recovery SHALL NOT resume the > previous Diadromí. Where retry is appropriate, client-side activity must initiate > a new interaction and therefore a new Diadromí.**
```text active external interaction → active Diadromí → communication retry ↑__________________________| same active interaction
failed / lost Diadromí → interaction terminates → NO RESUMPTION appropriate client retry → NEW interaction → NEW Diadromí ```
Transient state may exist for the active communication's lifetime. Active protocol retries differ from resuming a lost interaction. Terma may retry communication only while that interaction and its Diadromí remain active. Terma, Diadromí and its Controller provide no durable application recovery. Petasos and the established Harmonia execution architecture retain their durable messaging/recovery responsibilities; no lost Diadromí is resumed through them. Audit, Journey and operational evidence about the failed interaction may remain: **not recoverable does not mean not observable**.
Loss of interaction does not prove failure/non-occurrence of a previously requested state change. AX-15 uncertainty and safe-retry constraints still apply. A new Diadromí supplies no automatic permission to repeat an uncertain mutation.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Communication
element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Health Information Communication supplies standards-based transmission mediation between participating parties. It addresses protocol-facing transaction coordination and technical error handling while the business interaction retains its own meaning and authority. This differentiates the communication mechanism from the exchange model and from the clinical or operational purpose of the message.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Transport mediation does not own every communicated interaction or payload. External contracts must preserve standards semantics and exclude private operational metadata.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Standards-conformant communication boundaries are a direct interoperability responsibility.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT2] Rehabilitation
element.documentation:
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for rehabilitation services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Overview**
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for rehabilitation services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Intent**
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for rehabilitation services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Rehabilitation is an Adjacent clinical delivery context whose information can be represented without assigning the rehabilitation programme to Harmonia. No atomic Features are established in the current catalogue. Its presence records a healthcare context rather than requiring a new specialised coordination engine or a clinical outcome authority.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Information integration does not perform therapy, determine rehabilitation goals or judge clinical effectiveness.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Contextual participation is retained within the formal Adjacent classification.
## ARB identity continuity

element.name: [CT3] IT Infrastructure Management
element.documentation:
Operate/manage underlying technology infrastructure and its availability.
IT Infrastructure Management operates the underlying technology infrastructure and its availability. It supplies an enterprise support context for health-service activity that relies on functioning technology. Its business outcome is operational infrastructure, distinct from governance of health-information meaning or the application responsibilities realised on that infrastructure.
**Boundary**
Infrastructure machinery does not define Harmonia's information semantics or acquire clinical authority.

element.name: [CT2] Health Service Modelling
element.documentation:
Establish what service should exist and what it needs to become viable.
Health Service Modelling establishes the service needed and the ordinary business abilities required to make it viable. Its children distinguish recognising unmet need, identifying required abilities, supporting establishment and evaluating an existing service for improvement. The model can therefore revisit service assumptions without treating the original definition as permanently sufficient.
**Intent**
Connect a service's purpose with the abilities and preparation required for it to exist usefully.
**Boundary**
Capability Identification uses ordinary business meaning; it does not allocate Harmonia capability tiers. Implementation support does not take over recruitment, facilities, procurement or ICT responsibilities.
