element.name: [CT3] Authority & Constraint Governance
element.documentation:
Establish who may make, approve or govern organisational decisions/artefacts and the bounds within which authority may be exercised.
This capability establishes who may make or approve organisational decisions and the bounds within which that authority applies. It complements obligation governance by distinguishing required outcomes from legitimate decision powers. A participant can therefore be responsible for acting within constraints without being authorised to redefine the governing requirement.
**Boundary**
Authority allocation does not itself perform an operational decision or a runtime access-control evaluation.

element.name: [CT3] Health Innovation Evaluation
element.documentation:
Evaluate proposed/emerging innovation for suitability, value, implications and potential adoption.
Health Innovation Evaluation is the organisation's ability to form a considered view of a proposed or emerging innovation before treating it as suitable for use. Within Health Innovation it brings suitability, value and implications into the same evaluative context, so that potential benefit can be considered alongside consequences for the health-service or clinical setting. The outcome supports informed consideration of adoption rather than making adoption inevitable.
**Intent**
Give decision makers an intelligible basis for considering whether an innovation merits further adoption consideration.
**Boundary**
Evaluation does not establish adoption, authorise a clinical change or create an implementation responsibility. The single established child does not imply a complete innovation lifecycle.

element.name: [Feature] Identifier Resolution
element.documentation:
Ingest and resolve external identifiers against registered issuing authorities and namespace systems.
Identifier Resolution interprets an identifier in its issuing-authority and namespace context, so that the same local value is not assumed to identify the same person everywhere. It provides an identifiable subject reference without deciding an authoritative master-person match.

element.name: [CT2] Referral Administration
element.documentation:
Referral Administration receives referral material, associates the supporting clinical context and tracks the recipient's explicit disposition and outcome. Its purpose is to keep the request and its progression intelligible across care boundaries. It distinguishes a request for another participant's involvement from an order for bounded fulfilment and from actual acceptance of care responsibility.
**Overview**
Referral Administration receives referral material, associates the supporting clinical context and tracks the recipient's explicit disposition and outcome. Its purpose is to keep the request and its progression intelligible across care boundaries. It distinguishes a request for another participant's involvement from an order for bounded fulfilment and from actual acceptance of care responsibility.
**Intent**
Referral Administration receives referral material, associates the supporting clinical context and tracks the recipient's explicit disposition and outcome. Its purpose is to keep the request and its progression intelligible across care boundaries. It distinguishes a request for another participant's involvement from an order for bounded fulfilment and from actual acceptance of care responsibility.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Transport acceptance does not establish clinical acceptance. A referral need not universally produce an appointment, encounter, order or transfer of care.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Harmonia materially connects the referral, supporting information and reported disposition while the receiving service retains clinical and responsibility decisions.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT3] Diagnostic Data Management
element.documentation:
Manage acquired or produced diagnostic evidence as information, including identity, association, integrity, organisation, availability and lifecycle.
Diagnostic Data Management maintains acquired or produced diagnostic evidence as usable information. Its responsibility includes identity, association, integrity, organisation and lifecycle so that evidence can be found and understood in the right diagnostic context. It addresses the evidence record independently of the professional conclusion subsequently drawn from it.
**Boundary**
Managing diagnostic data neither interprets that data nor governs the authoritative expression of findings in a report.
## Capability model replacement history

Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: Assurance Process Design
element.documentation:
• Canonical Name: Assurance Process Design.
• Owning Capability: Assurance Design (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#assurance-design).
• Process Purpose: Establishes and maintains how satisfaction of a governed requirement, constraint or expected behaviour is to be assured.
• Principal Performing Role: Service Assurance Modeller (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md#service-assurance-modeller).
• Participating Functions: Design Service Assurance (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#design-service-assurance) and Manage Assurance Criteria (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#manage-assurance-criteria). Manage Assurance Criteria retains ownership within Assurance Criteria Management; its participation does not subsume that Capability's criteria lifecycle or transfer its information responsibility to Assurance Design.
• Conceptual Output: Assurance Definition (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#42-assurance-definition--conceptual-modelling-output), retaining its conceptual Business Architecture output/boundary treatment.
• Boundary: Governance Authority establishes what is authoritative. Design does not grant Service Assurance Modeller approval authority. Detailed Assurance Definition lifecycle, approval/publication workflows, criteria lifecycle and information modelling remain unresolved. Participation of the two Functions does not establish a cross-capability lifecycle or a new exchange/Service between their owners.
Assurance design establishes a reusable basis for how satisfaction will be evaluated, rather than running the evaluation itself. Criteria-management participation retains its separate owner and does not create an exchange Service or a shared criteria lifecycle. An Assurance Definition can be reused, so each execution need not imply a freshly performed Design Process.

Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: Continuous and Resilient Regional Health Information Exchange (O2)
element.documentation:
### Outcome Definition Regional healthcare facilities operate within an uninterrupted, highly available, and fault-tolerant digital integration fabric that reliably exchanges clinical events across heterogeneous systems without data loss or performance degradation.
### Clinical & Operational Value - **Zero Silent Data Loss**: Admission notifications, emergency referrals, and diagnostic alerts are guaranteed to cross durable boundaries before positive transport acknowledgement, ensuring that integration failures never result in dropped clinical events. - **High Concurrency & Responsiveness**: Point-of-care clinical queries and vital notification streams remain highly responsive, unblocked by background batch synchronization or database transaction locks. - **Coordinated Inter-Facility Workflows**: Multi-stage clinical activities (e.g., patient transfers, regional lab dispatch, pharmacy updates) progress deterministically across multiple destination systems, preventing divergence of clinical state between facilities. - **Seamless Standards Interoperability**: Seamless bridging of legacy HL7 v2 systems and modern FHIR RESTful repositories without expensive, disruptive rip-and-replace software upgrades.
### Direct Contributing Goals - [Vendor-Independent Longitudinal Clinical Information Coherence](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) (Thread 1) - [Durable Acceptance and Preservation of Clinical Events](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) (Thread 3) - [Responsive Access to Managed Information](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) (Thread 4) - [Coordinated Progression of Operational Activities and Associated Entity State](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) (Thread 7)

element.documentation:
Govern canonical clinical data definitions, terminology bindings, and exchange profiles across regional systems.
Semantic governance provides canonical definitions, bindings and profiles through which regional representations can be understood consistently. Its purpose concerns meaning and constraints rather than a particular schema technology, and consuming a definition does not transfer its governing authority.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Charging & Claims Administration
element.documentation:
This capability supplies clinical activity summaries and charging records to billing contexts. It preserves a route from activity information to the systems responsible for financial processing without treating the export as a completed bill or claim. No Feature decomposition or comprehensive revenue-cycle responsibility is established.
**Overview**
This capability supplies clinical activity summaries and charging records to billing contexts. It preserves a route from activity information to the systems responsible for financial processing without treating the export as a completed bill or claim. No Feature decomposition or comprehensive revenue-cycle responsibility is established.
**Intent**
This capability supplies clinical activity summaries and charging records to billing contexts. It preserves a route from activity information to the systems responsible for financial processing without treating the export as a completed bill or claim. No Feature decomposition or comprehensive revenue-cycle responsibility is established.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Export of activity evidence does not confer pricing, billing, claim or accounting authority.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Its Adjacent standing reflects information supplied to financial systems while the financial activity remains externally governed.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [44433108cc8f4f5f9d7581f9e5b29eb5](44433108cc8f4f5f9d7581f9e5b29eb5.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B15.04`; additional scope correspondences: `E09.03.05`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [UserStory] Referrals contain the required information
element.documentation:
Independent stakeholder need, expectation or desired outcome:
> Retrieve provider referral requirements so that referrals contain the required information.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.

Source-specific access conditions, supporting actors, alternative outcomes, verification and data-authority rules remain distinct in their cited source contributions. Legacy claims that each statement is a business capability are not adopted: this instance has native Requirement semantics. Source target-state scope is not a software delivery commitment for 1.1.21. Historical assessment findings remain recoverable and do not establish current coverage.

Its canonical identity, G01–G18 context, existing Composition and separately established Home assertions are preserved.
Native Grouping originally authored as `Audit-and-Accountability.Accountability-and-Traceability.Requirements` in the retained 004 export, incorporated under the Solution Architect's Subject Grouping hierarchy Task. It groups the source-qualified `Requirements` concern within the existing **Accountability and Traceability** SolutionFacet (G04.04). Its earlier authored name above is retained as provenance; current names follow the explicit properties in the 1.1.19 submission. That earlier incoming record has no Documentation or authored Properties; no normative definition, native statement, classification of individual statements, or additional responsibility is invented to complete that absence.
The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. These are distinct assertions. Neither diagram membership nor the Grouping's label alone establishes another Home or a statement allocation. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.
Source Exchange identifier: `id-96de76241ecd42b2ac583eed9fb161c1`. View placement corroborates the authorised containing SolutionFacet; the exact correspondence is retained in the iteration's folder/Grouping inventories. Existing canonical identities and all pre-existing architectural assertions retain their standing. Archi visual acceptance and HCRL closure remain separate.

**Overview**

**Intent**
Enable health-service operations through information about flow, care-places, capacity, workforce capability, operational work, logistics and discharge progression.

element.name: [CT2] On-Call Management
element.documentation:
On-Call Management resolves the active provider for a specialty, service or hospital at the relevant time. It turns changing coverage information into usable routing context so that operational communication can reach the intended capacity. This differs from authoring the roster or deciding who is professionally qualified for the requested activity.
**Overview**
On-Call Management resolves the active provider for a specialty, service or hospital at the relevant time. It turns changing coverage information into usable routing context so that operational communication can reach the intended capacity. This differs from authoring the roster or deciding who is professionally qualified for the requested activity.
**Intent**
On-Call Management resolves the active provider for a specialty, service or hospital at the relevant time. It turns changing coverage information into usable routing context so that operational communication can reach the intended capacity. This differs from authoring the roster or deciding who is professionally qualified for the requested activity.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Being on call does not by itself establish clinical privilege or assignment of a particular care responsibility.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Current provider resolution materially enables appropriate contact and routing across operational boundaries.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT2] Health Information Standards Governance
element.documentation:
Govern organisational adoption and use of health-information models and applicable standards.
This capability governs which information models and standards the organisation adopts and how their use is supported and evaluated. The model distinguishes discovering candidates, adopting models, educating users, addressing conformity and overseeing governance. Standards impact identification has a separate established place because its implications may extend into clinical practice, policy and obligations beyond information-system implementation.
**Intent**
Make organisational standards use deliberate and its consequences understandable.
**Boundary**
Oversight evaluates governance without performing every peer activity. Adoption includes its own model-impact consideration; the listed abilities do not establish a sequential adoption Process.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT3] Health Service Continuous Improvement
element.documentation:
Evaluate the established service and identify correction/improvement needs that may feed back into modelling and implementation support.
This capability evaluates an established service and identifies correction or improvement needs across its service-wide purpose. It allows experience of actual operation to inform reconsideration of the service model and implementation support. The scope is broader than reporting a clinical-quality finding, while remaining anchored to the service being improved.
**Boundary**
It does not establish generic Continuous Improvement placement or transfer the authority of specialist activities affected by improvement.

element.documentation:
- **Semantic Classification**: `Assertion` - **Definition**: A distinct identifier token issued within a specific namespace authority to identify a person. - **Key Semantic Decomposition**: - `Identifier Value`: The lexical string or token representing the identity code. - `Identifier Authority / Namespace`: The issuing organisation, national scheme, or local domain establishing the uniqueness and validity of the value. - **Architectural Rule**: An identifier is NEVER modelled as an unqualified, opaque string. It is always qualified by its originating authority/namespace.

element.name: [CT1] Community Health & Wellbeing
element.documentation:
Support community health and wellbeing, including the bounded preventative-health abilities required for R1/R2. Wider environmental health, outreach and social determinants remain enterprise context without inferred additional decomposition.
Community Health & Wellbeing frames organised activity supporting health beyond a single person's episode of care. The governed decomposition focuses on preventative health: identifying needs, defining programmes and cohorts, educating, observing programme operation and reporting. Wider outreach, environmental and social-determinant concerns remain enterprise context rather than additional modelled children.
**Intent**
Support organised prevention with a clear relationship between the health problem, intended population and programme activity.
**Boundary**
Programme management does not acquire the clinical or appointment responsibilities needed to deliver a programme.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Programme and cohort distinctions materially shape the information, notifications and care enablement required. This supports the Relevant classification without assigning wider public-health operating authority to Harmonia.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [175174c5cce549d2b154a4f6704721dc](175174c5cce549d2b154a4f6704721dc.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Communication Administration
element.documentation:
This capability manages secure clinical communication transactions, delivery and receipt evidence, and the required enduring audit trail. Verified provider and team endpoints support appropriate addressing while transaction correlation makes the communication history intelligible. The responsibility preserves separate meanings for transport delivery, recipient acknowledgement and clinical or business disposition.
**Overview**
This capability manages secure clinical communication transactions, delivery and receipt evidence, and the required enduring audit trail. Verified provider and team endpoints support appropriate addressing while transaction correlation makes the communication history intelligible. The responsibility preserves separate meanings for transport delivery, recipient acknowledgement and clinical or business disposition.
**Intent**
This capability manages secure clinical communication transactions, delivery and receipt evidence, and the required enduring audit trail. Verified provider and team endpoints support appropriate addressing while transaction correlation makes the communication history intelligible. The responsibility preserves separate meanings for transport delivery, recipient acknowledgement and clinical or business disposition.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Delivery or read receipts do not prove clinical review, incorporation, approval or acceptance. Audit evidence must remain governed without unmasked PHI in diagnostic streams.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Secure addressed communication and attributable transaction evidence are substantive platform responsibilities.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT2] Governance Framework Management
element.documentation:
Establish the authoritative WHAT and legitimate working parameters.
Governance Framework Management establishes what must be satisfied and the legitimate authority and bounds for organisational decisions. Its two children separate obligations attributable to source authority from the allocation and limitation of decision authority. Together they supply the authoritative reference against which operational arrangements and compliance assessments can be considered.
**Intent**
Keep required outcomes and legitimate decision parameters distinguishable and traceable to their authority.
**Boundary**
Interpreting an external obligation or engaging with a regulator does not transfer that body's authority. Operational means remain with management.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `B11.03`; additional scope correspondences: `B12.03`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

**Overview**

**Intent**

element.name: Coordinated Operational Activity and Entity State
element.documentation:
### Context & Pressure Healthcare integration is rarely a simple point-to-point message transmission. A single real-world clinical event—such as a patient admission or an emergency department transfer—triggers a cascade of multi-stage operational activities across multiple downstream systems (e.g., notifying pharmacy, updating bed management, triggering pre-admission lab orders, broadcasting HL7 ADT messages to billing and clinical portals).
When integration middleware treats these complex interactions simply as a stream of disconnected, fire-and-forget messages, failures in downstream destinations cause silent state divergence. The hospital's billing system may record the patient as discharged while the pharmacy continues dispensing medication.
### Architectural Imperative Harmonia must coordinate multi-stage operational activity in lockstep with the governed state of the real-world clinical entity. Activities must progress through explicit, observable state transitions, ensuring that fan-out status, acknowledgements, and retry progressions are fully trackable and recoverable.
- **Primary Stakeholders**: [Healthcare Delivery Organizations](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md), [Platform Operations & Integration Engineers](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md) - **Key Assessment**: [Unmonitored Destination Failure / Fan-Out Divergence](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/assessments.md) - **Associated Goal**: [Coordinated Progression of Operational Activities & Associated Entity State](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) - **Governing Axiom**: [AX-16 (Operational Activity & Entity State Progress Together)](../principle/de7e90f46127455a9ec9ad3b9b48ba54.md)

element.name: [Feature] Addressed Clinical Distribution
element.documentation:
Fan out clinical events and diagnostic reports to designated external and internal recipients with per-destination delivery tracking.
Addressed distribution sends information to explicitly designated recipients and tracks each destination's delivery separately. This preserves partial outcomes in a fan-out rather than collapsing several deliveries into a single success that hides a missing recipient.

element.name: [CT2] Therapeutic Services
element.documentation:
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for therapeutic services services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Overview**
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for therapeutic services services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Intent**
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for therapeutic services services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Therapeutic Services is retained as an Adjacent clinical delivery context, recognising care activity whose information may concern Harmonia without assigning treatment performance to it. The current model establishes no atomic Features for this context. The broad label is not used to invent therapy-specific Functions or reclassify clinical interventions as platform execution.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Information participation does not confer authority to select, perform or assess the clinical adequacy of therapy.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Adjacent standing preserves the contextual role while treatment remains the responsible service's activity.

element.name: Ponos
element.documentation:
### Approved 1.1.24 incorporation — resulting candidate pending
Each applicable execution JVM hosts the common Mneme-Workflow-Cache capability using **embedded Infinispan LOCAL**, holding authorised materialised IU working information. This is per JVM, not a shared site cache or distributed L1/near cache. Common Ergon context loading/unloading, checkpoints and execution recovery remain intact; specialised execution reuses them. Immutable inputs may have independent working manifestations, with no automatic mutation on newer authoritative versions. Existing sequencing, assurance independence and failure boundaries remain unchanged. After loss/eviction, reconstruct through governed Mneme/Mnemosyne acquisition and durable work at the existing recovery boundary; do not resume inside a failed Ergon or treat cache state as checkpoint authority. Memory/security/lifecycle/packaging policy is MC-03/07; no new execution/recovery subsystem is created.
- **Role/responsibility:** reusable execution framework/component pattern, peer to Energeia C39, for governed execution and observable activity progression. [U02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u02) adjudicates this role; [A02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#a02) and [L02/L01/L23](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#l02) retain responsibility context and historical detail. - **Features/contained constructs:** work ingress and dispatcher, workflow/sequence resolution where governed control is established, activity invocation, execution concurrency/timeouts, execution retry/re-attempts, checkpoint coordination and administrative inspection. Applies Praxis-defined output-processing/continuation semantics and routing; not every output-derived Pragma continues that Praxis. [U18](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u18) establishes the distinction, leaving representation open. Subscription matching belongs to Mneme; handoff redelivery/recovery and dead-letter semantics belong to Petasos. Consumer loops/thread pools are documented mechanisms, not logical children. Ordinary semantic interest fan-out to different Ergon types is orthogonal to ActionableTask.ExecutionConcurrency permitting concurrent undertakings by instances of the same type, each through its own FulfillmentTask. DigitalTwin specialises execution with serial Behaviour processing within a Twin; common concurrency facilities do not permit intra-Twin Behaviour concurrency (U19). - **Information:** executes consumer undertakings using governed information/context resolved through Mneme; consults established control definitions and produces execution/progression observations contributing to Journey. Petasos handoff does not make an opaque payload into a Ponos-owned Pragma. - **Persistence:** coordinates recoverable handoff through Petasos and governed information change through Mneme/Mnemosyne. Does not establish durable state by completing an activity or writing a checkpoint to a cache. - **Collaboration/exclusions:** tightly coupled to peer Ergo/Ergon responsibilities, executing/managing bounded Ergon activity conforming to the Ergo contract; does not structurally contain Ergo or Ergon. Uses Praxis, Erga, Themis, Mneme Pragma Management and Petasos. DigitalTwin C19 and Dokimasia C20 specialise/ reuse this pattern; they are not children inside a Ponos runtime. Conceptual supertype language does not mandate literal implementation inheritance. Does not own Pragma information management, Publishing/Subscription/Pattern semantic selection, workflow definitions, concrete domain logic, broker lifecycle, external standards/transport or universal clinical-work determination. - **Standing:** specialisation relationships adjudicated for the candidate by U02; detailed model remains candidate. CDG-03/08/16–18 retain incomplete control and continuation semantics. Numerical worker/retry defaults are not baselined.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F04 | Governed execution ingress and activity dispatch | [Ponos C04](component-register.md#c04) with consumer undertaking, Mneme context resolution, Petasos handoff and Themis; DigitalTwin/Dokimasia reuse common execution | Handoff identity/reference, governed Pragma/context, undertaking and Praxis expected/permitted operational context | U02/U05/U06. Mneme selects information; Petasos establishes concrete handoff; Ponos executes using Praxis without owning it. Detailed control contracts CDG-01/03/16 remain open. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
| F04 | Governed execution ingress and activity dispatch | [Ponos C04](b521762c1ea444b48cd5f66be3752d30.md) with consumer undertaking, Mneme context resolution, Petasos handoff and Themis; DigitalTwin/Dokimasia reuse common execution | Handoff identity/reference, governed Pragma/context, undertaking and Praxis expected/permitted operational context | U02/U05/U06. Mneme selects information; Petasos establishes concrete handoff; Ponos executes using Praxis without owning it. Detailed control contracts CDG-01/03/16 remain open. |
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F05 | Execution concurrency, timeout, failure control and execution retry | Ponos execution support reused by DigitalTwin/Dokimasia, subject to specialised contracts; Ergo/Ergon activity contracts | Interest fan-out across Ergon types differs from ActionableTask.ExecutionConcurrency across instances of the same type, each through its own FulfillmentTask | U02/U05/U19. Execution retry differs from Petasos redelivery. No intra-Twin Behaviour concurrency or automatic stopped-Twin resumption follows from common facilities; F32 governs. Detailed mechanisms CDG-03/07/08/16/17/54. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
| F05 | Execution concurrency, timeout, failure control and execution retry | Ponos execution support reused by DigitalTwin/Dokimasia, subject to specialised contracts; Ergo/Ergon activity contracts | Interest fan-out across Ergon types differs from ActionableTask.ExecutionConcurrency across instances of the same type, each through its own FulfillmentTask | U02/U05/U19. Execution retry differs from Petasos redelivery. No intra-Twin Behaviour concurrency or automatic stopped-Twin resumption follows from common facilities; F32 governs. Detailed mechanisms CDG-03/07/08/16/17/54. |
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/middleware.md` — ``table assertion: | M03 | **Ponos governed execution ingress, dispatch and progression** | Consumer resolves Pragma/context through Mneme and establishes its distinct FulfillmentTask for ActionableTask undertaking; Ponos manages execution and execution retry/re-attempts | U02/U05. Ponos does not convert an opaque transport payload into information it manages, match Subscriptions or own handoff dead-letter recovery. Detailed continuation/acknowledgement CDG-01/03/16/17. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
| M03 | **Ponos governed execution ingress, dispatch and progression** | Consumer resolves Pragma/context through Mneme and establishes its distinct FulfillmentTask for ActionableTask undertaking; Ponos manages execution and execution retry/re-attempts | U02/U05. Ponos does not convert an opaque transport payload into information it manages, match Subscriptions or own handoff dead-letter recovery. Detailed continuation/acknowledgement CDG-01/03/16/17. |
## ARB DesignNote assertion contributions
These bounded source assertions are reconciled under the cited U-decisions and ARB release Praxis. They retain the source's candidate, scope and detailed-design qualifications. They do not accept the whole Domain05 candidate or create a new element per paragraph. Later-corrected assertions are retained in the disposition evidence instead of being restored here.
### DesignNote-Energeia-DigitalTwin-Dokimasia-Specialisation — original lines 16-16
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Energeia-DigitalTwin-Dokimasia-Specialisation.md`; U02/U06/U19; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
Ponos is Harmonia's reusable execution framework/component pattern. It provides common execution machinery upon which specialised execution components can be built. Architecturally this is similar to a supertype/superclass relationship, without requiring literal implementation inheritance.
### DesignNote-Energeia-DigitalTwin-Dokimasia-Specialisation — original lines 18-18
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Energeia-DigitalTwin-Dokimasia-Specialisation.md`; U02/U06/U19; source-qualified assertion, current subject standing unchanged.
DigitalTwin and Dokimasia are specialised Ponos-based execution components. They are not structurally contained by the Ponos runtime component.

The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. These are distinct assertions. Neither diagram membership nor the Grouping's label alone establishes another Home or a statement allocation. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.
Source Exchange identifier: `id-918400789c3f471388455b18ac722408`. View placement corroborates the authorised containing SolutionFacet; the exact correspondence is retained in the iteration's folder/Grouping inventories. Existing canonical identities and all pre-existing architectural assertions retain their standing. Archi visual acceptance and HCRL closure remain separate.

element.documentation:
Resolve currently active on-call specialists, registrars, and operational managers for a given specialty and hospital at any point in time.
Active on-call resolution identifies the current provider in the required specialty and hospital context. It supports correct routing at the relevant time without authoring the roster or treating current coverage as proof of qualification, privilege or responsibility acceptance.

element.name: Criterion
element.documentation:
A Criterion represents a **governed permitted combination** across applicable dimensions, using [Calliope-controlled nomenclature](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#authorisation-nomenclature):
```text Criterion = Information.Compartment AND Information.Classification AND Function.Name AND Function.Scope AND applicable Temporal constraints ```
The four principal dimensions describe **what** is authorised; applicable temporal constraints describe **when**. Within an individual Criterion, applicable dimensions are **conjunctive**. Between Criteria, grants are **additive / UNION**: each Criterion independently contributes its permitted combination. Only explicitly governed combinations have authorisation meaning. Absence of a matching effective Criterion results in **DENY**.
**Explicit negative/DENY Criteria are not part of this Candidate Architecture.** Neither arbitrary Boolean policy expressions, deny-overrides semantics nor a general-purpose policy language is introduced by this model.

element.name: [CT2] Care Access Transaction Enablement
element.documentation:
Coordinate the intake, care-request disposition and appointment information through which a person accesses care.
**Overview**
Coordinate the intake, care-request disposition and appointment information through which a person accesses care. Its constituent abilities distinguish Client-Centred Administration; Referral Administration; Scheduling Administration.
**Intent**
Make an access request and its disposition traceable without confusing a booking with care responsibility or delivery.
**Boundary**
A referral requests care responsibility; an appointment concerns a booking. Neither establishes care delivery or host booking authority.

element.name: [BusinessObject] Search Result Set
element.documentation:
### Accepted Information Unit Framework incorporation — 1.1.22
Under the accepted IU Framework this remains a governed metadata collection of references to IU Versions, not the contents of every matched IU. Search authorisation and subsequent individual IU read authorisation may differ. Persistence in Ergon Context does not change underlying IU identity; operational Version, authoritative durable progression and Active Generation must retain their governing reference semantics. The [InformationUnit](../../application/data-object/class/74ec609de1ae498fbf9d13e4ef8c6cbe.md) framework establishes no new Search Result Set schema.
> **A search over Harmonia-managed information produces a governed > metadata-based Search Result Set referencing the Information Unit Versions > comprising that result. Search does not, by itself, duplicate or create new > versions of the returned managed information.**
**Search Result Set** names this managed metadata collection. It specialises the established [Collection meaning](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#21-semantic-classifications) and [membership distinction](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/containment-and-collections.md#3-collections-vs-containment-distinct-semantics) through search-specific Version-reference membership. It introduces no new semantic category or Information Concept-to-Information Unit equivalence. “Search Result Metadata-Set” describes the same concept rather than an additional concept or representation.
Management attaches to the result set's own governed search/result metadata and membership within its Information Unit boundary. The referenced Information Units / Versions retain their existing management boundaries, authority and history. Creating the result artefact SHALL NOT create copies of the returned Units, new Versions of those Units, a BLOB of duplicated managed information, or another authority for that information.
```text Harmonia-Managed Information | | search v Search Result Set (managed metadata collection) | +-- Search / Result Metadata | +-- Result Membership [0..*] | +-- Information Unit Version Reference ```
### 2.1 Information Unit Version Membership
Membership records the applicable **Information Unit Version**, expressing:
> **These were the managed Information Unit Versions comprising the result > of this search.**
It SHALL NOT resolve later to whichever Active Generation or current Version happens to exist when the result set is examined. For example, membership identifying Unit U's Version V7 continues to identify V7 after U progresses to V8 or has a different active manifestation. These labels establish no identifier scheme. The [closed Version / Active Generation semantics](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#651-version-and-active-generation) remain unchanged.
The set contains membership references, not copies of member content. The conceptual `0..*` membership permits an empty result. It establishes neither a reference encoding nor downstream retrieval, retention or manifestation mechanics, and implies no universal atomic observation of all members.
### 2.2 Search / Result Metadata
The set SHALL contain sufficient metadata to represent the search and its result as a governed information artefact. Semantic categories may include search context, search criteria, execution/result time, result-set identity, result membership and other metadata necessary to establish the governed meaning of the result.
These categories are not a complete metadata schema, mandatory field list, datatype or serialization. They prescribe no database, API or cache structure. Search context does not automatically persist operational security context as resource content; AX-07 remains applicable.
### 2.3 Search and Separate Self-Contained Artefacts
Version-specific membership preserves the meaning of a search result; it does not make ordinary search a generic snapshot mechanism. The Search Result Set is not a self-contained duplicated parcel of the referenced content.
Export, snapshot, document generation, archival package, transmission package or another self-contained information artefact requires a separate semantic act/capability. Such acts are not intrinsic to search and are not designed here. The existing [Assembly/View and snapshot distinctions](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/assemblies-views/assemblies-and-views.md#3-assembly-lifecycle-vs-constituent-lifecycle) remain applicable without an automatic Search Result Set-to-Assembly mapping.
Source standing: Adjudicated conceptual managed metadata collection; Search Result Metadata-Set is the same concept, not an additional element.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/search-results.md` — ## 1. Authority and Two Search Cases. Standing: Adjudicated search boundary; exact source qualifications retained.
The authorised 2026-10-10 search adjudication distinguishes:
1. **Harmonia-Managed Information Search** over existing managed Information Units / Information Unit Versions. 2. **External Information Search** intentionally performed as part of an Ergo activity.
These cases have different management semantics. A generic transition from observed information to accepted management SHALL NOT replace this distinction. The [Harmonia-managed information definition and Information Unit boundary](10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md) continue to govern. Management responsibility remains distinct from originating information authority and authority over the underlying domain activity.
The established upstream responsibilities are [Search & Discovery (EC-05)](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-05-search--discovery), [retrieval mediation and governed query/search (FEAT-ISE-05/08/09)](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#detailed-capability--feature-catalogue-intrinsic--shared-enablement), and Business [Health Information Exchange](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/05-intrinsic-enablement.md#22-health-information-exchange-hie) and [Health Information Access](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/05-intrinsic-enablement.md#23-health-information-access). The [Business ownership matrix](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/information-responsibility/information-responsibility.md#2-canonical-business-information-ownership-matrix) establishes Query Execution Context & Projection State without ownership of queried source records. Those sources establish search purpose and responsibility; the two-case management boundary below is the explicit Domain04 adjudication, not a claim that the upstream sources already specified result membership.
[AX-04](../../motivation/principle/54508cda80484a6caf95b901780eaf7d.md) preserves semantic authority independently of machinery; [AX-05](../../motivation/principle/0412a2084f0145babc4f022c71fea65f.md) preserves active/durable state distinctions; [AX-06](../../motivation/principle/952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md) and [AX-18](../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/b8cafe3cf5904d2bb9a9767260fddf78.md) preserve source and domain authority. [AX-07–09](../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md) govern security context and meaningful evidence; [AX-13](../../motivation/principle/b6a55decfeec4f1bb3d7f18534a2ffea.md) preserves the external management boundary; [AX-14](../../motivation/principle/d3fc6025dc7646d1b2020b51f7a44bfa.md) and [AX-17](../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) preserve the distinctions and explicitly unestablished details below. No new axiom is required.
## Source-qualified contribution

### 2.1 Information Unit Version Membership

The [closed Version / Active Generation semantics](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#651-version-and-active-generation) remain unchanged.

### 2.3 Search and Separate Self-Contained Artefacts

Such acts are not intrinsic to search and are not designed here. The existing [Assembly/View and snapshot distinctions](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/assemblies-views/assemblies-and-views.md#3-assembly-lifecycle-vs-constituent-lifecycle) remain applicable without an automatic Search Result Set-to-Assembly mapping.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/search-results.md` — ## 4. Search Result Information and Audit / Assurance. Standing: Adjudicated search boundary; exact source qualifications retained.
The Search Result Set establishes which managed Information Unit Versions comprised a search result. Audit / Assurance information may establish other meaning: requester/actor, applicable authority, access/control decisions, disclosure, operational evidence or assurance conclusions. These meanings SHALL remain distinct.
```text External Consumer | v Pylai | +----> Audit / Assurance information (according to policy) | v Harmonia-Managed Information Search | v Search Result Set ```
Overlapping metadata or references are legitimate; correlation does not make these artefacts equivalent and does not require eliminating the overlap. The result set SHALL NOT be collapsed into Audit / Assurance evidence. Its possible contextual evidentiary use does not redefine its information meaning or make every search operation audit evidence. Detailed Audit / Assurance semantics remain outside this adjudication.
An externally published search response remains governed by its applicable interoperability contract. AX-13 terminates Harmonia management of the emitted representation, while internally retained managed information remains governed. This conceptual result set prescribes no external envelope or response format.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/search-results.md` — ## 5. Resolution and Retained Boundaries. Standing: Adjudicated search boundary; exact source qualifications retained.
This two-case adjudication resolves the former generic search-management question retained in the metamodel and Assembly/View guidance. It establishes the managed metadata result boundary and governed external acquisition without a generic management-acceptance transition.
Search APIs, indexing, pagination, result encoding, reference realization, cache/persistence structures, component allocation and manifestation mechanics remain downstream concerns. Result metadata detail, retention and separate snapshot/export capabilities are not designed here. Existing explicit TaskOutcome detail, ReportedTask, candidate-family and Audit / Assurance deferrals retain their standing under AX-17. This bounded decision does not declare Domain04 complete or authorise Domain05 derivation.

element.name: [Feature] Mandatory Significant Activity Audit Capture
element.documentation:
Capture required significant activity evidence using the specifically governed authoritative audit-capture boundary.
**Overview**
The actor whose action is recorded need not be entitled to persist the audit. Required capture uses its own established authority and failure can block the governed operation.
**Boundary**
Specific audit authority is not borrowed from the audited identity or generalised to other operations.

element.name: AX-13 Harmonia Management Has an Explicit Boundary
element.documentation:
#### Axiom
Ingress establishes Harmonia management. Internal processing preserves Harmonia management. Egress terminates Harmonia management of the emitted representation.
Harmonia MAY retain evidence describing the information from which an external representation was derived, the transformation applied, the transmission performed and the externally observable outcome.
Harmonia SHALL NOT attribute its internal authority, governance, concurrency, security, availability or operational guarantees to an emitted representation after that representation crosses an external egress boundary.
#### Rationale
Harmonia can govern information while it is under Harmonia's control. It cannot govern a copy after that copy has been transferred to another system.
Provenance can describe what Harmonia emitted; it cannot extend Harmonia's operational control into another system.
#### Consequences
An HL7 v2 message ceases to be a Harmonia-managed representation when emitted through its external egress boundary.
A FHIR resource returned through REST similarly becomes an externally held representation after transmission.
A subsequent FHIR PUT, HL7 v2 message or other submission represents a new ingress interaction and is assessed accordingly.
An HTTP ETag, FHIR meta.versionId, HL7 acknowledgement or equivalent interoperability mechanism MAY communicate externally meaningful transaction or version semantics. It SHALL NOT be interpreted as extending Harmonia's internal operational control beyond its boundary.
#### Maxim
Provenance may describe or cross the boundary; operational control does not.
**This does not mean:**
- The underlying information inside Harmonia ceases to be managed when a representation is published. - Harmonia forgets what it transmitted. - Acknowledgements and transaction outcomes are irrelevant to audit or provenance.

element.name: [CT3] Access Control Enforcement
element.documentation:
Ensure physical, procedural and digital control mechanisms coherently impose intended controls.
Access Control Enforcement ensures that intended controls are coherently imposed through the applicable physical, procedural and digital mechanisms. It represents the organisational ability to make controls effective, rather than equating enforcement with one software decision. Its outcome depends on the controlled circumstances and the arrangements intended to apply there.
**Boundary**
A local software authorisation result alone does not establish coherent end-to-end organisational enforcement.

element.name: [CT2] Event & Subscription
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Publish, ingest, correlate, filter, and syndicate events and subscription-driven changes across the enterprise landscape. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Ingesting operational and clinical event triggers from external systems and internal state changes. - Managing topic- and criteria-based event subscriptions for internal and external consumers. - Evaluating dynamic subscription filters to match event payloads with interested subscriber criteria. - Delivering asynchronous event notifications reliably to registered subscribers. - **Decoupling Note**: Defined strictly in terms of event publishing, criteria matching, and notification delivery; entirely independent of broker topics, partitions, or queues.
Event & Subscription connects significant changes with participants whose registered interests match them. It makes event ingestion, correlation, interest criteria and notification reusable across clinical and operational contexts. The architectural meaning is the relationship between a change and an interested consumer, rather than the broker constructs used to carry it.
**Boundary**
Receiving a notification does not determine the consumer's business response; topics and queues do not define the capability.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E06.08`; additional scope correspondences: `E02.04`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [UserStory] I can effectively manage system resources
element.documentation:
Independent stakeholder need, expectation or desired outcome:
> As an Integration Administrator, I want to control when provider information is added to the Provider Directory, so that I can effectively manage system resources.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.
### Reconciled source contributions
- `SR-11` — Control National Provider Data Integration; Additional Source Use Cases and System Requirements; [source](../../../../../openspec/specs/provider-directory-integration/sr-11-control-national-provider-data-integration/spec.md). - `SR-25` — Control Internal Provider Data Integration; Additional Source Use Cases and System Requirements; [source](../../../../../openspec/specs/provider-directory-integration/sr-25-control-internal-provider-data-integration/spec.md). - `SR-6` — Control When Provider Information Is Added; Additional Source Use Cases and System Requirements; [source](../../../../../openspec/specs/provider-directory-integration/sr-6-control-when-provider-information-is-added/spec.md).
Source-specific access conditions, supporting actors, alternative outcomes, verification and data-authority rules remain distinct in their cited source contributions. Legacy claims that each statement is a business capability are not adopted: this instance has native Requirement semantics. Source target-state scope is not a software delivery commitment for 1.1.21. Historical assessment findings remain recoverable and do not establish current coverage.

element.name: [CT1] Corporate Resources & Enterprise Services
element.documentation:
Provide the bounded clinical-activity charging information and enterprise support context required for R1/R2, without assigning enterprise finance, HR, facilities or ICT operating authority to Harmonia.
This capability retains the financial and corporate-support context material to R1/R2. The financial branch concentrates on information about clinical activity relevant to charging or cost; corporate support covers administrative, physical, technical, people and communication conditions affecting service activity. The limited decomposition makes these dependencies visible without assigning a complete corporate enterprise architecture to Harmonia.
**Intent**
Support health-service activity with the required corporate context and legitimate activity information.
**Boundary**
Evidence about cost-relevant activity does not perform billing or accounting. Consuming corporate resource state does not acquire the authority to operate those resources.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Clinical activity evidence provides material financial support. Corporate constraints may also affect enablement, but contextual consumption does not classify every corporate descendant as Relevant or Core.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [a2dbd74847a44f4c879983229f5c9d08](a2dbd74847a44f4c879983229f5c9d08.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). element.name: [CT3] Organisation Contact
element.documentation:
Maintaining verified administrative and clinical communication channels.
**Overview**
Verified facility contact channels make an organisation reachable for appropriate administrative and clinical communication. The contact record says how it may be reached; recipient qualification and disclosure policy govern a particular use.
**Intent**
Provide verified channels for reaching the intended healthcare organisation.
**Boundary**
Contact validity is distinct from clinical recipient eligibility and policy permission.

element.name: Patient Safety & Identity Integrity
element.documentation:
### Context & Pressure Patient safety is a foundational operational priority in healthcare. Accurately associating a clinical observation, pathology result, or medication order with the correct individual human subject is essential.
Mismatched patient records lead directly to severe clinical harm: administering contraindicated blood transfusions, giving incorrect medication doses to patients with unrecorded allergies, or performing wrong-patient interventions. In distributed regional networks, patients move between multiple facilities where different local medical record numbers (MRNs) are assigned.
### Architectural Imperative Harmonia must rigorously preserve and validate subject referential integrity across all managed clinical events. It must prevent ambiguous, invalid, or contradictory subject associations from being silently treated as valid.
*Note on Architectural Boundary*: Harmonia does not act as an enterprise Master Patient Index (MPI) or deterministic golden-record matcher. Rather, it enforces strict referential validation and transparently captures identifier provenance without lossy unification.
- **Primary Stakeholders**: [Patients & Care Recipients](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md), [Clinicians & Care Teams](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md) - **External Constraint**: [Applicable National / Jurisdictional Healthcare Identifier Obligations](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/requirements-constraints/external-constraints.md) - **Associated Goal**: [Reliable Subject Identity & Referential Integrity](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) - **Governing Axioms**: [AX-06 (Explicit Information Authority)](../principle/952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md), [AX-14 (Preservation of Semantic Distinctions)](../principle/d3fc6025dc7646d1b2020b51f7a44bfa.md)

element.name: [UserStory] Provider status used by the Provider Directory is supported by current authoritative evidence
element.documentation:
Independent stakeholder need, expectation or desired outcome:
> As the Provider Directory, I need to verify a provider's current status against an authoritative national source, so that provider status used by the Provider Directory is supported by current authoritative evidence.
The need is independently identifiable. It may encompass interactions, governance, human and organisational activity beyond any associated UseCase. Successful execution of associated interactions does not establish satisfaction of this need.
### Reconciled source contributions

element.documentation:
Provide professional medication-specific advice about appropriate use, precautions, interactions, administration, adherence or safe handling.
Medication Advice provides professional guidance about medication use and its precautions, interactions, administration, adherence or handling. It supports understanding of how medication can be used safely without turning every advisory interaction into a prescribing decision. Within pharmacy services, the advice outcome is distinct from provision of the medicine itself.
**Boundary**
Advice does not confer authority to diagnose, prescribe or alter treatment; detailed scope remains subject to refinement.

element.name: [ArchitecturalAxiom] AX-18 Integration and Coordination Do Not Confer Domain Authority
element.documentation:
#### Axiom
> Harmonia MAY integrate information concerning, and coordinate operational activity associated with, an externally governed domain activity without thereby acquiring authority to determine or manage that domain activity. > > Authority to determine or manage a domain activity SHALL remain with the responsible actor, system or governed capability unless that authority is explicitly assigned to Harmonia by the architecture. > > Harmonia's observation, processing, persistence, distribution, presentation or use of information concerning a domain activity SHALL NOT, by itself, establish authority over that activity.
#### Rationale
Participation in a domain activity and authority over that activity are different architectural concerns. Information possession, observation, integration, coordination and processing do not, by themselves, confer domain authority. Authority requires explicit architectural assignment.
This new human-approved axiom generalises an already-established class of architectural boundary. It is established at the 2026-10-09 migration boundary; it is not a claim that AX-01 through AX-17 always contained this axiom.
#### Consequences and qualifications
AX-18 SHALL NOT be interpreted as preventing Harmonia from performing operational activity for which architecture has assigned Harmonia responsibility. Explicit architectural assignment may establish authority to determine or manage a domain activity.
In particular, AX-18 does not mean:
- Harmonia cannot execute Praxis/Ergo activity; - Harmonia cannot coordinate entity-specific operational activity through a Digital Twin; - Harmonia cannot process or transform clinical information; - Harmonia cannot perform workflow/activity coordination; - Harmonia cannot manage responsibilities explicitly assigned to Harmonia; - Harmonia cannot enforce policy, security, information governance or operational controls assigned to it.
Participation, information, integration and coordination do not, by themselves, establish authority to determine or manage the underlying domain activity. Assigned Harmonia operational responsibility remains applicable.
#### Examples and established specialisations (non-normative)
These examples explain the boundary; they do not expand the axiom or establish Application Components, Information Concepts, Services, Processes, AI allocation or implementation mechanisms.
- **Clinical work:** Harmonia may integrate and coordinate around clinical work without thereby acquiring authority to determine clinical work, manage clinical handover, own clinical worklists, allocate clinical work, make clinical decisions or become the EMR workflow authority. The detailed [Domain03 clinical-work integration boundary](../../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/metamodel/business-architecture-metamodel.md#37-clinical-work-integration-boundary) remains the Business specialisation. - **Digital Twins:** A Twin may coordinate operational activity associated with its real-world entity without thereby acquiring authority over originating clinical facts or domain decisions. The [Strategy entity-specific coordination rule](../../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/strategic-views/logical-component-responsibilities.md#entity-specific-operational-coordination) remains controlling for that coordination. - **Capacity:** Higher-order Service Capacity Management may consume context-specific capacity without acquiring the originating responsibility for Clinic, Ward, Theatre, ED, Outpatient or Mobile Service Capacity Management. The detailed [Business capacity responsibility boundary](../../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/04-health-service-operations.md#capacity-management-responsibility-boundary) remains in Business Architecture. - **Assurance:** Observation, access to evidence or establishment of an assurance conclusion does not confer management authority over the activity being assured. Independent Assurance remains governed by [REQ-FND-005](../../requirement/bbb7438e78604308abba93afc14f4e2e.md) and its established [Strategy](../../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md) and [Business](../../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md) derivation. - **Presentation / UI:** Presentation or collection of information does not, by itself, confer originating information or domain-decision authority on the presenting component. The existing [Iris contextual human interaction responsibility](../../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/strategic-views/logical-component-responsibilities.md#component-6-iris-contextual-human-interaction) remains distinct. - **AI:** Assistance with interpretation, pattern recognition, criteria evaluation or decision support does not, by itself, confer the authority of the governed actor, role or capability using that assistance. This example assigns no AI responsibility or capability.
#### Related architectural authority
- [AX-06](../952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md) governs information authority and credibility. - [AX-13](../b6a55decfeec4f1bb3d7f18534a2ffea.md) governs the Harmonia management boundary at ingress/egress. - [AX-14](../d3fc6025dc7646d1b2020b51f7a44bfa.md) preserves meaningful semantic distinctions. - [AX-16](../de7e90f46127455a9ec9ad3b9b48ba54.md) governs coordinated operational activity/entity progression. - [AX-17](8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) governs architectural authority and explicit uncertainty. - AX-18 governs inference of domain authority from participation, information, integration or coordination.

element.name: [CT1] Individual Care Delivery
element.documentation:
Assess, clinically determine, plan, intervene, monitor and review individual care independently of setting, mode, time pattern or organisational arrangement.
Individual Care Delivery is the organisation's ability to understand an individual's health and act on that understanding through purposeful care. Its six constituent abilities distinguish establishing findings, interpreting their clinical meaning, choosing a response, performing care, observing change and evaluating care against its objectives. These distinctions describe responsibilities and outcomes rather than a compulsory sequence: a consultation or continuing episode may revisit several of them.
The same ability can be exercised in a hospital, a general practice, a home or a virtual consultation. Setting and time pattern affect the circumstances of care without changing the responsibility represented by this capability.
**Intent**
Support clinically meaningful care whose intent, performance, observed effects and continuing appropriateness can be distinguished.
**Boundary**
Care access, appointments and operational coordination enable care but do not establish that it has been performed. Clinical judgement and the authority to deliver care remain with the responsible participants; possession or coordination of their information does not transfer that authority to Harmonia.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Harmonia supplies and connects information used in individual care. The approved Health Information Access support trace is bounded: records can inform care, but direct assessment can establish findings independently, and access to a proposed intervention does not authorise its performance.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: InformationRepresentation
element.documentation:
An InformationRepresentation is the singular governed presentation of the Content of one InformationUnit. Each IU contains **exactly one InformationRepresentation [1..1]**. This is a logical structured DataObject; it establishes no implementation Class, independently governed nested IU or additional information identity.
| Constituent concern | Accepted meaning | | --- | --- | | ContainerMetadata | Native container, envelope, assembly and carriage semantics: relevant source/destination, author/recipient, assembly and interaction context. Native envelope semantics are preserved where governed; they are not invariably disposable transport state or IU Metadata. | | ContentMetadata | Describes the represented Content independently of its values. Includes a Topic describing Content Structure and a Content Structure Version. Other characteristics, where governed, may include type/profile/model, concrete format/encoding, language, size, hash/digest and references. | | Content | The actual native information, structured/textual/binary/composite/opaque, inline or referenced, FHIR or non-FHIR. Native instance version, if supported (for example FHIR meta.versionId), remains inside Content; none is fabricated for an unversioned payload. |
**Unit Structure ≠ Content Structure ≠ Content Format.** ContentMetadata.Version means Content Structure Version, not Mneme operational Version or native payload instance version. Container Metadata, Content Metadata and IU Metadata remain distinguishable. These constituents are semantic structure, not additional Classes, Topics, schemas or a mandatory list of populated fields.
The IU maintains no alternate-representation collection, otherRepresentations(), reverse-transformation rules or synchronisation dependencies. A transforming consumer creates a **new IU with its own single representation** when the result is to be governed, with appropriate Provenance and any expressly supplied optional relationships. Transformation fidelity and any attempted reverse update remain that consumer's business logic; source updates remain governed. Lossy or irreversible transformations confer no automatic backlink or source-change obligation.
Mnemosyne and its PersistenceServices may decompose or reference physical storage and use provider-native forms. Retrieval must faithfully reconstruct/deliver the governed IU contract with required identity, Metadata/Content integrity and accepted state consistency. Provider-native storage is not another governed representation. Native Content integrity/byte fidelity and preservation obligations retain scope; large referenced binaries need not occupy one row, file or physical write.
Content-aware and Content-neutral services/providers may participate under their own governed contracts without redefining the IU. Content-aware integration may inspect/transform relevant ContainerMetadata under its owning Feature; this does not transfer integration business logic to Mnemosyne or require Content-neutral providers to interpret native payload meaning.

element.name: [CT2] Digital Identity & Access Governance
element.documentation:
Govern sufficient identity confidence and coherent access controls across the organisation.
This capability governs who may act and how controlled concerns are identified and protected across the organisation. Its children separate confidence in a claimed identity, identity models, contextual identity quality, authentication, access-control context, assurance, collaboration and enforcement. That separation prevents successful authentication from being treated as sufficient authority for every use.
**Intent**
Make identity confidence and control requirements appropriate to the circumstances in which access or activity occurs.
**Boundary**
Federation or Single Sign-On does not guarantee identity quality. Enforcement spans physical, procedural and digital controls; it is broader than a runtime policy engine.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [Feature] Communication Audit Logging
element.documentation:
Maintain an enduring, non-PHI, tamper-evident log of all clinical communication transactions.
Communication audit evidence preserves the attributable transaction history required for scrutiny of clinical communication. It records meaningful communication facts under the zero-PHI constraints rather than turning the audit trail into a copy of message content or a permanent diagnostic trace.

element.name: [CT3] Access Control Assurance & Reporting
element.documentation:
Establish organisational assurance/evidence of whether access-control arrangements are appropriately established and operating.
This capability establishes organisational evidence and assurance about whether access-control arrangements are appropriately established and operating. It makes control effectiveness a distinct concern from defining requirements or performing an individual enforcement action. Reporting communicates that established position without making an isolated successful check proof of end-to-end control.
**Boundary**
Subject-specific access-control assurance does not create another macro-level Health Service Assurance hierarchy.
## Capability model replacement history

Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT3] Identity Identification & Authentication
element.documentation:
Identify an actor and authenticate the asserted identity.
This capability identifies the acting participant and authenticates the asserted identity. It establishes who is acting under the applicable identity arrangements so that later control and accountability can be grounded in an identified actor. The outcome remains distinct from confidence established through identity evidence and from authority to access a controlled concern.
**Boundary**
Authentication neither establishes every required identity-quality condition nor authorises the requested activity.
