element.name: [CT2] Health Service Administration
element.documentation:
Health Service Administration represents identifiable services and the conditions under which organisations, locations and practitioner roles provide them. Catalogue publishing, service-location-provider association, operating schedules and eligibility definitions allow a service to be understood as more than a location or specialty label. The service context remains material wherever activity meaning or accountability depends on it.
**Overview**
Health Service Administration represents identifiable services and the conditions under which organisations, locations and practitioner roles provide them. Catalogue publishing, service-location-provider association, operating schedules and eligibility definitions allow a service to be understood as more than a location or specialty label. The service context remains material wherever activity meaning or accountability depends on it.
**Intent**
Health Service Administration represents identifiable services and the conditions under which organisations, locations and practitioner roles provide them. Catalogue publishing, service-location-provider association, operating schedules and eligibility definitions allow a service to be understood as more than a location or specialty label. The service context remains material wherever activity meaning or accountability depends on it.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
This capability owns the service mapping associations, not the mapped organisations, locations or practitioners. The supplied Domain03-to-Domain04 trace preserves that distinction; it does not transfer entity ownership.
## Qualified relationship assertions

element.name: [CT2] Health Information Exchange
element.documentation:
Exchange health information appropriately between participating parties, systems and services.
As a Business Capability, Health Information Exchange is the organisational ability to move health information appropriately between participating parties, systems and services. It explains the enterprise purpose served by exchange without defining that purpose as a protocol, server or software product. Its placement under Connected Health Services distinguishes information exchange from the broader interaction and notification purposes of Digital Communication Channel.
**Boundary**
No CT3 decomposition is established. The identically named BEC is a distinct enabling responsibility; the naming conflict remains unresolved, and this entry does not merge the two or assign the sharing-programme concern a parent.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

## ARB source correspondence
Scope/anti-responsibility and clinical/operational meaning establish the responsible Capability; descriptive ledger/registry/asset labels do not establish a separately bounded formal Information Concept. Preserve non-transfer and source authority.
Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/information-responsibility/information-responsibility.md` — information responsibility row 28. Standing: Established Business responsibility only; formal information identity/lifecycle not inferred.
```text | **Health Information Exchange** | **Exchange Transaction Ledger & Route Matrix** | Ingress message transaction receipts, federated query logs, point-to-point routing tables, and publish-subscribe syndication topic matrices. | Does not own transported message content. | ```

element.name: [CT3] Research Information De-identification & Minimisation
element.documentation:
Research-purpose information can be prepared through appropriate de-identification, pseudonymisation and minimisation, preserving research utility while managing re-identification risks. Participants' rights, information and wellbeing remain protected through consent, risk monitoring, withdrawal recognition and adverse-event response. De-identification does not authorise unrestricted disclosure: consent, authorisation and disclosure conditions remain governed. This Business capability does not imply that Harmonia performs every underlying transformation or makes every disclosure decision.

element.name: AuthorisationRole
element.documentation:
Criteria support containment, collection and nesting for management and reuse:
```text CriteriaCollection (conceptual label; final name unresolved) ├── Criterion ├── Criterion └── CriteriaCollection ├── Criterion └── Criterion ```
Flattening nested collections produces the same additive set of effective Criteria. Nesting creates no arbitrary Boolean semantics and requires no Role hierarchy. The exact implementation name/class hierarchy and representation remain deferred; this diagram establishes no lifecycle/ownership semantics beyond the stated management/reuse requirement.
An **AuthorisationRole** is named, governed and assignable and contains Criteria and/or Criteria collections. Its contents are additive:
```text EffectiveCriteria(AuthorisationRole) = UNION(all contained Criteria)
IdentityEffectiveCriteria = DirectCriteria UNION AuthorisationRole1.Criteria UNION AuthorisationRole2.Criteria UNION ... ```
An Identity may have directly assigned Criteria, one or more AuthorisationRoles, or both. This applies to human and system Identities. The UNION is of applicable grants, subject to governed assignments, temporal validity, revocation and applicable operational context; it does not remove a Criterion's conjunctions or require every contained Criterion to match simultaneously.

element.name: TopicMask
element.documentation:
TopicMask is Harmonia's shared logical discrimination structure, comprising regular-expression patterns applied **separately to corresponding individual canonical-name elements** of a Topic. Applicable element expressions must match under governed syntax/anchoring rules. It is neither one whole-name regex nor a precomputed enumeration/set of TopicIDs. An element wildcard cannot silently span adjacent dot-separated name elements. Matching can include subsequently introduced Topics whose canonical-name elements satisfy the pattern without editing a list.
For example, `<BusinessDomain>.<StandardsBodyName>.InformationCompartment.<CompartmentName>` illustrates a Topic hierarchy. `*.*.InformationCompartment.PersonalInformation*` is illustrative shorthand only: an unconstrained element might use `.*` in actual element-wise regex. Precise anchoring, escaping, missing/excess elements, variable depth and serialised syntax remain with the applicable common match contract. The example is not an implemented parser or prescribed regex dialect.
Publication/subscription, routing, discovery, security and other Topic-discriminating Features reuse the same semantics. A match is a discrimination result; consuming Features determine its consequence. Matching alone grants no access, publishes nothing, schedules no delivery and selects no persistence provider. IU SecurityContext is one consumer and does not own this common model. Canonical Topic renaming may change matching consequences without changing TopicID and requires governance.
This is a logical DataObject, not an inferred Class, SecurityMask subtype, Feature-specific wrapper, new named Topic, executable Function or universal IU get()/test() catalogue. Existing accepted action/compartment criteria retain scope; the IU model creates no parallel taxonomy or general-purpose policy interpreter.

element.name: REQ-FND-005: Independent Assurance of Governed Activity
element.documentation:
**Classification:** Foundational Platform Requirement. **Status:** APPROVED — human architectural approval recorded on 2026-10-08; normative wording and relationships unchanged. The authorised Independent Assurance reconciliation is APPROVED / CLOSED; Domain01 Motivation Architecture is CLOSED / FROZEN.
### Normative Requirement Statement
> **Harmonia shall support independent governed assurance of activities, information and outcomes for which assurance is required, such that assurance conclusions are established from sufficient and trustworthy evidence against applicable obligations, expectations or controls.** > > **The activity or mechanism responsible for performing or managing the subject being assured shall not be solely responsible for determining, suppressing, manufacturing or retrospectively altering its assurance outcome. Harmonia shall establish sufficient separation of assurance responsibility and authority from responsibility for performance or control of the subject so that assurance is not merely self-attestation by the subject being assured.** > > **Assurance may identify findings, exceptions and the need for operational response, but shall not thereby assume responsibility for management, assignment, delegation, escalation or remediation of the activity being assured.** > > **Assurance may manage its own assurance activity without thereby assuming management of the subject activity.** > > **Where available evidence is insufficient to establish an assurance conclusion with the required degree of confidence, that insufficiency shall remain explicit and shall not be interpreted as either assurance or non-assurance.**
### Architectural Intent & Rationale
Those accountable for health-information handling and operational activity need credible grounds for demonstrating that applicable obligations, expectations or controls have been met. The [Regional Health Network Operator's compliance and forensic-review concerns](../stakeholder/e76216c494fa4500bb80eda6f83513c1.md), [engineers' incident review and deterministic verification concerns](../stakeholder/c20aa17ce4aa4a58be5eb3cff2ecdd1d.md), and [O3's demonstrable protection and accountable handling](../outcome/75519ed8f7de4a619cc9065f525d703a.md) already establish the value of substantive review and trustworthy evidence.
Those existing concerns do not themselves establish performer independence. The approved reconciliation adds that obligation explicitly: a conclusion controlled solely by the activity or mechanism being assured can conceal findings or manufacture confidence and cannot provide the required independent assurance. Evidence availability and operational completion alone cannot establish whether the applicable obligations, expectations or controls have been satisfied.
### Applicability & Responsibility Boundary
The requirement applies where assurance is required. It does not require assurance of every activity, information item or outcome. The criteria establishing applicability, applicable obligations and the required degree of confidence remain for subsequent governed derivation; this requirement does not define an applicability model.
Independence concerns responsibility and authority. It does not prescribe physical, technical or organisational separation, nor require external assurance. It does not allocate an assessor or prohibit the subject's performer from contributing evidence. Assurance manages its own work and may inform an operational response; responsibility for managing that response remains distinct. The explanatory shorthand is: **the assurance capability is the QA service, not the Job Foreman.**
### Semantic & Uncertainty Boundaries
The following distinctions constrain this requirement; they do not define new information types or an assurance outcome taxonomy:
```text Provenance ≠ Assurance Audit information ≠ Assurance Evidence ≠ Assurance conclusion Operational progression ≠ Assurance Workflow completion ≠ Assurance Business Outcome ≠ Assurance Outcome Operational uncertainty ≠ Insufficient assurance evidence Independent assurance ≠ External assurance Assurance finding ≠ Operational response Assurance responsibility ≠ Operational management responsibility ```
[`REQ-FND-004`](fc732b64fc564127b73174e28d9ccce8.md) and [AX-15](../principle/ef8abbaec37e4890ad78b9f263e67906.md) continue to govern uncertainty about an operation's state, effect or outcome, including an assurance activity's own execution where applicable. Separately, an assurance activity may execute correctly yet lack sufficient evidence to establish a conclusion about its subject. This requirement preserves that insufficiency without treating it as an uncertain execution outcome, execution failure, assurance or non-assurance. Neither existing operational rule is rewritten or extended into an assurance-evidence sufficiency rule.
### Motivation Relationships
These are branching relationships, not a sequential motivation pipeline. The independence, management boundary and evidence-insufficiency obligations are newly approved intent for reconciliation, not meanings retrospectively attributed to the reused elements.
| Existing element | Relationship to `REQ-FND-005` | Semantic limit | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [Regional Health Network Operator](../stakeholder/e76216c494fa4500bb80eda6f83513c1.md) | Compliance demonstration and forensic-review concerns motivate the requirement directly. | No new Operator-to-Privacy-Driver relationship or statutory independence mandate is inferred. | | [Platform Operations & Integration Engineers](../stakeholder/c20aa17ce4aa4a58be5eb3cff2ecdd1d.md) | Incident review and deterministic verification concerns motivate the requirement directly. | Operational diagnosis and monitoring remain distinct from independent assurance. | | [Statutory Health Information Privacy & Protection Driver](../driver/1dbf34b452b6497f914c704e037aec24.md) | Supports the requirement's need to evaluate handling against applicable obligations and controls. | Privacy supplies one valid motivation, not the entire assurance scope or independence obligation. | | [O3](../outcome/75519ed8f7de4a619cc9065f525d703a.md) | The requirement supports O3's existing demonstrability and accountability purpose. | Textual contribution only; no new causal handover, intermediate Goal or assurance-outcome equivalence. | | [CST-EXT-001](../constraint/0ed6fb9fcc9547659ce76b917881274e.md) | Bounds assurance concerning health-information privacy and protection by applicable obligations. | No universal external requirement for independent assurance is claimed. | | [AX-06](../principle/952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md) | Co-governs interpretation of evidence authority and credibility independently of technical state. | Information authority does not establish assessor independence. | | [AX-07](../principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md) | Co-governs security context and policy for assurance activity. | Security enforcement does not establish independent conclusion authority. | | [AX-08](../principle/21d6864657964ba5b03e3f6b5eb29cd5.md) | Co-governs meaningful provenance and audit evidence used in assurance. | Preserving evidence does not perform assurance or establish a conclusion. | | [AX-14](../principle/d3fc6025dc7646d1b2020b51f7a44bfa.md) | Co-governs preservation of the requirement's semantic distinctions. | Distinct meanings do not prescribe separate technologies or information types. |
[AX-09](../principle/9a5cb9e8876844e58e660f909f7df9fc.md) remains an evidence-selection and retention boundary: observations and progression state are not automatically provenance or audit evidence. [`REQ-FND-002`](eaabcdb96aad4f32a050c94f9ecec049.md) can supply observable operational facts; it is a complementary evidence relationship, not an independence parent or assurance conclusion. `REQ-FND-004` / AX-15 have the complementary uncertainty relationship described above. [AX-17](../principle/architectural-axiom/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) governs this explicit reconciliation and preservation of unresolved downstream derivation; it is not a source of the real-world assurance need.
### Downstream Derivation Boundary
The requirement supplies upstream motivation from which Strategy responsibility, Business assurance behaviour and Information Architecture may subsequently be derived, followed by Application Architecture and an eventual solution. Those relationships remain unestablished here. No capability allocation, workflow specification, solution construct, outcome values, evidence model, execution mechanism or deployment boundary is defined by this requirement.

Coordinate participating care-team context and collaboration around care.
Care-Team Coordination maintains the participating team context and collaboration around care. It supports continuity by making participation intelligible across people and organisational boundaries, without assuming that membership itself assigns every clinical responsibility. Within Care Coordination & Transition it concerns collaboration around care rather than proof of a responsibility handoff.
**Boundary**
Harmonia's support for team information and collaboration does not confer management of clinical handover or clinical worklists.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Knowledge Services
element.documentation:
Administer clinical knowledge requests, distribute governed knowledge artefacts and administer approved reference datasets.
**Overview**
Administer clinical knowledge requests, distribute governed knowledge artefacts and administer approved reference datasets.
**Intent**
Administer clinical knowledge requests, distribute governed knowledge artefacts and administer approved reference datasets.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Clinical Knowledge Services resolves governed clinical concepts and applies governed terminology mappings. It makes codes usable across local and standard semantic systems while retaining their source meaning. The responsibility is semantic reference and mapping enablement, distinct from formulating reusable clinical knowledge or applying that knowledge to an individual.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Code translation does not establish equivalence beyond the governed map or confer clinical decision authority.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Concept resolution and mapping materially support meaningful information exchange and interpretation across regional systems.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

The [governed definition](../../governance/continuum-representation.md#solutionfacet-classification--1119-candidate) distinguishes accessible solution classification from Capability, responsibility and ownership. Its canonical identity, G01–G18 context, existing Composition and separately established Home assertions are preserved.
Native Grouping originally authored as `Interoperability-and-Integration.Interoperability-Standards.Drivers` in the retained 004 export, incorporated under the Solution Architect's Subject Grouping hierarchy Task. It groups the source-qualified `Drivers` concern within the existing **Interoperability Standards** SolutionFacet (G05.02). Its earlier authored name above is retained as provenance; current names follow the explicit properties in the 1.1.19 submission. That earlier incoming record has no Documentation or authored Properties; no normative definition, native statement, classification of individual statements, or additional responsibility is invented to complete that absence.
The Task explicitly establishes parent-to-child Composition as containment and a separate directed child-to-parent Home Association as authoritative architectural location. These are distinct assertions. Neither diagram membership nor the Grouping's label alone establishes another Home or a statement allocation. No component ownership, implementation dependency, Capability decomposition, new Motivation statement or OpenSpec candidate incorporation is conferred.
Source Exchange identifier: `id-39d7e8efb6f340d89c970838f45cf2cc`. View placement corroborates the authorised containing SolutionFacet; the exact correspondence is retained in the iteration's folder/Grouping inventories. Existing canonical identities and all pre-existing architectural assertions retain their standing. Archi visual acceptance and HCRL closure remain separate.

element.name: [Topic] ReferralProgression
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing the progression of a Referral over time, including significant changes in its state, handling or disposition.
**Status: RESOLVED — APPROVED. G2-Q01 is resolved; G2 remains open.**
Referral Disposition is **not retained as an independent Information Concept**. The assurance and governance requirement previously represented by that B candidate is instead represented by **Referral Outcome**.
> **Referral Outcome is the governed information concerning what ultimately became of a Referral, sufficient to support assurance, governance and traceability over the Referral and its progression.**
**Semantic classification:** Outcome; provenance-bearing information with Assertion characteristics where a source reports what became of the Referral. This is not ServiceOutcome equivalence or a downstream representation category.
Referral Outcome exists principally to support the ability to account for Referrals within the applicable governance/assurance scope. Where established and appropriate, it may include the resulting outcome, basis/reason, source/originator, authority, temporal context and relationships to relevant resulting activity or information. No canonical Referral Outcome value set is established.
```text Referral ≠ Referral Progression Event ≠ Referral Outcome Referral Outcome ≠ Responsibility Assumption ≠ Transfer of Care ≠ HealthcareServiceDelivery ≠ ServiceOutcome Referral information semantics ≠ Referral Administration workflow progression ```
Referral Outcome may reference or relate to those Concepts where appropriate; its existence establishes none of them. Recording that a Referral was accepted, progressed or otherwise reached an outcome does not itself prove that care responsibility was actually assumed or transferred. G1 K1's intent/disposition/responsibility/Transfer of Care distinctions remain intact. Outcome is not equated with acceptance.
**Referral Progression Event:** Retained as historical information concerning significant occurrences in the administrative/business progression of a Referral. Not every Event represents a Referral Outcome, and the historical progression record is not collapsed into the final/current Outcome.
**Assurance / governance coverage — RF-IR5:** Harmonia must support assurance that Referrals within the applicable governance scope can be accounted for through sufficient progression and outcome information to establish what became of them. This requirement is applied to established Referral Administration / Manage Referral Progression / Referral Status & Outcome Service responsibility without allocating a new owner, Feature, Service or Collection.
```text Referral population within governance scope → progression/outcome evidence → assurance coverage ```
An inability to establish what became of a Referral is itself an assurance gap. No Referral Outcome is manufactured to make coverage appear complete. Where the outcome is not known, its absence is preserved explicitly.
**Workflow closure / finalisation:** This belongs to the progression of the Business Process / Referral Administration activity, not intrinsic Referral disposition information. The workflow may reach a state in which no further Referral Administration activity is required. This does not require a Referral Finalisation or Referral Closure Information Concept, a terminal state intrinsic to Referral, or Referral Outcome to double as workflow state. No workflow terminal states are defined and the Business Process state machine is not reproduced as the Information Concept lifecycle.
**Authority, temporal meaning and provenance:** Harmonia governs the outcome information for assurance and traceability; it does not infer substantive authority from recording or possessing it. Outcome may require provenance sufficient to establish what outcome was understood, source/originator, authority where relevant, when established/effective, and rationale/qualification where relevant. These are not all universally mandatory attributes. Detailed governance-scope criteria, evidence sufficiency, authority eligibility and contextual provenance/temporal qualification remain unestablished where existing architecture supplies no detail.
**Review history and consequence:** Q01 retains its original B question. The former Referral Disposition candidate proposed an independent Assertion for an attributable decision/reported disposition, with acceptance, decline, redirection and context-specific waitlisting examples. Architectural review rejects that separate Concept and reframes its assurance/governance purpose as Referral Outcome. Recipient-decision meanings and the canonical upstream Referral Disposition Log label are not erased. Q01 is resolved, without answering acceptance's clinical responsibility effects or the precise Referral–delivery/outcome relationships under Q05. Responsibility Assumption Assertion remains a non-authoritative D suggestion.
**Persistence boundary:** Only the Referral family, this review record and the necessary Referral navigation text are reconciled. Q02–Q07 and the complete G2-D01–D03 record remain unchanged. Frozen upstream architecture, Foundation, Package1 and initial historical report/diff are not modified. No other G2 question, G3, later Package2 family, FHIR mapping or downstream representation is commenced. G1 remains CLOSED; G2 is not CLOSED.
Source standing: G2-D04 explicitly retains significant historical progression information; historical describes represented occurrences, not historical architectural standing.

element.name: [CT3] Medication Dose Administration Aid Provision
element.documentation:
Prepare and provide organised medication doses supporting administration according to an already established regimen.
This capability prepares and supplies organised doses to support administration under an already established medication regimen. Its purpose is to make that regimen easier to follow in practice while preserving the difference between organising doses and choosing therapy. The business responsibility is not defined by any particular commercial packaging arrangement.
**Boundary**
Preparing a dose aid does not establish the regimen or demonstrate that a dose was administered.

element.name: [Feature] Entity Behaviour Failure & Recovery Governance
element.documentation:
Apply explicit behaviour-failure dispositions and controlled, authorised resumption for entity-relative processing.
**Overview**
Failure may stop a behaviour, an input or the entity progression and may leave effects uncertain. Resumption must preserve that distinction rather than imply rollback or automatic safe retry.
**Boundary**
Recovery cannot silently declare no effects, bypass governance or resume a halted entity automatically.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Compartment Assurance
element.documentation:
Assure appropriate establishment and application of compartmentalisation without establishing access decisions.
This capability evaluates whether contextual information compartments are appropriately established and applied. It treats the correctness of the grouping as a concern distinct from permission to disclose a particular item. Such assurance can make compartment use more trustworthy without changing the business relationships that define membership.
**Boundary**
Assuring compartmentalisation does not establish access decisions or sensitivity classification.

element.name: Operational Need → Coordinated Activity → Resolved Outcome
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Purpose & Value Focus
Healthcare delivery involves dynamic, distributed operational coordination—from processing an urgent laboratory order, to coordinating an inpatient bed transfer, managing clinical task escalation, or fulfilling an outpatient referral. When operational activity is disconnected from the current state of affected patients, beds, and practitioners, clinical delays and administrative failures occur.
The strategic value created by **VS-03** is the **governed, coordinated progression of operational activity together with the corresponding state of affected real-world healthcare entities** (`AX-16`). It bridges operational demand and clinical execution without premature coupling to software execution threads or queueing systems.
```mermaid graph LR S1["S1: Operational Need Identified"] --> S2["S2: Required Activity Established"] S2 --> S3["S3: Activity Coordinated"] S3 --> S4["S4: Work Progressed"] S4 --> S5["S5: Outcome Established"] S5 --> S6["S6: Affected Entity State Progressed"] ```
#### Value Transformation Stages
1. **S1 — Operational Need Identified**: - *Stakeholder State*: A healthcare operational trigger occurs (e.g., patient admission, clinical order placed, diagnostic test requested, bed turnover required, specialist referral initiated). - *Value Generated*: Healthcare demands are captured systematically rather than relying on informal or uncoordinated communication. 2. **S2 — Required Activity Established**: - *Stakeholder State*: The activity required to address the operational need is established together with its relevant context, expected outcome, and completion conditions. - *Value Generated*: Vague operational requirements are translated into clear, governed, and accountable objectives with explicit success criteria. 3. **S3 — Activity Coordinated**: - *Stakeholder State*: Required activity is coordinated with the appropriate people, services, resources, and affected real-world entities. - *Value Generated*: Work is matched to capable, authorized actors and resources in harmony with real-time operational availability and clinical priorities. 4. **S4 — Work Progressed**: - *Stakeholder State*: Execution of the activity advances through observable, auditable lifecycle states with active oversight, milestone tracking, and escalation management. - *Value Generated*: Healthcare operations gain end-to-end transparency; bottlenecks, delays, and stalled activities are immediately visible and actionable. 5. **S5 — Outcome Established**: - *Stakeholder State*: Clinical or operational results are achieved, verified, and recorded with full attribution and provenance. - *Value Generated*: Activity resolution is verified against the original intent, establishing reliable evidence of care delivery. 6. **S6 — Affected Entity State Progressed**: - *Stakeholder State*: The state of affected real-world entities (e.g., patient clinical journey, bed occupancy status, practitioner assignment, care team schedule) advances to its next governed operational state in alignment with the activity outcome (`AX-16`). - *Value Generated*: The physical and organizational reality of the healthcare facility stays synchronized with system records, eliminating state drift and coordination failures.
#### Decoupling Note: Execution Constructs Below the Value Stream
Digital Twin activity is demand-driven and coordinated through the established activity-execution architecture; Digital Twin identity does not imply a dedicated or permanently active execution thread, process or runtime engine. The Twin remains the [entity-centred coordination construct](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/strategic-views/logical-component-responsibilities.md#component-7-digital-twin-entity-centred-operational-coordination-construct).
Activity execution constructs and downstream mechanisms (illustratively, worker pools, messaging queues and FHIR Tasks) remain **below** the Value Stream. Their names are not stage names or technology choices made by this Strategy view.
#### Representative Strategic Traceability
| Traceability level | Current architectural standing | | :--- | :--- | | Motivation | Established: [AX-15 — Uncertainty Is Preserved Until Resolved](../../motivation/principle/ef8abbaec37e4890ad78b9f263e67906.md) and [AX-16 — Operational Activity & Entity State Progress Together](../../motivation/principle/de7e90f46127455a9ec9ad3b9b48ba54.md). AX-16 is explicitly applied by this stream’s purpose and entity-state progression stage. Current named Driver/Goal relationships and replacement grounding for the other retired axiom meanings remain unresolved. | | Current Business Capability contribution | **Unresolved / not presently established.** The superseded BC relationships are retired; no relationship to BC-01 through BC-18 is supplied by identifier position or similarity. | | Current Business Enabling contribution and contextual view | **Unresolved / not presently established.** Old view ordinals and meanings are retired; no enabling-capability or Feature relationship is inferred. | | Existing current Enterprise Capability contributions | **Established, partial:** [EC-02 — Context Management](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-02-context-management); [EC-12 — Operational Assurance](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-12-operational-assurance). These previously documented contributions retain their canonical meanings. Other current contributions are unresolved; the retired EC labels do not establish replacements. |
- **Strategic Courses of Action**: `COA-04` (Governed Asynchronous Activity Progression), `COA-05` (Entity-Centred Operational Coordination), `COA-06` (Collaborative Reusable Capability Realisation).
### 1.1.21 Journey incorporation
This existing Value Stream is reused as a Journey with the same canonical and Exchange identities, names, original definition and standing. Its source-defined transformations are represented by independently identifiable constituent Journeys. The added Aggregation relationships express reusable structure; Triggering expresses meaningful progression with its stated conditions. Neither creates runtime orchestration. New, explicitly qualified capability contributions supplement the predecessor traceability account; the original unestablished relationships and qualifications above are not retrospectively rewritten or declared accepted.

element.name: GovernedSummaryWriter
element.documentation:
The initial contract supports **CREATE and RETIRE only**. CREATE durably registers an IU Summary with the supplied opaque ContentMetadata reference to Content represented as already managed externally. Mnemosyne does not retrieve, verify, copy, persist or rewrite that external Content. Local structural/metadata checks and security still apply. External custody, integrity, existence, currency, availability, durability and lifecycle are SEP under that service's own obligations. Success attests governed Summary/reference persistence only; later full-read failure does not invalidate registration.
RETIRE applies the governed Harmonia IU lifecycle while preserving required identity/history, immutable versions, retention holds, audit and provenance. It does not delete/retire/modify the external referent. Original Interaction DRP MI-07 remains the RETIRE/provider-DELETE mapping subject; any provider-specific physical disposition requires its own applicable authority.
There is **no UPDATE operation**. Full GovernedWriter updates its coherent IU Summary as part of the same full write, without calling SummaryWriter UPDATE. Version integrity may require a higher actual IU version, which is returned, while Mneme retains per-IU concurrency.
The IU Summary is the projection of the same accepted InformationUnit excluding **exactly InformationRepresentation.Content**. It retains Identity, applicable Metadata (ManagementContext, InformationCoordinates, SecurityContext, LifecycleContext and optional Relationships), ContainerMetadata and ContentMetadata. A Content reference belongs in ContentMetadata and is opaque to Mneme; Mnemosyne/PersistenceService resolve it with InformationCoordinates. ContentReference is illustrative vocabulary, not a prescribed field encoding. Summary projection does not promote transient ManagementContext data to mandatory durable metadata, create a second IU/InformationRepresentation, independent metadata authority or Summary version lineage. Logical separate Content addressability does not require separate physical databases or a particular native transaction.
All five contracts are synchronous governed request/response, with Calliope-owned factual Outcome (closed Success / Failure / Indeterminate and governed closed Reason vocabulary/extensions). Exact Reason members and stage codes remain deferred. Mnemosyne reports facts; Mneme determines consumer disposition without rewriting them. Transport/session timeout is not a factual operation Failure. Receipt, work acceptance, authoritative effect and end-to-end completion remain distinct.
Authentication and Themis policy apply: Readers require ACCESS + READ, SummarySearch invocation ACCESS + SEARCH and disclosed candidates ACCESS + READ, Writers CHANGE with the requested information operation. Protect identity, metadata, counts, pagination and other existence disclosures as well as Content. RequiredIU/SupportedIU capability matching grants no permission. Preserve source-near audit/provenance, Kleio mandatory capture authority/fail-closed obligations and Dokimasia/Provenance allocations; no blanket candidate event catalogue is promoted. Native database/query/provider values stay below the seam.
Every authoritative full or Summary mutation Success requires the applicable multi-site durable authoritative operation and actual resulting IU version, never cache success, local commit, replication queued or transport ACK. Immutable historical versions are preserved. Mneme retains individual-IU concurrency; eligible Mnemosyne instances must expose one coherent authoritative logical history or factual uncertainty. No extra seam transaction identifier or second version axis is introduced.
### Incorporation standing
Accepted complete Final.001 DRP semantics; authorised 1.1.24 ADD; actual incorporated candidate awaiting Solution Architect confirmation. Authority: operative Solution Architect Task and HCRL 1.1.24/001; input approval is distinct from result acceptance.

element.name: [Feature] Encounter State Progression
element.documentation:
Track encounter status transitions (PLANNED → ARRIVED → IN_PROGRESS → ON_LEAVE → DISCHARGED).
Encounter progression preserves the difference between planned, arrived, active, leave and discharged circumstances. These states make administrative activity interpretable without implying a clinical outcome. The source's ON_LEAVE transition detail remains incomplete in the corresponding Process and is not repaired here.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E07.03.06`; additional scope correspondences: `B05.04.02`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: PersistenceService
element.documentation:
The architectural persistence-service capability is jointly realised by GovernedPersistenceFramework state/workflow control and Persistence Adapter technology-specific execution/verification. It is a service of their collaboration, not a sixth Mnemosyne responsibility tier, independent engine authority, universal provider interface or additional deployment unit.
Mnemosyne can provide one or more concrete PersistenceServices with differing suitable provider capabilities. An additive native capability belongs only to the actual supporting service/contract; this generic service definition declares no uniform search, transaction, index, history, bulk or traversal support. Select suitability for the IU, operation and obligations. Authoritative search executes/co-ordinates where capabilities support it; there is no universal cross-provider search engine mandate.
Durable effect, verified delegated operation, request receipt, accepted recoverable work and remote/end-to-end completion remain different stages. Governed UUID/Topic, authoritative state/version, IU reconstruction, preservation, security, audit and provenance obligations survive provider mapping. A provider-native DELETE is not automatic authority for governed RETIRE or destruction; retention holds and governed lifecycle decisions remain binding. Ordinary persistence recoverability is partial; catastrophic recovery orchestration remains outside Mnemosyne.
### Incorporation standing
Accepted parent DRP semantics, incorporated under the operative Task for 1.1.23/001. Actual resulting candidate confirmation remains pending. Earlier component/source qualifications remain independently in force.

element.name: Information Unit Metadata
element.documentation:
Information Unit Metadata holds four distinguishable concerns within one IU and optional supplied relationships. It is a logical DataObject, not a second governed management entity, nested IU, implementation Class or undifferentiated context store.
| Context | Accepted information and responsibility | | --- | --- | | ManagementContext | Mneme operational working information outside IU identity and represented Content. Embedded, referenced (including a cache-table reference), or hybrid; operational data may be explicitly transient. Client visibility grants no write authority. A lost transient reference is not durable truth. Mneme operational Version and Active Generation belong here. | | InformationCoordinates | Four semantically distinct TopicID references: PersistenceGateway (named PersistenceService gateway/capability), GatewayEndpoint (named logical endpoint/parameter context), InformationLocation (logical location/node), InformationOwner (operational owner). Mnemosyne interprets them to resolve service and access context. They are names, not URLs, credentials, inline implementations, connection parameters or physical storage addresses. | | SecurityContext | IU-side required action, compartment and other criteria using explicit Topics and/or TopicMasks. It is not the requesting Identity's permissions, Passport or PEP-Criteria. Themis owns policy and local PEP enforcement; a match alone grants no access. | | LifecycleContext | Mneme–Mnemosyne persistence/lifecycle handshaking, preserving request, acceptance, commit and completion distinctions as required. No universal state machine or Content lifecycle owner; detailed vocabulary and preservation rules remain with governing contracts. |
**InformationCoordinates is independent of SecurityContext.** Operational owner, gateway or location grants no clearance, compartment membership or read right. Policy may separately consult a coordinate without turning it into a security rule. Presence/population rules are contract-specific; no universal mandatory-coordinate rule or configuration/deployment scheme is introduced.
| Version/generation concern | Home and meaning | | --- | --- | | Operational Version | ManagementContext: Mneme cache coherence, conflict/stale-write detection and optimistic concurrency. Does not substitute for Mnemosyne authoritative durable version progression. | | Active Generation | ManagementContext: an individual successfully established active manifestation of the same IU in a Mneme cache environment/endpoint. Multiple generations may express the same operational Version. No new IU, representation or Content version follows. | | Content Structure Version | InformationRepresentation.ContentMetadata: schema/structure version described by the Content Structure Topic. | | Native Content instance version, if any | InformationRepresentation.Content: native payload contract; no synthetic native version is required. |
Active Generation is not a timestamp or a global counter. AX-05's successful-state, failed/degraded-convergence and untrusted-coordination rules remain binding. Failure to establish a generation changes neither the IU's governed information state nor, by itself, an already established generation. No cache coherence, distributed locking, invalidation, retry or generation-selection algorithm is chosen.
Temporal information stays with its meaning: clinical/business event/effective times in Content; structure versions in ContentMetadata; needed working-cache timestamps in ManagementContext; needed persistence/handshake times in LifecycleContext. There is no mandatory TemporalContext or universal native payload lifecycle/history. Retention holds, archival, immutable history, authorised disposition, recovery and RETIRE versus physical destruction retain their distinct existing governance.
Optional **Relationships [0..*]** are creator/authorised-updater supplied IU-to-IU or external-resource attributes/references. relatesTo, partOf and basedOn are illustrative, not a mandatory vocabulary or a substitute for Provenance. Mneme validates local reference acceptability under the applicable governed contract, including suitable identity/authorised constraints; this is neither clinical-truth validation nor target access permission. Mneme preserves remote references without assuming responsibility for target existence, availability or correctness. There is no automatic relationship inference, reciprocal maintenance, update propagation, referent repair, distributed transaction or universal relationship database.
Provenance, AuditEvent, IU relationships and SecurityContext are distinct. Dokimasia owns the established Provenance Management framework/lifecycle and independent assurance; originating components use its existing Provenance Client Library. Kleio retains AuditEvent management and authoritative audit capture. Mneme manages active information; Mnemosyne establishes durable state. The IU carries appropriate references/correlation without implementing evidence or lifecycle orchestration. Request/session Passports/enforcement snapshots do not automatically become durable IU Metadata or Content. Detailed field schemas, local-reference constraints and provider acknowledgement/recovery vocabulary remain contract obligations.

element.name: [CT3] Preventative Health Problem Identification
element.documentation:
Identify and characterise a preventative-health problem warranting organised attention.
This capability establishes the preventative-health problem warranting organised attention. It gives an intended programme a reason grounded in the concern being addressed rather than assuming that a population statistic already defines the response. The identified problem can frame subsequent cohort and programme considerations without becoming an individual's clinical diagnosis.
**Boundary**
Population evidence informs problem identification but does not by itself establish a programme, cohort or individual care need.
## ARB identity continuity
Historical identity [b35d3521141c419fb676a79b2ede40bd](b35d3521141c419fb676a79b2ede40bd.md) has direct correspondence with this capability under HCRL 1.1.5-002. Historical provenance and UUID reservation remain with that record; this resource retains its existing identity and independent standing.

element.name: [CT3] Access Control Collaboration
element.documentation:
Coordinate arrangements across independently controlled domains/parties while retaining their control ownership.
Access Control Collaboration coordinates arrangements across parties or domains that retain independent control ownership. Its purpose is coherent cross-boundary control where a strong local arrangement alone cannot establish the whole result. Collaboration therefore concerns agreed control participation rather than silently centralising every participant's authority.
**Boundary**
Coordination does not transfer the parties' control ownership or guarantee identity quality across domains.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: [CT3] Health Service Capacity Planning
element.documentation:
Determine required strategic/tactical capacity to address assessed demand.
Health Service Capacity Planning determines the strategic or tactical capacity required to address assessed demand. It considers what should be available, preserving a distinction between requirement and the resources currently in service. Within Health-System Planning it gives demand a capacity response without performing operational allocation.
**Boundary**
Planned capacity is neither established resource availability nor the service's currently usable operational capacity.

element.name: Platform Operations & Integration Engineers
element.documentation:
### Profile & Role Platform Operations and Integration Engineers are the systems reliability engineers (SREs), DevOps professionals, integration middleware developers, and technical support teams tasked with running, monitoring, and maintaining the Harmonia platform.
### Core Responsibilities - Deploying, scaling, and configuring Harmonia runtime services across regional data centers and cloud infrastructure. - Monitoring system health, message queues, throughput, network latency, and integration error rates. - Diagnosing integration failures, investigating communication anomalies, and conducting incident retrospectives.
### Principal Architectural Concerns - **Deep Diagnosability Without PHI Leakage**: Rich operational metrics, traces, and diagnostic logs that provide full visibility into message processing without emitting Protected Health Information (PHI) into non-clinical tooling. - **Zero Unmonitored Message Loss**: Deterministic verification regarding the progression state of incoming events, ensuring that failed downstream deliveries are immediately flagged rather than lost in silent dead-letter sinks. - **Observable Multi-Stage Activity State**: Transparent visibility into complex, distributed workflows (such as fan-out distributions) where tasks progress across multiple hops and destination endpoints. - **Deterministic Failure Semantics**: Clean separation of active operational coordination from authoritative durable state, preventing data corruption during unexpected node crashes or network partitions.
### Approved stakeholder separation — 1.1.18 / 001
The original profile above is retained as the historical combined population. The Solution Architect approved its separation into two distinct actor populations through the complete Subject/Views Task. Its canonical UUID and Exchange ID are reserved and unchanged. Neither successor is assigned the predecessor identity.
- [Integration & Solution Engineers](1dc29678ec4a4a498620c84ffa03c2bb.md), canonical UUID `1dc29678ec4a4a498620c84ffa03c2bb`. - [Platform Operations & OA&M Personnel](ec45ffa1b7d841cf920aa467d4d2b1f4.md), canonical UUID `ec45ffa1b7d841cf920aa467d4d2b1f4`.
Existing references and relationships remain attached to the historical combined population. No relationship is duplicated or retargeted by the separation. The one-to-many evolution is recorded by these reciprocal explanations and attributable provenance, rather than an invented one-to-one equivalence.

element.name: Infinispan Server — Standard Cache
element.documentation:
Selected remote Infinispan Server machinery supporting Mneme-Standard-Cache through Hot Rod clients. The logical technology selection is explicit; it allocates no cluster, site, node count, process boundary, container layout, new durable store or coordination protocol. Multiple runtime instances share this architectural definition.
Synchronous distribution stores entries on configured owners, not automatically on every node/site. It does not establish linearizable reads, state-machine serialisation or safe same-key concurrent cross-site writes in independent active clusters. Single spanning cluster versus site-local clusters/cross-site backups, ownership/site placement, partition/failover and N+1 bounded degradation remain MC-01/02 technical/deployment verification. No cache acknowledgment proves authoritative write Success.
### Retained MC-01–MC-07 qualifications
- **MC-01:** Standard-Cache multi-site topology and active/active consistency need evidence; synchronous distribution/cross-site backup is not native linearizability or safe independent-cluster same-key concurrency. - **MC-02:** Owner count/site placement, majority/partition/failover and continued governed work after one site loss remain unproved; Mneme retains state-transition concurrency obligations beyond cache operations. - **MC-03:** Per-JVM memory bounds, safe eviction/lifetime relative to context load/unload/checkpoint and security isolation remain solution/deployment policy under existing Ergon semantics. - **MC-04:** Durable propagation does not prove immediate replica read visibility. Exact-version/currentness, read-after-write and wait/fail/Indeterminate behaviour use Mneme–Mnemosyne and PersistenceService contracts; no cache affinity mechanism is invented. - **MC-05:** Active/active N+1 (N > 0) is an architectural target, not a verified product guarantee. With only two physical sites, loss of one prevents **new multi-site durable write Success** without another eligible durable site or explicit owning NFR/persistence disposition. Never weaken Success or claim unqualified N+1 write continuity. Three-plus sites alone do not prove quorum/failover correctness. - **MC-06:** Five-service reconciliation is deterministically incorporated: historical GovernedSearch identity is reused as sole GovernedSummarySearch, Summary Reader/Writer added, full Reader/Writer retained; no independent Summary IU or sixth method. - **MC-07:** Existing capability/Feature contributions are reused. Physical remote-client/embedded ownership, observation, deployment and as-built integration remain downstream; no new module or implementation framework is selected.
### Incorporation standing
Accepted complete Final.001 DRP semantics; authorised 1.1.24 ADD; actual incorporated candidate awaiting Solution Architect confirmation. Authority: operative Solution Architect Task and HCRL 1.1.24/001; input approval is distinct from result acceptance.

element.name: [BusinessObject] Metabolē
element.documentation:
> **Metabolē** is a conceptual information construct representing the bounded > progression of one or more Information Units through a change or activity. > A Metabolē incorporates the input information, applicable Context and > provenance/derivation associated with that progression and accumulates the > resulting output information.
```text Metabolē ├── Input [IU 1..*] ├── Context │ ├── ActivityContext │ └── other applicable Context ├── Provenance / Derivation └── Output [IU 0..*] ```
The [Information Unit](10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md) remains the governed information boundary. Metabolē describes the bounded progression involving Units; it does not replace their identities, originating authority, Management Context or lifecycle. Its conceptual partitions do not prescribe nesting, copying, reference structures, physical representation or a new universal lifecycle.
Metabolē is conceptual. It is not an application subsystem, persistence service, execution component or runtime manager. No `MetaboleManager` or equivalent application responsibility SHALL be inferred.
Source standing: Adjudicated conceptual IA extension, 2026-10-13; no application manager.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/metabole.md` — ## 1. Concept and information boundary. Standing: Adjudicated conceptual Information Architecture; original qualifications retained.
> **Metabolē** is a conceptual information construct representing the bounded > progression of one or more Information Units through a change or activity. > A Metabolē incorporates the input information, applicable Context and > provenance/derivation associated with that progression and accumulates the > resulting output information.
```text Metabolē ├── Input [IU 1..*] ├── Context │ ├── ActivityContext │ └── other applicable Context ├── Provenance / Derivation └── Output [IU 0..*] ```
The [Information Unit](10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md) remains the governed information boundary. Metabolē describes the bounded progression involving Units; it does not replace their identities, originating authority, Management Context or lifecycle. Its conceptual partitions do not prescribe nesting, copying, reference structures, physical representation or a new universal lifecycle.
Metabolē is conceptual. It is not an application subsystem, persistence service, execution component or runtime manager. No `MetaboleManager` or equivalent application responsibility SHALL be inferred.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/metabole.md` — ## 2. Architectural Realisation. Standing: Adjudicated conceptual Information Architecture; original qualifications retained.
**Pragma realises Metabolē** for governed Harmonia information/activity progression. **Pylai.Diadromí realises Metabolē** for transient information progression through Pylai interoperability activity.
```text Metabolē «conceptual construct» ▲ │ Realisation ┌──────┴──────┐ │ │ Pragma Pylai.Diadromí ```
These are genuine architectural **Realisation** relationships in the architectural/ArchiMate/TOGAF sense: a concrete, domain-specific construct realises the conceptual construct. They are not analogy, synonymy or merely conceptual similarity. A realisation may introduce domain-specific lifecycle, semantics, structure and management responsibility.
Realisation SHALL NOT imply that Pragma and Diadromí inherit from each other, share a runtime type or application manager, or have identical physical representations, persistence requirements or lifecycles.
| Realisation | Preserved application responsibility and boundary | | :--- | :--- | | [Pragma](../../application/data-object/27ad143e7c784e378556af8a57c438f7.md) | Mneme retains Context and Pragma management. Execution does not acquire information-management responsibility. Mnemosyne alone establishes authoritative durable state where required. | | [Pylai.Diadromí](../../application/data-object/978f5c2bd2d343ffaf3a13dff700c258.md) | Pylai retains responsibility for transient interoperability progression. Diadromí remains non-recoverable after loss/termination; appropriate client retry creates a new interaction. Realisation does not make it a Pragma, Task, Ergon or durable handoff. |
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/metabole.md` — ## 3. Context and ActivityContext. Standing: Adjudicated conceptual Information Architecture; original qualifications retained.
`Metabolē.Context.ActivityContext` is a conceptual semantic classification describing the broad class of activity represented by the Metabolē. It answers:
> **What broad class of activity is this information progression undertaking?**
The initial architectural vocabulary is:
```text INFORMATION_REQUEST INFORMATION_CREATE INFORMATION_UPDATE
ACTIVITY_INITIATION ACTIVITY_UPDATE ACTIVITY_STOP ```
These are initial examples, not an exhaustive enumeration or an implementation enum. No further values are established merely for symmetry.
ActivityContext is distinct from a specific request action:
```text Metabolē.Context.ActivityContext = INFORMATION_REQUEST request.action = SEARCH request.content = <search criteria/content> ```
The path expresses conceptual semantics, not a required field layout. ActivityContext neither grants authority nor establishes the policy permission for a specific action. Its shared model, definition and nomenclature semantics are governed consistently with [Calliope](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md); runtime policy resolution, authorisation decisions and enforcement remain with Themis. No physical Models/DataSets allocation or new runtime vocabulary service is decided here.
Metabolē's applicable Context, the Information Unit's [Management Context](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#65-context), Mneme's [value-based activity Context](../../application/data-object/76ded4866bf443dabc0849d68b215690.md) and Themis PEP-Context retain their distinct meanings. This classification does not equate those Contexts or decide their detailed representation/mapping.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/metabole.md` — ## 4. Additive progression and information accountability. Standing: Adjudicated conceptual Information Architecture; original qualifications retained.
Service fulfilment may progress through a Metabolē carrying the governing Context and accumulated information associated with the Service Request. Functions act upon the information relevant to their defined state transition and add resulting information to the progressing Metabolē.
The originating request and information established by preceding Functions remain available to subsequent Functions, subject to applicable information-management, security and lifecycle constraints. Additive progression does not require unrestricted visibility, indefinite retention, automatic durable persistence, or publication of all accumulated information to the client.
**Additive progression does not mean every Function consumes everything already present within the Metabolē.** Carriage alone establishes neither a `requires`/`consumes` relationship nor Function accountability. The [Step B relationship rules](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/traceability/step-b-method.md#b1-r03) identify only relationships material to the Function's state transition.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/metabole.md` — ## 5. Provenance, evidence and architectural consistency. Standing: Adjudicated conceptual Information Architecture; original qualifications retained.
A progressing Metabolē SHALL retain sufficient provenance/derivation information to establish how accumulated information was derived and how it relates to the originating activity/request.
```text Provenance / derivation ≠ Audit Evidence ≠ Assurance Evidence ```
This is an information obligation, not a new evidence repository or manager. The [provenance framework](f3bd4181bb394db8a505705b03972cea.md) retains derivation meaning; Kleio retains audit information responsibility and Dokimasia retains assurance responsibility. Transient operational mechanics do not automatically become durable evidence.
The material [Architectural Axioms](../../../../docs/markdown/governance/architectural-axioms.md) are AX-01/04 (information meaning independent of machinery), AX-05 (active/durable separation), AX-07 (intrinsic security), AX-08/09 (meaningful evidence versus transient state), AX-13 (external management boundary), AX-14 (distinct concepts) and AX-17/18 (explicit uncertainty and no inferred authority). The conceptual definition and domain-specific realisations preserve these boundaries. Detailed schemas, lifecycle/retention mechanisms and application contracts remain downstream; the concept establishes no new persistence or management authority.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Structure Management
element.documentation:
Manage structures, element/reference definitions, constraints and semantic bindings giving content unambiguous meaning.
This capability manages the structures, element definitions, references and bindings that make content interpretable. It addresses how a represented item can have an unambiguous meaning without treating the structure as the clinical fact itself. Semantic bindings identify applicable governed references while preserving their external authority.
**Boundary**
Structure management is not terminology governance and does not prescribe FHIR resources, physical schemas or storage technology.
## Capability model replacement history

element.name: [CT2] Order Administration
element.documentation:
Order Administration manages the closed loop around a request for defined fulfilment. It receives the request, resolves and routes to a destination, distinguishes delivery from business disposition, tracks progress and associates the eventual outcome. This makes the difference between an order sent and an order fulfilled visible throughout the requester's interaction.
**Overview**
Order Administration manages the closed loop around a request for defined fulfilment. It receives the request, resolves and routes to a destination, distinguishes delivery from business disposition, tracks progress and associates the eventual outcome. This makes the difference between an order sent and an order fulfilled visible throughout the requester's interaction.
**Intent**
Order Administration manages the closed loop around a request for defined fulfilment. It receives the request, resolves and routes to a destination, distinguishes delivery from business disposition, tracks progress and associates the eventual outcome. This makes the difference between an order sent and an order fulfilled visible throughout the requester's interaction.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Intent — predecessor explanation
Preserve an intelligible connection between the original request, its destination, progression and returned outcome.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Technical acknowledgements have only their contractual meaning. Receipt does not universally establish durable acceptance, business acceptance or completion; outcome association has no invented Feature equivalence.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Reliable routing and closed-loop state are direct platform responsibilities. The performing service retains authority over clinical execution and its result.
## Qualified relationship assertions
Original source predicates, evidence and qualifications remain in the metadata. The ARB has now adjudicated their native treatment; explicitly unestablished relationship existence remains excluded. Native representation does not promote source standing.

element.name: [CT3] Identity Modelling & Interoperability
element.documentation:
Establish identity models and interoperability arrangements appropriate to organisational identity use.
This capability establishes identity models and arrangements through which identities can be understood across organisational use. It addresses the coherence needed when parties exchange or rely on identity information without assuming that their identity assertions have identical quality. Its purpose is meaningful interoperability, rather than a particular federation or Single Sign-On technology.
**Boundary**
Interoperability does not guarantee assurance quality or transfer each party's control ownership.
## Capability model replacement history
The original content above remains historical and unchanged. This resource is superseded under [the replacement task](../../../design/evidence/1.1.20/001/before/CapabilityReplacementTask.md). Primary replacement catalogue identity `E05.07.02`; additional scope correspondences: `E05.07.03`. Original canonical/Exchange identities and source contributions remain reserved. Correspondence does not assert complete semantic equivalence, implementation satisfaction or transfer domain authority.

element.name: [CT2] Location Administration
element.documentation:
Location Administration represents the places and physical relationships relevant to healthcare activity, from facilities to particular care places. Address and geospatial context answer where a place is; hierarchy explains its surroundings; care-place definition records the local characteristics relevant to care. These are stable descriptive responsibilities, distinct from the changing operational state of a bed or ward.
**Overview**
Location Administration represents the places and physical relationships relevant to healthcare activity, from facilities to particular care places. Address and geospatial context answer where a place is; hierarchy explains its surroundings; care-place definition records the local characteristics relevant to care. These are stable descriptive responsibilities, distinct from the changing operational state of a bed or ward.
**Intent**
Location Administration represents the places and physical relationships relevant to healthcare activity, from facilities to particular care places. Address and geospatial context answer where a place is; hierarchy explains its surroundings; care-place definition records the local characteristics relevant to care. These are stable descriptive responsibilities, distinct from the changing operational state of a bed or ward.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Defining a place does not establish occupancy, readiness, facilities maintenance or service capacity.
## Qualified relationship assertions

element.name: [Topic] Task
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing an identifiable instance of work to be completed, including its purpose, context, state and applicable completion expectations.
For example, the archetype **"Climb a ladder"** describes a kind of work; **"ladder-climb-0023"** identifies a particular `ActionableTask` of that kind. These are conceptual examples, not an identifier scheme.
An `ActionableTask` SHALL NOT mean the reusable definition or the execution / undertaking of the work. Its contextual work meaning remains distinct from information about particular undertakings.
An `ActionableTask` explicitly governs execution concurrency, which undertakings participate in resolving its outcome, and how their outputs establish its `Task.Output(s)`. The following three controls are independent semantic properties, not an implementation structure or execution mechanism.
#### 2.2.1 ActionableTask.ExecutionConcurrency
```text ActionableTask.ExecutionConcurrency = [1..x] ```
`ExecutionConcurrency` establishes how many `FulfillmentTask` undertakings of the `ActionableTask` may execute concurrently. It concerns execution concurrency only; it does not determine which undertakings establish the `TaskOutcome`. This permitted concurrency range does not require an undertaking to exist or execute: an ActionableTask may still have zero undertakings. No universal value for `x` or concurrency execution mechanism is established here.
#### 2.2.2 ActionableTask.OutcomeConcurrency.Mode
```text ActionableTask.OutcomeConcurrency.Mode = FirstToFinish | AssignedToFinish | Aggregate ```
This property determines **which FulfillmentTask undertaking or undertakings participate in resolving the ActionableTask outcome**.
| Mode | Participation semantics | | :--- | :--- | | **FirstToFinish** | The applicable first finishing/qualifying `FulfillmentTask` establishes participation in resolution of the outcome. This defines neither detailed terminal-state qualification nor cancellation or execution mechanics for other undertakings. | | **AssignedToFinish** | A particular assigned `FulfillmentTask` has responsibility for establishing the outcome. Other undertakings may exist or execute concurrently; their existence or completion does not independently establish the ActionableTask outcome. The assignment mechanism is not defined here. | | **Aggregate** | Multiple applicable `FulfillmentTask` undertakings participate in resolving the ActionableTask outcome. This selects the participating undertakings; it does not require recursive TaskOutcome composition or determine how their outputs form the resulting output. |
#### 2.2.3 ActionableTask.Outcome.OutputRules.Mode
```text ActionableTask.Outcome.OutputRules.Mode = Direct | Collection | Derived ```
This independent property determines **how the outputs of the participating FulfillmentTasks establish the ActionableTask's Task.Output(s)**.
| Mode | Output semantics | Conceptual path | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Direct** | The applicable participating `FulfillmentTask` output is used directly as the ActionableTask output. | `FulfillmentTask.Output` → `TaskOutcome` → `Task.Output`. | | **Collection** | The applicable participating `FulfillmentTask` outputs collectively form the ActionableTask output, preserving them as the relevant collection/set. Collection does not itself imply derivation of new domain meaning. | `FulfillmentTask.Output [0..*]` → Collection → `TaskOutcome` → `Task.Output(s)`. | | **Derived** | A new ActionableTask output is derived from the applicable participating `FulfillmentTask` outputs according to explicitly defined rules. | `FulfillmentTask.Output(s)` → Explicit Rules → `TaskOutcome` → `Task.Output(s)`. |
`Derived` is an information semantic. It prescribes no implementation mechanism for executing the explicit rules. Harmonia need not infer the encapsulated domain meaning of participating outputs in order to apply those rules; the [observable-information/domain-meaning boundary](../../../business/business-object/10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md) continues to apply. Developer-defined Ergo logic and optional runtime AI retain their existing boundaries; neither is prescribed as the means of derivation.
#### 2.2.4 Orthogonality of the Three Controls
| ActionableTask concern | Question answered | | :--- | :--- | | **ExecutionConcurrency** | How many FulfillmentTasks may execute concurrently? | | **OutcomeConcurrency.Mode** | Which FulfillmentTask undertaking(s) participate in resolving the ActionableTask outcome? | | **Outcome.OutputRules.Mode** | How are the participating FulfillmentTask outputs used to establish the ActionableTask Task.Output(s)? |
These controls SHALL remain orthogonal and SHALL NOT be collapsed into one lifecycle, state or concurrency mechanism. Multiple undertakings may execute concurrently while only one participates in the TaskOutcome. Multiple may participate while their outputs are collected or used to derive another output. No universal mode combination, default or execution algorithm is inferred from these examples.
Source standing: Bounded adjudicated conceptual Task meaning; section 5 reservations, including runtime TaskOutcome identity/lifecycle, remain unresolved.

element.name: To Do Progression Process
element.documentation:
• Owning Capability: Workflow & Activity Coordination • Activity Archetype: Human Reviewing / Updating / Deciding — clinical review, document countersignature, or administrative authorization task. • State Progression Lifecycle: RAD diagram: textual source notation. \begin{Verbatim}[breaklines,fontsize= ] graph LR I["Issued"] --> B["In-Inbox"] B --> R["Opened / Under-Review"] R --> A["Actioned / Decided"] D["Dismissed / Delegated
Disposition/position unresolved"] NOTE["Illustrative progression, not a normative transition model.
Relationship of dismissal/delegation to action/decision is unestablished."] classDef note fill:#fff8dc,stroke:#8a6d3b,stroke-dasharray:5 5; class NOTE,D note; \end{Verbatim} • Key State Dispositions: • Issued: To Do generated (e.g., review abnormal potassium result). • In-Inbox: Displayed in practitioner's actionable task list. • Opened / Under-Review: Clinician inspecting relevant clinical context. • Actioned / Decided: Decision executed (e.g., signed off, order placed, acknowledged). • Dismissed / Delegated: Task reassigned to registrar or dismissed with comment. • Preserved uncertainty: Whether dismissal/delegation is an alternative disposition, a subsequent action or a scoped variant remains unresolved; its disconnected diagram node establishes no transition or position in the illustrative progression. --- ## History ### Process Overview — predecessor explanation To Do progression coordinates a human review or decision item. Completion records progression of the item, while the significance and authority of the resulting judgement depend on the governed activity. A review being marked complete therefore does not independently establish clinical adequacy, signing authority or an assurance conclusion. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md` — entry lines 297-320. Standing: exact originating assertion; current resource standing unchanged. ### 5.15 To Do Progression Process - **Owning Capability**: `Workflow & Activity Coordination` - **Activity Archetype**: **Human Reviewing / Updating / Deciding** — clinical review, document countersignature, or administrative authorization task. - **State Progression Lifecycle**: ```mermaid graph LR I["Issued"] --> B["In-Inbox"] B --> R["Opened / Under-Review"] R --> A["Actioned / Decided"] D["Dismissed / Delegated
Disposition/position unresolved"] NOTE["Illustrative progression, not a normative transition model.
Relationship of dismissal/delegation to action/decision is unestablished."] classDef note fill:#fff8dc,stroke:#8a6d3b,stroke-dasharray:5 5; class NOTE,D note; ``` - **Key State Dispositions**: - `Issued`: To Do generated (e.g., review abnormal potassium result). - `In-Inbox`: Displayed in practitioner's actionable task list. - `Opened / Under-Review`: Clinician inspecting relevant clinical context. - `Actioned / Decided`: Decision executed (e.g., signed off, order placed, acknowledged). - `Dismissed / Delegated`: Task reassigned to registrar or dismissed with comment. - **Preserved uncertainty**: Whether dismissal/delegation is an alternative disposition, a subsequent action or a scoped variant remains unresolved; its disconnected diagram node establishes no transition or position in the illustrative progression. --- ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md` — entry lines 298-298.
